Spotlight: 120,000euros yearling; by Sioux Nation; closely related to 7f/1m winner City Runner (RPR 92), half-brother to winners Whatsgoingonmarvin (1m2f-14.3f; 94) and Flying Rock (7f 2yo; 71); dam placed at 7f (83); first 2yo runner of the season for Roger Varian.

RaceName: Rossdales British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: £52,000 yearling; half-brother by Space Traveller to winners Rikki Tiki Tavi (5f 2yo; RPR 84) and Yakfeek (French 5.5f); dam French maiden (placed 7.5f), half-sister to French 1m4f Group 3 winner Remus De La Tour; others look more interesting.

RaceName: Rossdales British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 28-1 but shaped quite well when third of 11 at Salisbury (6f, soft) five weeks ago, doing his best work late on; today's extra furlong should suit but he probably faces stronger opposition.

All races at 6f, winning on debut at Goodwood but having a difficult task when third in a Group 3 at Salisbury on her next and final juvenile start; never looked comfortable over the trip on belated return in an AW novice at Southwell last month but her powerful finish into fourth strongly suggests she'll improve for an extra furlong now handicapping; considered.

Lacks experience but not spirit as she showed when hanging on to her lead in a novice at Wetherby (from a subsequent winner) four weeks ago, making it 2-2 over 7f; open to improvement but will need it against some who already have solid handicap form under their belts.

Winner of first two starts, both over 7f, including at this course; hard to place since but her sights are lowered after running in the 1,000 Guineas and the Sandringham (1m, good to firm) at Royal Ascot, where she ran with great credit on the far side of the stands' group; solid chance back at 7f for last year's winning trainer-jockey combination.

Recorded 33-1 success in a valuable 6f York handicap last summer and has run some good races over that trip as a 3yo, including when overcoming a wide draw with aplomb at Chester in May; failed to stay 7f on the AW on her final 2yo start but might have needed a rest by then; has a bit to prove but it's possible she'll fare better on this second attempt at the trip.

Came on plenty as a 3yo, winning a 7f turf novice and her handicap debut on Newcastle AW (1m); showed her mettle back on turf at Ascot (1m, good) in May, when dividing subsequent winners of a Listed race and the Kensington Palace at Royal Ascot, and there's a good chance she can do just as well in a strongly run race back at 7f; has every chance.

A promising challenge petered out in sole 7f run, on Kempton AW last September, and she was all the better for the return to 6f when winning there next time; never involved from a wide draw behind Ruby's Angel at Chester (6f) on May return and, although the run was probably needed, she still has to prove her stamina for this far; hood left off on last two starts, now refitted.

Excellent second in this race (good to firm) last year, when conceding weight to a winner who went on to better things; back to form when outstaying Shallow at Yarmouth (7f, good; similar terms today) in April and has since run well in a Group 3; early stumble cost her at Musselburgh since but she shouldn't be far away back in a handicap.

Her one win from ten starts came in a Lingfield novice as 2yo but she's improving and produced best effort when dividing higher-rated fillies in a Listed race at Carlisle (7f, good to firm) last month; inevitably has torpedoed her handicap mark as a result, going up 10lb, and needs extra back at this level.

Often leads; all wins at 6f and although Havana Pusey wore her down only late on at Yarmouth in April, on her most recent 7f run, all the signs are that she will give best to stronger stayers, as in this race last year.

Won handicaps in May on the other course here and at Carlisle (both 1m on good to firm) but the rise in the weights and grade proved a step too far behind Moonfall in the Britannia at Royal Ascot; another tall order here.

Learning to settle proved a slow process but he had another go at front-running in a C&D novice three weeks ago and it paid off, albeit against four rivals in a very different type of contest to this; goes handicapping in a competitive contest with more to prove.

Overwhelmed rivals on handicap debut at Doncaster (7f, good to soft) last September and even better in defeat in a Group 3 at Newbury after; looked sure to improve upon a useful return at Goodwood (7f, good) in May when upped to 1m in the Britannia at Royal Ascot but he could never gather momentum after getting hampered 2f out; remains one to be interested in.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Promising profile included a Newbury novice win (extended 6f) last summer but it went into orbit, after running better than the bare result on Chester reappearance, when he got to the front over 1f out in the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) and held off allcomers; a 7lb rise may not interrupt his progress over 1m.

Won 7f AW maiden on final 2yo start; creditable show in a Group 3 at Leopardstown (7f, good to yielding) in April but he scoped dirty after finishing remote in Listed race on final start for Jessica Harrington; open to improvement at some stage for new yard but this is a testing start for them.

Promised much in two of first three starts, when a wide-margin winner on AW debut then successfully switched to turf on the other course here (1m, good) in May; however, his remote finish in the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m) was a reality check and he needs to redeem his reputation here; yard has won four of the last eight runnings.

Had a charmed run when winning first four handicaps, at 1m and 7f, but the spell was broken by St Anton at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) last time; raised a further 5lb against rivals who haven't shown their hand to the same extent; cheekpieces are now fitted.

Some good efforts at 7f and 1m in Listed events at home and Group 3s in Italy since winning a 7f novice at Doncaster as 2yo; quite badly hampered on handicap debut in the Golden Gates at Royal Ascot (upped to 1m2f) but his race was run at the time; probably needs to drop in the weights.

Showed career-best form in this race in 2024 (won by 2l) and 2025 (beaten only a nose), both off higher marks; posted a resurgent effort, behind Dark Tornado, returned to this C&D latest start; respected.
Reliable sort, this year over 7.5f/1m since being gelded; second on Newcastle AW with tongue-tie fitted last time; has gained both wins over a bare 7f; strong claims back down in distance.
Record of 3-9 includes two wins at the Newmarket tracks; good second, beaten only a neck, in the 7f handicap at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently; due to go up 3lb in future; strong contender.
Performed well (first and third) at Chester in last two turf attempts and may be capable of further progress returned to this sphere; helps to give his connections, who also run Aalto, a robust hand.

Useful on his day but a record of 010 for new stable shows that he's not a particularly solid option in another major handicap; held at Royal Ascot, failing to back up his Epsom win; wears first-time hood.
Has gained both handicap wins off a mark of 90, including when beating Aalto over C&D (good to firm) latest start; could go well but needs a career-best performance to defy a penalty; 1lb badly in.
Landed two major handicaps (6f/7f) last summer but is higher in the weights now and may be in the assessor's grip on home soil; sole success off a triple-digit mark came at Meydan (early this year).

Ran well, only a neck behind Elarak, in the 7f handicap at Royal Ascot to maintain his solid record in headgear; good second in the Victoria Cup the time before; threatening to win a big prize; shortlisted.
Quite a useful sort but has a stronger record at Meydan than on home soil and came up well short when an outsider in the 7f handicap at Royal Ascot most recently; others preferred.

Respectable fifth in this year's Victoria Cup; prevailed last Saturday to take C&D record to 2-2 and overall strike-rate to 7-23; incurs 6lb penalty but Conor Whiteley takes off a useful 5lb; major player.

Broadly disappointing since proving smart in his early days; form for new yard includes a couple of encouraging efforts but he dropped away rather tamely over C&D (race won by Dark Tornado) last time.
Has gradually come to hand for new stable and made all, unchallenged, over C&D (good) most recently; 3lb ahead of the assessor under a penalty but another easy lead isn't certain; back up two grades.

Has a suitable scenario as his form over C&D includes a win last summer and he turned in a resurgent effort on latest outing; has something to prove at this level, however, having raced only in lower grades.

Unbeaten bar a mishap at Yarmouth when unseating his rider; long odds-on over C&D (good to firm) three weeks ago and comfortably beat his four rivals; open to further progress, warrants this rise in grade and his stable has won the last two runnings of this event.

Wootton Bassett colt who cost 2,300,000euros as a yearling and made the perfect start when comfortably justifying favouritism at the Curragh (6f, good) last month, from Haffner who runs in the 1.40 on this card; bred to be suited by today's extra furlong and his stable won this in 2023 with subsequent Derby winner City Of Troy; strong claims.

Close second to Alfred Wallace at Thirsk on debut and stepped up markedly on that form when fifth of 14 in the Listed Chesham Stakes at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm), always up with the pace; open to further improvement and not ruled out by any means.
Well-bred son of Gleneagles who came out just on top in a three-way photo-finish at Newbury (6.5f, good to soft; 14-1) four weeks ago; should improve but he's in much deeper here.

Narrow winner of Thirsk novice (7f, good) in May on second start before finishing down the field in the Listed 6f Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (12-1) when meeting trouble; has plenty to find but he's well bred and it's unlikely we've seen the best of him yet.

Built on a promising debut when winning a Lingfield maiden (7f, good) in May by 6l, making all; still has untapped potential but there wasn't much strength in depth to that race and he'll need another chunk of improvement if he's to follow up.

Clearcut winner of maiden at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) in May and he caught the eye when eighth in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago, keeping on well after being short of room; remains unexposed and should stay 7f but this is a sterner assignment.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Prevailed at the Curragh in May to break his Group 2 duck; not disgraced in the 6f Group 1 at Royal Ascot since but that seventh-place finish confirms his slight limitations at the top level; will find better opportunities when back down in class.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: 3yo filly who is unbeaten (6-6) over sprint trips, mostly in Group races, including two at the top level; only narrowly justified favouritism in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently but it's hard to knock her record and there may yet be further advancement in terms of her rating; sire won the July Cup; receives all the allowances and duly warrants respect.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Japanese horse who is a two-time Grade 1 scorer on home soil and has finished a creditable second in the last two runnings of the 6f Group 1 at Royal Ascot, beaten only a nose by Almeraq the latest time; could go one better at Newmarket, as was the case with compatriot Agnes World who was runner-up at Royal Ascot prior to winning this contest in 2000.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Very useful 3yo but finished only eighth, albeit best of the near-side runners, in the Commonwealth Cup for 3yos at Royal Ascot when bidding to follow up his trial success over the same C&D; bare form of the latest effort gives him work to do with Venetian Sun and Division; furthermore, it took his Group 1 record to 0-3.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Solid performer who completed a hat-trick during his 2yo campaign and has strong placed form this season, the last two times behind Venetian Sun; switched and finished well for a close third in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot latest; has broadly progressive RPRs in tandem with a gradual rise in class; knocking on the door at Group level.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Joint-favourite with Almeraq in Salisbury Listed race last time but underperformed; bottom of this pack on ratings and accordingly faces a much stiffer assignment than when winning a handicap at this meeting last year; blinkers added.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Progressive 3yo gelding who brings impressive stats, being 3-3 (all over 5f against his elders) this term and 3-3 over 6f; finished strongly to get up in the final strides in the 5f Group 1 at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently; all bar one of his trainer's five July Cup winners have been 3yos; big player back up in distance.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Smart handicapper who brings excellent stats, being 3-3 at Newmarket (on the other course, admittedly, but it bodes well) and 3-3 (much improved) this term for new yard; prevailed only narrowly in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently but seems on his way to becoming a Group performer; adds great interest.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Progressive colt who got up on the line in a very tight finish to the 6f Group 1 at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently, taking record in completed starts to 4-6 and confirming that a heavy fall last September has not left a long-lasting mark; an emerging force in the sprinting division and he's from the family of a July Cup winner (Dream Ahead); major contender.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Respectable eighth in the 5f Group 1 at Royal Ascot with reappearance under his belt; better over 6f nowadays and posted one of his peak efforts in this race (good to firm) last year, finishing a neck second; later landed the Sprint Cup at Haydock in sole start under William Buick; interesting with that rider back on board.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Multiple winner, most recently when sent over to Qatar in February, but his form has regressed since and this is a difficult task even if a revival materialises; gained his C&D wins at handicap/Listed level; yet to score above Group 3.

Low-mileage 3yo; failed to get home over 1m at Carlisle last time when bidding for a hat-trick; gained her wins over 6f/7f (AW/turf) and remains open to further progress back down in distance; still of interest.

Arrives in good form having won at Goodwood (7f, good) then made the frame in competitive field at Epsom (7f, good to soft); however, he remains on a career-high mark and has to concede weight all round.
Gained last three wins on Newcastle AW; ran respectably back there on latest start; has bits of encouraging turf form this term but it's over two years since his last success in this sphere.
Ex-French gelding who has raced mainly at about 1m; ran with some promise at Newmarket on British/seasonal debut in June and may build on that effort, provided he copes with the return to 7f.

Has performed well in two runs at the July festival, notably a win (off just 1lb lower) in this race last year; narrowly justified favouritism at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) latest start, setting up him well for a return to this track; respected.

Belied his 80-1 odds with close third at York last time (7f, good; second start for new yard) but it remains to be seen whether he can back up that effort; has proved quirky and developed inconsistency.
Comfortably held over 1m at Royal Ascot last time; 2-2 in 7f handicaps, both Class 4 events from the front, including over C&D; may have more to offer back at this trip and back in calmer waters.
Record of 2-4, all over 6f, for previous yard; may still do better but has something to prove kept to 7f, having shown a dip in his form when upped to this trip at Doncaster for new stable last time.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Thrice-raced gelding who showed his strongest form on debut at Doncaster (7f) when beaten only half a length by a colt who currently has a mark of 102; open to progress in handicaps and looks interesting off an opening mark of 77, receiving weight all round.
Has shown major promise (won then good third) in two starts over 7f on AW, latest in January; had wind surgery since; interesting contender, being such an unexposed sort.
Successful over C&D on 2yo debut; 0-13 since but ran encouragingly at Windsor (6f) most recently, after a spell at Meydan; returns to this venue with a fighting chance off current mark.

Often front-runner; soundly beaten at the big Chester and York meetings in May but fairly solid otherwise this term and returned to winning ways in a five-runner race at Thirsk (1m4f, good to firm) ten days ago; back up 3lb but considered seriously in another small field.
Won under 7lb claimer in four-runner C&D race (good to firm) last July off 1lb higher; Yarmouth second one month ago and should be seriously involved.

Acts on good to firm; placed over 1m2f on first four starts this season, before comfortably justifying 4-6 favouritism in a 11.6f novice at Lingfield on latest outing; this unchanged, opening handicap mark seems to demand more but he may have more to offer at this sort of trip.

Sole win (12 races) came in a 1m2f handicap in April 2025; made a respectable debut for new yard this April but took a backward step next time; she's now 6lb below her peak mark and moves back up from 1m2f, having been below form once each over 1m3f and 1m4f last term; stamina in the family, though.

All four wins over 1m4f, the last three on Tapeta; not seen since a career best to win at Wolverhampton in January and he's 4lb higher here; twice runner-up on turf last year; may need to hit a new turf high but he requires a second look given this small field.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap (Whips to be carried but not used) (Racing Excellence)
Spotlight: Sole win came over a stiff 6f and she'll be happier back up in trip having lacked early toe at Windsor last time; yard won this last year, she's down to a career-low mark and sports first-time headgear under 5lb claimer Charlie Tucker; reasons for optimism.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap (Whips to be carried but not used) (Racing Excellence)
Spotlight: 2-2 over C&D (both in 2023) and tends to come to hand around this time of year; back on a fair mark and offered more last time, so there are positives for a yard that took this three years ago.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap (Whips to be carried but not used) (Racing Excellence)
Spotlight: Can miss the break and is usually ridden from off the pace; won a Brighton handicap (5.3f) by a wide margin on Tuesday for Jude Fernandes; that made it three wins from his last four starts and he is a leading player under his penalty.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap (Whips to be carried but not used) (Racing Excellence)
Spotlight: Plenty of near-misses before finally off the mark over 5f at Bath four weeks ago; the cheekpieces have had a positive effect and the extra furlong looks fine; upped 5lb; needs considering.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap (Whips to be carried but not used) (Racing Excellence)
Spotlight: Rare Flat runner for his jumps-orientated yard; his win for Stan Moore came over 1m (Polytrack) and he went 1m2f once, so he has a bit to overcome running after such a long absence and in a sprint for the first time.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well supported and finished the race strongly when winning here a month ago (6f, soft); different ground and he carries a penalty but the extra furlong seems sure to suit and he has potential.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 150,000gns breeze-up 2yo; among the favourites on debut last month at Pontefract (6f, good) but looked to need the experience, lugging left before sticking on (race has not worked out); will have learned from that and should appreciate the extra furlong.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Debut third might have worked out better but he improved on that last time, upped to a stiff 7f, when coming away with a long odds-on winner at Newmarket; sets the standard on that, especially in receipt of 4lb from Undiscovered.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 325,000gns yearling whose yard got on the board with 2yos for the season on Thursday (poor recent record with them here); no more than a fair debut at Yarmouth in May (7f, good to firm) and needs to improve on that.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 30,000gns yearling who's a half-brother to three useful winners in Ireland (including two for Johnny Murtagh who improved as 3yos); no surprise were he to want more time for a yard struggling for winners of late.

RaceName: Simon & Nerys Dutfield Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Already gelded late-April foal whose yard hasn't hit its usual high summer form as yet and is 0-9 with 2yos this season (3-42 with them here down the years); the market will be the best guide.

Debut fifth in a big field at Newbury (7f, good) in May has been well advertised by the principals since; easy to back that day and is open to improvement, having since been withdrawn on account of soft ground; shortlisted.

Blinkers on for her Newmarket debut (7f, good to firm) when coming from last to first in a small field, despite over-racing early; it is hard to know the merits of that as yet but she's entitled to improve for a yard with an unsurprisingly good record here.

OwnerName: D B Clark & A R Bentall
Spotlight: Trainer, who also saddles March Of Time, won this with a newcomer last season; this 8,000gns foal, who's a half-sister to winners over various distances, will have her anticipated chances reflected in the market.
Well-related filly who fared best of the newcomers, behind a long odds-on favourite, on her Windsor debut early last month; tonight's extra furlong will suit both on that evidence and on pedigree.
Beaten a long way on her soft-ground debut five weeks ago; likely she's one for handicaps later on, probably over a bit further.

420,000gns yearling who faced a useful winner when well held at odds-on on Tapeta in the spring; dam won over this trip and has produced a 1m2f winner, so the longer trip ought to help now she's handicapping; also wears a first-time tongue-tie; still has some potential.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Pulled hard when beaten at odds-on on her 7f comeback; it's not hard to pick holes in her Nottingham novice win, upped to this trip 16 days ago, but she did it in decent style and is unexposed entering handicap company; still holds an entry in next weekend's Irish Oaks.

Front-runner who's well suited by a stiff 1m2f, winning twice last summer and going close over C&D in the autumn off tonight's mark; soon gave way once headed on her recent AW comeback from eight months off and needs to improve a lot on that.

Second off this mark to a useful prospect last time and that was better, having run Flat at Chester and then over-raced and not seen out 1m4f at York; had plenty of racing this last year and this, however, and remains vulnerable to improvers.

Windsor fourth has been well advertised since (first three all successful next time) and she did her bit when winning a 1m2f Lingfield handicap last month; that continued the pattern of steady progress and she may well be up to defying a 5lb rise.

Comfortably on top in 0-55 handicap at Bath (1m2f, good) last time, opening her account at the fifth attempt; may build on that win and show further progress; receives weight all round upped in grade.

Absent since a comfortable novice win at Lingfield (kept to 1m on AW) in December; open to further progress now handicapping and upped in trip; interesting on reappearance, especially if strong in the betting.
Has a solid record in handicaps, completing an AW double then making the frame twice on turf; however, has shown no further improvement for the switch to this sphere.

Thrice-raced filly who finished only a modest fourth on soft going most recently; has a useful pedigree, represents major yard and may well improve returned to this faster ground on handicap debut; respected.

OwnerName: The 19th Hole Syndicate & J S Moore
Spotlight: Consistent record on AW features two wins; has failed to transfer that form back to turf in last two starts, taking record in this sphere to 0-7; something to prove.

Expensive to follow in her three starts as a 2yo but she returned as the form choice in an eight-runner fillies' novice at Ripon (6f, good) in May and won by 7l at 4-5 in first-time cheekpieces, going on over 1f out; that was an improved effort and she goes handicapping off a realistic mark.

Close call on debut (5f) last May was easily best effort until he won a seven-runner handicap at Nottingham (6f) last Saturday, coming from last to challenge over 1f out; they were his only two races on good to firm; tongue tied last two starts; back up 3lb but has a shout in this small field.

Won a 5f maiden at Catterick last August but he's 0-6 in handicaps this year and has generally underperformed; second in first-time headgear off this reduced mark at Kempton (6f, AW) on latest outing but markedly better is needed, even in this small field.

£140,000 breeze-up buy who justified favouritism on debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) in May; failed to build on that when fifth at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 11 days later but that was a warm conditions race and there can be optimism that he will appreciate the step back up to 6f; he's one to consider.

Down the field at 66-1 in the Brocklesby at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) before winning at Beverley (5f, good to soft) in May; has since left Stephen Hanlon; he was denied a clear run at Beverley and shaped as though he could be suited by the step up to 6f; not discounted back from a break.

Second/third on all three starts (5f/6f, good/AW), hanging right on the home turn when beaten at 1-2 at Wolverhampton last time; he's travelled from Newmarket and it's possible he has more to offer, but he's not obviously well treated off his opening mark.

Off the mark at the sixth attempt in Musselburgh seller (5f, good) in June and added a novice win at Redcar (6f, good) two starts later; runner-up in a novice over today's C&D (good) a fortnight ago and this tough gelding could give another good account on his nursery debut.

Having been gelded he showed improved form to win easily at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago on his third start; it remains to be seen where his limitations now lie; firmly in calculations.

£105,000 yearling who overcame his evident inexperience to win at 5-1 on debut at Pontefract (6f, good) last month; well beaten at 33-1 in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm) since but remains one to be interested in given his debut promise; could be on a good mark.

Left his first two runs behind when upped in trip and third at 125-1 over C&D (good) a fortnight ago; he's 4lb better off with the runner-up Furturra (stablemate) and this unexposed contender is not ruled out.

Disappointing when odds-on at Carlisle last time (7f, good to firm; failed to settle); promise previously, however, finishing third at Doncaster (5f, good to firm) on debut then fifth in the Woodcote at Epsom (6f, good to soft); not written off back down in trip.

Well beaten at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm) last month but he was in good heart previously, finishing fourth at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) two starts ago where the trip appeared to stretch him; possible player.

Won three times last year (including on good to firm ground) and he returned to form with 2l fourth of 11 at Newcastle (1m, AW) recently; could build on that latest performance and he might not be far away.

He's contested quality handicaps at Newbury and Ascot on his three starts this term, performing respectably and beaten around 4l each time; this 7yo probably needs something extra to snap a long losing run but he's edging down the weights and has run some big races here; worth a second look.

Following an encouraging reappearance fifth at Haydock in April he was beaten a long way on his final two starts for Ed Bethell; however, he's well treated on last season's form and perhaps he'll have been revived by a change of scenery; market check advised on stable debut.

Respectable seventh in the Dante here in May 2025 and he's one to watch in the betting back down in trip starting out for another new yard (remains in same ownership); however, he's very much struggled since the Dante and arrives with plenty to prove.

Not seen to best effect when mid-division in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm) last time out but prior to that he kept on well to make a winning reappearance at Haydock (7f, good to firm) and this very lightly raced 4yo retains potential, especially back up to 1m.
Went close on stable debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last November and he's 3lb lower here; however, his form has gone the wrong way since, particularly of late on his first two turf starts.

Two wins at Goodwood last autumn and admirably consistent in defeat this season, going close in a big field over C&D (good) then finishing fifth in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm; second of 20 in group); there is every chance that he will be bang there.

3yo who has been soundly beaten in handicaps this year on his first two runs for his new yard (7.5f then 5f; Royal Ascot latest); however, he was 2-4 in his 2yo campaign and a couple of rallying performances over 6f hinted that he may be suited by this sort of trip; may not be a forlorn hope.

Inconsistent sort who made it 1-20 on turf (that grass win came here in 2yo campaign) when well beaten at Royal Ascot last month; however, two starts ago he was a close sixth in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) when he was denied a clear run, and he's not ruled out.

Won four times in 2024; lightly raced last year and reappeared with close third off 4lb higher at Redcar (1m, good to firm) this April; however, three lesser runs have followed and he needs to turn things around.

Best form has come on AW and he hung left when 3l last of six at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) in May last time; however, the trip appeared to stretch him and he's off the same mark as for his win at Wolverhampton (8.4f, AW) in March; not written off back at 1m in first-time cheekpieces.

Dead-heated for first in 1m Group 3 on dirt at Jebel Ali in February; never going well when well beaten in dirt Group 2 at Meydan in March and gelded since; market check advised back from a break but he needs to be at the very top of his game to defy a lofty mark on his first turf start.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Built on an eye-catching reappearance (over this C&D) when justifying strong support in handicap at Windsor (5f, good) in May; only fourth to Washington Heights in Listed event at Carlisle next time but has had a break since and may well bounce back; has real possibilities if he does.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Third to Dickensian over C&D in May, stern assignments in Royal Ascot Group 1s since; sole win came in Yarmouth nursery and he's still in deep waters despite this apparent drop back in grade; cheekpieces replace visor.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: MPS Racing Ltd & The Ayrshire Tradesmen
Spotlight: Six wins to his name include 5f Group 2 at Goodwood last summer; not quite at his best this season, although a midfield run in Group 1 at Royal Ascot last time was a step in the right direction; third here 12 months ago and should be involved in the shake-up again.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won this race in 2024 and finished that campaign with a superb success in the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint (firm); lightly raced since (had a spell at stud) and well below par this season; needs first-time visor to spark a revival.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Likeable mare with a good strike-rate; ran at least as well as could have been expected when midfield in Group 1 at Royal Ascot (125-1) last time, but she was only fifth to Washington Heights in Listed event the time before; may again be up against it.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Didn't give his running in bid for back-to-back victories in Group 1 at Royal Ascot (last of 26) last month, but he'd previously shaped well when second in the Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock; this C&D winner (good to firm) takes a drop in grade and will be a danger to all if on a going day.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Clearly best effort when winning C&D Listed event (good ground) in May, coming from well off strong pace; well beaten in the big 5f 3yo handicap at Royal Ascot three weeks ago; needs another personal best, and by some way.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Made most to win this race (good to firm) 12 months ago and bounced back to form to beat seven rivals in Listed race at Carlisle six weeks ago; penalised this time but should give it another good go from the front.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 3-5 since joining Katie Scott, digging deep to win 13-runner handicap over C&D (good ground) two weeks ago; likely to keep progressing but she's up in grade here.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Often slowly away and comes from the rear; posted a personal best when eighth in big field for Group 1 at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm; 80-1) last month; second in this race 12 months ago; another with solid claims.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Three wins last year included a C&D Listed race and the Group 2 Flying Childers at Doncaster; well held both outings this term and yet to prove she has trained on.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Began her career in handicaps with a BHA mark of 60 and has improved in leaps and bounds since; seemed to excel herself when never-nearer sixth of 26 in Group 1 at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm; 40-1) last month; had run creditably over C&D the time before; big chance if repeating Ascot form.

RaceName: John Smith's City Walls Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Capped a productive 2yo campaign with a close second to Revival Power in Listed event over C&D (good to firm), but he was well beaten on his reappearance and he's a long way down the pecking order on ratings.

2-2 in last season's first campaign (1m, AW) and he built upon his comeback run with a close second in a first-time hood (retained) at Sandown (1m, good) last month; his finishing effort last time suggests this step up in trip could prompt further improvement; due a 3lb rise and he's one to consider.

5yo who has raced only ten times; looked very promising in the first part of the 2024 season and things clicked again with a 2l win at Newbury (1m2f, good) two months ago; possible player after a 5lb rise.

Ex-French 4yo who won easily at Hamilton (1m1f, good) in May on his second stable start and bounced back from heavy defeat to Danger Bay at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) when third at Ayr (1m, good) last Sunday; he may still have more to offer but others are more compelling in this hot race.

Has been headstrong in the past and he returned to form in a first-time hood (retained) with a close second of 16 over C&D (good) four weeks ago; today's company is tougher but he seems to like it here and remains well treated on last season's best efforts; due a 4lb rise; each-way chance.

Looked one to follow prior to disappointing when favourite over C&D last September, and he confirmed the earlier impression with a stylish Zetland Gold Cup win at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) in May on return; raised 8lb but this unexposed and well-regarded 4yo may be able to take it in his stride.

Two-time 7f winner who returned to form on his second start for this yard with a close third at Newmarket (1m, good) three weeks ago, when he raced alone on the near-side rail; however, he's up in grade today and untested at the trip, and he's not bred for this distance.

Dual winner here (both on good to firm) who was sixth in this last year and was runner-up to Warrant Holder over C&D (good) this May; soundly beaten at Royal Ascot since but he's an each-way possible back at York.

Back to form with close third of six at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) in May; however, only seventh of 16 at Epsom (1m2f, good to soft) last time on ground he should have handled; can be slowly away; others preferred.

Lightly raced 4yo who made it two wins for the year when scoring easily at Chester (10.3f, good) in May then finished second of 16 at Epsom (1m2f, good to soft) on Oaks day, albeit no match for the highly progressive winner; yard has won three of the last seven runnings and he could be a contender.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Reappeared over C&D (good) in May in a first-time tongue-tie (retained since) having been gelded, and he won that big-field handicap from Thunder Run and Altareq to make it 3-6; fine effort in clear second in the Duke Of Edinburgh at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm), where outstayed, and he's due to be 6lb higher in future handicaps; leading claims back down in trip.

Did well to finish fifth of 16 over C&D (good) on reappearance four weeks ago having been hampered soon after the start and raced wide; however, he goes well fresh so may not improve for that outing, and it's likely this 9yo will be vulnerable against numerous unexposed contenders.
Progressive last autumn and rediscovered that thread to win at Redcar (1m, good) in May; hasn't been running badly over about 1m2f subsequently but needs something extra if he's to take this.

Progressive 3yo for Andrew Balding in the first half of last year, culminating in a win in the Golden Gates Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); changed hands for 775,000gns the following month; failed to settle and shaped as though he needed the run when a nevertheless-respectable sixth on last month's comeback and stable debut at Epsom (1m2f, good to soft); the first-time hood could help and he's an intriguing contender.

Won at Pontefract (1m2f, good) in April and respectable fifth of 15 to Warrant Holder over this C&D (good) in May; the return to Epsom maybe didn't suit latest (well beaten) but he needs to bounce back with a career best.

Returned to form to win over C&D (good) in May and close second of three at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm) subsequently; he's the sole 3yo in the field and further improvement is possible, but necessary from out of the handicap in this much hotter contest.

Won at Meydan (1m4f, good) in March and bounced back from a heavy defeat here in May to win with plenty in hand at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last month; it was a slowly run race last time and he benefited from a good ride, but given his dominance he's entitled to respect under a 5lb penalty.

Two wins in light campaign last season (1m2f/1m4f, good to firm/good) and he easily made all on his reappearance at Goodwood (1m2f, good) in May; has a 12lb rise to contend with in this hotter race but it remains to be seen where the ceiling of his ability lies; top yard has won this race three times.

Well beaten in Bahrain in February when last seen and a wide draw could prove tough for this front-runner; however, he won two C&D handicaps last summer (good/good to firm) and was back on the scoresheet in Bahrain in January; unbeaten at York and could make a bold bid at a big price.

Lightly raced 4yo who was an eye-catching third from the rear behind Warrant Holder over C&D (good) in May on his stable/handicap debut, following a year off, and four runs later he got off the mark at Ayr (1m2f, good) last Sunday when making most of the running; back up in grade under a 5lb penalty but he may well have more left in the tank.

Some good C&D form, beaten just a neck in a big field last August (good to firm) and fourth of 16 two starts ago (good); he has an each-way squeak if he's on song but that wasn't the case at Newcastle last time (slowly away) and he's won just one of his last 22 starts.

Easy win at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) in May before solid third of 16 over this C&D (good), and he improved again to win at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) last Saturday; today's assignment is tougher still but this thriving 5yo could be in the each-way mix under a 5lb penalty.

Two wins on soft going last season and he's been placed in big-field handicaps at Cork (10.4f, good to yielding) and the Curragh (1m2f, good) on his last two starts; each-way shout if fast ground isn't an issue.

Beaten a nose in a 3m1f hurdle race at Carlisle in April 2025 and the same margin over 1m6f at Goodwood (good; unraced on firmer) this May on his return to Flat turf; second again over Goodwood's 1m6f four weeks ago, this time on soft, and both runs there suggested that a return to 2m should be okay.

Won handicap debut for Ed Walker off 4lb higher last September (extended 1m3f, heavy); got closer to that level in on his last two runs for his new connections and seemed to stay 2m at Chester last time, but he was only fifth of seven in that race and others have more pressing claims.

Probably best known for Musselburgh exploits but last two wins were at Nottingham last October and Carlisle last month; below form on sole start here (last October) but probably best forgiven being well beaten 17 days ago as that was just 1m3f; chief concern is that he needs another career best.

Five-runner race at Carlisle (1m3f) last Saturday was first win since 2023 and she's a dependable sort who finished a C&D second (twice) and fourth in July 2024 and 2025 on her only three appearances at York; going back up 5lb since Carlisle seems to pose the difficulty but she should be on the premises.

Four months off before winning a six-runner race at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) early last month; disappointing in a maiden hurdle (fourth at 10-11) 12 days later but remember also that he raised his game markedly when upped to 1m6f on Flat last autumn; this first 2m Flat assignment is interesting.

4yo who's relatively lightly raced and has found his niche in 2m races this season, winning at Ripon (good; made all) in April and Catterick (good to firm) last month; didn't show it in the Northumberland Vase at Newcastle two weeks ago but that was on AW and after just a five-day break; 3lb lower today and still has more to offer with stamina tests.

Sole run on good to firm was last July when tailed off in a novice race; staying-on third here (1m4f) this June and he knuckled down well to score over 2m2f at Pontefract (also on good) eight days later; that win was the first time he'd worn this headgear combination and his first go at a staying trip on the Flat; up 4lb but probably has more to offer and he's a big player if he goes on the ground.

Won this race last year (good to firm) in good style and has a 1lb lower mark today; 2026 build-up has been far less auspicious than last season's, however, and the first-time visor of latest start is now replaced with a first-time tongue-tie.

Three wins last summer included two over C&D; started this season in good form but well beaten on last two outings when back to York for a Group 3 and, more worryingly, a 1m6f handicap; off 2lb higher than her last winning mark, she'll have a shout if returning to her best.
5yo who is an improved performer this season and registered career-best form when a close third in C&D Listed race last time, a neck behind Tabletalk; should be bang there once again.

Won the Melrose Handicap over C&D in August 2024; 0-9 since but he was runner-up in five of those races, including when beaten a neck in C&D Listed event four weeks ago, narrowly in front of Mount Atlas; the lack of a recent win is a touch frustrating but he's clearly a leading contender.

Progressed very well last term, culminating in his close third in Group 2 Great Voltigeur here (1m4f, good to firm) in August, until not so good trying 1m6f on final outing; rallied when close second in 1m4f French Listed event on reappearance but needs to bounce back from a tame show in Newbury Group 3; tongue tied first time on this second attempt at 1m6f.

Won at Hexham last August in the first of her three bumpers but a Grade 2 at Aintree (125-1) proved far too tough in April; will build at some point on the modest form shown in a 9.4f maiden on her recent first venture under Flat rules, but she's impossible to fancy today.

7yo who is 0-12 since winning at Meydan in January 2025; has run really well in plenty of Group races in the interim, including the last two runnings of the Yorkshire Cup over C&D, but he ran a stinker in C&D Listed event four weeks ago; bang there if he bounces straight back.

OwnerName: A Cope, B Roberts And J Biggane
Spotlight: Eight AW wins, two last winter in 2m handicaps; however, he failed to beat a rival in Group 3 at Sandown (2m, good) on turf return, has tons to prove on turf record (0-5) and even best AW form does not look good enough.
7f winner at Redcar last November; two solid efforts (6f/7f, good ground) last month but he will need more if he is to defy this mark.

Looked as good as ever when second of nine at Catterick (6f, good) on his reappearance in April but that hasn't been a springboard to better things; conditions no problem and he's on a manageable mark but this is a warm race in which to try to bounce back.
Ended 2025 in good form on AW; some solid efforts back on turf this year without suggesting he had much in hand of his mark; minor money perhaps his best hope.
Ran his best race for new connections when third of 21 in a 0-85 over C&D four weeks ago; mark left unchanged but he does need to prove himself on ground firmer than good.
Thrown in on last season's best; yet to get going for David O'Meara this time around but he has dropped 10lb for his troubles and the addition of a visor could help; stable also runs Yes I'm Mali.
The handicapper has been in command since his runaway win at Leicester (6f, good) in April; today's return to sprinting is in his favour but he's likely to be vulnerable at this level.

Rejuvenated with James Owen, reeling off an AW hat-trick in January and making it four on the bounce when scoring at Catterick (6f, good) in May; only just missed out at Doncaster last month and it was 5f when beaten favourite at Sandown last time; now 3lb higher but she did look promising early in her career and Mason Paetel's claim helps too.
No problem with fast turf but he has a much better strike-rate on AW; midfield finish at Doncaster last month didn't suggest he is the answer here.

Hold-up sprinter who ended a near two-year losing run at Pontefract (6f, good) last month; better form when second there three weeks ago; has plenty of C&D form in big fields and he has each-way claims.

Not the force of old but that is reflected in his handicap mark; has undergone wind surgery since his latest run but it isn't enough to earn him the vote in this competitive race; usual headgear is absent today.
Both wins have come on good to soft ground but he does have one good run on good to firm to his name; disappointed at Windsor last month but this is an ease in grade.
He has been threatening to add to his six wins, with a third at Pontefract and second at Thirsk on his last two starts; on the downside he has been unplaced in all seven visits to York.

String of good runs since returning in May from a 167-day absence, latterly keeping on for second at Redcar (5f, good) three weeks ago; steps back up to 6f for the first time this year and it could suit.
Won two 6f events (good/good to soft) for Michael Dods as a 2yo; drew a blank in 2025; makes stable debut in a competitive race after 259 days off; likely best watched.
Arrives on the crest of a wave having won four of her last five starts; a 4lb rise for her small-field Class 5 win at Ripon last month could just find her out here, though.
Good run of form ground to a halt at Thirsk ten days ago when he wasn't on his best behaviour in the stalls; has the ability to feature off this mark but is not without risk.

OwnerName: S Thompson, Mrs R Carr & G Shields
Spotlight: Picking up his share of prize money this season, making the frame five times either side of his Pontefract (6f, good) win last month; despite that he is still 5lb lower than when a close fourth in this race 12 months ago; each-way shout.
Won this race in 2022 as a 5yo; no sign of his enthusiasm waning this year, winning three 6f handicaps, and stepping back up in  trip will suit after two good 5f efforts last month; chance.

OwnerName: Alfa Site Services & Alan Gove Racing
Spotlight: Made a winning handicap debut (6f, AW) in March and a perfect start to her turf career when making all at Pontefract (6f, good) in June; Doncaster third on latest outing was another good run and this track should prove more to her liking; still capable of better.

OwnerName: R A Holburt, B R Holburt Et Al
Spotlight: Strong win from just off the leaders this course at this journey. Unbeaten at track and distance. Can challenge again.
Resuming (32-weeks). Has a good first up record. Recent Cranbourne jump-out winner. Right in the mix fresh.

OwnerName: D L Hewitt & Ms J C Preston
Spotlight: Looked likely but had a real fight on his hands and just missed at Morphettville Parks. Tougher here but draws to do no work. Each way hope.

OwnerName: D J Oliphant, P J Salter Et Al
Spotlight: First-up (35-weeks). In the minors at Moonee Valley first-up last campaign while building fitness through 2 trials and a jump-out win. Should mean business first-up.

OwnerName: A J Hehir, D W Rasheed Et Al
Spotlight: Let-up (63-days). Kept finding the line without threatening in the Goodwood on a soft deck at Morphettville. At optimum distance. Looks a key contender.

OwnerName: N S Psaltis, Mrs G C Psaltis Et Al
Spotlight: Just missed in a crackerjack finish in the Open Hcp at Flemington and over this trip when drifting in the betting. Previous winner in wet here. Capable of making an impact.

OwnerName: G N Peters, J Baker Et Al
Spotlight: Ears scrubbed off early to cross and lead but kept on bravely in rain affected going for the minors at this trip. Can play a role.

TrainerName: Mick Price & Michael Kent Jnr right
OwnerName: Werrett Bloodstock Pty Ltd, S Tsalikidis Et Al
Spotlight: Placed Bel Esprit Stakes at Caulfield 30 May. Battled home okay at Randwick. Both efforts here stack up. Worth a look.

OwnerName: N Morgan, J F Naffine & Bula Bula
Spotlight: Resuming (23-weeks). Nabbed on the wire in Benchmark 100 company at Caulfield first-up last campaign while cruising through a winning trial at Murray Bridge Gh. One for multiples fresh in this company.
Let-up (42-days). Had all before him at turn and went home tamely this track at this distance. Others more persuasive.

OwnerName: Best Bloodstock Syndicate, Broady Cats Syndicate Et Al
Spotlight: Given time to freshen up after 1st-up run. Made running, no answer when challenged but held on for second in the (Bm84) at Sandown-Hillside. Strips fitter second run back. Place claims.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
Spotlight: Career wins-runs record of 7-20 and he was in the money in a stakes last August; close up second at Churchill Downs when dropped to 1m 1/2f 51 days ago in an allowance optional claimer; leading contender; absence is no concern as has previously gone well off a break and he can take this step up in class in his stride.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
Spotlight: Steadily progressive sort who has taken well to Pattern company in best effort when second to prolific scorer Rebel's Romance in the Group 2 City Of Gold (1m4f) at Meydan in February having previously won the Group 3 Dubail Millennium (1m2f); not disgraced when sixth to Ombudsmen in Group 1 Dubai Turf (1m2f); handlwes quick ground and a major player here.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
Spotlight: Not beaten far in an allowance Grade 3 at Churchill Downs six weeks ago; has been consistent of late and has made an impressive start to his career with three wins from six starts; up in class but ought to be on the premises.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
OwnerName: Stonelea Stable LLC & Bonnie Rye Stable
Spotlight: Admirable career strike-rate (four from 19 to date); recent efforts have generally been solid; close up behind Soleil Volant when fourth 28 days ago beaten just over 4l at Delaware Park in an allowance listed; faces a tougher assignment this time so he can be taken on.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
Spotlight: Finished fourth, beaten a fair way at Belmont At The Big A upped to 1m1 1/2f in May in an allowance optional claimer; useful at this level; possesses winning form at this track; tackling an extra 1 1/2f now.

RaceName: Bowling Green Stakes presented by Emerald Evocations (Grade 2) (Turf)
OwnerName: Jacques Dupuis Jr, Luke Bourque & Bobby Sutton
Spotlight: Successful twice in his last five starts; displayed a fair level of form when 3 1/2l runner-up in an allowance listed at Delaware Park four weeks ago; more on his plate but not dismissed.

OwnerName: Michael Scaife/Liam Ferguson/Simon Murphy/H S Khunkhuna
Spotlight: Won four for Clive Cox, including the Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock in 2024, his last victory; yet to hit those heights for this yard and has been soundly beaten on his last three starts; 0-2 on the AW but did run well here behind Valiant Force in February; blinkers replace cheekpieces worn last time.

Speedy filly has an excellent strike rate over C&D (4-6) including this race last year off 2lb lower; went close behind Howd'yadoit at Navan in May but has failed to fire in three runs since; return to this track offers hope of a revival and cheekpieces are added; bold bid likely from plum draw.

OwnerName: Exors of the Late Mrs S Power
Spotlight: Six-time course winner, including twice over C&D, but his last four wins here have come over 6f; however, he did go close off this mark over C&D in May and should get a strong pace to aim at; not out of this.

Won over C&D in October off 13lb lower; poor on first two starts this season but roared back to form to make all at Bellewstown 10 days ago (5f, good); career-high mark now but this 3yo could have more to offer and top rider booked; player.

Won his maiden over C&D last December and overall form figures here read 2313; not as consistent on turf this season; ran well at Cork in June but down the field on latest at the Curragh; another one that could potentially improve now returned to the AW, but he's 4lb wrong here.

Back on song when just failing to reel in the winner at Navan on latest; four C&D wins to his name, including a Group 3, and is 5lb better off for a 1.75l defeat behind Valiant Force in a rated race here in February; third in this last year and should go well again.

OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Struggling on turf this season but won his last start over C&D in February and, overall, he has won five times at this venue over a variety of trips; second behind Eclairage in this last season; a return to form would come as no surprise but David Egan prefers Ipanema Queen.

3yo landed the third win of his career when beating Eclairage by a head at Navan in May (5f, yielding); has been beaten in conditions races twice since and is 7lb higher on return to handicap company; sole previous AW run wasn't his best, but his yard is red-hot so can't discount.

OwnerName: Gary Devlin & Kevin Osborne & N W T Dalzell & Tracey Wylie
Spotlight: C&D winner; finished off last year in fine form at this venue, backing up her C&D handicap win with a short-head second in a conditions race over C&D when last seen in December; is 4lb wrong here, however, and lacks a recent run so is probably best watched unless the market speaks.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
OwnerName: David Daly & Gerard Shevlin & D Battersby
Spotlight: Twelve-race maiden ran one of her better races when runner-up over 6f here in April off 56; soundly beaten on turf in four runs since, but now 4lb lower than she was for that April run and not dismissed back at this venue.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden was a close third in a fillies' maiden over C&D in December on final start for Sheila Lavery; mixed bag on turf in three starts for this stable; ran well at Gowran on penultimate outing but never figured in visor (retained) at Fairyhouse on latest.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: 0-7 overall and 0-4 on AW; ran okay when a 2.75l third over 1m here in December but two runs this season have not been her best; tongue-tie now added to usual hood; more needed and is 5lb wrong.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: 6f Windsor novice winner for former yard; three turf runs for this yard have all been at that trip and yet to get closer than 4l to the winner; mark sliding but unproven on this surface, and others make more appeal.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Won on handicap debut here over 6f off 1lb higher, but that is starting to look like a flash in the pan; poor form otherwise and soundly beaten all three starts this season; others appeal more.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Won fillies' maiden over C&D in December; back to form with a 1l third of seven at Down Royal on latest (5f, soft); return to 7f and this surface are positives; player.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Pretty modest form in maidens and no sign of progress in first two handicaps; never figured on seasonal return at the Curragh and now makes AW debut; not easy to fancy.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Has held form well since sent handicapping; won off 6lb lower over 6f here in December; beaten 0.5l off this mark over 1m here in March; solid efforts over 7f and 8.5f at Fairyhouse the last twice; place claims at the very least.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
OwnerName: Gary Devlin & N W T Dalzell
Spotlight: Best effort came on debut over C&D in January; five starts since (four on turf) have not been at the same level and never involved when 33-1 on handicap debut at Gowran last month; blinkers tried that day are left off here.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner in February off 8lb lower; beaten less than 2l in a big field at the Curragh on latest (6f, good), staying on well, and eased 1lb for that effort; return to 7f on the AW could enable him to get his head back in front; leading claims.

RaceName: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap
Spotlight: Didn't achieve much in three turf maidens at 6f-7f on varying ground; could do better now tackling a handicap, and worth checking in the market.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Never worse than third in six starts, over this trip last twice; tongue-tie returns for AW debut and plenty of horses by Mehmas win on synthetic surfaces.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Placed four times from six starts on turf, including when nailed on the line at Bellewstown having tried to make all; reckon he'll be in the front rank again with cheekpieces now fitted, after another solid run at the Curragh; sire was classy turf horse in the US, yet to sire AW winner from limited runners; dam did win on AW.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Profitable gelding with an interesting pedigree; closely related to a Godolphin Group 1-winning 2yo and half-brother to Heavy Metal, a prolific winner on the dirt at Meydan; 16s, got tired late on when fifth over 1m at The Curragh, 5l off third-placed Karrygrant.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Mark of 78 after three C&D runs, but remains to be seen if he merits that rating because it's winter form; hung right the first day and missed the break in a hood last time, so he might have a few quirks, but right man on board to sort him out.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Well-bred son of Palace Pier; 18s for Curragh debut over extended 6f, trailed home in rear after a slow start.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Phoenix Of Spain filly cost E13,000 as a yearling and sports a tongue-tie for debut; related to three prolific and useful winners, two of them on AW.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Boiled over, bolted to post and unseated rider before Curragh debut, where he ran keen and dropped out to finish in rear (Karrygrant third); hood now on.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Didn't make it to the breeze-ups after costing 40,000gns as a yearling; half-brother to 7f Group 3 winner Breathtaking Look (also won on AW) and to two other winners; dam Listed-placed 1m-9.4f AW winner; not hard to see him running well.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Starman filly had three turf runs over 5f last year, modest enough form; dam was placed on AW in France; 10 months off and McAteer on stablemate.

RaceName: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
Spotlight: Homebred son of The Gurkha; half-brother to 8.6f/1m4f winner Space Kid (inc AW/Belgium); unraced dam out of Group-placed 1m1f winning half-sister to 1m1f/1m2f Listed winner Livadiya; trainer doesn't have debut winners.
Winner over 6f here and twice placed over this trip; been off 14 months and new stable (same owners)
Hold-up performer by necessity, really, as he can be tardy from the gates; C&D winner and just failed to get up here in April; only 1lb higher now and if they go hard, it will be a big help.
Defied a similarly-wide draw when winning over C&D in March; only 1lb higher now and little wrong with her turf form since.
Lightly raced and back from over a year off with creditable mid-field run over this trip at Leoprdstown, keeping on steadily from off the pace; first start on AW.
Well beaten in two turf handicaps over 6f; first run here and dam is related to AW winners; visor on and stamina to prove.

Went close from a wide draw over C&D last August; should come on from fair seasonal debut over 1m1f at Leopardstown where she was disputing the lead a furlong down; this is only her fifth start in handicaps.

OwnerName: Mrs P McCourt/Whyte's Stamullen Syndicate/S Sweeney
Spotlight: Won a division of this last year off a mark of 60, but has been out of form on turf this season and only mid-field when favourite over C&D in April on sole AW start in 2026.

OwnerName: Charles Kerwin & Brendan Kerwin & Liam Kehoe
Spotlight: C&D winner in the winter and has added two wins on turf; likes a bit of space, so draw is okay, but she might be high enough in the handicap now.

OwnerName: P E Ryan & J G Shanahan
Spotlight: Has winning and placed form over C&D, but has a habit of starting slowly which has been evident on turf lately; placed on last two visits here earlier this year.
Maiden was second over a longer trip on soft last year; slowly away before late headway behind Micasso at Bellewstown latest; unplaced in four runs here, albeit three of them were non-handicaps.

Second over 1m4f here in November, but that's her only time to place in 10 starts here and 1m likely too sharp; another headgear combo tried, but even the champion jockey will struggle to get this one involved
One good run last year and popped up at 22-1 on return at Bellewstown; burst here on a previous visit and making a quick return to action, so the 'bounce factor' sirens are sounding.
Maiden not beaten far a few times here earlier in the year, over trips between 6f-1m; likely to find a few too strong but minor place claims.
Four wins here, three of them over this trip, and may step up on recent turf efforts which were probably with a view to getting him fit for AW action.
Two wins here in the spring, including over this trip, and last couple of turf runs have been fine, 2m looking too far last time.
Back-to-back C&D wins under this rider in the spring and really good third in higher grade at the Curragh last time; lots to like.
Been racing prominently before weakening in her races over longer trips; cheekpieces added for first outing here and half-sister won on AW.
Twice placed over 10.5f here in November; off the mark over 1m1f at Ballinrobe and fair runs since; hasn't gone this far before but is by a St Leger winner.
Fair fifth over C&D in May on sole AW run; did nothing in a hurry at Leopardstown (1m1f) on Thursday, but stuck to his task and not beaten far; big horse has one in him, but maybe not quite yet.
AW winner at two in Britain, but has never raced here; won a claiming hurdle two runs back, but trip looks too sharp as well as the query about him on Polytrack.

Nice run here over 10.5f for previous yard; having been gelded, encouraging fourth (posted wide) over same trip at Down Royal on stable debut (strong form); half-sister won three handicaps here, two of them over this trip, and Elzaams have a great record here.
Forget his two recent turf runs as they were probably preps for this; useful record here with two wins over 10.5f and some good runs over this trip.
Sole win came at Sligo last summer; placed loads of times here, including over this trip in May, but burst only five days ago which makes him too risky.
Dual turf winner and thrice runner-up here, including in last year's renewal; form tailed off later last year, but better for his return to action.
Famous colours and he won 10.5f maiden here in February, but that's weak form and he was lapped on handicap debut at Down Royal; steps up in trip and bred for it.
Both starts have come here; soundly beaten on debut over 1m in April; didn't quite get home upped to 1m4f on latest when beaten 9l into third; new headgear goes on and he drops in trip; more needed.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Progressive without winning in three maidens on turf; best effort yet over 1m2f (yielding) on latest at Navan 57 days ago; has since been gelded and cheekpieces now go on for AW debut; rated 85 and the one to beat.

Sent off at 22-1 here on debut (1m) in December and found just one too good, beaten a neck into second; off since, which is slightly concerning, but pedigree suggests that this longer trip might suit and should run well again if ready after his break.

Almanzor gelding was a 15,000gns foal; half-brother to 7f/1m winner Beagle Bay (inc AW; RPR 101); dam Listed-placed 6f-1m winner (inc 2yo/AW; 103), half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Limetree Lady; a bit of appeal on paper and worth a market check.
Heavy defeats all four starts, including twice here over 7f; no improvement for step up in trip at Ballinrobe latest; hard to make a case for.
Modest form in bumpers and maiden hurdles; makes Flat and AW debut; best watched.

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Promise in all three maiden runs at 1m2f-1m5f; the latter trip on soft ground probably stretched her on latest at Down Royal; form of previous second at Roscommon (1m4f, good) looks solid in the context of this race; rated 74 and big chance if taking to this surface (half-sister won on AW).

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Standout effort a head second at Gowran on third start last October (9.5f, heavy); has failed to build on that and soundly beaten in handicaps on last three starts; rated 65 and a fair bit to find on AW debut.

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: All four turf runs have come on soft and heavy ground at 1m3f-1m4f; beaten favourite when second at Killarney in October and at the Curragh in November; well below best on seasonal return at Bellewstown in April and off since; claims on best form if handling the AW.

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Showed enough to suggest she could win a race when trained in Britain; below best when last seen at Pontefract in September; has joined yard that can ready one and has run well on the AW before, so monitor the market.

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Heavy defeats at huge odds in maidens at Down Royal and Bellewstown; seems safe to rule out.

RaceName: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Very modest form so far in turf maidens; beaten 29l on latest; can only be watched in first-time cheekpieces on AW debut.

RaceName: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Making headway when unseating at Downpatrick (2m3f) and then made no mistake at the expense of a subsequent winner at Clonmel (2m, good); sets the standard on RPRs and Rian Corcoran's claim takes away 5lb of his penalty.

RaceName: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 50-1 when scraping home in a modest 2m4f maiden at Hexham and she has more on her plate here, especially with a penalty.

RaceName: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Looks limited and was 125-1 when tailed off behind Dolly Dior at Hexham.

RaceName: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in good-ground bumpers in France and at Southwell (good; tongue tied); should make a hurdler but this is no easy starter.

RaceName: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Worcester winner who was found wanting under a penalty at Uttoxeter (2m, good), though that wasn't too bad a race and the second has won since; should also improve for this longer trip with his pointing background.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: All four wins have been at Hexham and it was never in much doubt there three weeks ago (1m7f, good); hard to grumble with the 8lb rise but now has to continue his good work on a very different track, and he was a lot lower in the weights when second to Garde Des Champs in this 12 months ago.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Better at this trip than the 2m4f over which he was third here ten days ago, but even when on a good day he's become extremely hard to win with (1-24 as a chaser and 2-39 overall); the clear plus is that he won this last year off 5lb higher.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Free-goer who often makes the running and ultimately paid for giving chase to an improving winner when behind Garde Des Champs here a month ago; ran better behind the same winner the time before when he finished ahead of the Russell/Scudamore runner; a soft lead would help matters.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won all sorts in France, following Flat wins on turf and AW with two wins over fences and four as a hurdler (the latest in May on good ground over 2m2f); might not be on too bad a mark for this British debut; has won from the front and when held up.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won two handicap hurdles for Stuart Crawford but he's not looking as good over fences and was behind Garde Des Champs here last time.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sole win came in a three-runner maiden hurdle; this mark should be manageable on the balance of his hurdle form but a forgettable chase debut in January needs forgiving; absent since.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won her maiden over C&D on good ground last May (four ran); hasn't looked on that good a mark since sent into handicaps and has been ridden by Jack Power in all bar one of those; cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: All good in three runs for Olly Murphy, and after winning over C&D (good), she wasn't far from defying a 5lb rise at Aintree; just 2lb higher this time and looks sure to put up another bold show.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Thp Racing & D A Harrison Racing
Spotlight: C&D winner who hasn't found her form in three starts following a break and there are stamina concerns to overcome at this trip.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Hasn't had that much racing for a 10yo; enjoys this ground and has a solid record over C&D, so one to consider as he ran quite well last time at Bangor in a higher grade (finished last but weakened only late on).

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Should be well handicapped but has been below par for a good while now and more new headgear is tried after flirting with a tongue-tie last time; capable but risky.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Former smart Flat horse who is 0-6 over hurdles and was beaten a little under 10l on handicap debut here a month ago; he was boxing on over 2m and this longer trip could bring him on (stayed well on the Flat).

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner who is finding her feet after a long absence and she's an assured stayer over this far; looks handicapped about right but has each-way claims.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Struggled with consistency towards the end of his time in Ireland, and failed to stay 3m6f on April's stable debut; more in his favour here, but others more persuasive.

RaceName: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Regressed in Ireland, including in two handicaps, after finishing runner-up in a maiden hurdle; could have needed the run when beaten 9l in a 2m novice at Kelso (good) in May but it's hard to make a compelling case.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Had long career in France before four British runs this season; won by 17l at Uttoxeter in May and has posted another two good efforts since, more recently when battling on for fourth in valuable contest back at Uttoxeter (also 3m, good) a fortnight ago; respected.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won three-runner contest at Kelso (2m7f, good) in May and is still on a workable mark but never really got competitive in last month's Perth Gold Cup and needs to put that run behind him.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Exploited much-reduced mark over C&D (good) in April and finished second over C&D on both subsequent appearances (good to soft/good) but is no longer the force of old and others in this field have more appealing profiles.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has modest 2-30 strike-rate under rules but kept on well for second at Aintree (2m4f, good) in May and has now filled that position twice since his wind operation in March; could plausibly still have untapped potential over 3m; no surprise if he features.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Miss D Sellars & Exors Of Mrs Ic Sellars
Spotlight: Gained both chase wins over 2m4f (one here); no match for progressive rival when second at Hexham (1m7f, good; first run after wind surgery) last month but that was still a good effort; a possible if suited by this new trip.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Gained all seven chase wins at the track, the latest a dead-heat over this trip in April (good ground); on fairly tough mark now but last month's Perth Gold Cup fourth was respectable and he probably won't be far away.

RaceName: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Abbadis Racing & D A Harrison Racing
Spotlight: Four-time C&D winner; returned from break with two low-key runs this spring (hurdle/chase) but may have been aided by refitted cheekpieces when running big race in defeat here (2m4f, good) ten days ago; up in grade today but still on a good mark and this return to 3m is sure to suit.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Thp Racing & D A Harrison Racing
Spotlight: Course regular who looked as good as ever when keeping on strongly from off the pace for clearcut C&D (good) win ten days ago; 6lb higher in a stronger race today but can make his presence felt again.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Six-time hurdle winner who was placed off today's mark on his last four appearances, most recently when second at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) last month; seems very likely to be on the premises again.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Disappointed at Huntingdon (a course he likes) in May, after a break, and didn't find much at business end when last of four finishers at Worcester (2m7f, good) last month; on a good mark but arrives here with questions to answer.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Made all in 2m4f maiden here (good) in May, after a break, and also ran well when second on handicap return at Cartmel (2m6f, good) a fortnight later; upped further in trip today and remains lightly raced for her age; could still have more to offer; highly respected.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 2-4 for new stable this year, with both wins gained from the front here (3m/3m2f); below form at Hexham last month but sure to be suited by the return to this track and could take some catching; cheekpieces refitted.

RaceName: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Two hurdles wins last season, the latter when upped to 2m7f at Bangor (good) in April; still unexposed over this sort of trip but was tailed off when dropped back to 2m4f last month; hard to predict.
