Spotlight: Seventh foal; Palace Pier half-brother to four winners including Great David (Listed-placed 1m 2yo/1m2f; RPR 105), Kinderfrau (1m5f/2m; 87) and Leadership (UAE 7f/1m; 84); dam Group-placed 1m-10.4f winner (107) out of 12.5f Group 2 winner; trainer's 2yos have 25% strike-rate (6-24) this term.

RaceName: Betfred "The Classic Bookmaker" EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Third foal; Kingman half-brother to winners San Juanito (8.6f/9.4f; RPR 89) and Proposal (7f; 77); dam 7f 2yo/1m2f Group 3 winner (116) out of 7f-1m4f winner; newcomer to note from strong yard.

RaceName: Betfred "The Classic Bookmaker" EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 48,000gns yearling by Kodi Bear; first foal; dam 5f winner (RPR 68) out of 6f 2yo Group 3 winning half-sister to 7f Group 1 winner Toylsome; others are a bit more striking on paper.

OwnerName: M H Dixon & J L Rowsell
Spotlight: 3yo who's had respectable efforts in her first four handicaps, before a lesser show from wide draw at Kempton latest; place chance if back to her best.
Three wins this year, the last two at Bath (1m/1m2f) in April and she's continued to look in good form, beaten a head at Salisbury (1m) on latest start; firmly in the mix if she adapts to this track.

15-race maiden who's in his third season; runner-up over 1m2f in one of his two visits here last summer and two minor honours (7.6f/1m) from three starts this term; cheekpieces (tried once as 3yo, well held) return but he does not look the percentage call for win purposes.

Marked improvement is needed but he's had just four races; fifth of ten on seasonal/handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good) four weeks ago failed to match his market position but he staged something of a rally, after hanging left over 2f out, and might build on that.

Front-runner; latest win was under Mason Paetel here (1m2f) early last July for Ed Dunlop; 4lb lower today but that's after he went off the boil and there's been only a partial revival for new yard this year, finishing sixth of nine here last time in the race he won last year; the last time he raced over a trip this short was May 2025.
14-race maiden; latest of his three seconds was in April 2025 and he's not made a serious impact since; off since January and hard to fancy.

OwnerName: J Machale, S Tucker & S Jewell
Spotlight: 5-21 on AW compared to 0-10 on turf and he's been well beaten in his two races here; turf mark is 12lb below AW figure and he should have come on since his recent, creditable reappearance, but others are more persuasive.
Eight-race maiden and his best show in five handicaps was on first occasion (1m, AW); 8lb lower today but lacks any pressing claims.

The only impact he made in three turf races (last April-July) came when third on good ground at Chester, which is up with his best AW form; pretty reliable with his minor AW honours this year, so needs considering.

OwnerName: Mrs F Cotton, Mr & Mrs P Conway
Spotlight: Best efforts from his five handicaps were on last two starts when third at Goodwood (1m1f, good to soft) and beaten a head at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm); back up 2lb but his first win should not be far away.

Reliable 3yo whose two wins (from 13 races) were in very small fields, latterly when making all at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; that was a runaway win and the first time he's made the running, but he's 5lb higher today in what looks a more competitive race.

Held up; ran creditably sole start here (2024); latest of his two wins came when dropped into Class 6 at Bath (1m2f, firm) in May, before a Class 4 at Yarmouth saw a lesser effort; should be competitive in this race.

Spent last year in France; fine record here, including two wins in summer 2024 and a third off this mark in a blanket finish two weeks ago; the latter followed a Windsor win (1m2f, win); looks set for another big run.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Did well on AW last winter and even better form when the cheekpieces replaced a visor at Goodwood (1m4f, good) four weeks ago, leading over 1f out to score with rather more authority than the half-length winning margin suggests; used to act on good to firm; up 3lb but firmly in the picture.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 1m2f Listed winner here in 2023 but well beaten on his only visit since; no win since a Group 3 in August 2023 but placed in AW/turf handicaps (1m-1m4f) this spring and continues down the weights; needs much better than he produced on last two outings.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Bumper and 1m4f AW handicap winner; only three runs on Flat turf, the latest when second of 13 at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) in May in first-time cheekpieces, which have been kept since; not disgraced when Georgia King was on again back on AW latest outing; needs a second look.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: All wins have been at 1m2f and he ran well over the extended 1m here on reappearance, before a lesser show at Sandown; his record at this track is very solid, but those on good to firm and at 1m4f less so.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Six-race maiden whose easily best display in three handicaps came when fifth of ten at Chester (1m2f) in June; the lesser shows on either side were over about 1m3f; blinkers (worn on last two starts) are removed; 7lb lower than on handicap/seasonal debut but something to prove.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Creditable third off 9lb higher over C&D on soft ground (acts on good to firm) last September in his only Epsom race; AW campaign in the winter for new yard did not go at all well until he perked up a bit in February on his last two outings; needs to build on that after his break but he's too well handicapped to be ignored.

RaceName: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 8yo who went 21 months without a win but has now scored at Windsor, Lingfield, Chepstow and Ripon in his four races this turf season; his second in this race last year was a remote one and the 6lb rise since his latest start asks a question, but conditions fine and he's on a major roll, ridden by Sarah Bowen on last two starts (two in four days); major player.

Can make the running and he went on before halfway when gamely winning a six-runnner handicap at Catterick (7f, good to soft) five weeks ago, getting off the mark at eighth attempt; back up 2lb and unraced on good to firm, with this track a new experience too, but that latest run gives him a shot.

Won at Newmarket (7f, good) in May, ran respectably at Goodwood next time and beaten a neck at Newmarket four weeks ago; finished last in April (reappearance) in his only race on good to firm but otherwise needs plenty of respect.

Made all last term in a maiden at Brighton (good to firm) and a handicap over C&D (good to soft), the latter in September on final run for Andrew Balding; back over C&D on last two outings and not disgraced when sixth of ten on latest (co-favourite); case can be made back on last winning mark.

C&D winner in 2024 but three subsequent visits have not gone nearly so well; none too consistent but two of his last four AW runs, including in January latest, give him a shout if he's ready following the absence; he's twice been runner-up after longer layoffs.

Reliable sort (on turf and AW) who won twice last summer and was runner-up in March/April on his last two outings; stable has struck often enough this summer for him to be given a close look despite this new track.

Eight-race maiden who made the running on first three starts this term but switched to trying to come from the rear when hooded on both since; Newmarket latest (7f, good to firm; 40-1) was a positive performance as he seemed to be gathering momentum in the closing stages and was beaten just 2l in sixth of 11; dropped 2lb today and everything may well click into place soon.

Best effort in eight starts for Richard Hannon when beaten a neck in a Wolverhampton nursery (8.6f, AW) in December; 6,000gns buy in February before never dangerous in a small field at Brighton (7f, good to firm; 28-1) 16 days ago; needs a rapid revival.

Debut (well beaten) was her only start on turf; sent handicapping for last two outings and came second of eight at Wolverhampton (7f) in February on latest, albeit beaten 13l; relatively early days but it's not yet clear that she's worth this mark.

Probably started handicap life on a demanding mark and he'd dropped 10lb before going down by just under 2l when fifth of 15 at Doncaster (7f, good) in first-time blinkers on latest outing; hit the front over 1f out that day but wandered under pressure; needs to see it out better.

Best form when fourth of 13 on handicap debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm), faring best of those held up; readily outgunned once in the clear at Haydock (upped to 7f) later in May but soft ground was a possible excuse.

Sole win from 17 races was on Kempton AW (6f) in January; new yard when back on turf for last three outings, not far away in two of those but better is needed to win this; his only two attempts over this far did not convince.

Unraced on good to firm except on debut (last of four); yard is among the winners and a recent, never-nearer fifth of 12 on the Kempton AW (7f; 12-1) was a respectable start to this filly's 3yo campaign, not getting the clearest of runs late on; needs a close look.

Nine-race maiden; reappearance was his best show this term and, having had four starts since, it's hard to get excited about his chance today despite the falling mark; first wore a visor on latest outing.

RaceName: British Stallions Studs EBF Nursery Handicap (A Hamilton Park 2-Y-O Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has run to a similar level in four starts since her debut, coming home strongly when winning a C&D maiden three weeks ago (good to firm; runner-up went close in a handicap next time); mark adjusted by 4lb since but in the thick of it now handicapping.

RaceName: British Stallions Studs EBF Nursery Handicap (A Hamilton Park 2-Y-O Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has improved with each start, running creditably in a valuable seller at Musselburgh on second start, then coming clear in Ffos Las maiden (5f, soft) four weeks ago, where the stiffer test at the trip, soft ground and possibly first-time cheekpieces may all have played a part; this provides a different test but she may be up to it.

RaceName: British Stallions Studs EBF Nursery Handicap (A Hamilton Park 2-Y-O Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has ability but he was difficult to keep on the straight and narrow when making his handicap debut at Yarmouth (5f, good to firm) last week and was eased inside the final furlong; queried now with first-time visor replaced with cheekpieces.
Enjoying a fine season and his fifth win (including over C&D) of the campaign came at Wolverhampton (7f) two days ago when completing a quick hat-trick; leading claims turned out under a 5lb penalty.
Low-mileage sort who posted easily his best effort for new yard with second in 5f Ayr handicap last month; needs considering off an unchanged mark.
Took this in 2025 but winless since and just a fair fifth of eight over C&D five days ago; this veteran needs to take a step forward.
Gained a second win of 2026 at Musselburgh (5f) in June; only seventh of 11 in 5f Ayr handicap three days ago so she needs to bounce back.

Resumed winning ways at Wolverhampton (5f) in May and comes here on the back of a solid third of 13 in 6f Ayr handicap ten days ago; must enter calculations eased 1lb in his bid for a first turf victory.
Remains winless and she beat one over C&D five days ago; more is required if she's to gain a breakthrough win at the 12th attempt.

OwnerName: Let's Be Lucky Racing 38 & Steven Wilson
Spotlight: 0-20 and he arrives below par, just fifth of ten in 5f Musselburgh handicap last month; others appeal more.

OwnerName: N Bradley Racing 29 & South Bank Racing
Spotlight: Runner-up in C&D novice in May but she has failed to go on sent handicapping, last of ten at Musselburgh (5f) last month;  cheekpieces are reached for now.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has shown fair form when runner-up on all four starts, most recently in 1m2f novice at Doncaster last month; since gelded and this son of Blue Point is the one to beat with cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Victor Ludorum gelding; half-brother to 7f 2yo winner Brastias (RPR 72); dam 1m-1m6f maiden (RPR 66), sister to 1m4f-15.5f winner Theatro; has had wind surgery ahead of his debut but in good hands and needs considering.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 66-1, hinted at promise with a staying-on fourth of seven in maiden here (1m1f, good to firm) on his debut three weeks ago; this son of Churchill can do better in the longer term.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well held in a pair of 7f novices at Newcastle and Carlisle eight months apart; significantly more is required.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 80-1 but shaped well when fourth of ten in Doncaster maiden (1m, soft) on his debut in September; off since but this Time Test gelding remains with potential.

RaceName: Alex McWilliams Memorial Celebrations Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 40-1 and green when a never-dangerous sixth of eight in maiden at Ayr (6f, soft) on her debut last month; needs to take a big step forward.

RaceName: Wellman Cars Private Hire Almada Mile Handicap
Spotlight: Justified short odds in 6f Doncaster maiden on sole 2yo start; much better form on reappearance at Leicester (7f, good) in April, looking strong in the closing stages against rivals who have given the form a weighty look since; has to prove stamina over the new trip, and his pedigree is more about sprinting on the dam's side, but still intriguing on handicap debut if ground is thought suitable (missed recent intended run on good to firm).

RaceName: Wellman Cars Private Hire Almada Mile Handicap
Spotlight: High-class handicap form at 6f to 1m on a range of surfaces and he was up against it when second to a progressive winner in this race last year; has since won two handicaps at Meydan for new yard and perhaps felt the lack of a recent run when mid-division in the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot last month; leading player.

RaceName: Wellman Cars Private Hire Almada Mile Handicap
Spotlight: Two 6f AW wins as a juvenile and he nearly pulled off a step up in trip when going down narrowly at Chester (extended 7f, good) in May; had no chance of getting involved after getting badly hampered on the rail at Epsom in June; gelded since; open to some improvement but he's another trying a new trip.

RaceName: Wellman Cars Private Hire Almada Mile Handicap
Spotlight: Sole French win on heavy ground but he's excelled on good and quicker for new yard, having far too much power for his rivals when making all here (about 1m1f) in May and doing really well to be third (demoted to fifth) in a major York handicap (extended 1m2f) on Saturday; needs a strong pace back at this trip which he may well set himself; good claims.

RaceName: Wellman Cars Private Hire Almada Mile Handicap
Spotlight: A superstar down the years and he's quite well treated again now but all his handicap wins at 7f and 1m have been on downhill tracks on good to soft or slower ground; better days ahead once the rains come.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
OwnerName: Fine Claret Racing,Mrs Burke & C Wood
Spotlight: Scored at Newcastle (1m) in December and has proved reliable without adding to his tally this season, a clear second of seven to Jannas Journey in 1m Carlisle handicap 12 days ago; not taken lightly despite a 2lb weights rise.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: A fair 1m scorer for Andrew Balding in 2024; off 22 months but quickly back on track with second of ten in 1m2f handicap at Ayr 11 days ago; needs considering off an unchanged mark.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-German 1m1f winner; gained a first win for current yard over C&D in May and not discredited when third of five (Kaleido runner-up) over C&D five days ago; not out of things with relatively few miles still on the clock.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Gained a first win of 2026 in 1m handicap at Carlisle 12 days ago, getting up late to deny Inspired having been set a lot to do; bagged a remarkable seven successes (including here) last season so merits serious consideration now she's up and running this time around.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: A fair 7f winner for John and Thady Gosden last summer; has steadily found his form for current yard, runner-up in five-runner event over C&D five days ago; player off an unchanged mark.

Has an ordinary strike-rate overall but he broke his turf duck over C&D (good to soft; acts well on good to firm) in June and nearly always runs well in sprints on this track; one of the better options.

OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And Partner
Spotlight: Not in the same form as he was in May and June last year but he's on a lowly mark now and, after being pushed along from some way out, he did stick well to the task when fourth over C&D (good to firm) recently; form case to be made down in grade.

OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And Partner
Spotlight: Had a good run of form in early summer last year, getting off the mark at Redcar (6f, good to firm), but rather up and down since and she found little at Ayr ten days ago; hard to rule out if back to best, though.
All three turf wins at 5f, including on this course, but she has won over this trip on the AW and ran well enough over 6f at Pontefract (good) recently to expect her to be on the premises.

Won this race in 2022 and finished runner-up in two of three subsequent runnings; looked to be running into form again when fourth of eight at Catterick (7f, good to firm) 24 days ago and a very good run is likely.

Minor form in a handful of starts, including at classified level and in handicaps, but this is only her third run for Jim Goldie and the return to 6f could suit on second run since wind surgery; may yet improve; cheekpieces fitted.

Winning return from a long absence in early 2025 but she's finding it hard to sustain her effort in sprints on AW and turf this year, even allowing for finishing second of eight on Newcastle AW (5f) in June; headgear left off; up against it.

OwnerName: A Whillans, C Spark, J Wright
Spotlight: Winless since January 2024 but he arrives in good nick, third in 1m5f classified event at Ayr (disqualified for riding weighing in light) last month; not out of things back in handicap company.

Gained a breakthrough success at Newcastle (1m4f) in January; back from five months off in good nick, though seemed unsuited by the drop back in trip when fifth of eight at Nottingham (1m2f) 12 days ago; remains unexposed over this trip so very much one to consider.
Finally got off the mark when a wide-margin winner over C&D three weeks ago; able to dictate the pace there so more is probably needed from a 6lb higher mark.

A dual 1m4f AW winner (also scored over hurdles) in 2025; running with credit without winning this season until only fourth of five at Beverley (1m4f) 13 days ago; he's the sort to bounce back in a change of headgear.
A two-time winner (at up to 1m7f) last autumn; failed to build on earlier promise when only sixth of eight in 1m5f handicap at Ayr ten days ago; this course winner needs to get back on track.

Very promising start when a close third in valuable Fairyhouse bumper (2m, sft-hvy) in April 2025; not seen again until a 4.5l fourth of five back at Fairyhouse (2m, yielding) in January; now steps up in trip for hurdling debut after another absence with Townend up; could go well.

Runner up on last two starts over hurdles; rated 117 and leading claims on paper but disappointing effort when beaten at short odds in 1m4f Limerick claimer on the Flat on latest, hanging to the right.

OwnerName: Ms P Twiss & J Twiss & M O'Sullivan & S Nevin Twiss
Spotlight: Flat maiden placed on all five starts over hurdles at 2m-2m1f, earning a rating of 118; a shade unlucky on the Flat at Limerick last time; beaten 5.5l when third of 14 on penultimate in a maiden hurdle at Cork; longer trip and good ground are queries; tongue tie goes on.
Affinisea gelding; 1-4 in point-to-points but the form of his win hasn't worked out; beaten 26l when second of two finishers in winners' race at Necarne latest; more needed on belated Rules' debut.
0-15 over hurdles and rated 100; has a few placed efforts to his name in maidens, but pulled up at Wexford on latest and needs to bounce back.
Soundly beaten in a Kilbeggan bumper on debut a month ago when a 12-1 shot; likely best watched upped in trip for hurdling bow.
Berkshire mare was pulled up and beaten 21l in two point-to-points; tongue tie is applied for rules debut; best watched.

Castle Du Berlais gelding; unsold as 3yo; half-brother to French 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Joly Risk; dam maiden half-sister to 1m7f-2m5f chase winner Joly Maker; best watched on debut unless the market speaks.
Remote third in a Kilbeggan bumper on debut for Willie Mullins; poor form so far for this yard, including in maiden hurdles the last twice; hard to fancy.

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
Spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner, both at around 2m on good to yielding and good to firm ground; soundly beaten behind a couple of these on return from a break at Listowel in May; more needed and stamina to prove over this far.

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
Spotlight: Grade 1 winner at Aintree (2m1f, gd-sft) in April 2025; regained the winning thread in mares' race at Listowel (16.5f, good) on latest (Grainne A Chroi 6.25l behind); the one to beat on ratings, but has never run beyond 2m1f so she has stamina to prove (mixed messages in pedigree).

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
Spotlight: Solid placed graded form in France on testing ground; shed the maiden tag for this stable at Ludlow in February (2m5f, soft); not disgraced in sole start on good in the Grade 2 mares' novice at Cheltenham (2m1f); beaten 5l in Listed novice at Punchestown when last seen in April; Townend prefers Murcia.

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
Spotlight: 2-7 over hurdles and some smart form in the book; better known as a chaser these days, but has been out of sorts in that sphere on recent starts; third at Punchestown on latest, but was still beaten over 9l; needs to revive on first run over timber since March 2024.

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
OwnerName: Ms Eileen O'Brien & John Anthony Harrington
Spotlight: Useful mare won a Grade 3 at Punchestown in February (2m4f, soft); outclassed in Grade 2 at Fairyhouse before finishing a 6.25l third behind Murcia over inadequate trip at Listowel (16.5f, good) on latest; this trip more her bag and may close the gap; any rain would be a plus.

RaceName: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-7 over hurdles and rated just 88; out of her depth in this company.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Has improved for better ground; edging up the weights after placed efforts at Punchestown (3m, gd-yld), Listowel (20.5f, gd-yld) and on latest at Limerick (22.5f, good); nudged up another 2lb, but should be on the premises again.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but did show some promise in two of his maidens; pulled up on handicap bow at Ballinrobe (2m, good) on latest, however, and needs to leave that behind upped in trip.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Maiden whose three best efforts have come on testing ground at Limerick; has a race in him, but has to prove he acts on this quicker ground.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Won off 8lb higher at Galway in September 2024 but has shown virtually nothing since; tailed off at Sligo on latest and impossible to fancy on recent form.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Long-standing maiden ran okay at Listowel last September, but was still beaten 11.5l into third; mid-field over 2m7f here when last seen in October; may need this on return.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Best effort yet on return from 131 days off at Kilbeggan (17.5f, gd-yld) when a 7.75l fourth of 13; should strip fitter now, eased 1lb and pedigree suggests that this trip might suit; not discounted.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: 0-7 and yet to trouble the judge; a bit better at Kilbeggan on latest (24.5f, good), but much more needed dropped back in trip.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Struggled in all three maiden hurdles on soft and soft to heavy ground; given a break since soundly beaten at Clonmel and tongue tie goes on for handicap debut; best watched unless the market speaks.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Didn't show a whole lot in maidens and similar story in first two handicaps; assessor relenting, but others have more appealing profiles.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Flat winner on fast ground for David O'Meara; huge odds and well held in three maiden hurdles for this yard at 2m-2m1f; potential improver stepped up in trip for handicap debut.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Point winner off the mark under rules at Fairyhouse in October off 6lb lower (2m, yielding); held off revised mark twice since, though may have needed latest; step up in trip needs to unlock further improvement.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: 0-7 over hurdles but has run well on two of last three starts; beaten 15l when runner up in maiden hurdle at Wexford in May; hung badly left when pulled up on handicap debut at Sligo; solid third off this mark at Bellewstown latest; chance if building on that.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Conditions are fine for this veteran; has gone well here before and he's well handicapped but hasn't won since October 2024 and his recent efforts have been well below par; revival needed.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Maiden pointer; 0-15 over hurdles and has yet to display winning potential; soundly beaten again at Kilbeggan on return from break latest; others preferred.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Arguably best effort yet on handicap debut at Kilbeggan (15.5f, gd-yld) when keeping on from the back for a 9l fifth of 13; bred to appreciate this longer trip; could go well.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Solid placed maiden form on good ground last season; struggled in testing conditions the last twice, including on handicap debut at Cork in December; returns from a break now with ground to suit, so check the market.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Left modest maiden form behind to run a fine race when 1.75l second on handicap debut at Clonmel (19.5f, gd-yld); stayed on well from the back that day so whether this sharper track will suit is up for debate, but unexposed and enters calculations.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Two wins last season included one here over 2m7f (yielding) off 4lb lower; has also won a chase here and is 2-3 at this venue; should be sharper for latest run after break over an inadequate trip, but probably not much wriggle room off this mark.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: 1-24 over hurdles, the win coming over 3m on heavy ground at Clonmel in 2023; is now 12lb lower, but has disappointed the last twice after showing a bit more at Clonmel in May.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles; best efforts have come on soft and soft to heavy ground; beaten 15l on soft at Limerick on latest and only 1lb lower here; more needed.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Maiden seemed to appreciate the step up to 22.5f (good) at Clonmel last time when keeping on for a 9.25l third; eased 1lb, but not sure whether the drop back in trip here will suit.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Off the mark off 6lb lower in Tramore handicap hurdle in April (20.5f, yielding); came up short off revised rating at Clonmel; was feeling the pinch when unseating two out at Tramore latest; place shout.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
OwnerName: Eamon Nolan & Mrs Catherine Anne Nolan
Spotlight: Glimmers of promise in maidens before fine 1l second on handicap debut at Limerick in March (2m, soft); didn't quite see out 2m4f at Wexford on latest (gd-yld); stamina a query again here.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: AW winner on the Flat; 0-5 over hurdles and pulled up in first two handicaps; can only be watched for now.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: 16-race maiden over hurdles; her Sligo third from last July off 3lb higher would give her a squeak, but well below that level in two runs since returning from a break, the latest over fences; more needed.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Veteran's five career wins include a handicap chase here in August 2024 (2m5f, yielding); that's the last time he won and pulled up on return from long layoff at Listowel 47 days ago.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Consistent and holding form well enough in handicaps; beaten around 6l off this mark the last twice, at Down Royal (2m4f, good) and Wexford (2m1f, gd-yld) when wearing first-time cheekpieces (retained); step back up to this trip should suit; in the mix again.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Four wins over hurdles, the most recent coming in this race last year off 2lb lower on yielding to soft, his second win over C&D; out of depth on the Flat last time, but this is more suitable and acts on good ground; player.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Showed little in maidens and well beaten on handicap debut here over 2m1f last October (2m1f, yielding); brought down two out when near the rear at Downpatrick on return from break; a bit to prove.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Exors of the Late E Blaney
Spotlight: Dual Flat winner is only 1-18 over hurdles, but has put up solid runs the last twice at Downpatrick; the blinkers worn last time are retained and can be involved, but needs more to win.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Hurdle and chase winner when trained in the UK; hit and miss, kept to hurdles, since switched to this yard; well beaten when last seen and others appeal more today.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has been in fine form since the spring, winning a 2m6f Down Royal novice handicap before runner-up in Cork and Listowel handicaps over 3m; should be fine dropped in trip and blinkers replace cheekpieces; up 2lb; player.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Chase winner has won twice over hurdles with last score coming at Clonmel in June 2025; some decent runs this term, but was beaten a long way at Sligo four days ago.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Flat winner has shown much-improved form over hurdles this season, winning at Clonmel and Limerick the last twice over approximately this trip; another 7lb rise demands more, but he has to be on the shortlist.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden was beaten 5l by today's rival Global Skies at Clonmel last time, his best handicap run; raised 2lb for that and, if he has progressed since, can run respectably again.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Got off the mark in a Kilbeggan handicap hurdle in May and a solid run in a Cartmel chase since; 5lb higher than for his win and is up in grade too, but can run well.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a novice chase at Cork last October, but is a maiden over hurdles; well beaten in this sphere at Ballinrobe last time over 2m, but this trip could suit; is capable of better, so not ruled out.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Some decent efforts in defeat in maidens and handicaps in varying ground conditions; beaten favourite in a Clonmel maiden last time; steps up in trip today and a tongue-tie added; needs more but not ruled out.

RaceName: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner in France; ran respectably on Irish debut at Limerick after a long absence in a race where the winner was on a faster wide strip of ground; should have improved from that and has a shout.
Useful Flat sort on the continent got off the mark over hurdles last time at Downpatrick; got an 11lb hike for that, but goes well fresh and is still rated 90 on the Flat, so has to be respected.
Record of 1-18 over hurdles; third in a Clonmel claimer in May, but was beaten a long way on debut for this yard at Downpatrcik since; has to rebound.
Wexford maiden hurdle winner for Joseph O'Brien last year; however, has been below that form in four runs for this yard; blinkers replace previously-worn cheekpieces.

Winless, but some good runs, since taking a Listowel maiden hurdle in 2024; well beaten chasing last twice, but can't be ruled out back in this discipline with an in-form rider aboard; third runner for yard; watch market.
Flat winner won a 2m1f Wexford handicap and a solid run off this mark there since; needs more up in grade, but shouldn't be far away.
Won back-to-back handicaps last year for Tony Mullins, but lost his form after; hit and miss chasing lately for this yard, but would have a chance if back to his best.
Hasn't won since May 2023, but some solid runs last year; however, is best watched on return unless strong in the market.

OwnerName: Exors of the Late M Mortell
Spotlight: Won at Listowel last September, but has been well below that level twice this term; needs a return to best; second of three runners for yard.
Maiden has been placed in bumpers and hurdles, but has been poor the last thrice in handicaps and has to do much better.
Maiden hurdle winner in 2023 and also two Flat wins for Tony Martin; won a Kilbeggan handicap on stable debut returning from a 214-day break; needs more up 7lb but a player.
Dual bumper winner in France; won a Thurles handicap hurdle last October, but was poor at Cheltenham next time; market can guide on return with yard in form.

OwnerName: John Joseph Flynn & Conor Lannen & Mrs Miriam Queally
Spotlight: Beaten a long way in a bumper and three hurdles, so has to improve loads on handicap bow off what looks a stiff mark.
Sligo maiden winner last year hasn't matched that form since; was poor at Punchestown, but was better at Downpatrick since; needs a return to his best.
Promise in first two bumpers; soundly beaten in maiden hurdles, but can do better in this sphere; one of three for a yard that does well here, so watch the market.
Promise in a bumper, but well beaten on first two hurdle starts; much-improved when fourth in a Roscommon maiden last time; has a shout if building on that.

Solid debut effort at Roscommon on yielding to soft ground, but didn't improve from that at Limerick since, albeit still a decent effort; sets the standard on form, but vulnerable to a decent newcomer.

Fourth foal; half-brother to point winner Diamond Jetaway; dam placed 2m3f-3m hurdles, sister to useful 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner Jet Master, from family of high-class chaser Blazing Walker; unsold for E4,800 as a 3yo; yard can ready a newcomer, so needs a market check.

First foal; dam point winner, half-sister to 2m3f-3m3f hurdle winner Bryden Boy and bumper winner Hideaway Vic, out of bumper/2m4f hurdle winner; E10,000 foal is by a quality French sire and his yard does well at this track, so worth a market check.
Second runner for yard; raced too keenly when beaten 28l in a Down Royal bumper in May; will need to settle better and a hood may help.

Ninth foal; half-brother to AW bumper and useful 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner Golden Taipan; dam unraced and from the family of high-class chaser The Grey Monk; by a promising young sire and cost E22,000 as a 3yo; tongue-tie on for debut; top rider booked and one to be interested in, especially if there is market strength.

OwnerName: Exors of the Late Michael Moloney
Spotlight: Second foal; brother to point winner Fox Walk; dam 1m7f hurdle winner, out of 2m hurdle-winning half-sister to Grand National winner Rule The World; by the champion sire but cost only E16,000 as a 3yo; top rider booked and one to check for market strength.

First foal; dam 1m2f winner (inc AW; RPR 82), sister to 1m4f-2m winner Pantomime, half-sister to 7f/1m winner Darkening, out of 6f winner; Flat-bred but there is stamina in his damline; could run respectably on debut.

One of two runners for yard; second foal; dam placed 2m2f-3m1f hurdles, sister to winner Montys Meadow (useful bumper/2m hurdle/2m4f chase) and family of Grand National winner Monty's Pass; decent pedigree but a E5,000 vendor buyback as a foal; worth a market check; tongue-tie.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Beaten 23l on debut at Punchestown and will have to improve plenty on that to score.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Beaten 9l on sole point start by a rival that made E100,000 since; ran a cracker on bumper debut at Downpatrick when runner-up to a more experienced rival; can improve for that and a leading lady rider aboard, so a solid chance.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Ninth foal; half-sister to winners Thou Art Peter (1m/1m2f inc HK dirt; RPR 80) and Bungle Inthedesert (1m AW; 73); dam unraced half-sister to useful 1m2f winner Saab Alamanal; Flat-bred filly was a E5,000 vendor buyback as a yearling; stamina concerns, so best watched for future reference.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Beaten 17l and 23l in two bumpers on varying ground conditions; fitted with a hood and tongue-tie today, but best watched for the time being.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Sister to 2m5f-3m2f chase winner Village Master, half-sister to four winners including Bun Doran (high-class bumper and 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase) and Shantou Village (smart bumper and 2m4f-2m7f hurdle/chase); a sibling to some smart sorts, but seems the champion trainer's second-string; could still run well; tongue-tie.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Half-sister to Champion Bumper winner Bambino Fever; was weak in the market when beaten 13l on debut at Ballinrobe last September; likely to do better after an absence and is one for the shortlist.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Not a lot of promise when failing to complete in two point starts; however, a different story over C&D on bumper debut when beaten only 11l; the tongue-tie worn then is retained and should have improved since, so is a player.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Eighth foal; dam placed 2m4f/2m6f hurdles, half-sister to 7f Group 3 winner Marvada (dam of 1m2f Group 2 winner Terebellum), out of French 1m3f winner; dam hasn't a great record at stud; unsold for E1,800 as a 3yo; doesn't make a lot of appeal on debut.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
OwnerName: John F Doyle & R Bannerman & Mrs Sheila O'Ryan
Spotlight: Well beaten in the Goffs Defender bumper on debut and not much better in a Limerick maiden hurdle; best watched for the time being.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Respectable debut effort for former yard when beaten 16l in a Galway bumper nearly a year ago; absence since is a concern, but could run well for a respected local yard.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Third foal; half-brother to bumper winner Wilton Mills Trier; dam unraced half-sister to winners Solsbury Hill (2m hurdle/chase) and Reelingintheyears (2m3f hurdle); E5,000 foal was unsold for E4,500 as a 3yo; not a bad pedigree and could be capable of running well.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Beaten 18l on sole completed point start and doesn't make much appeal on bumper debut.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Second foal; dam runner-up in 1m3f/1m4f AQPS Flat races and 2m4f hurdle, half-sister to high-class bumper and 2m-2m7f/chase hurdle winner Bacardys; E25,000 foal then made only E16,000 as a 3yo; decent pedigree; tongue-tie for debut; best watched unless market support.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Ninth foal; half-sister to winners Slainte Mhor (3m chase) and Persian Daughter (2m6f hurdle); dam unraced half-sister to high-class 2m5f-3m6f hurdle/chase winner Ad Hoc; by a useful sire and a decent damline; cost E4,000 as a 3yo; will likely improve from this.

RaceName: Kate Kearney's Cottage (Ladies Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: By a useful sire and from the family of Gold Cup winner Long Run; however, has been pulled-up on both point runs, so isn't easy to fancy; tongue-tie on.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Chased home a strongly-fancied rival from the Ger Lyons stable at Fairyhouse last week; should go one better now, since the winner had two runs under her belt and is reportedly a candidate for the valuable Ballyhane Stakes; stable maintaining terrific form.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 125,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-sister by top-class juvenile sprinter Perfect Power to useful Group-placed winner Thunder Of Niagara, and to a minor 1m winner; dam placed, half-sister to US 1m4f Grade 3 winner Dress Rehearsal.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E16,000 Y, £45,000 2yo; third foal; half-sister to Polish 1m winner Cotai Spirit; dam placed 7f AW 2yo, half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Lajooje, out of 7f/1m Listed winning half-sister to 5f Group 1 winner Equiano.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 65,000gns yearling; Sergei Prokofiev colt is the first foal out of an unraced half-sister to French 6f 2yo Listed winner Royal Grey, out of 6f 2yo Group 2 winner; trainer introduced a smart juvenile at this venue last week.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Fair first effort at Roscommon with this rider aboard; stable's newcomer has a senior rider aboard; will probably need a handicap mark.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E25,000 yearling; third foal; half-brother by Ardad to two winners; dam 6f winner, half-sister to 6f Listed winner Bounty Box; one of two here for the stable, a senior jockey aboard.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Failed to sell at 50,000gns as a yearling; second foal; half-brother by Pinatubo to a 5f/6f winner in Britain and Hong Kong; dam 1m AW 2yo winner.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Gave problems at the start and never showed with a chance first time out at Cork.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made late headway from an unpromising position at Bellewstown; longer trip should suit, but needs to find considerable improvement.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 50,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-brother by the speedy Caturra to three winners; dam Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner, half-sister to 6f 2yo Listed winner System.

RaceName: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: (E6,000 vendor Y); second foal; half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Nakamura; unraced dam closely related to 5f-1m winner Bernie's Boy, half-sister to useful 5f-7f winner Gentlemen; hooded for debut; in good hands but best watched.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ran green and did not get a clear passage at Roscommon; has a bit to find with Sea Of Rain (second) and Jezzie Bea (fourth); could feature with normal progress.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Got upset in the stalls on debut at the Curragh; merit in her run in the circumstances, keeping on to finish sixth of 12; withdrawn after a stalls issue here last time; significant element of risk with that in mind.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Beaten favourite at Roscommon on debut, fourth behind a rival who had run twice; went within a whisker of opening her account over C&D on second start, beaten by a Jessica Harrington-trained favourite; beaten favourite for a second time at Roscommon; obvious prospects here, since she should again have the measure of Jezzie Bea and Ballyskeagh.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Left an impression that she still had plenty to learn when keeping on well at Roscommon on debut; fourth placing was promising in the circumstances; may get closer to runner-up Sea Of Rain; same remark could apply to fifth-placed Ballyskeagh.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 30,000gns as a yearling; half-brother to seven winners over distances between 7f and 1m2f; dam French 1m 2yo winner

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made some late headway over C&D on debut; potential for improvement but no reason why he should reverse form with runner-up Sea Of Rain.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 42,000 euros as a yearling; tenth foal and half-brother to four winners; pedigree is perhaps more middle distance-oriented; one of two newcomers, both by Without Parole, for his trainer.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Not a bad run at a huge price on debut at the Curragh, will benefit from more experience.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Not disgraced at a big price on her introduction at the Curragh; might be one for handicaps in due course, if building on that.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 40,000 euros as a yearling;; third foal; half-brother by Cotai Glory to 6f winner Ceo Stealth Mode; dam unraced half-sister to winners Gangster Granny (Flat and hurdles) and Ballinea Star (6f 2yo Group 3), out of Group-placed 6f 2yo winner; potentially interesting.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cheap purchase; third in Naas barrier trial in May; slowly into stride and never a factor at Fairyhouse (6f) last month; failed to improve in a 5f maiden at Bellewstown and now fitted with a hood.

RaceName: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 20,000 euros as a yearling; seventh foal; half-brother to winners Determined Effort (US 5f turf) and Karacrown (Mexican 2yo); dam French Listed-placed 1m 2yo/US 8.5f turf winner (RPR 98), half-sister to French 1m Listed winner Night Bokbel; jockey booking is noteworthy.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Placed over 7f on the second of three maiden starts at two; disappointing on only nursery attempt; after losing a prominent position, finished well for this rider to take third over 5f at Naas on her seasonal debut; every chance she can feature over this longer trip.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Last win came in a 1m Killarney claimer in 2024; fifth in a claimer last time at Bellewstown, only 24 hours after finishing fourth in a handicap at the same venue; overall handicap form has been satisfactory; needs to raise his game

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Has made the frame on her last three starts; does not need much to improve from her recent close-up third at Fairyhouse; addition of cheekpieces may provide that little bit extra that she needs to get her head in front for the first time.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Was in the form of his life around this time two seasons ago with back-to-back 6f wins for Michael O'Callaghan; signs of a revival when seventh of 21 at Naas last month; needs to provide further reassurance to become a betting proposition.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: AW winner over 1m; that had seemed like a flash in the pan until a revival in form when third behind the well-fancied Glen Breeze at Limerick last Saturday; 2lb wrong here but not without a chance of reaching the money.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Heavily-raced gelding; gained a tenth career win at Dundalk in April and seems to be holding his form well; 3l second at the Curragh and a fair fifth at Bellewstown 13 days ago; 0-11 record at this venue is a negative, placed three times.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ended last season with fine second placings at Down Royal and the Curragh; especially good effort behind the progressive Syzygy on the second occasion; no sign of similar form in three starts this term.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Last season's 50-1 success in a 27-runner 6f contest at the Curragh now looks like a fluke; hard to fancy on this season's form; new headgear combination.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Five-time turf winner; out of sorts on AW last winter, unseated rider at start on reappearance at Bellewstown 13 days ago; jockey booking is the main positive.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Went up 12lb for a Fairyhouse success last month; beat subsequent winner Monastere then; however, unable to sustain her improvement when down the field at the same venue at the beginning of the month; held by Bear Right on that evidence.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Just one placed effort from eight starts last season; tailed off at the Curragh on his return and down the field at Roscommon two months ago; not a big price on the second occasion, so perhaps capable of better.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Prolific AW winner (9-32); off-putting 1-31 record on turf; placed this season at Cork and the Curragh; below best on three most recent starts.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Enjoyed a good spell last summer, including a win and a short-head second in two outings over 1m here in June; twice made the frame over 1m here this year before winning over this trip at Down Royal in May; out of the money twice since then.

RaceName: Bulmers Live At Leopardstown Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Won 6f maiden for Ralph Beckett and later some decent efforts in defeat in France up to 1m2f; weak Irish form, in rear on both starts this season.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mrs E Irwin & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: St Mark's Basilica half-sister to eight winners including Australian Group 2 winner Adjusted; dam won over 1m1f in France; first home in a barrier trial before last week's debut here over 7f; 7-2, finished off well when second to a promising type; entered in the Group 1 Moyglare; slightly unusual that she's out again so quickly.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: By Wootton Bassett; first living foal out of Love, who won on her third start at two before going on to win the Moyglare, and completed the 1,000 Guineas/Oaks double the following year; holds a Moyglare entry.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: By multiple champion US sire Into Mischief; half-sister to five winners, notably Derby winner City Of Troy, out of a Group 1 winner; 16-1, slowly away and never got in to it at the Curragh in 7f maiden where stablemates were first and second; entered in the Moyglare, though, and no surprise to see a much better showing this time.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 100,000 euros at the breeze-ups and is speedily bred; 10-1, caught late over 1m at Naas in Listed race won by rival now rated 89, so it's not form to get carried away with and had a relatively hard race into the bargain; backs up fairly quickly as well, but obviously has a good level of ability.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Good American pedigree and cost $150,000 as a yearling; 25s, prominent until weakening quickly 1f out in hot 6f maiden at the Curragh on Guineas weekend.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Daughter of Australia was bought back for 18,000 euro at the yearling sales; closely related to 6f/7f winner Orchidaceae (inc 2yo; RPR 98), half-sister to 1m AW winner Another Day Done; dam 7f 2yo winner, half-sister to 7f 2yo Listed winner Mountain Bear; stable second-string and no fancy entries.

Front-running second over this trip at Gowran leaves him with a little bit to find with How'sthebai on a line through the winner; went one better at the Curragh, and third's subsequent run suggests this opening mark is about right; scratched at Killarney on Monday due to ground described as good.

Unlucky a few times on turf last year, but won three times at Dundalk, notably when beating subsequent Group 2 winner Jancis in a Listed contest over this trip; favourite/joint favourite all three outings in premier handicaps this term, twice running well at the Curragh over 6f/7f; mark remains 7lb lower than AW rating; doesn't usually lead, but can race handily.

Likeable 3yo; won AW maiden last year; good fourth in hot Naas handicap over 1m before making most to beat in-form rival over 1m1f on probably unsuitably soft ground here; had that rival a little further back when fourth in 1m1f premier handicap at the Curragh, where missing a beat at the start proved costly in a race where the leaders didn't come back; takes on older horses for the first time.

Three wins on AW, but 0-21 on turf; did well at Dundalk over the winter and carried that form through to soft-ground contests in the spring; second over 7f at Naas and fourth over 1m2f here in April (strong form); not so good since; likes to come from off the pace, and there wasn't enough on when he was fourth (only 7-2) at Killarney on Monday.

Will like the ground; won over 1m1f here last year and has dropped back to just 1lb higher mark; ground too soft first two starts this year; latest 6l Curragh defeat can be marked up somewhat (upset in stalls and met some interference) and generally runs this track well.

OwnerName: Thomas J O'Connor & Ms Hazel McGuinness
Spotlight: Nine wins in all, but only one on turf from 32 starts; led when third over 7f at Fairyhouse last week, and that's probably his optimum trip on turf, rather than the stiff mile here; unplaced all four runs here, too.

Smart Curragh form at two; beat top-class filly Kensington Lane on debut and then finished second in Group 2 races won by Constitution River and Hawk Mountain; 2026 form includes links to top-class performers Thesecretadversary and Causeway; a promoted second behind Isaac Newton in a 1m1f Listed event at Navan; reversed form with that rival on latest.

Group 3 winner over 7f at Deauville as a 2yo; lost way last season but back to form this term; runner-up to City Of Memphis in conditions race at Gowran (7f, soft) and won conditions race at Fairyhouse (7f, good); fair third of six in a 1m Listed race at the Curragh on latest.

Goodwood maiden winner on debut last August (7f, good to soft); creditable run in Group 1 at Saint-Cloud (1m2f, very soft) in October; moderate efforts first two runs this term; back on song when winning a 1m1f Listed race at Navan (Geryon promoted to second); lost a lot of ground at the start when failing to confirm form with Geryon at the Curragh last time.

Progressive handicapper on heavy ground late last season; began this season with an excellent third in the 25-runner Irish Lincoln; placed in a 1m handicap at this venue in April; career-best on latest when chasing home stablemate and subsequent Group 3 winner Duckadilly in a 1m Listed race at Navan; 50-1 then, and is the outsider on figures here.

Second in the Irish Derby and Grand Prix de Paris for Aidan O'Brien in 2023; mostly below that level in Australia, apart from a nose second in 1m2f Group 3 at Randwick last September; marked his return to Ireland with a pleasing staying-on third to Minnie Hauk in 1m2f Curragh Group 2 (good) in May; failed to feature in Royal Ascot's Wolferton Stakes.

Three starts at Royal Ascot have yielded a win in the 2023 Chesham (7f), an excellent second of 23 in the Kensington Palace (1m) last year, and a creditable fifth in last month's Duke of Cambridge (1m); produced her best display on home soil when beating the odds-on Purview in this race 12 months ago; began this season with a solid third in a 7f Group 3 at this track.

Ballinrobe maiden winner was a length off Daler back there last month (now 1lb better off); seemingly outstayed over 1m4f last time; touched off at Navan last year, so she goes left-handed; handicapped to win when everything falls into place.

Came good late in his three-year-old campaign when the blinds went on; back-to-back wins in 0-60 company at Gowran (1m, heavy) and  Dundalk (10.5f); after eight months off, ran okay when upgraded to this level, finishing pretty much upsides Unterberg and Sinbad My Dad at Roscommon (10.5f).

AW winner surprised his trainer when handling soft ground here last month, beating Monday's ready Killarney winner Molto Amichi over 1m1f in first-time cheekpieces; winner got first run on him at Ballinrobe over almost this far, where he kept on well along with third-home Marmeladova.

OwnerName: Mrs Helen Butler & John A Griffin & Mrs Bernadette Fahey
Spotlight: Sole win in 26 Flat starts was over 1m1f in lower-grade contest here last August; that is possibly his optimum trip, although only beaten half-a-length over 10.5f on AW in December; after five months off, not a bad run at Roscommon lately.

Gained her second AW win off 72 in February, but just 1-28 on turf; good fourth of 20 over 1m at the Curragh last time; best form over 7f/1m, and just one inconclusive run over this trip here last year; yet to finish in the first three in five visits to this venue.

Both wins have come right-handed on yielding ground, over 1m3f last year and under a brilliant ride from the champion jockey over 9.5f at Gowran last month; has run well this way round, too; handled quick ground okay when ridden to get 1m4f (upped to this grade) at the Curragh last time; cheekpieces swapped for blinkers.
Veteran front-runner won over 1m4f at Roscommon last year and was second at Fairyhouse in May; all eight wins have been at right-handed tracks; has to be opposed here.

Loves Dundalk and won three in a row there in the spring (10.5f/1m4f); sole turf win came here last summer over 1m1f (off 60) and will be sharper for Roscommon run after nearly three months off; AW mark of 87; turf mark of 78 reflects his good AW form earlier in the year, rather than his actual achievements on grass.

Three Flat wins for this yard, including over 1m6f and 2m; unplaced in five starts on the level since winning over 10.5f on AW in late 2024, but was placed in a maiden hurdle in February; has gone to Galway the last three years, and this is most likely a prep run.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap
Spotlight: Won over 1m at Gowran last summer, and twice in the autumn over 10.5f at Dundalk; return over 1m4f was respectable; slow to stride and weakened tamely over 1m2f at Navan on Saturday; tongue-tie and blinkers worn then replaced by the cheekpieces worn for AW wins; stamina on dam's side of pedigree, but not sure to stay this far.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap
Spotlight: Latest of four wins was over 1m4f three years ago, but he's on a good mark nowadays and came home well when around 3l fifth to Killyclogher Rose at Naas (1m3f); she's a lot less exposed though, and he might struggle to turn around that form.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap
Spotlight: Placed over 1m4f on AW and, after five months off, wasn't stopping when 20-1 winner of first  handicap at Naas (1m3f, good); by a Derby winner and dam (by Dubawi) won over 10.5f; should stay and obvious chance.

Posted an improved effort when runner-up at Ripon (1m, good) last month and went one better at Beverley (8.5f, good to firm; made all) two weeks ago, form that has since been franked by the second; cheekpieces now go on and he should give it a good go from the front.

Well held on her debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) in April but she has taken a small step forward in each of her two starts since; kept on into fourth at Thirsk (7f, good) last month and could be suited by this step up to 1m on her handicap debut.

Won two nurseries at Beverley over 7.5f last August (both on good to firm) but she struggled in a competitive sales race at Doncaster (6.5f, good to soft) in September when last seen; returns off a mark 8lb higher than for that latest success but she can't be dismissed back in a handicap.

Promising third at Lingfield (7f, AW) in March but he was well beaten on his other two outings for Richard Hughes, and he was beaten a long way on his stable/handicap debut at Carlisle (1m1f, good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) last month; dropped 5lb.

RaceName: Sell Your Business With Anderson Barrowcliff Handicap

RaceName: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes

RaceName: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes

RaceName: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden who was runner-up at Gowran Park (1m, good to yielding) in May but below that level in both starts since, including when last of 14 on her yard debut at Beverley (8.5f, good) a month ago.

RaceName: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three-time winner, the most recent in a classified at Newcastle (1m, AW) in February; ran well there three weeks ago and has to be considered returned to this level.

RaceName: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Eight-race maiden who failed to improved for the addition of a tongue-tie (retained) at Ayr (1m, soft) last month; better needed.

Ten-race maiden but he went close at Chepstow (6f, good to soft) on his final start for Adrian Wintle, and ran well at Wetherby (5.5f, good to firm; didn't get the clearest run) last month on his stable debut; this trip will be no issue and he's considered.
Won four times last year, the most recent coming at Catterick off a 9lb higher mark than today's; her last two efforts have been solid and she's an each-way contender.

Won a handicap at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in February and was runner-up there over 5f on his next start; below his best on turf on his last two outings and has a bit to prove on this surface on his first try over 7f.
Yet to win in handicap company but she's been placed on her last two outings, most recently at Carlisle (1m, good) 12 days ago; drops back in trip with each-way claims.
Nine-race maiden but he's been shaping quite well in recent starts, including when fourth of 18 here last time over 6f, doing best of those drawn low; looks worth another try over this longer trip.

Course winner last April when trained by Declan Carroll; runner-up in two of his six starts since joining this stable and shaped as if still in form when sixth of eight at Catterick (7f, good to firm) 24 days ago; can go well if things drop right (usually held up).
Beaten 13l when sixth of 12 on her debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in April and has been well beaten in both starts since (7.5f/7f); makes her handicap debut with better needed.
Lightly-raced 6yo mare who has hinted at ability in two of her three starts (6f/1m; soft/good to firm) but she was still well beaten here two weeks ago; drops back in trip on her handicap debut.

RaceName: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time winner, the most recent coming at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) in June 2024; placed in each of his last four starts, albeit he was below his best last time, and once again has an each-way chance.

RaceName: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap

RaceName: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap

RaceName: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap

RaceName: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won off 10lb higher at Huntingdon (2m3f, good) last May but he's been disappointing since and was beaten 10l back on the Flat (1m6f) two weeks ago; has lots to prove and this is his first run beyond 2m5f.

RaceName: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 5yo who made it 2-7 over hurdles when scoring in a first-time visor at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) last month; that was by a nose but he hit a personal best with that success and is still unexposed at staying trips; respected up 4lb.

RaceName: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Her sole win was over fences in France in January 2024; has dropped a long way in the weights and she's been tailed off in last two runs and is now 0-10 for current yard; opposable.

RaceName: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Pulled up in his final run during winter but that was in the mud and he won by 7l over this trip at Exeter (good to soft) in December; looks interesting on that form and he needs a close look back from five months off.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Useful bumper winner for Ben Brookhouse; still lightly raced and runner-up in both his handicaps, only narrowly failing to justify market support last time here over 2m; only 3lb higher and should stay this far; has been held up in recent races.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Warwick winner in May (2m5f, good) and kept on to go down by only a length over C&D a month ago; solid chance off 2lb higher.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: The last of his four hurdle wins was in late 2023; well beaten in this discipline before pulling up on last week's belated return to fences.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Winning pointer; 0-14 over hurdles but has placed form and interesting that he was sent off the 7-2 favourite when pretty much tailed off here 15 days ago (after three months off); hard to trust on the back of that effort, for all that better was presumably expected.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Exploited much-reduced mark at Southwell (2m4f, good) and it was over 2m7f when not so good at Bangor; this should be more her trip but she is a hard mare to predict.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Out of form in two runs last winter but she is 3-12 over hurdles and realistically handicapped if she can rediscover her form; market could be helpful back from a break.

RaceName: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won four of his first five for Olly Murphy (including a handicap off much higher mark) but he's lost his way badly.

OwnerName: Alain Jathiere, Ecurie David R Layani Famille Et Al

Spotlight: No match for runaway winner at Lingfield last week but finished a long way clear of the rest.; conditions here are fine for her and she's capable of winning of this mark; solid claims. (R21 W2 P12) (OR 55)
Having a third quick run with cheekpieces replacing a visor; should find this company a bit easier than her first two runs and with a positive jockey booking is likely to go close. (R2 W0 P2) (OR 59)
Has looked a work in progress on both starts to date; this looks his easiest task to date as cheekpieces go on for the first time and improvement is likely at some stage.  (R2 W0 P0) (OR 60)
Unplaced twice last season and return here off a mark where improvement is likely; from a late maturing family and should do better this season, market moves should be noted. (R2 W0 P0) (OR 52)

Hasn't really kicked on after her winning here final start as a juvenile; her latest run in Listed company was a step back in the right direction and has to be respected if in the same form. (R11 W1 P7) (OR 52)
Won twice last season and has now returned to her last winning mark; back down to a more suitable grade, at a track she likes better can be expected this time. (R17 W3 P7) (OR 54)

Course winner who can often be slowly away; when in the mood she usually finishes strongly and she stays well; didn't show much on her seasonal debut but might improve for the run; small each way claims in a very open heat. (R23 W3 P5) (OR 37)

Looked in need of the experience on both starts to date; makes her seasonal and handicap debut off a workable mark and is open to lots of improvement for the Champion Trainer; the market will reveal more. (R2 W0 P0) (OR 52)

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Best effort of three came on debut at Cork over this trip on soft ground; below that level twice since, so questions to be answered about her ability to handle this lively surface.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Has been consistent in defeat in maidens over 5f-6f including once over C&D; best effort came at Bellewstown last time and handles a sound surface well, so is a major player on nursery bow.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: All three runs over this trip came within the space of three weeks; best effort came on debut at Naas on good ground; has a shout if resuming progress on nursery debut.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Soundly beaten in three maidens under varying ground conditions; gelded since last run at Naas, which was his best effort; needs to improve, even tackling nurseries now, but not ruled out.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Was poor on first two maiden starts but much-improved when third over C&D on soft last time; was nearly 2l in front of Bit Of A Buzz that day but the latter is better suited to drier ground; a major player.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden after 14 runs but some fine efforts in defeat, all over this trip; solid effort again at Bellewstown last time in first-time cheekpieces (retained), just behind Bye Bye Now; a player but needs more.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Some promise in maidens; best handicap run came last time at Bellewstown over this trip when ran on from the rear; hasn't much to find with Bye Bye Now on that run; added visor could help.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden hasn't built on early promise, but some good runs all the same between turf and AW; third in a big field at the Curragh two starts ago, but a lesser effort on soft over 7f here since; can do better.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Not beaten far a couple of times in maidens, but didn't progress in AW handicaps over the winter; has to return to best on stable debut after a break.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden after 32 starts has been mostly running well this season, but getting bumped up in the handicap for being placed isn't helping matters; likely to run well again.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner in 2023 won for the second time in a 6f Fairyhouse claimer in May; raised 19lb for that win but has been solid in defeat since including over C&D; got no run at Fairyhouse last time; a player.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Got off the mark over this trip at Dundalk in March and a solid fourth back there next time; put in a cracking effort from the front on turf debut at Bellewstown behind an in-form rival; up 3lb but can improve from that; big player.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Regressive maiden but ran a cracker over this trip at Naas before a lesser run over 6.5f at Limerick since; cheekpieces retained; back to 5f will suit but needs more.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Showed improved form lately, winning over 6f at Fairyhouse but a lesser effort at Limerick over 6.5f since; should have the speed for this trip, but a few other front-runners in this field too.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden raced mostly on AW for Natalia Lupini and some solid runs up to 1m; the best of two runs for this yard when fourth over C&D on soft a month ago; a player if as effective on this faster ground.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: The best of three maiden runs last year came over C&D; lacks experience for a race of this nature, but yard does well with sprinters and could go well on return.
A Eur500,000 yearling; started a short-priced favourite on debut at Navan over 6f but never landed a blow; marginal improvement upped to 7f at Leopardstown since; has to do more today.

Both starts came at Roscommon over a similar trip to this; not beaten far on debut, but produced a lesser effort last time; seems to be the yard's second-string, but can be involved if resuming progress.

Promise on debut at the Curragh over 6f behind a smart winner; a lesser run at Listowel since; the step up in trip should suit on breeding and looks to be the yard's first-string, but has to resume progress.

Promise on debut at Leopardstown over 7f (soft) and built on that over a mile at Bellewstown on good ground; cheekpieces are added today and can be a major player,  though the drop in trip is a concern.
Similar efforts in 6f maidens at Cork and Navan the last twice; has to do more up in trip and mixed messages about stamina in pedigree.
Beaten a long way in two maidens and will be better off in nurseries after this; visor added.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: Ghaiyyath colt from a talented Juddmonte family; 18s for quick-ground 1m2f Curragh maiden on Derby weekend, showed ability when beaten 5l by winner who now sits on a mark of 88; spoilt his chance significantly by hanging left up the straight; form of that run yet to be tested.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Ran well in red-hot 1m maiden at Naas on her return; again stable second-string (20-1) when running much the same race over same C&D last month; dam 1m2f Listed winner, sister to Irish Derby winner Latrobe, so Dubawi filly is bred to get this trip, although the visual evidence from her two runs this year is inconclusive in that regard.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: River Boyne gelding from good family; 66s, sixth to Irish 2,000 Guineas also-ran Bamako Beach over 7f at Fairyhouse, but he was beaten miles.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: Front-running third over 1m2f at Leopardstown; weakened over 1m4f on testing ground at Cork; third over C&D last month and the second easily went one better at Killarney on Monday; has only run on yielding or worse; headgear.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: Dandy Man 4yo is brother to Italian 6f-7.5f winner; cost 7,000 euros as a yearling; dam 6f winner, out of US 7f/1m winning half-sister to US 1m Grade 2 winner Habaya; respected yard, but best watched unless money arrives.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: Well beaten both starts; will be in handicaps after this.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
Spotlight: Nice Jim Bolger pedigree but showed nothing in 1m4f maiden on debut; tongue-tie discarded.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Five wins, two of them on turf, including 25-1 success over extended 1m6f at Bellewstown earlier this month; needed every yard that day, and his previous win was over 2m; got an 8lb rise, which is likely to prevent a follow-up; placed once in seven previous runs here.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Bit of promise over hurdles last year for Mags Mullins; made all to beat 18 rivals over this trip on good ground at Leopardstown; little wrong with stable debut third over 1m4f at Bellewstown (second touched off since); 2lb wrong matters little and front-runner is a player.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
