Spotlight: Consistent on AW at three, winning over 1m4f; had some good hurdling form, without winning, in 2024; just one run over flights last year; ran well in a charity race at the Curragh on Derby weekend; has to enter calculations in such a weak contest.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Trainer's four-timer last weekend makes this 1m1f winner of interest; narrowly beaten over 1m3f here in September, too, and some decent runs hurdling during the winter; nice run over 1m at Leopardstown but unplaced at Navan since; tongue-tie left off; doubt she wants it too fast.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: AW winner over 10.5f in March and her higher-grade third at Naas was a good effort; 1m4f has seemed a bridge too far, though, and long way behind Masego over that trip at Bellewstown; excuse for latest run (1m2f) at Navan.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Placed at two and went close to making all in 1m4f Leopardstown handicap last year, only beaten half-a-length; left Natalia Lupini after; tailed off on stable debut last month.

RaceName: GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Runner-up in soft-ground 1m4f handicap at Doncaster at three for Charlie Johnston; lightly raced for this yard; okay run over hurdles last year; out the back in 1m2f Roscommon handicap when last seen.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies & Mares Handicap
Spotlight: Has shown improved form lately when winning twice at this track over extended 1m2f, a maiden on good ground and a 3yo handicap on soft; raised 13lb for latter success, but still has to be taken seriously; should stay this trip.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies & Mares Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins apiece on turf and AW up to 1m4f; best turf effort this term when second at Gowran last month; not as good over 1m2f twice since; stepping back up to this trip will suit and cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies & Mares Handicap
Spotlight: The last of her three wins came at Ballinrobe off 14lb higher nearly two years ago; has been regressive in the last year and needs to do more, even off a falling mark

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies & Mares Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs Tracey O'Hare & D W Sloan & William Jones
Spotlight: Sole win came here in last year's Ulster Cesarewitch over 2m2f; a fine effort over this trip back here next time; however, has been well below her best in three runs this term; has to rebound; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies & Mares Handicap
Spotlight: Won a 1m4f maiden at Bellewstown last August on second start; first two runs this season were solid, but was poor at Ballinrobe last time; only dropped 1lb and needs more, but cheekpieces might help.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
OwnerName: Anthony Head & Stephen E McCarthy & Mrs Paul Shanahan
Spotlight: No worries about the trip for this stoutly-bred filly; best of three handicap runs was front-running fourth over 1m4f at Cork in April; winner has gone in again twice and third won maiden next time; was given a break after Roscommon fifth in May.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Flopped when 3-1 for seasonal/handicap debut at Sligo in May; it was probably soft ground, rather than this trip, which proved his undoing because (having been gelded and given a break) he ran much better over 1m3f at Killarney on Monday; looked slow but kept plugging away, and gets another change of headgear now.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Quiet in maidens and unable to land a blow when 50s for 1m4f handicap at Limerick; still early days for Snellen's half-brother; dam was 1m4f winner and is half-sister to dam of King George winner Novellist, so no surprise they're giving him another go over a trip.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Showed ability in a Galway maiden last year when with Mick Mulvany; well backed into joint-favouritism for return at Fairyhouse, but didn't feature; off the bridle 3f out when okay fifth here over 10.5f (soft); had a wide trip from a bad draw when fourth over 1m3f at Naas and reckon he's on a good mark now; not bred to stay, but might.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Twice made the frame in soft-ground 7f Gowran handicaps in the spring; finished well when fourth against older horses over 1m1f on fast ground at Leopardstown, but bombed over 1m3f at Naas last time; yet to string two good runs together and trip is a big question mark.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Well-bred son of Frankel; couple of respectable maiden runs; only 15-2 for handicap debut over 1m4f at Limerick, a race won easily by stablemate and favourite; dropped out from a bad draw and couldn't go on after making a bit of headway early in the straight; blinkers.

RaceName: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap
Spotlight: Had fair AW form in headgear for Charlie Johnston during the winter, winning over 1m2f and runner-up over 1m4f; better on third Irish start when fourth against older rivals at Fairyhouse (1m2f); starting to stay on from rear when carried wide on the home bend at Ballinrobe; stepping back up in trip might help and can lead.

RaceName: Joe Mac's Big Retirement Bash Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ex-Irish 4yo who got off the mark at the ninth attempt at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago, prevailing by 3l on his second stable start; kept on for close third over 1m3f on his stable debut and there can be optimism that 1m4f will be within range; strong claims up 7lb for last time.

RaceName: Joe Mac's Big Retirement Bash Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: David Kilburn, Mrs Corbett, Chris Wright
Spotlight: She remains 5lb higher than for her last win last August but that's because she's been admirably consistent in defeat this year; runner-up at York (1m4f, good to firm) last Friday and she can be bang there.

RaceName: Joe Mac's Big Retirement Bash Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Course winner (1m5f, good) who went very close at Ripon (1m4f, good) last month; she was last of five here (1m5f, good) last Saturday but was beaten just under 2l having led at a steady pace, and she's not ruled out.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: £95,000 breeze-up buy who finished among some pricey recruits when runner-up at 9-1 on recent debut at Nottingham (6f, good to firm); that was a promising start and there is every chance that she'll progress; key player.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: 75,000gns breeze-up buy who was sent off the 4-9 favourite when a head second of four on debut at Ayr (6f, good) 12 days ago; Trumpety Trump was half a length behind and is 5lb better off today, but this fellow is open to improvement for his top yard and could play a leading role.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Backed into 11-4 when keeping on for clear second on debut at Beverley (5f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; shaped as though the step up to 6f could be a positive move and he's firmly in calculations.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: £28,000 breeze-up buy who was a close third of four at 33-1 on recent debut at Ayr (6f, good); he's 5lb better off with the runner-up Instant Force and his trainer isn't known for first-time-out 2yo winners, so it was a very encouraging start to his career and he could have lots more to offer.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Failed to beat a rival last month on her first two starts (6f/5f, soft/good to firm), when 20-1 then 50-1; she would be a shock winner today.

Kept on well to win at Beverley (5f, good to soft) in May on second start and returned from a break with good second at 50-1 on stable debut at York (6f, good to firm) last Saturday; leading claims off the same mark.

Improved upon her first two runs (5f, good to soft/good) when winning a five-runner maiden at Ffos Las (5f, soft) last month in first-time cheekpieces (retained) and she did it in good style; second of three in a 5f nursery here yesterday; the step up to 6f seems a likely plus; respected.

Took a step forward with 4l third of six at Ayr (6f, soft) on her second start and similar form when sixth of 11, beaten about 3l, at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; not obviously well treated off his opening mark but his pedigree provides optimism that he'll improve.

Showed improved form when getting off the mark at the fourth attempt at Pontefract (6f, good) last month; unsuited by the step up to 7.4f at Beverley since and she could play a leading role back down in trip with a tongue-tie added on nursery debut.

Promising second when 33-1 on debut at Southwell (5f, AW) in April and a market check is advised on this first nursery start, but two lesser runs have followed (5f, good to firm/good) and she needs to get back on track.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
Spotlight: 8yo who can be in and out but he won at Leicester (6f, good to firm) in April and has run well in defeat on his last two starts, at Epsom (6f, soft) and Newcastle (6f, AW); he was a close second of 14 last time and this C&D winner can be in the mix if he's once more on a going day.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
Spotlight: Unraced on turf this year and his best form has come on AW; however, he has a lower mark on grass and was third in a Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) last August; capable of playing a leading role.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
OwnerName: B Jordan, Brian Jordan, S Jordan & N McConnell
Spotlight: 10yo who is winless since August 2024 and needs to improve upon his last few performances; however, he's a nine-time course winner, including this race in 2024, and his reduced mark appeals on form as recent as this May; not discounted.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
Spotlight: Got up in the final strides over 5f here (good to firm) three weeks ago on his fourth start for this yard; he could have more to offer for this stable, especially back up in trip with his Irish wins having come at 7.5f/7f; respected up 4lb for last time.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
Spotlight: Having dropped down the weights he was a close second at Ascot (6f, good) in May on his stable/seasonal debut, and perhaps the soft ground didn't suit at Epsom last time; not written off but this 8yo has been regressive and remains without a win since June 2023.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
Spotlight: Reappeared with a win at Catterick (6f, good) in April and then made all at Epsom (6f, good) this month; his stable is a dab hand when it comes to older horses progressing through the ranks and, with the Epsom form having been franked, a 3lb rise could prove lenient for this thriving 5yo.

RaceName: Jordan Electrics Scottish Stewards' Cup Handicap
OwnerName: Doug Graham, Ian Davison, Alan Drysdale
Spotlight: 9yo whose last win was in September 2023 and it's possible that he'll need this first outing since February; however, he won this in 2021 and showed spark when twice finishing second in Bahrain this January (6f, good/good to firm); not ruled out.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Built upon the promise of his sole 2yo run to win Leicester maiden (1m2f, good to firm) on reappearance, and he followed up in a small-field novice at Newmarket (1m2f, good) last month; today is a much tougher test of his credentials but this blue-blooded colt may well be up to the task.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Two-time AW novice winner (1m/1m4f) who was runner-up in the Lingfield Oaks Trial (11.6f, good to firm) before respectable fifth of 15 in the Italian Oaks (10.5f, good); the Lingfield form hasn't worked out but she's nevertheless a leading contender today.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Made it two wins from her four starts when easily winning a Class 3 handicap here (1m1f, good) in May; stamina to prove today and she was only fifth in a Listed race at Goodwood (1m2f, soft) last time, but the ground may not have suited and she remains one to be interested in, especially back here.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won Redcar novice (1m2f, good to firm) in April on reappearance before respectable third of five in Group 3 Chester Vase (1m4f, good), behind subsequent Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini; early interference when down the field at Royal Ascot and could have a part to play back down in grade.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Won three handicaps in a row in May/June (1m2f/10.3f, good/soft); down the field in Royal Ascot handicap next time and same story there last Friday, so she needs to turn things around, but she's not discounted in view of her previous promise.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Five unsuccessful starts for Joseph O'Brien, finishing second in a couple of 2yo maidens; changed hands for 2,500gns this month and she would be a surprise winner on her stable debut, for which a hood is applied.

RaceName: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap
Spotlight: 6yo who has enjoyed a renaissance in 2026, winning twice (5f, AW/good) and posting a close second at Ripon (5f, good) latest; there remains mileage in his mark judged on old form and this course winner is respected.

RaceName: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap
Spotlight: She's been running well in the main this season and has finished second at Ayr (5f, good/good to firm) on her two starts this month; she's won over C&D and there's every chance that she'll be bang there.

RaceName: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap
Spotlight: Returned to form when making all in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) in a selling handicap over C&D (good to firm) last month; lost a shoe when down the field at Ayr (5f, good to firm) on Monday but this is a hotter race than the one he won here two starts ago and others are more compelling.

RaceName: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap
Spotlight: Made all twice in a row this spring (including over C&D on good to firm) and bounced back from his third of six at Yarmouth for another front-running win at Lingfield (5f, AW) last Monday; had plenty in hand last time and he's 5lb well in under a 5lb penalty; could prove tough to catch.

RaceName: Hamilton Park Celebrates 100 Years Of Racing Handicap
Spotlight: 3yo who won at Newcastle (5f, AW) in January on his second stable start but slim pickings across his three runs since; upset in stalls and withdrawn at Musselburgh in June (33-1 at the time); wears a first-time hood.

RaceName: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 3yo who has finished second or third on all six starts, most recently runner-up at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) 11 days ago in first-time blinkers (retained); she'll be fine back on turf and can again be in the shake-up.

RaceName: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Ayr (1m, good to firm) in May and she's twice gone close here since, over C&D and at 1m3f; features prominently in calculations.

RaceName: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Six wins last September-December (including C&D) and she's gone very close to adding to that tally on her last two outings, beaten just a neck over C&D (good) last Saturday despite being badly hampered; lots to like.

RaceName: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Encouraging debut for Jessica Harrington at Punchestown (1m, good to yielding) last September; however, her form went the wrong way across her next three starts and she was sold for 2,200gns last month; needs to turn things around on her stable debut.

RaceName: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 80-1 winner here (1m1f, good to firm) in May on her reappearance and second start; tailed off on handicap debut at Redcar (1m2f, good) since and needs to prove her course win was no fluke, but she's not written off.
110,000euros yearling; two good placed efforts in Flat maidens this season; her Flat rating of 74 is one of the best in this field for her hurdling debut.

Beat very few rivals in three Flat maidens last year; modest sixth of 14 on Flat handicap debut at Gowran last time; hails from a yard that means he can't be ruled out despite a Flat rating of 45; hood goes on for hurdling debut
Surprise winner (20-1) on his seventh Flat start at Bellewstown last time (1m4f, good); that brings him up to a rating of 63, which still leaves him with a bit to find with a few of these.
Rated 51 on the Flat after seven runs with little success; mid-field here over 1m4f on Monday; Misty Cove is the more appealing of yard's two runners.

Couple of okay AW runs over the winter before making a winning turf/handicap debut in May (1m3f, yielding to soft), runner-up has won since; slight concern how poor she was at Down Royal when last seen (beaten 21l); however, her Flat rating of 74 gives her a big shout here on hurdling bow.

Placed twice in Roscommon maidens last year and again twice on AW earlier this year; claimed for 5,000euros after disappointing in a Ballinrobe claimer in May; not too bad in a Down Royal maiden last time; rated 63 on Flat and not discounted.

One of only three in the field with hurdling experience and he has finished well ahead of the other two; the 85,000euros yearling lost third late on at Limerick (2m1f, good), but it was a positive first-ever run and there is likely improvement to come.
No wins from 12 Flat starts and rated 48 in that sphere; 18l behind Words Unspoken at Limerick on hurdling debut.
Ran poorly on sole Flat start and was pulled up on his first run over hurdles at Limerick, jumping lacking fluency; unlikely.
Best of eight Flat runs came in a 1m3f handicap here in May (good) when a close third; below that level twice since; rated 62 on Flat, so may get involved on hurdling/stable debut.
Basement rating of 37 on Flat following nine unplaced runs; others preferred.
Beaten out of sight in sole Flat maiden; didn't look a natural jumper when unseating at the second on hurdling debut at Limerick (150-1).

Off the mark in bumpers last month at Sligo (2m2f, good), having previously only just been denied in a 3-finisher 3m Kilbeggan novice hurdle; yard in flying form this week, one to consider although this looks a tougher test.

Nice bit of improvement on third maiden hurdle outing, left in second at the last to chase home an odds-on shot over 2m4f at Limerick in late May (yielding); definite contender if seeing out this longer trip.

OwnerName: Mrs Paul Shanahan & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Sister to 134-rated hurdler Dream On Baby showed potential in two bumpers last season and much better effort on hurdles debut when returning last month, effort just flattening out from last when third in 2m Listowel mares maiden; 1.25l to find with Fraher Field, but now gets 7lb from that rival and bred to relish this longer trip.
Slowly improving, fair fifth over C&D in May and later in month stayed on late to chase home a hot favourite at Tramore; tongue-tie now added to hood; more likely needed to play a major role.

Debut Galway festival bumper winner last season before running solid races for third in three subsequent Listed bumpers without showing much progress; last month's hurdles debut in 2m6f Punchestown mares maiden was tame; surely capable of better, although stamina a possible issue.

OwnerName: John J Flynn, Pierce Flynn, Conor Lannen
Spotlight: Wexford bumper winner last summer and easily pick of three attempts hurdling when second to an odds-on shot in 2m Listowel mares maiden last month (yielding); later in month just okay effort in Leopardstown amateur flat maiden on fast ground; probably prefers easier ground and could struggle to confirm Listowel form with Tumbling In on these terms.
Limited level of ability hurdling in 2024 and more recent point-to-point form doesn't inspire confidence.
Huge odds and well beaten in all five starts; hard to make a case for on form.

HorseName: Uno Me I Like My T right
Spotlight: Poor overall form including in three maiden hurdles; tongue-tie tried.
Soundly beaten in maidens at Kilbeggan and Bellewstown; best watched for now.
Not much promise in three point-to-to-points and well held on last month's bumper debut; easily passed over now switched to hurdles.
Moderate bumper form and two maiden hurdle runs no better.
Tailed off in both bumpers in the spring; 4yo can only be watched now switched to hurdles.
Order Of St George filly is first foal of a modest half-sister to winners Early Morning Rain (bumper and 2m/2m1f hurdle), Rosa Damascena (1m2f) and Matavia Bay (1m2f); debutante best watched.
Huge price when showing mild promise with a recent fourth placing at Downpatrick but unable to build on that at Limerick since; upped in trip and lots more needed.
Dual chase winner who is rated lower over hurdles, making all over 2m7f at Clonmel in April and fair fourth here following month (2m4f); return to longer trip to suit and yard going well.
First reserve; three hurdle wins have been at Limerick but also won 2m5f handicap chase here last summer; absent since pulled up over fences at Limerick's Christmas meeting so may need this.
Dual winner over both hurdles and fences on decent ground; two recent runs leave her with a fair bit to find and cheekpieces now tried.

Two hurdle wins came over shorter trips and off the mark chasing in 2m5f Kilbeggan handicap in May, following that up with good third in competitive 2m4f handicap at same track; clearly in good order and could go well here off 8lb lower hurdles mark.

Limerick maiden winner last year (2m1f, good) and finished good third in the Lartigue at Listowel; easily best run since and just beginning his challenge (going well) when unseating two out here in May in race won by Burru over 2m4f; poor Listowel run later in month and has had a break since (upped in trip).
Both hurdle wins have been at around 2m on soft ground; tame enough Listowel effort last month at similar trip, now takes a marked step up in distance and others look more likely.

Capable handicap hurdler back in the day (won here in 2022 over 2m4f); series of absences in recent years, most recently good run in the circumstances when hampered by loose horse in finishing fourth in 2m4f Ballinrobe handicap chase in May; first run over hurdles in three years (11lb lower here).

Three-time winner for Mark Fahey in 2023, including over this trip at Galway off today's mark; some lengthy absences since, most recently encouraging comeback run at Ballinrobe in late May when staying-on third (Jacovec Cavern second) over this trip (good) in first-time cheekpieces; entitled to improve for that and has 4l to find with Jacovec Cavern.

Four-time winner over hurdles in Britain with Jamie Snowden at up to 2m5f, also a dual winner over fences; well beaten in Pertemps Final and pulled up (lost right shoe) at Haydock in April final start before bought for 18,000GBP following month; interesting to see if new yard can spark a revival, ground to suit.

Two-time winner over hurdles, including 2m4f novice here in 2024; not so effective a chaser, most recently dropping away tamely after forcing much of pace in 2m5f Kilbeggan handicap in May; blinkers now replace cheekpieces on hurdles return with a bit to prove.

Three hurdle wins in second half of 2024 haven't been added to, including in a stint chasing; most recently creditable fourth in 2m5f Kilbeggan handicap in May; back hurdling and ideally wants softer ground.

In fine form, winning over 2m4f at Punchestown festival and good efforts off much higher marks since, chasing home an 8l winner over this trip at Ballinrobe and not quite getting home over 3m1f when third at Kilbeggan last month; trip/ground okay and should go well again.
Both hurdle wins came at Cork on good ground last year; 0-4 chasing this year, just headed when unseating two out at Limerick last time; reverts to hurdles with trip/ground to suit.
Sligo maiden hurdle winner last year (2m2f, good) but needs to improve a fair bit on both recent handicap efforts; steps up in trip; due to run here yesterday.

Got up late to win a 2m Kilbeggan maiden hurdle in September 2024 (good-to-yielding) but hasn't been seen since; very much an unknown quantity on handicap debut after such an absence and market probably best guide.

OwnerName: J T O'Connor & M P Gleeson & P M Fortune & A McGonigle
Spotlight: Winner of a 2m2f Cork novice event on good ground in May, not so good in Wexford conditions event later same month; seemingly has a bit to do back in handicap company off this sort of mark.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Bumper and hurdles winner for Willie Mullins in 2023-24; didn't add to her tally for Paul Kiely last year, but back to form on both recent starts for current yard in 2m handicap chases on good ground, winning at Tramore and chasing home clear winner Mic Drop off 6lb higher at Wexford; more needed to reverse that form.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Much better chaser than hurdler, three wins include handicaps at Punchestown and Cork in 2024; long losing run since, but has shown himself in good heart on the Flat of late.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: In the form of his life and seeking a hat-trick, following wins at Limerick and when beating Femme Magnifique decisively at Wexford last month (good); 2lb wrong here, but talented rider's claim offsets that; big player again, although may need to jump better now raised in class.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Seven career wins capped by 2m1f Listed handicap chase win at Fairyhouse last November; recent Kilbeggan runs over longer trips well below best, but yard has returned to form so could improve for this drop in trip, although yard have a more obvious contender in Gaelic Arc.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Two chase wins came in 2024 but some good runs in competitive handicaps last season, notably Grand Annual fifth and decent fourth in Red Rum at Aintree; down in grade with conditions to suit, so big player.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Mark Devlin & Philip Smith & Nigel O'Hare & P J Rothwell
Spotlight: Veteran's most recent win came in this race last year off 2lb lower; rediscovered form in the spring in 2m4f veterans' handicaps, finishing fine third at Haydock and good second (having hit last) at Ballinrobe; has to be considered.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 0-7 since winning on chase debut early last year but has faced some tough tasks in competitive handicaps, notably good third over 2m1f at Ascot in November; not much luck in running when midfield in Grand Annual in March and has had a break since; drops in class here, so has to be respected.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Mark R D Fleming / T Westropp Bennett
Spotlight: Won this in 2024 off 1lb higher mark and timely return to form last month under forcing tactics, winning over 2m at Punchestown and only denied by a neck off 5lb higher over 2m4f at Kilbeggan; up another 3lb but likely big player again.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdles winner has been placed only twice in 12 chase starts, notably beaten a neck in 2m2f Limerick novice at Christmas on testing ground; pulled up in first-time cheekpieces (now discarded) on Kilbeggan comeback in late May and questions to answer now, especially on this quicker ground.

Top-rated of these over hurdles (133), winning four from ten; trounced his four rivals on chasing debut at Limerick in May (2m4f, good to yielding), jumping fluently and travelling strongly; that was a very promising first run over fences and he can make it back-to-back wins despite dropping back in trip.

Improved form lately in easily winning a Downpatrick maiden hurdle before adding a Tramore beginners' chase (2m, good), keeping on well; his chase win was the least impressive of the three last-time winners, but not ruled out given his good form.

Won his second hurdles start at Limerick in November (2m, heavy) and placed a couple of times since then; beaten 23l off 105 at Roscommon last time on chase debut (2m1f, yielding to soft); others make more appeal.

Won back-to-back hurdle races in August/September on good ground; creditable fourth at this track in May (2m1f, good) but below that at Listowel last time; makes chasing debut, but has a lot to find with a few of these.

Won back-to-back handicaps at Cork (2m1f, good) and Tipperary (2m, good to yielding) in August/October; hasn't hit the same heights in three runs since, beaten 16.5l at this track last time (2m1f, good to yielding); unplaced in three points so this switch to chasing may not bring the required improvement.
1-11 over hurdles having won a Downpatrick handicap off 86 in August (2m2f, good); made a bad mistake when tailed off on chasing bow at Wexford last time (2m4f, good); others preferred.

1-5 over hurdles and rated 121; unseated at the third on chase debut at Leopardstown in March; made amends when comfortably winning at Ballinrobe last time (2m1f, good); that run gives him a shot here.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Running for the 45th time when opening her account over hurdles at Kilbeggan (3m1f, good to yielding, 100-30 fav) last month; couldn't follow up back there next time (3m1f, good, 12-1) off 5lb higher; regular 7lb claimer has been replaced for this return to fences (0-9), but her overall profile is unappealing.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Belatedly off the mark in point-to-points in May after 14 attempts; no impact in a handicap chase or hurdle race since then.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Sole career win came at Listowel over hurdles in September (2m6f, good to yielding); okay chase debut in a handicap here (2m5f, good to yielding) in May and improved on that when beaten just half a length back at Listowel last time in a beginners' (2m3f, yielding); this trip looks more suitable and she's in the mix.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Maiden in all spheres after 33 starts, but was second at Downpatrick on penultimate (3m, good), 0.5l behind Fr Gilligansvoyge; sent off favourite up in grade at Wexford last time (2m7f, good), but was a modest third; in the mix on his Downpatrick run, but his record is a concern.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Dual winning pointer but his form under rules isn't compelling; pulled up in a handicap chase at Roscommon last time.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Shed his maiden tag at Wexford last time when winning a 3m handicap hurdle off 87 (good to yielding); that was his first try at a 3m trip and he won going away; didn't disgrace himself in his two beginners' chase runs last season; shortlisted.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Modest strike-rate of 3-40 over fences, although one of his wins came here; latest success was in August 2024 at Kilbeggan; showed more promise returned to there last time (2m5f, yielding) when a distant third of 11; he's now 19lb below his last winning mark, but must build on his last run.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Better hurdler than a chaser, and her last three runs over fences do nothing to dispute that; pulled up at Roscommon on her return.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Dual hurdles winner won a Tramore beginners' chase in 2024, but is yet to win a handicap; must improve on recent form.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Doubled his tally over fences when winning this race last year off 8lb lower (yielding to soft) under O'Keeffe; has run just once since then, on seasonal return at Punchestown when an okay eighth of 18 in a 2m handicap hurdle (good to yielding); cheekpieces go on now and he has won on good; interesting.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
Spotlight: Some fair placed form in maiden hurdles last year on good; no impact in a pair of beginners' chases at Kilbeggan recently; cheekpieces need to get more from him on his handicap chase debut.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div I)
OwnerName: John P Coleman & M J Caffrey
Spotlight: No wins from 11 attempts over hurdles; one of his better efforts came in first-time cheekpieces at Kilbeggan last time when an 8.25l sixth; that headgear is retained for his chasing bow, but fences need to get more from him.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Modest strike rate of 1-21 over fences; took the runner-up spot on consecutive occasions at Limerick and Tramore in April/May, both over 2m6f on good; lesser run back at Tramore when last seen over fences (2m6f, good); poor effort back over hurdles at Limerick earlier this month.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
OwnerName: Aiden Larkin & John Larkin & Paudie Dowling & Kenneth Fox
Spotlight: Underwhelming in opening two chase starts before taking a big step forward at Roscommon (2m6f, yielding to soft) to shed his maiden tag convincingly off 90 under today's rider following the reapplication of blinkers; a repeat of that will see him go very close, but overall form suggests that is not a sure thing.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Won a Punchestown handicap hurdle in May (3m, good) off 84 and placed twice since then; made a positive chase debut at Wexford (2m4f, yielding) in April when third off this mark, but pulled up at Tramore next time after making a bad mistake; could go well.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: 0-14 in all spheres; has tended to give his best at Downpatrick and was an okay 10.5l fifth of 14 on his handicap chase debut there last time (2m4f, good); needs more.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Maiden was placed in a couple of handicap hurdles for Henrietta Knight last year; poor form in opening three chase runs for this yard and return to hurdles last time didn't help.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Has struggled in handicap chases and recent pointing exploits do not bode well.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Has run poorly since returning from a huge absence last winter; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Point winner and won a Clonmel handicap hurdle in 2024 (2m4f, good); not a lot to recommend him in three runs this season.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Won a pair of chases for Charles Byrnes, the latest of them over three years ago; not shown much in hunter chases for this yard and weakened when tried in blinkers in a handicap last time.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Just 1-21 over hurdles; posted a decent effort on his second chase start at Tramore in May when running on well to take fourth of ten (2m6f, good); others preferred.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Winner of a Sligo maiden hurdle in May last year (2m4f, good); beat precious few rivals in four beginners' chases to date; pulled up at Tramore when badly hampered at the first last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: 0-20 at the age of nine, but broke a poor run of form back from a break when runner-up over 3m at Bellewstown in April (yielding); pulled up next time and was beaten 24l on his chasing debut at Downpatrick in a beginners' last time; others make more appeal.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Winning point-to-pointer got off the mark under rules in a 2m5f Sligo beginners' chase in October (good to yielding) for Gordon Elliott; failed to build on that in three runs afterwards and no sign of a revival over hurdles at Limerick on his stable debut.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Never a factor in seven hurdle starts; narrow winner of a Ballysteen point-to-point in April; pulled up on handicap chase debut at Limerick, hanging left; an unlikely winner.

RaceName: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Chase (Div II)
Spotlight: Point winner easily won a Tipperary hunter chase in May last year; has been hit or miss since, but one of his better efforts came at Downpatrick last month when taking third (3m, good), making a mistake at two out; way below that level over hurdles at Limerick last time; return to fences should help.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Looked raw on both runs over the winter, plenty green in Cork bumper and too keen when remote fourth in Limerick mares maiden hurdle; tongue-tied now fitted and encounters much quicker ground.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Signs of ability in point-to-points and on bumper debut last month at Listowel (hooded) over 2m4f (yielding); more needed.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Getaway half-sister to winners Rioga Choice (useful 2m hurdle), Its Gonnahappen (2m hurdle) and Special John (3m/3m2f chase); dam 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner; never sighted on Limerick debut in late March on soft; better ground may suit, but can only be watched.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Jukebox Jury mare is sister to bumper/2m2f hurdle winner Korinthia; dam bumper winner, sister to bumper/2m4f hurdle winners Baker's Bridge and Backtothekingsnest; top trainer/rider combination and yard have won three of last four renewals, so demands utmost respect.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Footstepsinthesand sister to bumper winner Walk On The Beach; dam unraced sister to useful 2m4f hurdler/chaser Go All The Way; justified favouritism on debut in Limerick mares' bumper in late May (soft), asserting late on despite taking a hold early on; interesting prospect, quicker ground to contend with here.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Mount Nelson mare cost 4,000euros as a 3yo; half-sister to 2m3f chase winner Opechee; dam placed 2m/2m2f hurdles, half-sister to useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner Sobers; newcomer likely best watched.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Reappeared last month and much improved from debut run for a previous yard in finishing second at Downpatrick; better again to win Roscommon ladies contest early this month under a positive ride (good); can continue progressing.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Flat-bred daughter of Free Eagle showed nice bit of improvement on second start when runner-up at Kilbeggan last month (good-to-yielding); didn't run to same level at Wexford, though, hanging left in straight; more needed.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Mild promise in two point-to-points in the spring for William Codd; debuts for new yard and worth a market check.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Sholokhov filly cost 7,500euros as a foal; third foal; dam unraced half-sister to high-class bumper and 2m4f-3m hurdle/chase winner No More Heroes, family high-class jumpers Celestial Gold and Fiveforthree; debutante worth a market check.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Belardo mare cost 3,000euros as a foal; half-sister to winners Female Approach (11.4f/1m4f) and New Star (Qatari 7.5f-1m2f); dam placed 7f 2yo; unlikely type to make an immediate impact.

RaceName: Christy Lucey Transport Mares Finale (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Jet Away half-sister to winners Exciting Oscar (3m hurdle) and Chasing Unicorn (bumper); dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m-3m hurdle winner Kilfenora; another newcomer likely best watched, unless market speaks.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Market mover prior to his debut at Thirsk (7f, good) in May, a race where he shaped nicely; he will need a good step forward to come out on top here though.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in novice events at Nottingham (6f, good) and Sandown (7f, good) either side of his midfield finish in the Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot; sets the standard and should win races but this could be warm.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Second run was more promising than his debut but it would still be surprising if there weren't a few stronger in today's field; stable run three in the race.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Clear signs of ability in novice events here (6.5f, good to soft) and Lingfield (7f, AW) this summer; that form will likely need bettering if he is to get off the mark in this field; Richard Hannon runs three here.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Seventh foal; brother to 6f/7f 2yo winner Shadow Of Light (including 2yo Group 1; RPR 119), closely related to 5.5f-7f winner Earthlight (including 2yo Group 1; 119), half-brother to two winners including Wild Desert (7f 2yo; 105); dam Group-placed 7f 2yo winner (109); looks the part on paper and stable's 2yos operating at a fine strike-rate.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; half-brother to 1m 2yo/9.4f AW winner Crockham Heath (RPR 85); dam French Listed-placed 1m winner (85), half-sister to winners All Rumours (1m2f Listed) and Trachonitus (1m 2yo); Andrew Balding has won this with subsequent Dewhurst winners Gewan (on debut) and Chaldean (second time out) in recent seasons; of obvious interest.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 27,000euros foal, 28,000euros yearling; third foal; half-brother to winners Akvarel (Polish 5f-1m including 2yo) and Argon Flash (Italian 7f/7.5f); dam made frame 10.5f-12.5f in France, half-sister to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Coral Beach; stable house an exciting 2yo prospect, who made a winning debut, so worth a market check.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Met all sorts of trouble when sixth on his debut at Nottingham (6f, good; Ciilician second); hot favourite for a 6f Kempton maiden 18 days ago on the strength of it but he could only manage fourth; still has time on his side but Oisin Murphy rides stablemate Arthurian.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 85,000euros yearling; fourth foal; brother to 7f 2yo winner Major Neigh Sayer (RPR 86); dam placed 1m2f-1m4f (79), half-sister to 6f/7f 2yo Group 1 winner Dabirsim; should have a future but this looks a tough starting point.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Teme Valley, C Rosier & Mrs J Rosier
Spotlight: 30,000euros yearling, 80,000euros breeze-up 2yo; third foal; dam Listed-placed 7f 2yo winner (RPR 99), half-sister to winners Ocean Tempest (1m Listed) and Mohawk Ridge (1m-2m); one to note for market confidence.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Won a 6f maiden at Brighton (good to firm) on debut in May; well-beaten last at Kempton (7f) 18 days ago and surprising if he could overcome his penalty in this company.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 32,000gns yearling; fourth foal; closely related to Swedish 1m/8.6f winner Showgal, half-brother to winners Orchard Keeper (1m2f/1m6f; RPR 99) and The Hrse Horse (Qatari 7f); dam unraced half-sister to Group 3 winners Best Name (1m2f) and February Sun (1m3f); stable in fine form but others have more appealing pedigrees.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 70,000euros foal, 145,000gns yearling; fourth foal; half-sister to winners Utxa (French 1m1f 2yo/Czech 1m3f) and Sopran Beethoven (Italian 6f); dam once-raced close relative of 6f/7f Listed winner Rose Bonheur, out of 1m Group 3 winner; William Buick booked; one to consider.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Smart pedigree; made a promising debut when fourth of ten in a fillies' maiden at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago; should do much better; respected.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam Group-placed 6f/7f 2yo winner (including AW; RPR 100), closely related to 6f/7f winner William Dewhirst, half-sister to Italian Listed-placed 7.5f/1m1f winner Crook; enough paper appeal to warrant a market check.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fifth foal; dam 6f/7f 2yo winner (including Group 3; RPR 102), half-sister to Group-placed 5f-7.4f winner Motafaawit, out of 6f 2yo winning half-sister to 7f Listed winner Mankib; another well-bred newcomer who requires a market check.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 66-1 for her debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month when showing some ability but ultimately finishing well beaten; likely  a longer-term prospect.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Third foal; half-sister to winners Anna Swan (Listed-placed 7f 2yo; RPR 90) and Dark Shore (Qatari 1m2f); dam Group-placed 7f-1m2f winner (including 2yo; 106), sister to German/UAE 1m6f Group 3 winner Ispolini; bred to need more of a test but she represents powerful connections and a market check is advised.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: £52,000 yearling, 90,000euros breeze-up 2yo; seventh foal; half-sister to winners Manhattan Jungle (French 5f 2yo/US 6.5f Listed; RPR 95), She's A Warrior (1m; 89), Gregory Ligh (Italian 8.7f) and Raccontero Di Te (prolific Italian 5f/6f); dam 1m AW 2yo winner (59); hooded for debut; another to monitor closely in the betting.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 92,000gns foal, 100,000gns yearling; first foal of an unraced half-sister to winners Galmarley (useful 1m5f) and Gallifrey (1m 2yo/12.4f), out of 1m Listed winner from family of Derby runner-up Walk In The Park; may need more of a test in time.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 7,000gns foal, 32,000gns yearling; first foal; dam unraced sister to winners Monaasib (Group-placed 6f/6.4f 2yo) and Just A Girl (7.6f 2yo), half-sister to 5f Listed winner Tarboosh, out of 6f Listed winner; likely best watched on debut.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Third foal; dam a maiden (RPR 62) half-sister to a German Listed winner;  perhaps one for the longer term.

RaceName: Boost Tokens Now Live At BetVictor EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away and never in the hunt at Windsor (6f, good to soft) on last month's debut; big leap forward needed.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Well found in the market prior to his winning debut at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) in May; played up in the stalls before being withdrawn at Beverley four weeks later; easily justified 2-9 favouritism back at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) 16 days ago and he's a promising juvenile; well worth his place in this higher grade.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 850,000gns yearling; unextended when landing odds of 2-9 in a four-runner maiden at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago; this is a much sterner test of his credentials but no surprise to see him in the thick of it.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: All runs at 5f, winning an AW novice in May before a creditable eighth in the Group 2 Norfolk Stakes at the Royal meeting; 6f should suit; not fully exposed.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Ready win at Ripon (5f, good) on debut; finished fastest when fourth of 21 in the Norfolk Stakes four weeks ago; 6f looks sure to suit and he retains considerable potential.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Impressed when winning a maiden at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) in May; confirmed he was a promising juvenile by finishing fifth in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm), doing best of those racing on the unfavoured far side; capable of better still and he's a major player.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won well over C&D (good) on his debut in May; 25-1 and well beaten in the Coventry Stakes last month; still has time to do better but others bring more compelling credentials.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 120,000euros yearling; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Online Alexander (useful 5f including 2yo) and Bnedel (1m 2yo/10.4f), out of 7f winning half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Red Clubs; stiff task on debut; stable also run Agamemnon.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: A Bit On The Side & Partner
Spotlight: Won the Brocklesby in March; ran well at Royal Ascot (sixth of 25) and showed better form when second of eight in a Listed race at Sandown (5f, good; Ronson and Underdog in behind) two weeks ago; return to 6f should suit; respected.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 3l behind God Given Talent over C&D on debut; 200-1 when appearing to excel himself in the Coventry Stakes, beaten just over 4l into tenth; remains capable of better.

RaceName: Apple Print & Creative Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a 5f novice at Sandown on debut; he has finished behind reopposing rivals in two runs since and others look more persuasive.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: May have needed the run when down the field on her seasonal/handicap debut in May; took a good step forward with her win at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) two weeks ago; up 7lb and stamina for 1m has to be taken on trust but she still has time on her side.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice as a 2yo; improved efforts when in the frame in turf handicaps at Lingfield and over C&D on her last two starts; no obvious reason why she wouldn't give her running again.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
OwnerName: Duaij Al Khalifa & Ahmad Al Qassimi
Spotlight: Promise in maiden/novice events and she ran well for second (of 14; Areti fourth) on her handicap debut at Southwell 12 days ago; 3lb well in and she remains capable of better.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Ran as well as she ever has when fourth of 14 on her handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) 12 days ago; each-way prospects off the same mark.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Consistent rather than progressive in five runs over sprint trips for William Haggas; returns from 172 days off for Jack Channon (same owners) with a point to prove, not least her stamina.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Improved her RPR with each of her three runs in AW maiden/novice events (6f-8.6f); Oisin Murphy takes over for her handicap debut and further progress could be on the cards.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Placed on four occasions prior to his 7f handicap win at Salisbury in May; that form has worked out well enough to think this mark was in range and his disappointing run here 24 days ago can be excused (lost his position after some early scrimmaging); has to prove his stamina but he will be a danger to all if seeing out the mile.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Absent since a low-key nursery debut at Newmarket (7f, good) 268 days ago; gelded prior to his return; improvement essential for today's step up in trip.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Modest form in three fillies' events from 7f-1m2f; open to improvement now handicapping but she will require a good leap forward.

RaceName: Bet On The Open With BetVictor Handicap
Spotlight: Promise on debut (6f, good to firm) but she was easy to back and ran poorly on AW on her second run; back to form with a 7f novice win at Chepstow two weeks ago but that form isn't easy to quantify with the form horses failing to give their running; not bred to need this far but shapes as though it's worth a try.

RaceName: Uhy Ross Brooke Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Modest form under both codes for David Pipe; she has proved a different proposition since joining Rod Millman, running away with a small-field Class 5 at Chepstow (1m4f, good to firm) two weeks ago and making light of her penalty at York (1m4f, good to firm) last week; didn't look straightforward under pressure there but she was well on top at the finish and Oisin Murphy replaces an apprentice today; 7lb ahead of her mark and she's a major player.

RaceName: Uhy Ross Brooke Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: She has hit the frame in each of her three runs in maiden/novice company, recording best form when second of ten in a 1m6f event at Goodwood four weeks ago; the front pair pulled 12l clear of the third on that occasion and she moves into handicaps with untapped potential.

RaceName: Uhy Ross Brooke Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Unexposed 4yo; won a 1m2f maiden on AW last September; weak in the betting prior to her seasonal/handicap debut here (1m2f, good to firm) last month, a race where she plugged on for third; stepping up in trip could unlock more from her but it will need to.

A string of minor honours but no win from his eight races; disappointing on good to firm at Ascot in May, in between showing his best form at Kempton (1m3f, AW) and Sandown (1m2f, good); blinkers were fitted for that latest start, when he came from the back for fifth of 12 despite carrying his head high, and this race is markedly less competitive.

Didn't look straightforward when the race got serious on last two outings but he was nevertheless better at keeping a straight line when cheekpieces were enlisted for six-runner maiden at Sandown (1m2f, good) last time and stuck his neck out well to win by 1l; some improvement is probably needed going handicapping but he has to be considered seriously in this small field.

Unraced on good to firm except on debut (fourth); won twice from five starts as 2yo and creditable fourth of ten here on reappearance; faded right out of it at Newmarket (also 1m on good) four weeks later, which sees him visored today with a step up in trip; may need overall improvement.

Best efforts on AW, including second at Newcastle (1m2f) late last month; never dangerous when 16-1 at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm) nine days later, but today's race is much less competitive than his other two turf handicaps this term.
Minor honours over 1m3f/1m4f in his two Flat handicaps this term (his last runs for Alan King) prior to his creditable second 19 days ago for new yard over hurdles; should be a serious player.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Dubawi; first foal; dam 7f-10.5f winner (including 2yo/Group 3; RPR 108), half-sister to multiple 9.5f-10.5f Group 1/Grade 1 winner State Of Rest, is granddaughter of 1m2f Listed winner; powerful yard is looking strong in the 2yo department and she's an obvious contender on this debut.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Churchill filly and 44,000euros yearling who went for 170,000euros after a breeze-up in May; first foal; dam 6f/7f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 93), half-sister to winners Powerful Breeze (1m 2yo Group 2) and Power To Exceed (6f), out of Listed-placed 1m 2yo winner; a likely newcomer from respected yard.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Mohaather first foal; dam 1m AW winner (RPR 69), half-sister to winners Chocoya (useful 6f including 2yo) and Chiringuita (6f 2yo/7.5f), out of 7f 2yo/1m winner; probably best watched on her first go.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: The Ten Fools & A Horse Partnership
Spotlight: Sent off 100-1 and the penny appeared to be dropping late on when beaten 16l on her debut over C&D (good) four weeks ago; most likely capable of better but will still need to take a good step forward.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Too Darn Hot sixth foal; half-sister to winners Raja Raja (1m4f AW; RPR 104) and Chola Empire (7f AW including October 2yo debut; 85); dam 6f/7f AW winner (including 2yo; 83), out of unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Keraka; look for any market clues on this debut.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Flattered to get so close when chasing home a stablemate who easily won five-runner Yarmouth novice (7f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; that was still an encouraging first go and she's got the scope to progress.

RaceName: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 1,000gns foal by Lope Y Fernandez; fourth foal; half-sister to Polish 7f 2yo winner Damashal; dam 6f winner (RPR 70), out of unraced sister to 7f/1m winner Mustaqbal; best watched on this introduction unless the market suggests otherwise.

Unseated rider and slowly away when 11l fifth of seven at 20-1 on debut at Nottingham (8.3f, good) in May; this 45,000gns yearling is open to improvement but may be of greater interest when tackling further.

OwnerName: L J Vaessen And Stephen Barber
Spotlight: Left her debut run behind when eighth of 11 at 250-1 at Yarmouth (7f, good to soft) last month but was still soundly beaten and she needs another big step forward today.

Sent off at 8-1 on debut at Chepstow (7f, good to firm) a fortnight ago and kept on for second, albeit no match for the winner; a chunk of improvement is needed if he's to bother Cerro Blanco but it was a promising start to his career and he should have more to offer.

OwnerName: The Boys Are Back In Town
Spotlight: He raced seven times during last season's 2yo campaign and showed only very modest form; looks up against it on his reappearance.

Made debut last month and not devoid of ability on his two starts (1m2f, soft/good); however, soundly beaten each time and lots of improvement is needed on stable debut; sold out of Andrew Balding's yard for 10,000gns.

1,800gns foal; first foal; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 99) for connections, half-sister to three winners, out of 8.6f 2yo winner from talented family; a market check is advised but this Advertise newcomer may be best watched.
She is another that has been getting her act together, most recently winning a five-runner Thirsk novice (1m4f, good) one month ago; opening mark looks reasonable; leading candidate.

Still looked a touch raw when bagging 1m4f Catterick maiden (good) in April but he didn't build on that when fourth of five on his handicap debut at Doncaster four weeks ago; still early days and the added blinkers may help.

Last won when sharing the spoils at Southwell (1m4f, AW) over 15 months ago but he was in good form this spring and can be excused his latest effort on account of soft ground; ran well on his only previous visit here too; considered.

Has made good strides across three AW starts, latterly winning four-runner novice at Newcastle (1m2f) in January; goes up in trip again for this turf/handicap debut and market support would increase confidence on this first start since.

Sole win from 16 races came in France (9.5f, AW) as a 2yo; sinking in the weights and well handicapped judged on plenty of 2025 French form, with a step back in the right direction when fifth of 14 at Sandown (1m2f) on penultimate start; not at all discredited in a hot race here 13 days ago when the move up to 1m4f may have stretched him; wore first-time cheekpieces that day and blinkers are now given a go; not dismissed.

His only race on firmer than good was on debut, when runner-up; sole win came in a 1m Ffos Las maiden as 3yo; that's from nine races and despite being favourite in his last five handicaps but all three starts this season (1m2f, 1m and 1m1f; never nearer at evens last time) confirmed that he is well capable of being seriously involved.

He's had a long career but never been better than this season, winning at Wolverhampton (9.4f) and Lingfield (1m4f) with a close third in between; they were all on AW in March/April under Olivia Tubb and he's not raced since, with turf runs in the last two years hinting that he's not quite so good in this sphere; also, the last time he raced on firmer than good was 2022.

Made the running when 1m2f handicap winner (good to firm) this year at Doncaster and Beverley; 25-1 and again set the pace when fourth of five in Listed race at Beverley (1m4f) 13 days ago, which was another good run but whether it's worth another 3lb rise in today's mark can be questioned.

AW and dual turf winner over about 1m2f last April-June; some minor honours in his November-March campaign in the UAE, mostly on dirt, without reproducing best efforts; tongue tied first time for today's return from four months off and he needs to be back at his peak; has a bit to prove on firmer than good (after one attempt) but his yard is among the winners.

Dual AW winner last November who also took a handicap at Newmarket (1m, good) in April; unsurprisingly lost her unbeaten record in the 1,000 Guineas (80-1) and her handicap at Royal Ascot (again 1m on good to firm; 25-1) was pretty tough too but she was well beaten in the latter; this should be vastly more manageable and there's more than enough stamina in her family to boost interest.

He's on a hat-trick in this race and followed last year's win by also scoring at Windsor and Yarmouth (all 5f on good to firm in cheekpieces) in August; no wins since but he didn't get much cover when midfield over C&D one week ago and his race record means he can't be discounted; also ran well sole previous go in a visor.

Ran out of puff having lost a shoe at Windsor on his comeback last month and he again faded having attempted to make all over C&D (good to firm) 19 days later; becoming attractively handicapped, however, and could be building up to something bigger.

Three wins include a successful stable debut at Brighton (5.5f, good to firm) and he wasn't beaten far under a penalty when fourth of five at Lingfield (5f, AW) three weeks ago; career-high mark but he's respected.
Started well for this yard but the wheels have come off lately, finishing last over C&D one month ago then finishing tailed off on AW last Monday; not easy to suggest after that.

0-13 and he hasn't suggested he's about to cash in on a reduced mark, including when sixth of ten at Carlisle (7f) last Thursday; he's never gone closer than when a neck second at Musselburgh last August on his sole start at 5f, however, which could be a straw to clutch to.

Six wins, all at 5f, include five on turf, most recently when making a winning reappearance at Nottingham (good) in April; slight concern that his sole run here was his worst but he's won off this mark and looks a player.

Good run of form in the spring included successive wins on AW in April and solid second on turf (also 6f wearing eye-shields) in May; not so good subsequently and he couldn't justify a strong market move back on AW a fortnight ago; bit to prove on this drop back to 5f but last time was a step back in the right direction.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won Goodwood novice (6f, good) in October for William Haggas and her handicap debut the following month can be written off (lame); joined her new yard for 6,000gns at the start of this month and best watched unless the market speaks positively.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Beat five others to win this race off 3lb higher last year and she chased home Powdering over C&D three weeks ago; bombed out in a better race over 7f here on Saturday but that might be best ignored; visor enlisted.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Multiple winner at up to 1m who scored for the ninth time when landing a not dissimilar event over C&D three weeks ago; has never won off a mark this high but seems to be getting quicker as she ages and has gone back-to-back before.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Has a very good C&D record with three wins (all good to firm) last term; had dipped below her last winning mark when attempting to make it four three weeks ago, so her sixth of seven behind Powdering was underwhelming; dropped a further 2lb and she's not readily dismissed.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Dual 6f AW novice winner who was competing in just her third handicap when posting a career best for second at Southwell (6f, AW) off this mark four weeks ago; needs to carry that progress back to turf but she's unexposed and likely capable of better again.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: She rattled off a hat-trick at 6f on good ground around this time last year and was back in the groove when scoring at Ayr (6f, soft) four weeks ago; has been put back to her career-high mark (0-2) but there's a solid chance she can defy it this time.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 2-2 in AW novices last year and she retained her unbeaten record on handicap debut at Doncaster (also 6f, good to firm) in May; drop to 5f and soft ground didn't see her replicate her best in Ayr Listed event four weeks ago but better can be expected in this scenario.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Constant progress last year saw her win four nurseries (5f, sound turf and AW) and she completed her season with very creditable fourth of 19 in a Listed event at the other Newmarket track (6f, good) in October; look for market interest ahead of this reappearance.

Has been revitalised since joining this yard with form figures of 23121; latest win came in this headgear combination at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) last Wednesday; drop back to 7f is no problem and she's a leading candidate under the penalty.
Last win came at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in May 2025; has slipped to a dangerous mark and any market support should be noted.

Made the breakthrough at Chelmsford in December and nearly doubled up at Lingfield (also 7f, AW) that month; way off that when last seen in January though and would become of interest only with market support on this comeback.
Can miss the break but she won this race last year off 10lb lower and swiftly got over a Chester aberration when second of 11 here (1m, good to firm) under Arron D'Arcy four weeks ago; a player.
Solid strike-rate on AW but not so good on turf and latest sixth of 12 at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) will need improving on; nothing wrong with this mark, though.
Sole win on turf came over two years ago and his last two efforts have been moderate; this mark is fine if first-time cheekpieces spark him back to life, however.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Dam was a limited maiden and this filly has followed suit thus far; lost a shoe on her handicap debut last time but, while this race is less competitive, she's had plenty of chances now.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Started a single-figure price for the Wolverhampton maiden won by Hauteluce late last month but blew the start and was never a factor; blinkers are tried after that.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Needed the experience in one run last winter and fared much better on her Tapeta comeback, when easily beating a subsequent winner in a weak maiden at Wolverhampton (upped to 9.5f; stamina on the dam's side); should have more to offer under the penalty.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Shaped nicely at a big price on her soft-ground debut early last month and ran to a similar level last time (good; both over this trip); enters calculations on either effort.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 25,000euros yearling whose dam won on the AW at around 1m in France; hood goes on for her debut and the market will be the best guide for a yard that's enjoying a decent summer.
Yard won this with a debutant in 2023; this 325,000euros Irish breeze-up 2yo, who's a half-brother to two Irish winners, holds a Gimcrack (Group 2) entry and is a likely looking newcomer.
Boasts a decent pedigree but started a big price on his C&D debut three weeks ago, when well held having been inclined to pull hard; will need to improve a deal on that.

Half-brother to the yard's dual 6f 2yo winner Egoli; started among the favourites for a Salisbury novice that's produced winners a month ago; blew the start and was never involved that day but is entitled to improve.
First foal of an unraced sister to useful Irish sprinter Son Of Rest; trainer's strike-rate with 2yos is down a touch this season and the market will guide.
Big price and badly needed the experience on his recent Epsom debut, blowing the start and finishing a remote last of eight; needs a lot more, dropping back from 7f.

RaceName: When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins over hurdles since last seen on the Flat, going almost two stone up the weights; withdrawn on account of unsuitable (good to firm) ground last summer, which would be a concern, but she's much better treated on the Flat now.

RaceName: When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap
Spotlight: Better expected last time, after two poor efforts and back to the visor from cheekpieces, but ran below market expectations in finishing behind Merrijig; 2lb better off today but has work to do if he's to turn things round.

RaceName: When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap
Spotlight: Adaptable regarding ground and tactics; this looks less competitive than the Ffos Las 0-65 in which he finished second last time (hampered; two of these behind) and his claims are obvious.

RaceName: When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap
OwnerName: Case Racing Partnership & Anita J Lush
Spotlight: Made all off 3lb higher here (1m6f) last July; not in the same form this season, including in that same race a fortnight ago, when a long way off the front pair; needs more.

RaceName: When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap
Spotlight: String of poor efforts to date, latterly when a long way behind Merrijig and Simiyann at Ffos Las late last month; would be a shock winner.

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)
Spotlight: Stayed on as strongly as any at Windsor latest (6f, good to firm) after a slow start; more galloping test at the trip is a likely plus, and just a case of whether he helps himself sufficiently; eased 1lb.

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)
Spotlight: Neck second at Newcastle (5f, AW) last time rates a clear career best, and a 3lb rise doesn't look prohibitive; yet to see out a galloping 6f completely convincingly, albeit not having yet tried to on going as quick as today's.

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)
Spotlight: Unimproved for the addition of cheekpieces (retained here nonetheless) at Ripon in May, and wind surgery resorted to since; effectiveness over a galloping 6f yet to be tested, but 2lb lower mark looks competitive judged against the RPR of last autumn's Leicester debut (5f).

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)
Spotlight: Podium finishes on all three 2yo novice starts for Mark Rimell, almost holding on at Redcar (6f, good; bumped late); yet to scale those heights in handicaps this term despite starting off on a tolerable mark, traffic not costing him a win latest; hopes rest with change of scenery since.

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)
Spotlight: Won going away at Newcastle in March (6f, AW) for a perfect start to life in handicaps; refusal to settle and (latest) traffic issues offer excuses since, but less margin for error now stepped up beyond 0-60 class.

RaceName: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)

0-11 over hurdles and prone to clumsy jumping; belied 33-1 odds when second at Perth (2m, good) last month and didn't run badly over 2m4f there 16 days ago but others look less risky.

Spotlight: Won a juvenile hurdle for Gavin Cromwell at Punchestown (2m, good to yielding) in October and was also on target in 2m2f Flat marathon for new stable in June; still unexposed over jumps; no surprise if he features.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Not quite at his best this year but last month's Hexham third was respectable and she remains only 2lb higher than when beating Saligo Bay to win this race under Thomasina Eyston in 2025; can't be ruled out.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Ex-Irish 6yo who is 2-3 in maiden/novice hurdles for new stable this season, the latter win gained by 18l at Uttoxeter (2m, good; first-time hood) 11 days ago; faces tougher opposition on this British handicap debut but still commands respect.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in a Listed bumper last season and 2-3 since switched to hurdles this spring, having beaten subsequent wide-margin winner Eternal Angel at Uttoxeter on latest outing; must be considered on handicap debut.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Appreciated drop to 0-110 grade when second under Amber Jackson-Fennell at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good; wore cheekpieces) last month but is not as good as he was and needs change of headgear to give him a boost here.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up (albeit no match for winner) off today's mark at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) in May and didn't run badly on the Flat (1m6f) last month; could yet have a bigger effort in him over jumps but this drop back in trip may not be in his favour.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Built upon pleasing stable debut when coming from off the pace for C&D (good) success under Leah Noreci in May; subsequent 3lb rise ought to be manageable and she can make her presence felt again.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Progressive on the Flat and over hurdles last year, collecting eight wins (one over C&D) in total; absent since respectable fifth in Scottish County Hurdle at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft) in January, though, and current mark demands another personal best.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Bounced back to form with narrow win at Kelso (2m5f, good) in May but that seems to be his favourite track and he ran poorly here (2m6f) last month; this drop back in trip is not ideal; not the percentage call.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up three consecutive times at Hexham (2m-2m4f, good) this spring and also suited by this track but his latest run was below par and he's 2lb wrong today.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Professional Jockeys & Amateur Riders' Race)
OwnerName: T Alderson & Ales And Dales Syndicate
Spotlight: Won four-runner Sedgefield maiden (2m4f, soft) in December and remains unexposed under rules but his next two hurdle runs were disappointing and he unseated rider mid-race on last month's chase/handicap debut; dropped in trip and reverts to hurdling today; others have more obvious claims.

In good form over fences here since wind op in April, most notably when winning over 3m1f (good) three weeks ago; should be fine back over this hurdles and over this shorter trip; respected in current mood.
Won twice on good ground this spring (2m7f/2m4f) and last month's close second at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) was a career-best performance; likely contender again here.
