Returned from eight-month break in excellent form three weeks ago, winning comfortably by 10l over C&D (good); 8lb higher in higher-grade race today but still considered.

Popular veteran who runs this track well and capitalised upon some significant help from the handicapper when winning Norfolk National at Fakenham (3m5f, good) in May; this drop back in trip is not ideal on his return to hurdling, though; cheekpieces (worn for last three races) left off today.
In career-best form this season, most notably when coming from the rear to win Class 2 handicap at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) three weeks ago; still unexposed over this sort of trip; might be the answer.
Came good for current stable at Hexham (2m, good) last month, his second run in cheekpieces; up 4lb to career-high mark but will be suited by this move back up in trip and is evidently in good nick.

OwnerName: Mrs D Chapman & Mrs E Quinlan
Spotlight: Three-time C&D winner, most recently in May; needs to bounce back from below-par run here three weeks ago but probably still on a workable mark; dangerous to ignore.

Teenager who was useful in his prime and is well handicapped on form as recent as the autumn; returned from break with satisfactory run in June but was well beaten on only previous visit to Cartmel; younger rivals preferred.

Dual C&D winner for Warren Greatrex; ran as though something was amiss on latest outing in January and was sold for £10,000 in May but starts off for new stable on workable mark; tongue-tie on; market helpful.

Belied 40-1 odds when creditable third at Kelso (2m5f, good to soft; wore cheekpieces) in March but weakened quickly after making a lot of the running over C&D (good; visored, as today) three weeks ago and is now 0-9 for stable; needs recent wind op to have made a big difference.

Returned from break with two underwhelming chase runs this season and unseated rider when back over hurdles in plating company 12 days ago; tricky to weigh up at present but represents respected Irish stable.

Well below best during five-race campaign last season but took step back in right direction when third over fences at Bangor (2m1f, good) two months ago; remains on good mark for this hurdle return and could plausibly be better suited by this sort of trip nowadays; cheekpieces replace blinkers.

Unraced over hurdles since winning Cheltenham novice in 2024 but recent 2m7f/3m chase form has been very respectable and he's edging down the weights; swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers; could have a say.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Not seen over fences since two disappointing attempts in spring 2024 but in good form over hurdles, notably when winning at Hexham (2m7f, good) in May; reverts to chasing on a lower mark; player if able to find some fluency.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Gained all three chase wins at this track (2m5f-3m1f) and has slipped to a dangerous mark but looked out of sorts on both starts here last month (2m5f/3m1f) and now has questions to answer.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Came good with game hurdle win here (3m1f, good) in May and fended off Star Turn to follow up in C&D (good) chase three weeks ago; makes obvious appeal in current form.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual C&D winner (including this race in 2024); good third to Halfway House over C&D in May, after a break, but pulled up after looking reluctant (not for the first time) at Hexham last month and comes with risk.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Returned from long absence with two hurdling seconds this spring (visored) and filled same position behind Kingofthegame in C&D chase three weeks ago (good; first-time blinkers); not yet exposed over fences; shortlisted.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Runner-up twice over hurdles in recent weeks, latterly in refitted cheekpieces at Worcester (2m7f, good), but was well beaten in both chases last year and needs to prove he can transfer his recent good form to fences.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Ended 2025 with two poor hurdle runs for Maurice Barnes and was also well beaten when reappearing for new stable this month (first-time hood); makes chasing debut with quite a bit to prove.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; not beaten that far when fifth of seven here (2m5f, good) three weeks ago and might be better suited by today's trip but others in this line-up have much more obvious claims.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Dennis J Coppola & Mrs Dianne Sayer
Spotlight: Placed in two 2m7f Kelso chases in the autumn (good/good to soft) but absent since below-par hurdle run in February and returns with rules strike-rate standing at 0-21.

RaceName: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Started off for James Moffatt with two good-ground wins in May, the latter over C&D; ran as though something was amiss here three weeks ago but could still have more improvement to come for new stable if quickly back on song; cheekpieces (worn twice in 2024) are given another whirl.

11-race maiden who has a patchy profile and made it 0-5 over fences when pulled up at Market Rasen (2m6f, good) in May; comes with risks attached but he may have had stamina issues last time and he looks interesting on his placed effort at Hereford (2m, good) in March; tongue-tie and cheekpieces are removed and visor returns.

Four-time chase winner who bounced back with a close second at Uttoxeter (2m, good) 11 days ago; 3lb higher here but he remains well treated on old form and all of his wins have been under Brian Hughes; key player.

Record of 5-18 over fences but all of those wins have come at Sedgefield (2m/2m4f); only 2lb higher than for his last win in April but he's not gone on from that and was a well-held fifth of seven over C&D (good; 16-1) last time; others preferred.

Defied this mark over C&D (good) last August but he's been out of sorts in his last three runs and latest was at Cartmel three weeks ago; has something to prove and he needs to get back on track; blinkers are removed and cheekpieces return.

Overall record of 0-12 but she's unexposed over fences and went clear some way out before fading into a 9l fourth here (2m5f, good) three weeks ago; continues to edge down the weights and she could make a bold bid on this drop back in trip; hood removed.

Triple hurdle winner who is 0-8 over fences but he's on a dangerous mark and wasn't beaten far when third at Market Rasen (2m2f, good) on penultimate run; has possibilities if he can get back near that level and yard is in good form; wore blinkers last time but regular cheekpieces now return.

Won off 16lb higher at Worcester (2m4f, good) in August 2024 but he's lost his way and has failed to complete in his last three runs; has lots to prove and he needs a major revival on this big drop back in trip.

Both wins over fences came over C&D in 2024; well handicapped on his old form but he's generally struggled in the last 12 months and was last of seven over C&D (good) when last seen in May; plenty to prove and all of his wins have been on soft or heavy ground.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: All five wins over fences have been at this track and latest was over C&D (good) in May; didn't shine here last time but that was a Class 2 handicap and he still looks on a workable mark; respected on this big drop back in grade.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has won four chases and latest was at Newcastle in October (2m4f, good); well handicapped on that form but he's been disappointing since and was pulled up at Perth two weeks ago.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Nine-time chase winner including twice at Cartmel; didn't fire at Worcester in May but that was after a close second at Ffos Las (2m4f, good) and he's a player if he can recapture that form; not ruled out for yard that won this last year.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won twice over hurdles and once over fences for Dan Skelton; wasn't beaten far when third of three on stable debut here (2m1f, good) in May but he was well held in another small-field event over C&D last time; still lightly raced over fences but he needs to step up again after that last run; cheekpieces reapplied.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Major improver who made it 5-7 over fences when completing a five-timer over C&D (good) three weeks ago; up another 5lb but he's on a roll and this tough 7yo could continue on the upgrade; big player.

RaceName: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Completed a hat-trick at around 3m during the opening quarter of 2025 but following a year off he's refused to race on two occasions and was pulled up here (3m1f, good) last time.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Spotlight: Frankel colt; brother to winners Homeless Songs (7f/1m inc 2yo/Irish 1,000 Guineas; RPR 122) and Spoken Truth (1m2f; 98), half-brother to winners Reve De Vol (7f 2yo/1m2f Listed; 106) and Time Tells All (1m2f; 85); dam 7f winner (inc Listed; 104); impeccably bred and holds multiple Group 1 entries; interesting debutant.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt; brother to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Beautify (RPR 107), half-brother to winners Library (7.5f 2yo/1m2f Listed; 109) and Vice President (1m2f; 93); dam 7f 2yo/1m4f Group 3 winner (105); lots to like on paper and Lordan rode The Lion In Winter when he won this maiden in 2023; can't discount.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Spotlight: Dark Angel colt sent off at 4-1 on debut over 6f here (gd-fm) 22 days ago and found things happening a bit quickly before staying on very nicely into fifth, after meeting traffic problems; wasn't knocked about and looks almost certain to improve for this longer trip.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt; dam Group-placed 8.4f winner (RPR 104), sister to winners Delphi (Australian 1m4f Group 2), Matchless (7f-1m4f Flat and 2m hurdle) and Last Galileo (1m 2yo), out of 6f 2yo Group 3 winner; preferred by Moore and yard has farmed this race in recent years.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
OwnerName: Samuel M Mencoff & Anthony Paul Smurfit
Spotlight: Starspangledbanner colt; E150,000 yearling; dam French 1m 2yo winner (RPR 96), sister to 7f winner Borjina, half-sister to useful 1m4f/12.5f winner Plage De Havre, out of maiden half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 2 winner Rich Legacy; holds Group 1 entry; market can guide.

RaceName: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
OwnerName: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt; 200,000gns foal; half-brother to 1m-1m2f winner Garden Route (RPR 93); dam South African 5f-6f 2yo winner (inc Group 1), half-sister to South African 1m Group 1 winner Silver Mountain; nicely bred and holds Group 1 entries, but looks down the stable's pecking order on rider arrangements.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: New Bay filly ran okay without really threatening in her first two maidens, but big step forward at Limerick on latest (7f, soft) when beaten a head by a 77-rated rival; leading form claims on that run, but has to prove she handles this quicker ground (mixed signals on breeding).

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Pinatubo filly; unsold E220,000 yearling; half-sister to four winners inc Irish Territory (US 1m turf; RPR 105), Moment Of Silence (7f AW; 99) and Zaragoza (6f; 71); dam Listed-placed 1m2f winner (91), half-sister to 1m2f-1m4f Group 1 winner Ghaiyyath; likely type on paper and in-form yard can ready one.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: J Kirkland & Mrs J M Ryan
Spotlight: Promise in all three maidens over 7f; decent third of 20 on handicap debut off a mark of 75 here last month (1m, good), not quite getting home; the drop back to 7f should suit on that evidence, and should be in the mix again returned to maiden company.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Philip Antonacci & Mrs Paul Shanahan & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: E330,000 No Nay Never filly was sent off at 12-1 on debut at Dundalk (6f) last November and finished in mid-field; off since and looks the stable's second string here on rider arrangements.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Cotai Glory filly; E105,000 yearling; closely related to US 5f turf winner Rebel With A Clue, half-sister to three winners inc Cosmic Vega (7f/1m inc 2yo/Listed/Australia; RPR 111) and The X O (6f AW; 106); dam unraced half-sister to 5f Group 2 winner Danehurst; attractively bred and from respected source; check market.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Seventh in barrier trial at Naas last year; promise in a couple of AW maidens over 7f and 1m in the autumn; off since and much more needed on turf debut, but the booking of Oisin Murphy catches the eye (2-5 when riding for this stable in Britain and Ireland); check the market.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Promising start in 7f maiden at Leopardstown in May, beaten 3.25l into fourth of nine despite racing a shade keenly; off since and that form hasn't really worked out, but she's open to improvement and could go well if settling better.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Slowly away and never got involved on debut over 6f here (gd-fm) last month when sent off at 28-1; a bit of stamina in pedigree so worth a go at this longer trip, but lots more needed.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Well-bred daughter of Wootton Bassett has so far failed to live up to her pedigree; rated 76 after three runs in maidens at around 1m2f, the best of which was a 7.25l third of 10 at Leopardstown in May (1m2f, good); markedly dropped in trip now; needs more.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Huge odds and soundly beaten in maidens at Bellewstown (5f, good) and Navan (6f, good); major improvement needed upped further in trip.

RaceName: Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: 150-1 and failed to beat a rival on debut at Navan; seems safe to rule out.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: One of two for last year's winning yard; won on her second start for Andre Fabre last year; bought for E125,000 in December and has won back-to-back Listed races on her first two starts for Paddy Twomey, over 1m4f at Cork (sft-hvy) and 1m6f at Gowran (gd-yld); up in class  and drops back in trip; might prefer a bit of an ease in the ground.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: British raider is 2-6, her wins coming last season in a Yarmouth novice and a class 4 handicap at York off 83; signed off with a Listed third in Italy and ran a blinder on her seasonal return in the Kensington Palace Handicap at Royal Ascot when not getting the clearest of runs; her official rating of 92 may underestimate her and she could outrun her likely odds.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: German recruit is 1-11 but has run some cracking races in defeat; respectable Listed run here over 1m4f (good) on first run for this stable; even better when just 0.5l behind Oaks contender Sparan Nua in 1m4f Cork Group 3 (good) on latest, when conceding lots of weight; non-runner on account of good to firm ground here last month, however, and similar conditions likely again.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: British raider is talented on her day; two-time winner at Listed level, but has come up well short in a trio of Group 2s this season, most recently when beaten 12.5l in the Duke Of Cambridge at Royal Ascot (1m, gd-fm); needs a revival stepped back up in trip.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
OwnerName: Hot To Trot Racing 2 & J Fill
Spotlight: Lightly-raced British challenger is a three-time winner; 2-4 on turf, the wins coming off 81 in a Salisbury handicap in May (1m2f, gd-fm) and a Listed race at Haydock later that month (10.5f, gd-sft); 3.75l fourth of seven in a Group 3 on the AW at Newcastle last time; place claims.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Five wins from 16 starts, the most recent coming in this race a year ago; fine efforts in defeat in both starts this term, in a Group 2 here over 1m and when beaten 1.5l into second behind the talented Estrange in the Pretty Polly last time over C&D (gd-fm); may prove hard to beat with a repeat of that.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: C&D maiden winner on yielding to soft last September; good third on seasonal return in Listed heat at Gowran (9.5f, good to yielding) but soundly beaten in another Listed race at Naas on latest (1m1f, good); moves up in grade and trip; new headgear combination needs to eke out more.

RaceName: Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Sole success came in a 3yo Dundalk maiden early last year; 0-10 in stakes races and yet to trouble the judge, though was only 1.75l behind the winner in a 1m Listed race here on latest (good); more needed upped in trip and grade.

Runner-up in the Ayr Silver Cup (6f, soft) last September when first home on his side; repeated a 2025 Epsom win (6f, soft) early last month; first of his small group when ninth in the Wokingham; generally dependable sort; stable won this in 2016.

Ex-Richard Hannon; off the mark for the Quinn team when making virtually all in a 22-runner handicap at York Dante meeting (6f, good); bounced straight back from a lesser run at Thirsk when second at Ripon; made all for a 6f Chester win three weeks ago; stable won this with Mr Wagyu in 2022.

Dual AW winner who got off the mark on turf in a 6f handicap here in May; badly hampered in the race won by Headmaster later that month; 3lb wrong when taking the 5f Rockingham Handicap here last time; stiff task off his new rating,

Has recorded six of his eight wins over 5f, including last year's Rockingham Handicap here; proved that he is in good shape with a conditions race victory at Naas a fortnight ago; has run well in Listed events this term; trainer has a strong contender in Headmaster.
Two wins last season, a Listowel maiden and a 6f Dundalk event; beaten by the odds-on Oro Blanco in a two-horse race last time; previously unplaced favourite in a 7f handicap here.

Nine-time turf winner, including a 6f Group 3 at this venue in 2023, Listed contests and this event 12 months ago; was once rated 108, so has dropped a long way; inconsistent this year; good run when second here last time, 3lb wrong

Won twice last year over 5f at Cork and also finished second to Keke here in the Rockingham, a fine effort for a horse of his age; not at his best at Dundalk on first start this year; down the field behind Genesis in the Rockingham last month.
Stable second-string when landing a 7f maiden at Fairyhouse on his third start; added to his score by beating Gavoo in a two-horse race at Naas; still relatively unexposed.

Runner-up six times before belatedly opening his account in a premier handicap over 6f here; fifth in this race last year; two satisfactory runs this term; could go well, but a record of one win from 22 starts makes it hard to be overly confident.

OwnerName: J Fairhurst & Damian McCann & Cyril McMullan
Spotlight: Has become highly dependable since being gelded, winning three of his last eight starts, including two on AW in Britain; leading contender after Rockingham third with several of these rivals behind him; overall form favours him over the winner Genesis.

Smart turf form at up to 7f in Bahrain for George Scott early last year; some good runs this year, second to Sir Les Patterson on the AW (6f) in February and close fourth at Chester in May (7.5f, good); no luck in running in the Habitat here (won by Headmaster), again behind that rival at Cork.
Both wins have come at this track but over 6f/7f; this season's form linked to Genesis and Headmaster puts her in the mix, although several others would seem to have marginally stronger claims.
Both wins this season have been gained over 7f; asserted late in a seven-runner contest at Fairyhouse ten days ago; may find some of these rivals too speedy.

All five wins have come on the AW, including two at 6f last winter; highlight of turf form when third to Tango Flare here last autumn; fair form this term, but needs first-time cheekpieces to have an improving effect.
Best known for AW exploits, also effective on turf; second to Bodhi Bear in a 5f handicap at Navan; visor now replaces blinkers following a below-par Dundalk run last Sunday.
7f maiden winner at Limerick last season on his sixth and final start for Aidan O'Brien; went close in a 6f handicap at Navan three starts ago; 4lb wrong, up against it.

Added to two British 7f wins when bagging the Habitat Handicap (6f, good) here in May on second start for new yard; had difficulty finding a gap before storming home to win by a neck with several of these behind; another solid display over 7f at Cork; top trainer of sprinters won this in 2020 and 2021.

Two handicap wins this season, over 5f here (sft-hvy) and over the same trip at Navan on (good); virtually inseparable from Tango Flare based on Listed third behind course specialist here last time; both could feature.

Beat course specialist Big Gossey when winning the Bold Lad Handicap here last September; no luck in running in two handicaps this term; won a Fairyhouse conditions race for the third time in four years before a fine second to Big Gossey in a Listed race here last time, a whisker in front of Bodhi Bear.
Lacks an outing this year and is 6lb out of the handicap; signed off last year with 6f AW maiden win; gelded since; rider's claim the main plus.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: British raider was in fine form at Meydan at the turn of the year, winning a Listed (yielding) and a Group 2 (good), both over 5f; didn't get the smoothest of runs when beaten 3.5l in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot last time (behind Rosy Affair and Jakajaro) and could get closer here if getting a clear passage.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: British challenger a five-time handicap winner, most recently scoring off 92 at York in May;  creditable first run in stakes company in a Sandown Group 3 last time when a 1.25l third behind the 110-rated Rumstar; that's solid form and Colin Keane keeps the faith; place chance.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Prominent racer started his campaign with back-to-back handicap wins at Newmarket (5f, good) and York (5f, good); yet to score at Pattern level but huge runs the last twice in the Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock (5f, good) and when a 1.5l fifth of 26 in the King Charles III (5f, gd-fm) at Royal Ascot; fourth in this last year and should be in the mix again.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Consistent British raider boasts a decent strike rate of 5-13 but her last four wins have come over 6f; finished a 1.5l fourth (a nose ahead of Jakajaro) over 5f in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot last time and there shouldn't be much between them again here; big player.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: 3yo son of Wootton Bassett signed off last term with an excellent second at the Breeders' Cup (5f, firm) but form has been regressive this season, albeit all three runs have come over 6f; the drop back to 5f is a positive, but he has a fair bit to find on the figures and Ryan Moore prefers the chances of Charles Darwin.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Classy juvenile and a six-time winner, including four times at this track over 5f/6f; two wins last season included a Listed heat over 5f at Naas and the Group 3 Phoenix Sprint Stakes here over 6f (both on good); weakened late over 6f in a Group 2 here last time, and not dismissed back at 5f.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: 3yo filly is 3-9 with all three of her wins coming over 5f/6f at Naas; won a Group 3 over the latter trip on her seasonal return (good) and outran her odds of 28-1 when a fine 2l fourth in the Commonwealth Cup (6f, gd-fm); gets all the allowances here and the drop back to 5f should pose no problems; big chance.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
OwnerName: Stonestreet Stables, LLC & AMO Racing Limited
Spotlight: Speedy two-time Listed winner (including over C&D); yet to win this season; beaten off 95 in a handicap over C&D in June and again off 1lb lower in the Palace Of Holyrood at Royal Ascot on latest; much more needed upped in grade.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
OwnerName: Miss Kate McGivern & Thomas Hore & Shane M Power
Spotlight: Six-time handicap winner (including over C&D); took his form to a new level when winning a Listed heat at Cork (5f, good) last month when wearing this headgear combination for the first time; this is much harder, so another step forward is required.

RaceName: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: 3yo won three of his four starts last season, including the Norfolk Stakes (5f, gd-fm); started off this campaign with a Listed win at Naas (6f, gd-yld) but has questions to answer after finishing well beaten in a Group 3 back at Naas and in the Commonwealth Cup in first-time blinkers (retained) on latest; the pick of Moore, but needs to get back on track down in trip.
Refused to enter the stalls on his intended debut at Navan; made a good impression over C&D early last month; missed the break in the Windsor Castle; will need to be a lot sharper.

OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Mrs A O'Callaghan
Spotlight: Form of debut win at Navan has worked out; finished behind Carry The Flag in the Norfolk; Robson De Aguiar also saddles Immortal Guard, who was involved in the stable's Group 3 one-two here last month.

Just denied over 5f here on soft first time out; won with plenty to spare over 6f at Naas; ran respectably, but well below general expectations, when sixth behind stablemate Great Barrier Reef in the Coventry Stakes; needs to redeem himself after odds-on Group 3 defeat behind two De Aguiar-trained runners here three weeks ago; needs to settle better; Moore sticks with him.
Listowel maiden winner on his third outing; out of his depth in the Coventry; 90-rated colt will need others to underperform.
Promising debut behind a Ballydoyle-trained colt over C&D; still looked raw when winning narrowly at Fairyhouse; will need to be a lot more streetwise here.

OwnerName: Ramiro Restrepo & Jacob West & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Won a C&D maiden on debut before a fine effort in the Group 3 Marble Hill Stakes; third behind the subsequent Coventry winner Great Barrier Reef then, 1 1/4l off Carry The Flag; second to a longer-priced stablemate in Group 3 Anglesey Stakes here three weeks ago, a head in front of the odds-on Confucius.

Not especially convincing when landing the odds over 5f at Naas on second start; much sharper next time over C&D when second to the subsequent Coventry winner Great Barrier Reef; beaten 7l into ninth after going off 5-2 favourite in the Norfolk; got up late to win a 5f Listed race at Naas a fortnight ago; cheekpieces on now.

Won at the third attempt, making all in a maiden at Leopardstown (1m2f, good) in May; took the sharp rise in class in her stride when going very close against Earth Shot in the Ribblesdale; further improvement on the cards; helps to give Joseph O'Brien a strong hand.

Two 7f Newmarket wins and a fine second in France as a juvenile; fourth in the Nell Gwyn and failed to feature in the 1,000 Guineas; found her vocation when upped to 1m2f at Goodwood, getting the better of Earth Shot; enhanced her reputation with fine third behind  Diamond Necklace in the Prix de Diane; Earth Shot may have her measure at this trip.

Unbeaten filly; won a Naas maiden at 25-1 on debut (1m, good) and confirmed ability when showing a good turn of foot in a slowly-run Gowran conditions race (9.5f good to yielding); deserves to take her chance after a Group 3 win over this trip at Cork.

Debut winner on soft in a maiden at Gowran in March, relegating stablemate Johanna Walsh to third; coped well with good ground and a furlong further when landing a Group 3 at Naas; now takes on her Oaks-winning stable's Thundering On and the much-improved Johanna Walsh.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Won a maiden at Leopardstown (1m, yielding) last October on her fifth start; reappeared with 2l win in the Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good) in first-time hood and blinkers; failed to handle the track when favourite for the Oaks; change of headgear, Moore stays loyal; pick of a Ballydoyle quintet.

5l win at Newmarket (1m2f, good) in May on second start and then went very close against Inis Mor in a Listed race at Goodwood (1m2f, good); appreciated the step up in trip when gaining a narrow win from Johanna Walsh in the Ribblesdale; highly likely to be involved in the finish.

OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Group 2 winner over 6f at this venue last summer and close second to Precise in the Moyglare; well beaten in the Cheveley Park, and down the field in the Nell Gwyn on seasonal debut; sixth of 11 in the Irish 1,000 Guineas; unconvincing run in the 1m2f Pretty Polly; unappealing on first attempt at 1m4f.

OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Course 7f maiden winner at two (soft to heavy); took a big step forward to win in the Listed Oaks Trial at Lingfield (good to firm) on her sixth start, and her first run beyond 1m; appeared to have a good chance of staying the Oaks trip, but faded from over two furlongs down; limitations evident at Naas.

Dual Pattern winner in busy 2025 campaign; has raced six times to much less effect since her 7f Group 2 success here last August; sole runner for Ballydoyle in the Ribblesdale, hampered and hung right; not a bad effort, but well held by Earth Shot and Johanna Walsh.

OwnerName: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
Spotlight: Third in Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster last September and readily made all in Group 3 here in October; fourth of five behind Amelia Earhart at Chester on reappearance, reversed form with her disappointing stablemate when third at Epsom, weakened late, beaten almost 10l; first-time cheekpieces.

OwnerName: David Spratt & Sean Jones & Mrs Lynne Lyons
Spotlight: Failed to win at two, but got off the mark on second start of this season in 1m2f (yielding) maiden at Navan; never landed a blow on handicap debut in the King George V handicap at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) last time; capable of better, but has to prove he handles quick ground.

Cork maiden winner in May (1m2f, soft); beaten off 78 in handicap on her previous start (also at Cork) over 1m4f (gd-yld) and is 5lb higher now; remote third in 1m4f (soft) Listed race at Leopardstown on latest; drop back in trip a plus and probably capable of better.

Handicap debutante; shed the maiden tag at the third attempt over 1m4f at Fairyhouse (good) 17 days ago; opening mark doesn't look overly generous and it's debatable whether this drop back in trip will suit, but unexposed and can't be discounted.

Unplaced in all three maidens but has shown ability; stayed on well over 1m at Leopardstown in May; well behind Noble Honour and Tanzanite Diamond at Fairyhouse upped to 1m2f (good) on latest; gelded since and blinkers go on for handicap debut; could improve, but others have stronger form claims.

Fairly modest form in four maidens; behind Noble Honour at Fairyhouse on penultimate over 1m2f (good); beaten 13l when fourth of 17 over 1m4f (good) back there on latest; tongue tie and cheekpieces go on for handicap debut; probably best watched.

Handicap debutante; placed in all three maiden starts at 1m-10.5f on varying ground; found just one too good at Fairyhouse on latest (1m2f, good) where she had Tanzanite Diamond 5.5l behind; bred to be better than her opening mark of 78 and interesting runner for yard that won this last year and in 2021.
Two of her three wins have come over C&D, including this race in 2024 off a mark of 60 (now 6lb higher); limited appeal on recent form, but could surprise.

Nine-time winner, including twice over C&D; no joy yet this season; ran better than the bare result from 10lb out of the handicap in the Rockingham; finished well in the recent Naas event won by Sovereign Cry; not ruled out.

Failed to win at two; put that right when making all in a Navan maiden (5f, yielding) in first-time cheekpieces; not beaten far on handicap debut at the same venue in blinkers (5f, good); another good run in cheekpieces (retained) at Bellewstown; big burden, rider's claim will help.

OwnerName: Ms Yvonne Hennessy & Ms S O'Neill
Spotlight: Gained fourth win of his career at Down Royal (5f, soft) last month; solid overall form this season; close fourth behind Sovereign Cry at Naas two weeks ago, form boosted by the third when scoring at Leopardstown on Thursday.

Belatedly off the mark at Navan last month in first-time cheekpieces; another good run at Naas (third of 21); underlined his rate of improvement when winning again at Bellewstown; up an aggregate 17lb.
First run after being gelded when showing much-improved form to beat Foccacia in a 5f AW maiden in May; outpaced at Cork in his first handicap
In rear in a C&D handicap last month; on the upgrade now judged on the evidence of a front-running maiden win at Bellewstown; raised 7lb.

OwnerName: John B O'Hagan & Mrs John Murphy
Spotlight: 5f Dundalk winner last season; stepped up on previous turf form when winning at Naas; more on his plate now; worth noting form was boosted by the third when scoring at Leopardstown on Thursday.

Nine-time winner, including five on turf; last won over 6f (good) here in May 2025; went close in a 21-runner 5f handicap at Naas three starts ago; faded late into fifth behind Sovereign Cry when favourite back at Naas last time.
Showed some promise in Britain at two; will need to have improved to feature here on debut for this stable.
Solid form in four runs on turf since an unproductive spell on AW; needs to find extra on the evidence of last Saturday's third at Limerick; previous third at this venue was over 7f.

Narrowly beaten in a 6f Dundalk maiden in April before winning over 5f there 13 days later; definite merit in handicap debut at Naas, close up until reportedly hitting a ridge over a furlong down, before rallying; went close in a C&D handicap before a solid third over 6f on latest; likely to make her presence felt.
Won two of her first three races at two in Britain; made low-key Irish debut at Down Royal; hard to be confident, but no surprise if she is competitive.
Won fillies' maiden at Dundalk last December; fair third at Down Royal on her sole 5f attempt; outstayed over 7f at Dundalk last Sunday.
Most recent of three wins came here nearly two years ago (6f, good-to-firm); has never run over this trip; hard to make a case for him.

OwnerName: Gary Devlin & Kevin Osborne & N W T Dalzell & Tracey Wylie
Spotlight: Finished off last year in fine form at Dundalk, backing up a nursery win with a short-head second in a conditions race; had previously finished second in two turf nurseries; was entitled to need last Sunday's Dundalk run when 4lb out of the handicap and slowly away; could be a different proposition now
Showed hints of ability in three maidens at 7f; second over 6f at Fairyhouse on handicap debut; not as good at the same venue last time; may find 5f too sharp.
Enjoyed a successful 2025, winning three sprint handicaps; yet to hit form this term; some sign of a revival in a 7f event at Fairyhouse ten days ago.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Took advantage of a declining mark to register her first AW/handicap win, at Southwell (5f) last month; hung right throughout when fourth of five at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) since; should not be far away if on her best behaviour.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Scored off a career-low mark to land his eighth success, at Epsom (6f, good to firm) nine days ago; back up 2lb but has recorded back-to-back wins previously so cannot be discounted.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins on AW; not beaten far when third over C&D in April but ran no sort of race when last of nine over C&D when last seen in May; another headgear switch and is becoming frustrating.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins have came on AW but has been placed on her last two runs on turf; needs a shade more to win but not out of this.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Summer Festival Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Landed a Wolverhampton maiden (6f, AW) in March; has been found wanting in six handicaps since but he wasn't disgraced at Newbury last week and is down to a career-low mark on the return to 5f; place claims.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: Out of a 7f winning half-sister to Group 3 scorer Breathtaking Look; well backed into 5-1 on Kempton debut (7f, AW) last month and he made a bold bid before finishing a clear second; that was a promising start and he sets a fair standard; key player.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Shaped with promise on his Salisbury debut (6f, good to firm) last month and he built on that when third of seven behind a smart rival at Ascot last Friday; was beaten around 6l in that race but he rallied in the closing stages and is open to more progress at this new trip; shortlisted.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5-1 on Kempton debut (7f, AW) last month but he faded into sixth of 11 and was almost 8l behind Sanbona Warrior; should benefit from that experience but he needs a transformation on his second start.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; second foal; dam unraced half-sister to smart French 1m/1m1f winner Kokaltash, out of French 1m3f winner from family of Derby winner High Chaparral; yard 18% with 2yos this season and he needs watching in the market on debut.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 43,000euros yearling, £48,000 breeze-up 2yo; thirteenth foal; brother to 6f AW winner Elvetham (RPR 66), half-brother to four Flat winners including Dragoon Guard (8.6f AW 2yo; 84) and Gertcha (1m AW; 73); dam placed 12.5f in France, half-sister to smart 6f-1m4f winner Mons; interesting newcomer and he needs a close look for top yard.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 120,000euros foal, 42,000gns yearling; closely related to winners Madeline (6f 2yo including Listed; RPR 105) and Tiberia (French 7f 2yo), half-brother to 10.5f-1m6f winner Adeline (93); dam Swiss 1m1f-1m4f winner, sister to French 6f/7f Listed winner Dolma; already been gelded and market should guide on debut.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5,000gns foal; third foal; dam unraced sister to 1m4f winners La Joya and Empyrea, out of useful maiden half-sister to 7f/1m Group 1 winner Belardo; has good standard to aim at on debut and he could be a longer-term prospect.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well held at a big price on Redcar debut (6f, good) last month and same story at Thirsk 17 days ago; has lots to find upped in trip and nurseries will be more suitable.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: RPRs in the 50s when well held in 6f novice events at Nottingham (good) and Wolverhampton (AW) last month; hood is now added and he needs lots of improvement upped in trip.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 66-1 and she didn't show much after a slow start at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago; best watched.
Highly tried after winning a York maiden (6f, good to firm) and a Newbury novice (6f, good) last season; gelded in November; disappointing this season; first run at 7f.

Lightly raced 6yo who hasn't won on turf since May 2024, when dead-heating at Thirsk (7f, good to firm); down the field in two decent handicaps this season but beaten less than 6l on each occasion and takes a significant drop in grade; has to be considered.

Newmarket maiden winner for Harry Charlton last August (6f, good to firm); subsequently sold for 90,000gns; best run for the Faheys when third at Chester last time; (7f, good); on a fair mark; a possible.

Four wins over 7f/1m, two on the AW; fair third at Newmarket in April (1m, good) but not so good since; acts on any ground although withdrawn on account of the going (officially good to firm) last time.
In good form last June, winning off this mark over C&D (good) before an excellent second at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm); some fair efforts this season and on a good mark now; not out of it.
Won a maiden on turf (1m, good to soft) in 2023, but his other wins have been on the AW; beaten only 2l when seventh of 11 over  C&D last time; each-way chance.

Made a winning debut in the Hilary Needler at Beverley two years ago (5f, good to firm) but hasn't won since; fair second in a Thirsk fillies' handicap two runs ago (1m, good) but well beaten at Royal Ascot last time.
Two novice wins over 6f last term (good); best run this term when second in a York handicap in May (7f, good); disappointing since; fast ground is a concern.

OwnerName: D J Cash & Mrs E Cash Racing
Spotlight: Won over 6f at Haydock in May 2025 (good) and a couple of fair runs over 7f after that; acts on fast ground but he lacks a recent run (has been off since October).

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Ran three sound races in June, notably when 0.75l third over C&D (good to firm) then beaten a head at Bath next time (1m, good); below par on AW latest but has an each-way chance back on turf.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: All three wins have been over 7f/1m on good/good to firm at Brighton; has finished second over 7f/1m there in blinkers on last three runs; each-way chance.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Back to form when winning at Redcar in June (7f, good) and finished a sound third off 6lb higher at Beverley last time (7.5f, good to firm); down 1lb; a possible.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-Sir Mark Prescott; beaten more than 8l in two starts for Brian Ellison this term, over 1m at Redcar and Ripon; bit to prove.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: 13-race maiden; two decent seconds this season, including last time when beaten 1.25l in a 6f handicap at Pontefract (good; ran on well in closing stages); interesting on first try at 7f.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Only turf win was at Yarmouth on his debut in 2019 (6f, good to firm); best runs this season have been over 6f/7f here, including last time when 2.5l fourth over 6f; each-way chance.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Both turf wins have been over C&D on good to firm, the latest last August; close third to a subsequent winner at Yarmouth last time (7f, good to firm) and has a fair chance here.

RaceName: Summer Fun At Lakeside Village Outlet Shopping Handicap
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden; showed some promise for Seb Spencer but well beaten on last three starts; makes stable debut after a 173-day break.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Off the mark when making all in a novice at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) in April; runner-up in two of her three handicaps since but she was no match for the winner at Salisbury (1m2f, soft) last time; still lightly raced but she needs more improvement at this new trip.

OwnerName: W G & A G Vestey, E Gerber And P Inglett
Spotlight: 0-6 but he went close in a Thirsk handicap (1m4f, good) in May and backed that up with a creditable third in similar conditions at Goodwood last month; on the same mark as last time and he should be in the mix again; cheekpieces added.

0-7 but he ran well upped to 1m4f when a staying-on second in an Epsom handicap (good to firm) last week; hit a personal best behind an unexposed rival in that race and he's respected off the same mark.

Failed to beat a rival in three of his four runs including when last of six on handicap debut at Nottingham (1m2f, good; first run since gelded) last month; still early days but he needs a transformation on this step up to 1m4f; cheekpieces added.

200,000gns breeze-up 2yo; well held in her first four starts but she found lots of improvement upped to 1m4f when an easy winner of a Ffos Las handicap (good to soft) last month; this is a different test on quicker ground but a 6lb rise looks fair and she's a half-sister to a Listed winner on good to firm; major player.
1-27 on turf; has a chance on his head second at Musselburgh in June (1m, good) but well beaten back on the AW last time.

OwnerName: MDP Racing And Mrs R Carr
Spotlight: Off the mark on first run over 1m at Leicester (good to firm) two weeks ago, despite not getting the best of runs; should go well again off 2lb higher.
Two of three wins over 1m2f at Beverley, the latest in May 2025; some fair efforts at 1m-1m4f this season; on a decent mark now.
C&D winner off 1lb lower last July (good); best run this term when runner-up to a subsequent winner at Beverley last time (7.5f, good to firm; fifth has also won since); solid chance.
Won at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) in May and over C&D in June (good to soft; 18-runner handicap); beaten 8l on AW last time; could bounce back.
Record of 1-21, the win in September 2022; fair fourth over 7f at Redcar two runs back, but not so good there next time (1m); others preferred.
Two wins last season, the first over 1m at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm); two heavy defeats on turf this season (beaten 23l at Yarmouth last time); returns after a 59-day break.

In good form, winning at Ripon (1m, good) and Beverley (8.5f, good to firm) before a decent third off this mark (10lb higher than second win) back at Beverley last time (8.5f, good to firm); should go well.

Ex-Katie Scott; off the mark on stable debut at Yarmouth last August (7f, good to firm); tailed off over 6f on reappearance in June on first run since; now tries 1m again (well beaten two previous attempts at the trip).
Ten-race maiden; creditable fifth of seven in first-time blinkers at Yarmouth last time (1m, good to firm); headgear retained; each-way chance.
Both turf wins have been at 1m on good to firm; has won twice in blinkers on AW this year; although not in top form last twice, these conditions are ideal and could go well on this return to turf.

0-6 but she ran her best race so far when close second in a Sandown handicap (1m6f, good) two weeks ago; has shaped as though this step up to 2m should be fine and she's strongly respected off only 1lb higher than last time.

Dam is related to St Leger winner Hurricane Lane and Group-class stayer Sweet William; consistent form in her first five starts but she raised her game upped to 1m4f when runner-up in an Epsom handicap (good) 17 days ago; nudged up 2lb but she kept on well and is open to more progress now switched to a staying trip; needs a close look.

Big improver over hurdles and he made it 5-8 in that sphere when completing a hat-trick at Perth (2m, good) two weeks ago; looks interesting off dangerous mark on the Flat and he won over 1m7f in France as a 3yo.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Progressive form over shorter, winning a maiden over an extended 2m at Kilbeggan (good to yielding); weakened over 2m4f next time and then ran poorly at 3m; strong form claims if he can prove himself over this far.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Cherry Knoll Farm, M Ward & D Skelton
Spotlight: Doubly penalised for winning a match at Huntingdon (2m4f145yds) and a weak race at Uttoxeter (2m; again on good), since when he's undergone wind surgery; hasn't been beating a lot but he's probably progressive.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Went close in two bumpers and was pulled up sharply on hurdle debut when jockey felt something was amiss; has since left David Pipe; bred to improve for this longer distance but he needs to.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Bumper winner who made all in a Kelso novice hurdle (2m, good); came up shy under a penalty at Hexham but was clear of the rest in chasing home the odds-on favourite; steps up in distance this afternoon.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 0-22 in points and now 0-18 under rules (0-14 over fences) after finishing a tailed-off runner-up in a novice hurdle at Newton Abbot.

RaceName: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 0-11 on the Flat and has been contesting low-grade handicaps at about 2m; unlikely to be winning this on hurdle debut.

Useful Flat performer and also 2-15 as a hurdler (regularly placed); left Harry Fry for £15,000 and was a 6l third over 1m4f at York on last week's stable debut (no headgear); first-time visored now (effective in tongue-tie/cheekpieces).

Best on good ground as he showed when running away with the Sussex Champion Hurdle at Plumpton in April; however, that came at a cost to the tune of 10lb and he failed to fire behind Moon Chime in the Swinton; others might be better in here.

1m4f winner who has gone 3-4 over hurdles for Tom Lacey and easily won on handicap debut last time at Southwell (good; second run in this headgear combination), albeit against only four rivals; up 8lb but has momentum behind him.
Contrasting performances at Newton Abbot last month, winning well but then finishing last of four; cheekpieces fitted for this much tougher test.
Record of 4-7 over hurdles but this is tougher than usual and he could have run a lot better back from a break at Newton Abbot; others appeal more.

OwnerName: DL Adams, JA Adams & G McPherson
Spotlight: 2-3 in bumpers and 5-11 over hurdles after leading late on in the Swinton (good); that was in a first-time tongue-tie that was also on when winning a 2m AW handicap in late May; off just 4lb higher than at Haydock, he's very much in the mix.

Unexposed 5yo who makes his handicap debut after easy odds-on wins on good ground at Warwick and Stratford, posting an eye-catching RPR last time when barely put through the gears; could easily be on a lenient mark.

Back from a long absence to justify favouritism at Perth in April (2m4f, good) where she came from off the pace to hit the front when left clear at the last; up 6lb but consistent in the main and wouldn't be exposed just yet.
Three hurdle wins at around 2m; has been running well in defeat this summer (2m-2m4f), mostly in a hood but in no headgear last time; cheekpieces now added; others are more compelling.

Useful Flat form in France; after winning a maiden hurdle for Willie Mullins he was essentially disappointing under both codes and has got nothing going for Dan Skelton, with his latest run after wind surgery at Newton Abbot thoroughly underwhelming (8-1 and weak in the betting); very much the stable second string.
Changed hands in March after winning a claimer; only four ran when a half-length runner-up here a month ago; opposable at this level.

Front runner; 2-8 over hurdles and returns to this discipline off a good mark having completed a hat-trick over fences three weeks ago off 4lb higher; has found his best form since joining this yard in January and this track should suit him well.

Lightly raced winning hurdler in France; had a wind operation prior to posting career-best form when a fast-closing second at Ascot in March; up 4lb but has his age allowance now tackling his elders and also the assistance of Harry Cobden.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 1-7 over fences; gifted a walkover before finishing second in a four-runner handicap at Uttoxeter where he failed to fire when favourite for their Summer Cup 20 days ago; he's better than that and further progress is possible with cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Clearcut winner on chase debut (2m4f, good) on final run for Rebecca Menzies and similar sort of form in defeat in two runs for the Skeltons, last time pushing earlier-race contender Newton Rambler all the way back over 2m at Uttoxeter; returning to further looks a plus and this hold-up performer should have this run to suit him.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Win/placed form in his usual cheekpieces before making all for a narrow success in the newly fitted visor (with tongue-tie worn for last seven starts) at Cartmel (2m5f, good); he's getting high in the weights now (raised another 4lb) and he won't be the only one racing prominently.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: C Nightingale & Hold My Beer Partnership
Spotlight: Very capable prominent racer on his day and he had one of those in winning by 2l over C&D a month ago; 4lb rise elevates him to a career-high mark and he won't be the only one putting pace to the race.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Consistent chaser who was better than ever in dominating a small field at Fakenham two runs back (2m5f185yds, good); didn't run badly in defeat last time and off a light weight he could have a part to play.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Two good runs in defeat at 3m before coming down at the Canal Turn in the Topham Trophy; went close to winning this two years ago and that was after a two-month break; definite possibilities, as this mark isn't beyond him; Harry Cobden has won the last three renewals of this race.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: In a solid run of form but this is a tough mark for an exposed 9yo and he's undergone a fourth wind operation since finishing fifth at Perth in early June.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Useful Flat and hurdles performer who has gone 0-5 over fences since a winning start in May 2025 and he'll need to run better than he did in a handicap chase at Ballinrobe last time; however, a case can be made off this mark on best form; versatile trip-wise from 2m to beyond 3m.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Three wins at around 2m4f last season, all in small fields on good ground; after some blips he got himself back on track when second to a well-handicapped horse over C&D a month ago on first visit here; likely to run well with Shane Fenelon now taking off 5lb; one of three runners for a yard that's captured this eight times.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Wasn't disgraced in finishing third of six over 2m4f at Uttoxeter on stable debut but he's not as good as he was and an 11yo now.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: His defeat of the smart Jesse Evans at Sligo in October heightens interest and new headgear is tried after two lesser efforts, particularly the latest; he has become hard to predict but it's unwise to put a line through him.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ex-Gordon Elliott; made a successful handicap chase debut for this yard at Ffos Las (2m3f, soft) in January but up and down since, with recent thirds just okay efforts (latest in this new headgear combination when behind Breizh River); may prefer softer ground ideally.

RaceName: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Hurdle/chase winner who has won four times on the Flat since moving to current yard earlier this year; lacks recent match practice over jumps and that could count against him in this competitive a race.

RaceName: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Race-fit off the Flat when a battling winner over a little shorter at Worcester a month ago (visor back on) and looks a good thing to give his running once more off 4lb higher; respected.

RaceName: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Only win in 12 hurdle starts was a maiden; likes to crack on with things and probably went off a bit too hot when a well-held fourth at Cartmel (2m1f; after 99 days off); has another front-runner to deal with in Hello Sweety, but the ability is there to win off this mark.

RaceName: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Small fields suit this free-going mare, as do sharp, flat tracks; perhaps on a fairly tough mark after coming up short last time but shouldn't be far away.

RaceName: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual AW winner who is 0-7 over hurdles; good first run in cheekpieces when second at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft) but never got involved the last time (2m6f); perhaps a fast-run race back at this distance will benefit her.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 0-18 under rules but he was an easy winner of an Irish point in May; well held back over regulation fences at Uttoxeter (3m, good) last month but he took a strong hold and ran well to a point in that race; could benefit from this drop back in trip and it wouldn't be a surprise if he was in the mix.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who scored over fences at Sedgefield (2m, good to soft) last December but he hasn't really fired in his last three runs; chase record is now 1-11 and others are more persuasive.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Hard Held Partnership And Angus Racing
Spotlight: Ended last year with a brave win at Catterick (1m7f, good to soft) but he's not gone on from that in two runs this summer; needs to raise his game but he's now only 1lb higher than for his last success and his first two chase wins were over C&D (good).

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Triple chase winner including over C&D but he's been beaten 35l in both runs since returning from an absence in May; has something to prove and he needs a major revival.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won a C&D handicap in April and was runner-up at Southwell last month but he's not easy to predict and was well below form at Stratford last time; that took his chase record to 1-15 and he needs to bounce back again.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
OwnerName: M Enticott / Ella Pickard Racing Club
Spotlight: Sole success was at Stratford (2m1f, good) last May and she's been out of sorts in her last seven starts; 5lb out of the weights this time and she has a lot to prove.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Flat winner who is 0-6 over hurdles but he won on chase debut at Fakenham (2m, good) in May before a creditable third at Uttoxeter 11 days ago; did well to hang in there after being pestered for the lead last time and he's been an improved performer since switched to fences; respected.

RaceName: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won an Irish point on yielding ground in March; struggled in hunter chases in next four runs but he was an eye-catching fourth on handicap debut at Wexford (2m3f, good) two weeks ago; needs to build on that but he's still lightly raced and should have more to offer in this sphere.

OwnerName: Readers & Wiggy, The 8 Amigos & J Burns
Spotlight: Six of his nine wins have come at Market Rasen including over C&D; only 1lb higher than for his win at Wetherby in March but he's been vulnerable in three runs since and needs to rediscover his spark.

Career has had its ups and downs but he won two chases (3m1f and 3m6f) in March 2025 and he's been placed at Stratford (second of five) and Worcester (third of 11) in his last two runs; remains well treated off 10lb lower than his last success and he's in the mix back up in trip.
Just 1-11 in British points but she's shown some ability in novice/maiden hurdles this year; now makes her handicap/chase debut and she needs checking in market on this big step back up in trip.

Won over hurdles at Hexham (2m4f, good) and Musselburgh (3m, soft) last season; only 1lb higher than for his last success but he's struggled in his last three runs and has something to prove on chase debut.

Appreciated the step back up to 3m when winning at Warwick (good) in May but he was a well-held fourth when favourite at Worcester (2m7f) last month; has bit to prove again after that and this is competitive.

6yo who made it 4-10 over fences when completing a double with his late thrust at Hexham (3m, good) last month; up 3lb but he's been as good as ever in his last two starts and he's strong stayer as this trip; key player.

Made it 3-5 over fences when scoring at Bangor (3m, good) in May and he went very close behind his main market rival at Fontwell four weeks later; up another 2lb but he still looks on a workable mark and is open to more progress as a chaser; respected.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Bumper winner who is 0-9 over hurdles but has been bang there in his last two races, over C&D and 2m7f at Worcester; raised 3lb but he enters the reckoning.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has returned from a break in good form, winning back-to-back Class 5 handicaps at about 2m4f on good ground (the first here); remains on a fair mark but this is a better race and a competitive one.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Ursa Major Ltd & Hicky Parmar Racing
Spotlight: Four-time hurdle winner who was second in a Cheltenham handicap last October on final jumps run; 2lb lower now and he was a recent 2m winner at Newmarket; should go well.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had a lengthy break after her breakthrough win but better than ever a month ago when breezing home off 9lb lower over C&D; something seems to have clicked.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Inconsistent 9yo who kept on for third at Uttoxeter (2m4f) without threatening; others preferred.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Joined Fergal O'Brien after finishing well beaten in a selling handicap; dropped to a good mark on best form and prevailed in a tight finish at Worcester 17 days ago (2m); respected off 4lb higher.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Hard-fought win back over hurdles at Hexham (2m) before a 10l defeat returned to fences; no great significance in the return of cheekpieces (blinkered last two races) but entitled to have some say.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Fontwell maiden winner last April; some good runs since in cheekpieces and the visor tried last time is soon dispensed with; could feature off what should be a good mark.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: All of his seven wins have been at either Hexham or here, so merits attention after finishing a close third at Uttoxeter a month ago; 2lb below last winning mark.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up in a bumper for former Irish yard; three heavy defeats in four runs for current one and was tailed off on handicap debut; has since had a wind operation and now goes in cheekpieces.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who has run well in all four handicaps; may need another jolt of improvement to defy current mark but now tries cheekpieces.

RaceName: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 5lb higher than for his runaway win at Hereford (2m; handicap debut); fell early next time and then only fourth of the five runners at Worcester; probably needs his best yet here but it's still early days.

Went close when bidding for a second win in the Group 3 Diomed at Epsom (8.5f) in June, back to his best; respectable efforts over 1m2f since at Royal Ascot (good to firm; just over 3l ahead of Arabian Light) and Sandown (good) suggest he won't be far away.

Group 2 Great Voltigeur entry; French Group 3 winner (1m, soft) last September; well behind Al Zanati in the Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f, good) on reappearance but resumed improvement with a big run at 80-1 in Group 3 at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) one month ago, keeping on admirably for a close fourth of ten; better still may be needed in today's first-time headgear but he's in calculations.

Success at Meydan early this year was followed by a creditable return to Britain, then a lesser show at Royal Ascot; the same happened in 2025, preceding another below-form effort in July, so that has to be a worry even though best efforts would see him on the premises; William Buick seemingly prefers Al Zanati.

Won his first three races in France last year (twice from the front) and just 9-1 when brought over for the Derby but faded badly into tenth; just useful form since, best of three runs for new yard when 3l fourth of six in a Listed race at Goodwood (1m4f, soft) last time but he needs markedly better than that.

Won debut last August and a 1m1f AW Group 3 at Chantilly in November; runner-up in British Group 3s in two other starts, one on good to firm last October and the other in Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f) this April; that's not the best form in this field and he wasn't so good in the Dante at York in May on latest outing, but this lightly raced 3yo could still bring potential and William Buick seemingly prefers him to Arabian Light.

Pretty consistent in seven AW runs and well backed when leading final 1f to win the 17-runner Chester Plate (2m2f, good) in May on return to turf; failed to live up to favouritism in another consolation race at Newcastle (2m Vase, AW) three weeks ago but that sixth of 20 off this mark was his best form, so he remains one to be interested in.

With tongue-tie enlisted he's hit major new heights for new yard this year, with two wins preceding his excellent fifth of 15 in the 2m2f Chester Cup; comes from off the pace but never got seriously involved wearing first-time cheekpieces when ninth of 20 as second favourite in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (2m); needs to bounce back from that pretty disappointing show.

Maiden winner who's been on the premises in all his five handicaps, albeit managing only sixth of 20 from midfield when clear favourite for the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (upped to 2m) last time on AW debut; no handicap win but he's been pretty reliable and this race is a lot less competitive.

Only 1-10 for Dermot Weld but was highly tried on occasions; made most from wide draw in major handicaps on both starts for Richard Hughes, reeled in late on when third in the Chester Cup (2m2f, good) but backpedalling before the home straight at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm); big shout if he reverts to the Chester performance.

Made most for two game wins in four-runner C&D races (good to firm) last summer, latterly in this race off 2lb higher than today; second to Baileys Khelstar over C&D on latest outing was in just a three-runner race but easily his best Flat effort this year, so he could be on his way back.

OwnerName: Baileys Horse Feeds (F H Nash Ltd)
Spotlight: Gained a deserved first success of the season in three-runner handicap over C&D (good to firm; from Almuhit) last month and got up close home in nine-runner race at Kempton (2m, AW) ten days ago; up 3lb to career-high mark but he's on a roll.

OwnerName: J William Rowley & S P C Woods
Spotlight: Progressive on AW last autumn and he's been a bit better this season too; won five-runner race at Goodwood (upped to 2m, good) in May and, having been mid-division at Royal Ascot (2m4f), made most when fifth of 20 in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (2m, AW); in the mix.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Still below best when third at Newcastle (AW debut) last time but that was something of resurgence; progressive spell culminated in wins over C&D (Listed) and at Haydock (Group 2) in May 2025; possibilities provided he returns to that sort of form.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Very lightly raced in recent times but latest effort, namely fifth in the Wokingham, suggests he retains a very useful level of ability aged seven; however, needs to prove he's still capable of peak form, which includes Group wins at Newbury and the Curragh.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Ex-Irish 5yo who has low mileage and progressive form; record since switched to turf and dropped to 6f reads 233; has performed well in Listed event at Salisbury and the Wokingham at Royal Ascot for new yard; already very useful and warrants respect with further progress plausible.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Broadly progressive 4yo whose form in notable handicaps suggests he could develop into a Group horse; went close on reappearance in his bid for a York double, then finished a respectable sixth when favourite for the Wokingham at Royal Ascot; remains of major interest.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Has an underwhelming strike-rate for a horse of his ability and losing spell goes back over two years; that said, has spent over half of his career in Group 1 races, best effort when third in the 2024 Commonwealth Cup; drops back in class after a heavy defeat at this year's Royal Ascot.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Clear best in the 2025 Jersey at Royal Ascot (7f) but was pulled up (lost action) in only subsequent start last term and has failed to show his form this year; drop back to 6f had no effect last time; enough to prove.

RaceName: Hallgarten And Novum Wines Hackwood Stakes (Group 3)
OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Cxx & M Parker
Spotlight: Sole 3yo in this field; largely progressive colt whose form features wins in York sales race as a 2yo and C&D Listed event on penultimate outing; creditable seventh in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot latest; may have more to offer back down in class; major player.

Justified favouritism with something to spare at Yarmouth (good to firm) in latest 6f start, building on her debut promise; gives the impression she'll be as effective over 5f and should have more to offer; helps to give her connections, who also run Etienne, an interesting hand.

Harry Angel filly who is hitherto her trainer's only 2yo runner this year and bids to take her record to 2-2; won only an ordinary maiden at Chepstow (5f, soft) but is open to progress and gets in here off an attractive weight; one to consider.
Absent and gelded since a rather disappointing effort in the Lily Agnes at Chester, failing to back up April promise that featured a comfortable win at Wolverhampton (5f, AW); something to prove.

By a Coventry winner for his connections; posted a promising effort in tight finish at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) where he split a couple of rivals who had the benefit of experience; one of the bigger players at the weights and has possibilities with progress on the cards.

Started favourite for two Leicester maidens (5f, good to firm) in the spring, making all and nicely on top at the finish last time; comes back fresh for a crack at this bigger prize, looks likely to show further improvement and represents a trainer who has a growing tally in sales races; interesting contender.

Represents a trainer who landed this prize in 2022; campaigned non-domestically since scoring at Redcar on debut; ran well in French Listed races (5f) the last twice, good third at Deauville latest occasion; major contender provided that form is transferred back to home soil.
Has failed to show progress in two starts since prevailing narrowly at Musselburgh (5f); fitting of hood needs to have a major effect on these difficult terms.
Won on debut then ran well when favourite for the Lily Agnes at Chester; however, his form has dipped markedly in two starts since, gelded prior to nursery defeat latest; huge turnaround is required.

Failed to beat a rival at Royal Ascot but is a progressive 5f filly otherwise and registered a half-length success in Sandown Listed event (good) most recently, taking record to 2-4; sole attempt under William Buick resulted in the earlier win; leading player even with a 5lb penalty.
Gradually getting the hang of things but RPRs in the 50s reflect that he holds modest claims in this field and would have been more interesting in a low-grade handicap.

Has shown significant promise in Goodwood races, finishing second over 5f (good) then going one better in clearcut fashion over 6f (soft); open to further improvement and is the Hannon first string on form and jockey arrangements; yard has a great record in this race; shortlisted.

Ran as if something perhaps went amiss when co-favourite for the Sandown Listed contest won by Bint Archange last time; now goes in tongue-tie and may resume the steady progress that culminated in a Bath maiden success (5.7f, good); remains of interest.
Ran creditably at Yarmouth last week when bidding for a 5f nursery double; beat Past Passion at Nottingham the time before; remains in form but faces a much stiffer assignment on these terms.
Maintained consistency by finishing a good second to Holi Scarlett in Nottingham nursery last time; however, both fillies face a markedly tougher task in this field.
Four-race maiden whose form includes a couple of second-place finishes but who hasn't progressed and still needs to learn to relax, having failed to settle when posting her lesser efforts.
Has posted similar efforts in 5f novice events, finishing fourth both times, latest at Windsor; a nursery would have been more suitable than this assignment, as a mark of 65 reflects.
Won at Thirsk (5f) on debut; down the field in notable races since, latest at Royal Ascot, and still needs to prove she's capable of progress; however, these terms may enable her to prove resurgent.
Thrice-raced filly who has consistent form but played second fiddle in a Goodwood seller (5f) most recently and looks well out of her depth in this much deeper company.

Similar type to stablemate Final Appeal, being a thrice-raced contender who proved disappointing when last seen; however, made all at Thirsk (5f, good) the time before and may still do better; rating suggests she's no forlorn hope at the weights.

Gained valuable experience for a scenario of this nature by finishing second in big field at Newbury (6f, good to firm; well-supported favourite) last week, backing up the promise of his eye-catching effort at Windsor (5f); still open to progress and looks likely to go well.
Thrice-raced filly who posted clear best effort in sole AW attempt; has something to prove and a lot to find.

Proving consistent, as a series of placed efforts reflect; however, chance of overcoming a difficult task at the weights depends on the effects of first-time headgear and return to 5f for first time since debut.

Faces a stiff task off top weight in this field, based on his spring form; however, may improve for physical tweak (gelded since last run) and he represents a yard that has an excellent record in the Super Sprint; market support should be heeded.
Gives the impression she may benefit from this drop in distance but not the rise in grade; holds very weak claims on her 6f form.

RaceName: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 650,000gns yearling by Night Of Thunder; readily made a winning debut at Leicester (7f, good to soft) last September; 5-4 favourite when hooded for a novice here (1m1f, good to soft) five weeks ago and always prominent before losing out by half a length; that rival was making her debut but Miss Scott is weighted to turn the tables today.

RaceName: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 370,000gns yearling by St Mark's Basilica, half-sister to the stable's prolific winner Dubai Honour (1m-1m4f including Group 1); 8-1 for novice here (1m1f, good to soft) five weeks ago, coming from midfield to beat Miss Scott by half a length as the pair drew clear; 7lb worse off with that rival today but that debut win for this filly was full of promise.

RaceName: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 110,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; 17-2 from 11-1 for a conditions stakes here (7f, good to soft) last September when a close third of seven, always prominent; that was a bright start against fairly useful opposition, which earns respect despite her coming from a speedy family.

RaceName: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
