Spotlight: 85,000euros yearling by Sea The Stars; 80-1 and never dangerous in novice here (1m1f, good to soft) five weeks ago; should improve but she has about 9l to find with Manaar and Miss Scott.

RaceName: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 33-1 when sixth of seven at Nottingham (1m, good to soft) in October and last of four at Lingfield (1m2f, good) this May; early days but that's modest maiden form.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Xvii & M Parker
Spotlight: Incurs 4lb penalty for a Windsor success (6f, good to firm; made all) that hasn't worked out well but brings upside, being a once-raced colt who is in good hands and may progress.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Naval Crown colt who showed promise with close fifth of 11 at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) having attracted support; possibilities with progress on the cards.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Finished second of four in Yarmouth maiden (6f, good to firm) won by fellow newcomer who was odds-on and looks a useful prospect; respected assuming he builds on that promise.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 100,000gns yearling; by Mehmas and first foal of Listed-placed 5f/6f 2yo winner (RPR 94), from family of top miler Attraction; stablemate of once-raced Can't Stop; market instructive.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Brings the worst form, having finished last of seven in 6f contest on the turf course at Lingfield; gelded since; perhaps best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 150,000euros foal, 90,000gns yearling, 140,000gns (brreeze-up) 2yo; Starspangledbanner half-brother to four winners, notably Harrow (Group-placed 6.5f-7.3f 2yo; RPR 102); dam 5f AW winner (67); interesting newcomer.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 27,000euros foal, 55,000euros yearling; Naval Crown half-brother to three winners, notably Romanovich (7f-8.6f; RPR 67); dam maiden (75); yard first string on jockey arrangements; betting may give further guidance.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 120,000euros yearling, 370,000euros (breeze-up) 2yo; by Too Darn Hot; sibling to winners in Poland and Sweden; dam unraced, out of Oaks/King George winner Taghrooda; looks the pick of the debutants.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 55,000gns yearling; Mattmu half-brother to two winners, notably Anaisa (5f/6f 2yo including Listed; RPR 80); dam 1m1f winner (78); the stable second string on jockey arrangements.

RaceName: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 11,000gns foal, 60,000gns yearling; Harry Angel half-brother to six winners. notably Hoodwinker (1m-1m2f inc AW 2yo; RPR 92); dam unraced; notable connections; heed the market signals.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Hindered by unfavourable draw (fared best in her group) at Royal Ascot last time; progressive on AW otherwise, posting form figures of 3111, and may still have more to offer; remains of interest, assuming she can prove as effective on turf.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Not particularly solid on her 1m form this term but wasn't entirely disgraced at Royal Ascot on penultimate start; appears likely to benefit from this drop back in trip/class and return to the scene of one of her 2yo wins; could go well.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Justified favouritism in another Class 5 event last week, taking Catterick record to 3-3 and strike-rate since handicapping to 4-6; Newmarket win shows she's versatile as regards track; upped in class but receives weight all round and possibly hasn't stopped improving yet.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Has a record of 0-5 since debut success (6f) but she ran encouragingly upped in trip and fitted with a hood at Newmarket (good to firm) most recently; may build on that effort kept to 7f in the retained headgear; now 5lb lower than her opening mark; respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

RaceName: Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

Didn't build on a promising start on AW last spring, including well held in 1m Haydock handicap (good to soft) on sole turf start; has been gelded and had a second wind operation ahead of this return from eight months off; it's still early days but his profile isn't compelling.

OwnerName: J Morley D Reynolds C Watkins & Partner

Runner-up for the third time in five starts since joining John Butler when best of the rest behind the well-treated Ancient State (won next time) in 16-runner race over C&D (good) 29 days ago; same mark today.

Took 17 attempts to get off the mark but now on a four-timer after wins at Leicester (twice) and Nottingham in recent months (all 6f on good/good to firm); only up another 2lb and merits plenty of respect in his current mood.

OwnerName: J P Morris, Mrs V A Tunnicliffe Et Al

Goes well on both Newmarket courses, including a win in this race on good to firm two years ago; good third over C&D last month but behind Yes I'm Mali when only sixth back here a fortnight ago.

6-21 on AW but still seeking a first turf win after 15 attempts; latest Thirsk fourth (6f, good to firm) as good as anything he's produced on the grass but may find at least the odd one too strong again.

Kempton novice win (6f, AW) for Oliver Cole last October; respectable efforts in 6f/7f handicaps for new yard this year and first-time cheekpieces won't need to give him too much extra having been eased a further 2lb.

Winner over 1m on AW at Chantilly at the end of 2025 but below par on completed outing there (unseated start second occasion) at the beginning of 2026; well held over hurdles at Dieppe (2m1f, soft) in April (only start for Noel George & Amanda Zetterholm) and can only really watch dropped to sprinting for another new yard.

RaceName: National Stud 'Confined' Handicap (For Horses With No More Than One Win)
Spotlight: Showed just modest form as a juvenile and she was beaten a fair way out on comeback in her first handicap, on Wolverhampton AW in first-time cheekpieces; upped to 1m2f with plenty to find.

RaceName: National Stud 'Confined' Handicap (For Horses With No More Than One Win)
Spotlight: Step forward when keeping on at one pace in first handicap, on Lingfield AW (1m) in January; off the track and gelded after but he came home with a wet sail when a close third of six at Salisbury (1m, good to firm) recently; looks well worth a go at 1m2f; respected.

RaceName: National Stud 'Confined' Handicap (For Horses With No More Than One Win)

RaceName: National Stud 'Confined' Handicap (For Horses With No More Than One Win)
Spotlight: He's been up against some good rivals in his qualifying runs but has shown signs of ability and there's every chance he'll give a good show now switched to this new level.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap
Spotlight: Had some good 2yo form, as when winning both starts at about 7f, and this campaign has a somewhat luckless look to it so far, albeit slow starts aren't helping; his one start over 1m, in a valuable Carlisle handicap in May, was inconclusive regarding stamina but he remains of interest.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap
Spotlight: Impressive winner of two of his three AW handicaps as 2yo, at 7f and 1m, and his reappearance fifth of nine on the Rowley course (1m, good to firm) in May hinted at better to come; never reached a challenging position over C&D in June but has less to do this time; has to be considered.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins at 1m2f in 2024 but he has run well over this C&D and, after a slow start to the year, he showed more when a close third of eight at Ascot (1m, good to firm) last week; on the premises again.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap
Spotlight: A stout stayer over 1m and Salisbury's stiff test suited him in May (good) where he overcame trouble in running to lead near the line; has had excuses since but he has a good run in him if this is truly run.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap
Spotlight: Turf wins at 7f and latest success was over 6f on AW in April; has rarely tackled 1m and she was highly tried over this trip in the Kensington Palace at Royal Ascot in June but she did look to stay an extended 1m at Nottingham in 2025 for previous yard; has possibilities.

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)

RaceName: Follow @racingtv On X Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The RE Series)
Spotlight: Both wins were on AW last summer when trained by Hugo Palmer; decent second at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) last month but below that level at Carlisle and Ripon since; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Racing TV Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Racing TV Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Racing TV Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Racing TV Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Displayed a good attitude to lead again over 1f out after attempting to make all, only to be denied close home at Kempton (6f, AW) last month on debut; first start on turf and looks sure to run well.

RaceName: Racing TV Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Download The Free Racing TV App Now Fillies' Handicap

RaceName: Download The Free Racing TV App Now Fillies' Handicap

RaceName: Download The Free Racing TV App Now Fillies' Handicap

RaceName: Download The Free Racing TV App Now Fillies' Handicap

Consistent maiden but has been favourite three times; ran his best race last time when runner-up at Newbury (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago; steps up in trip and should not be far away.

Performed with credit when runner-up on her second start, at Southwell (1m, AW) in January; comfortably held in two turf maidens on soft last month; needs to show more on this sounder surface on her handicap debut.

RaceName: Join Racing TV Now Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has finished second on all of her three starts this year, going down by a neck at Sandown (1m, good) 15 days ago on her handicap debut; this looks a good opportunity for her to get off the mark.

RaceName: Join Racing TV Now Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made the frame for the first time when fourth on her handicap debut at Sandown (1m, good) last month; probably best chance of first success would be to go back down that route.

RaceName: Join Racing TV Now Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Took a step forward from her debut when runner-up to an easy winner at Pontefract (1m, good) last month; going the right way and holds claims.

Spotlight: 730,000euros yearling; first foal; by Sea The Stars; dam unraced half-sister to winners The Fugue (multiple 1m2f/1m4f Group 1s) and Excellency (Group-placed 1m, by Sea The Stars), out of useful 1m1f winning half-sister to Group 1 winners Summoner (QEII) and Compton Admiral (Eclipse); has an exemplary pedigree and should make an impact on this debut; stable also has Effetto entered.

RaceName: Join Racing TV Now Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 12,000euros yearling; 30,000euros breeze-up 2yo; fifth foal; by Galiway; half-sister to winners Energia Tourismo (French 12.5f/14.5f), Kentucky Go Go (US 1m turf) and British Crown (Canadian 6.5f turf); dam 5f-1m4f winner (including 2yo/Group 3/Brazilian Grade 1; RPR 108); yard going great guns, especially with their 3yos, so she must be of interest on debut; stable also has Stellar entered.

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice in Britain for current yard since winning twice in France; however, beaten 21l at Leicester (1m2f, good) last month following five-month layoff and lacks the scope of his rivals.

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the 18th attempt over C&D (good to firm) two weeks ago off 3lb lower on his second run for this yard, with Jake Dickson aboard him; needs to come on again in this higher grade.

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap
Spotlight: Showed much improved form when stepping up in trip on his handicap debut to be runner-up at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; should step on from that and holds strong claims.

RaceName: Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

RaceName: Dobsons Gaskets EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

Spotlight: Belied 28-1 odds to win on debut at Redcar (5f, good) four weeks ago; his stable is not known for first-time-out 2yo winners so this £80,000 yearling could have a very bright future; major player under a penalty.

RaceName: Dobsons Gaskets EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: £50,000 breeze-up buy who showed promise and pace when 16-1 and beaten just over 1l in last of four on recent debut at Ayr (6f, good); this half-brother to four winners is open to improvement and could be a contender.

RaceName: Dobsons Gaskets EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: Dobsons Gaskets EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: Dobsons Gaskets EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

RaceName: Simon's 20 Year Heart Transplant Anniversary Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

RaceName: Simon's 20 Year Heart Transplant Anniversary Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in C&D handicap (good) in May on stable/seasonal debut and that form puts him in the picture; however, disappointing at Redcar (5f, good) since and now 0-10; needs to bounce back.

RaceName: Simon's 20 Year Heart Transplant Anniversary Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten eight times and the drop back to 6f isn't an obvious positive, but he's run some good races and was third in a handicap at Catterick (7f, good to firm) last Wednesday; prominent in calculations.

RaceName: Simon's 20 Year Heart Transplant Anniversary Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

5yo mare whose form has gone to a new level this season, with wins at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) and Goodwood (1m4f, good to soft) sandwiching a runner-up finish at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm); she may be the type who only just does enough and therefore she could have more still left in the tank.

Down the field at York and Windsor on his last two starts but he's won on his last four visits to Ripon (1m2f, good/good to soft), including twice this year; it's surprising he's only ever had one crack at 1m4f, given how well he kept on over that trip in 2024; firmly in calculations back here.

Disappointing at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) a fortnight ago but prior to that he was 2-2 since being gelded, with convincing wins at Southwell (1m3f, AW) and Hamilton (1m3f, good); could bounce back.

He's won just one of his last 23 starts and has failed to fire on his last two outings; however, he had a tough assignment in the John Smith's Cup at York last Saturday and he's dropped to a handy mark; runner-up to the 4-7 favourite in this race last year and he's not ruled out.

8yo who has been beaten 23 times since his last win in September 2024 and failed to threaten at the Curragh three weeks ago; however, prior to that this Irish raider was second at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm) behind a subsequent Royal Ascot winner, and he's in the picture on that form.

He's edged down the weights for his new yard this season and has been placed off this mark on his last two starts, finishing third at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) then beaten just a neck at Hamilton (1m5f, good); back up in grade this afternoon but he might not be far away.

3yo who has improved with each of his four starts and finished a close second of five on handicap debut at Thirsk (1m4f, good to firm) this month; the winner has followed up and this progressive colt could play a leading role following a 1lb rise.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 11yo who has been up and down this season but has won twice, including over C&D (good), and he ran pretty well when third here (1m, good) last time; finished third in this last year and he could give a good account.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 8yo who capitalised on a reduced mark to win over C&D (good) last month before 7l second to easy winner in amateur jockeys' race at Pontefract (1m2f, good); he's not ruled out back here.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Often ran well in 2yo campaign and he got off the mark on his reappearance in a novice at Redcar (7f, good to firm); it's possible he'll stay this far but there is a question mark on that score, and also one about his current form as he's been well beaten on handicaps on his last two starts.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 7yo whose losing sequence goes back 21 races to September 2024 but he went close behind Yermanthere over C&D (good) last month and was a good third at Ayr (1m2f, good) last time; might not be far away.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
OwnerName: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
Spotlight: Capitalised on a golden opportunity for easy win at 8-13 in a seller at Beverley (8.4f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; that may have given his confidence a boost and he's unexposed in the retained tongue-tie/cheekpieces, but he's opposable on what he's achieved in handicaps this season.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Runner-up at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in May on second start and won a novice at Salisbury (1m2f, good) last month; her latest form looks solid and this unexposed handicap newcomer could continue to progress; player.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time turf winner who won two in a row at Wolverhampton (8.6f/7f, AW) in March and is 1lb below his last winning mark; he ran okay on his final few starts for the Newland/Insole yard but this 8yo needs something extra on today's stable debut, following 8,500gns sale.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: 11yo who needs to produce more than he's managed on his last three starts but he's 3lb lower than when a close third at Ayr (1m, good to firm) in May and has won at Ripon seven times; went close here in August 2024 when he last wore these blinkers (which replace cheekpieces); not discounted.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Returned to form to make all at 28-1 at York (1m, good) three weeks ago in a reapplied tongue-tie (retained); strong claims up 3lb if he can back up that latest performance.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Kicked off this campaign with two wins in a row (7f, good to soft/AW) before solid second at Newmarket (1m, good); didn't run badly in mid-division in Class 2 at Epsom (8.5f, good to soft) last time and he could be in the mix back down in grade.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: In good heart this season and he returned to winning ways over C&D (good) last Monday; a 5lb rise takes this 5yo to a career-high mark but he has a solid record here and could be firmly in the shake-up once more.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins last summer and he showed spark as recently as this April; he's dropped to a dangerous mark but has failed to shine on his last three outings and arrives with something to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Won 1m AW maiden at Dundalk in February but not at the top of his game on final two runs for Jessica Harrington and well beaten at 28-1 on stable debut at York three weeks ago; he may be best watched.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: Won over C&D (good) in May in first-time cheekpieces (retained since); pulled hard when 7l third at Leicester (1m, good) next time and down the field at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) most recently, but the return to Ripon could trigger a revival.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: Won two in a row this spring (1m, firm/good) and has continued in good heart, finishing second of three at Bath (1m, firm) then third of nine at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm); shaped last time as though he may benefit from the return to 1m and he could be thereabouts.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well for a long way in front before fading into fourth when upped to 1m at Redcar (good) four weeks ago; it's possible she'd benefit from the return to 7f but is not ruled out today.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: It's still early days and there's potential in his pedigree; market check advised but he's finished well beaten in both handicaps and needs to be an entirely different proposition today.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: Ran okay on her first two starts this season and has dropped down the weights but she's struggled on her last three runs; major turnaround needed in a first-time hood (replacing the cheekpieces adopted last time).

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
OwnerName: D Bishop, S Bland & T Coyle
Spotlight: Didn't run badly at Beverley (8.4f, good to firm) a fortnight ago when fifth of seven in first-time cheekpieces (retained); however, he probably needs more help from the handicapper before he posts his first win.

RaceName: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap
Spotlight: Triple-figure odds on all three starts; down the field on first two outings and same story at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) last month after a break, but there were signs of ability that day; this half-sister to Group 3 winner Making Dreams goes handicapping off a modest mark and it will be no surprise if she plays a leading role, especially if strong in the betting.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: He's regressed and is winless since scoring over C&D in July 2024; only fourth of six on stable debut at Chepstow (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago but he was the 7-4 favourite and got upset in the stalls, and may have needed that run; interesting to see if he's again strong in the betting.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Runner-up on his first three starts (6f/5f, AW), the latest at Southwell in May, but he's struggled to get competitive on turf in his four handicaps; needs to raise his game.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: 13-race maiden who has been expensive to follow and underwhelming on his last two starts; however, his season began with two positive performances in the spring and he's in the picture if rediscovering that form.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
OwnerName: Hard Held Partnership And Angus Racing
Spotlight: Four-time course winner whose mark continues to fall and he hasn't been devoid of spark this season; however, this 9yo needs to better what he's shown on his last three starts (the first of them over C&D).

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Just one win from his 22 starts and merely mid-division at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) last time in first-time blinkers (retained); however, he's twice finished runner-up this season and is not ruled out.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Course winner who is well handicapped on last season's form and is one to watch in the betting; however, he finished down the field on his three starts this spring and needs to turn things around.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Her 22 starts have yielded just one win but she was a close second of 18 at 25-1 at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) two starts ago and backed that up when runner-up to at Catterick (7f, good to firm) last Wednesday, albeit no match for the thriving winner; firmly in calculations given recent showings.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Third on handicap/seasonal debut at Nottingham (5f, good) in May and bounced back from lesser run to finish second at Redcar (6f, good) four weeks ago; got loose and withdrawn at Beverley three days later (5-2 at the time); subsequently sold for 4,200gns; respected on stable debut.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: In good form in the main this year, twice running well at Pontefract (5f/6f, good) last month before respectable fourth of seven at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) on Thursday; possible player.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: 13-race maiden who may be better at 5f but he's run some good races this year, including beaten just a nose at Beverley (5f, good to firm) two starts ago, and he might not be far away.

RaceName: Aldwark Manor Estate Luxury Yorkshire Hotel 'Confined' Handicap (Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)
Spotlight: Ten-race maiden who wasn't quite at his best when fourth of nine over C&D (good) last week but was in good form previously, coming second at Redcar (7f, good) in May and at Catterick (6f, good to firm) last month; chance.

OwnerName: Cosmo Stables And Delta Squad Racing, Llc
Spotlight: Impressive winner of Listed Pegasus Stakes here (8.5f), the acknowledged local prep for this; that form still leaves him with a lot to find.

Strong-running horse with a ton of early pace; career-best effort to beat Iron Honor by just over 1l in Preakness Stakes at Laurel (9.5f; second Grade 1 win) in May; travelled really strongly to take command there and value for more than winning margin (had suffered foot problems and may have been short of work); could still be open to more improvement and likely the one to beat.

OwnerName: St Elias Stable, William H Lawrence & Glassman Racing
Spotlight: Successful on first two starts, both at Aqueduct, in maiden last December and Grade 3 Gotham Stakes (1m; by 1l) in April; ran best race yet when second to Napoleon Solo in Grade 1 Preakness Stakes at Laurel (9.5f) in May, closing to just over 1l behind winner; open to more improvement and strong claims.

OwnerName: OGMA Investments LLC, JR Ranch & High Step Racing LLC
Spotlight: Very smart form in four starts, winning Grade 3 Tampa Bay Derby (8.5f) in March but better effort still when beaten nose by Commandment in Grade 1 Florida Derby (1m1f) later same month; missed Kentucky Derby (and training time since) with skin infection but could still take a hand after the layoff.

Very impressive in Grade 1 Blue Grass Stakes at Keeneland (1m1f; won by 11l) in May but disappointing favourite for Grade 1 Kentucky Derby (11th of 18, never looking likely to take hand in finish); returned to best to win Grade 3 Matt Winn Stakes at Churchill Downs in June by 2l; seems to need daylight tracking leaders and should get that kind of scenario here.

OwnerName: Bran Jam Stable & David W Clark
Spotlight: Useful form in Listed and black type events but no form close to the level needed to defeat these.

OwnerName: Ashley Durr, Anthony Tate & Front Page Equestrian LLC
Spotlight: Late-running horse capable of smart efforts but not necessarily wins of same class; in frame in Grade 1 company in May in Kentucky Derby and Preakness Stakes; another belated effort when 1l second to Chip Honcho in Grade 3 Ohio Derby at Thistledown (1m1f) last month; strong chance of a minor place.

Progressive form over three seasons, looking a very smart prospect; won Grade 3 Modesty Stakes at Churchill Downs in May by just over 1l, again showing good turn of foot; creditable effort (raced wide) when about 2l third to Portfolio Duration in Grade 1 New York Stakes over slightly further here; freshened and must go well.

Signed off last season with impressive Grade 1 Matriarch Stakes win at Del Mar (1m) but has not quite reached the same level this season, including when dead-heating for Grade 1 Jenny Wiley Stakes at Keeneland (8.5f) in May; again found less than anticipated when about 2l third in Grade 1 Just A Game here last time (1m; may be worth riding more patiently); has to be respected but needs to return to 2025 best.

Has made into smart performer in just five starts; unlucky in Grade 2 on penultimate occasion, then made all in Grade 1 New York Stakes over slightly further here, receiving brilliant ride from Flavien Prat; unlikely to catch rivals so cold this time, but improving profile demands respect.

Sole win in a maiden but very useful form, including when fourth in Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare Turf at Del Mar (1m3f) last November and when just under 2l third to Jancis in Group 2 Dahlia at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) in May; run best ignored (trapped wide, did too much early) behind Blue Bolt in Group 2 at Royal Ascot latest; can reward enterprising bid with at least a place.

Night Of Thunder mare who has won five of 14 starts, notably Grade 1 Just A Game Stakes here (1m, yielding) last June; creditable third in this race last year; favourite, good second to City Girl in Grade 3 Beaugay Stakes at Aqueduct last time; goes well here (form 3131) and has good claims, especially if forecast rain comes early.

Best effort to win Grade 2 Ballston Spa Stakes here (8.5f) last August but looked a bit out of her depth in two Grade 1s afterwards; won minor event at Monmouth on comeback but only sixth when favourite for Grade 3 at Woodbine last time; needs to improve a fair bit to challenge these rivals.

Very useful form on dirt; lightly raced on turf, including when 1l third in a conditions race here (8.5f) last time, running on willingly in a slowly run event; far from exposed but has plenty to find.

OwnerName: Medallion Racing, Swinbank Stables LLC et al
The Estate Of R Larry Johnson

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: One of two for trainer; has started slowly in both runs to date; improved on his moderate debut over 6f here in June when a 1.25l fourth of eight at Fairyhouse in first-time blinkers (retained) earlier this month (6f, good); drops to 5f, but may get involved if getting away quicker.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: 42,000euros yearling; (30,000gns vendor 2yo); dam unplaced 5f/6f (RPR 58), sister to 5f winner Heiba, half-sister to winners Golden Stunner (useful 7f/1m) and Colonel Carter (1m-1m2f), out of half-sister to dam of top miler Canford Cliffs; best watched for the moment.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: One of two for trainer; No Nay Never filly cost 110,000euros as a yearling; relatively unfancied for her Naas debut (5f, good) and was beaten 9l; improvement probable but Keane rides La Tache.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: 10,000euros foal, 23,000euros yearling; bought for 300,000euros at a Breeze-Up in May; ninth foal; half-brother to four winners inc Ruby's Profit (5f inc 2yo/AW; RPR 97), Miss Power (5f; 95) and Between Hills (6f 2yo; 94); dam Listed placed over 5f as 2yo but did not win (92?); holds Group 1 entries here; yard does well with juveniles, but is a little cold at the moment.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Well-bred No Nay Never colt was a 6.5l fifth on debut at Cork when stable second string (6f, good, 6-1); dropped back to 5f at Bellewstown and improved on his initial effort when a 2.5l second of eight (good); obvious chance with Moore up for the first time, but by no means unbeatable at the same time.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Took a huge step forward when getting to within a head of Carry The Flag in his second career start dropped back to 5f at Naas in May (good, 80-1); ran keenly when 6l behind Carry The Flag in a Naas Listed race earlier this month; down in grade now and claims on the basis of his penultimate run; holds a Group 1 entry here and sets the standard on 93.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: 160,000gns yearling finished second of six behind an Aidan O'Brien-trained odds-on chance at Dundalk on debut (5f); shaped like he will have learned plenty from that and a tongue tie and cheekpieces have been added; in the mix.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Has beaten just one rival in two maiden runs over 5f/6.5f on different ground; tongue tie on but of no appeal.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Hung right when sixth over 5f on debut at Cork (soft); well beaten when upped to 6.5f at Listowel next time; a bit better back over 5f at Bellewstown last time; hood goes on, but a lot of improvement needed.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Minzaal filly cost 160,000euros as a yearling; well beaten on debut when sixth of seven and 3.5l behind Southern Boulevard; others more likely.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Partners Of Irish Sport Irish EBF Maiden
Spotlight: Second foal; dam 5f-1m maiden (RPR 65), sister to Listed-placed 5f/6f winner Gold Filigree, out of 5f 2yo winning half-sister to 1m Group 2 winner Emerald Commander; not super appealing on paper.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: One of two for trainer; Sea The Stars filly; 75,000yearling, 160,000euros 2yo; second foal; dam 5f/6f winner (inc 2yo/AW/German Group 3; RPR 101), half-sister to winners Back To Brussels (Listed-placed 5f 2yo/6f) and Green Sense (6f 2yo Group 2), is granddaughter of US 6f Listed winner; appeals on paper and chosen by Browne McMonagle.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Slowly away when beaten 17l on debut over 1m at Naas; likely needs more time.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Down the field on her only juvenile start, but much better on her return at Rocommon last month when fourth of 12 (7.5f, good); ran green that day so could improve again, but will need to.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Placed six times in maidens from 7f-11.5f on different ground; longer trip didn't bring improvement from her at Killarney last time when again runner-up (11.5f, good); she's expensive to follow, but  sets the standard and her day is sure to come someday soon.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Well-bred filly is rated 76 after four starts; went close at Thurles on her second and final start last term (1m, good to yielding); hasn't really progressed in two runs this year, the latest in cheekpieces at Naas (10.5f, good); Moore rides White Sand Beach.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Calyx filly made a positive impression when running green but taking the runner-up spot ahead of subsequent winner Vauntingly at Gowran (1m2f, good); only an 8l third at Fairyhouse next time (1m2f, good), but was 2l behind the runner-up Mai Dahlia, who won easily next time; interesting.

RaceName: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Second foal; half-sister to French Listed-placed 6f-7f winner Summer Sail (RPR 103); dam unraced half-sister to 6f-1m winner Beau Jardine, out of Listed-placed 7f/1m winner; Browne McMonagle rides Star Performer.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 6-4 favourite on debut over 5f at Naas last month, weakened late into fifth; failed to improve as much as might have been expected when fourth over the same course and trip on second start, 1 1/4 behind her bigger-priced stablemate Fly Smart.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Blue Point filly; third foal; dam French 1m2f winner, closely related to Australian 6.5f Group 2 winner Home Of The Brave.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Satisfactory debut at Leopardstown, but has 4 1/2l to find with Ibelieveicanfly who has picked up further experience into the bargain.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Flaxman S
Spotlight: Well clear of fifth-placed Citrus Springs when ridden by Ryan Moore on her debut at Leopardstown; had Wayne Lordan aboard when chasing home Moore's mount Alpha over C&D three weeks ago; form was given a strong boost by a win for Livenka at Fairyhouse last week.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Mehmas filly; E135,000 yearling; dam 7f 2yo winner; finished 1 1/4l in front of her shorter-priced stablemate Shi Yang when third of seven in a 5f maiden at Navan early this month.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Half-sister by No Nay Never to Listed winner Boogie Woogie; dam won the Irish and Yorkshire Oaks; half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Crusade; Ryan Moore on Ibelieveicanfly.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 10,500gns yearling; eleventh foal; half-sister by State Of Rest to five winners, best of them a 7f Listed scorer.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Half-sister by No Nay Never to three winners, including Concert Hall, a Group 3-winning filly for this stable; dam, by Galileo, won the Oaks, sister to Group 3 winners at 1m2f and 1m6f; a leading apprentice aboard, but looks like the yard's third string.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Supporting Irish Sport Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E120,000 Y; seventh foal; Lope De Vega filly is closely related to 5f AW winner Real Encounter, half-sister to four winners, including Real Appeal (eight wins, including a 1m Group 2); champion jockey prefers the once-raced Citrus Springs.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Won a Group 1 over 6f here on his final juvenile start (good); runner-up behind subsequent Royal Ascot and Group 1 winner on his reappearance in a Group 3 over 7f at Leopardstown in April (good to yielding); probably not up to the top level as shown in three Group 1 runs over 1m since, but his latest two were meritable; big danger dropping in class and trip; top rated of the field too; stable a little cold currently though.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Entering legendary course specialist status after adding a tenth win at the venue in a Listed race last time (6f, good); prior to that he won a C&D Listed contest in March (soft to heavy) when seeing off East Hampton by 1.5l; got closest to subsequent Group 1 winner Comanche Brave when a 2l second in a 6f Group 2 here on penultimate (good); always a danger around here and should go well again.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Group 1 Lockinge winner in 2024 and Group 2 winner at Goodwood the same year; on a losing run since but his runner-up finish in a Leopardstown Group 3 showed definite signs of encouragement (7f, soft) when ridden by Keane for the first time; his wins came on good so if he repeats that latest run he is firmly in the mix.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Won three times as a juvenile, including the valuable Goffs Million over course and distance; finished 2.5l behind Power Blue on seasonal return at Leopardstown when seventh of 11 (7f, good to yielding); faced a tough task in the French 2,000 Guineas; weakened into a modest ninth in the Jersey Stakes last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Gained first win at stakes level when taking a Listed fillies' event at Navan last month (1m, good); found wanting in a deeper race over 1m here on Irish Derby weekend next time; resumed winning ways when landing a Group 3 at Leopardstown last time (7f, good), however, the proximity of an 83-rated rival (1l) to her takes the sheen off the form a bit.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Won his maiden over 6f here in 2024 (yielding to soft) and bagged the Madrid handicap at Naas last season (7f, soft to heavy); best run since was when beaten a neck by Diego Velazquez in this race last year (good to yielding); beaten 1.5l behind Big Gossey in a C&D Listed race on return (soft to heavy); not at his best at Leopardstown last time; appears to give his best on softer ground.

RaceName: Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Cafe Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Okay fourth in the Group 3 Ballycorus Stakes at Leopardstown on return (7f, soft) and built on that when making all and keeping on well to win a 1m Listed race here last time (good); cheekpieces added and drop back to 7f should be okay; having just his sixth career run so improvement still feasible.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Failed to make an impact in three maidens at 7f/1m; no significant improvement when upped to 1m4f for her handicap debut at Limerick; a different story when tackling an extended 1m on better ground at Fairyhouse, travelled well and took command under two furlongs down to score easily; has turned a corner and can remain competitive despite a 12lb rise.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Four wins last year, including this event; career best when landing a highly competitive fillies' handicap at Leopardstown in September; has run five times this season, only once showing her best form; two lesser displays since a creditable third placing at Gowran in April; 10lb higher than 12 months ago.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins last season, including handicaps at Leopardstown (1m, good to firm) and Tipperary (7.5f, good); out of her depth in a Group 3 on seasonal debut; below form on soft at Leopardstown; much more like it on quick going over 7f here last time, chasing home one of the stars of the season, Meriden, who has won a Listed race to complete a five-timer; strong chance.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Consistent in maidens and handicaps before breakthrough win in a 1m maiden at Gowran on her tenth start; got away with a 2lb rise but her chance was dismissed by punters when she ran in a 1m1f premier handicap here three weeks ago; 33-1 then, not disgraced in mid-division after meeting trouble in running; visor replaces cheekpieces worn then.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Rarely runs a bad race; won a maiden at Dundalk in March; not beaten far in a 7f handicap at this venue in May; second in a small-field conditions race at Leopardstown, before third behind the same winner in a Killarney handicap on Monday; first-time cheekpieces; 2lb wrong, but good 5lb claimer.

RaceName: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice as a juvenile, including over 6f at this venue; won a 7f Fairyhouse handicap last year; well below that level on final two starts of the campaign; looked an awkward ride on her reappearance in a 7f premier handicap here last month; may simply have been ring-rusty; should improve from the run, and first-time cheekpieces may help.

RaceName: 1xBet.ie Proud Supporters Of Irish Racing Curragh Cup (Group 2)

RaceName: Sharon Pardy 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Awr Consultancy Ltd & The Folly Partners
Spotlight: Returned from break in career-best form over fences this spring and subsequently exploited her novice hurdle status at Hexham (2m, good), albeit unimpressive in justifying skinny odds; suited by fast ground and features prominently in calculations.

RaceName: Sharon Pardy 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten here on both recent hurdling starts (2m2f/2m), the latter after a wind op; can't be recommended.

RaceName: Sharon Pardy 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Not disgraced in the second of his two bumpers last season but tailed off when switched to hurdling this month; tongue-tie now added.

RaceName: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 0-4 over fences for new stable this year but ran well over 2m1f here on last two appearances, losing out only by half a length on latter occasion; should be fine over this longer trip; good chance.

RaceName: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won over hurdles last season and made pretty good start to chasing career when third of seven at Bangor (2m4f, good; wore cheekpieces) in April; weakened out of contention on run-in at Worcester (2m7f, good; first-time visor) this month but drops back in trip here and remains of interest.

RaceName: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Both wins over hurdles when making all, one here on fast ground; ridden with more restraint since returning this year but was in contention before last-fence fall at Bangor (2m4f, good) two starts ago, and last month's Uttoxeter third was respectable; can go well again and it will be interesting to see whether she reverts to more positive tactics.

RaceName: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well suited by this track when a useful hurdler for Nicky Henderson a few years ago but, following a long absence, has been safely held on both starts for new stable this season, latterly back here in a three-runner race; needs a revival on first chasing attempt since 2022.

RaceName: George & Dragon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 1-9 over hurdles; makes chasing debut from a workable mark but has become very inconsistent and was well beaten in first-time cheekpieces last month (2m7f); drops back in trip with visor tried here; not easy to predict.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Fair Flat-racer who returned to hurdling with two fast-ground course wins (2m/2m2f) this season; drew nicely clear on run-in on latter occasion and commands respect in current mood.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-25 over hurdles but has run some good races at this track, most recently when close second over 2m (good to firm) three weeks ago; also suited by this longer trip and can make her presence felt again.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Safely held when fifth in first-time cheekpieces here (2m, good) last month and now 0-10 over hurdles; upped in trip and tried in a visor today; improvement required.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Held up in rear and showed nothing more than glimmers of promise in three 2m maiden/novice hurdles this spring but has a tongue-tie fitted and moves up in trip for this handicap debut; improvement possible.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Unexposed over hurdles after only five runs but was beaten about 23l when seventh of 12 here (2m, good) on last month's handicap debut and is effectively 4lb higher today.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Unplaced all eight hurdling starts for David Jeffreys and absent since pulled up over 3m in November; 3lb out of the weights for this stable debut and could be considered only if lively in the betting.

RaceName: Dave Shrader Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
TrainerName: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole right
Spotlight: Dual chase winner (2m5f/2m3f) this spring, after a break; didn't see out 3m on latest outing but drops back in trip for this switch back to hurdling and his current mark is workable; respected.

Not at best on the Flat this year (albeit still capable of useful form) and managed only fourth of six when warm favourite for latest hurdle race, at Worcester (2m, good) in May; that said, he's a stout stayer on the Flat and could have untapped potential over this new trip over jumps.

Slightly disappointing at Perth last week but was placed on consecutive outings beforehand, once over C&D on fast ground; swaps blinkers for refitted visor (worn once on Flat in 2020); no surprise if she's on the premises.
Improving 6yo who kept on resolutely to score over C&D (good to firm) 19 days ago and has now won three times since the spring; another 5lb higher now but a likely contender again.

Flopped badly when favourite at Hexham last month and needs to put that behind him but looked in good nick when making all for clearcut success at Hereford (3m1f, good) two runs ago; dangerous if back at that level.

Regressive 10yo who has been lightly raced in recent years and returned from a break with two low-key runs this spring; pulled up (lost action) in first-time cheekpieces (retained) recently; revival needed.

RaceName: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Veteran with 11 chase wins on his CV, including 2023 edition of this race; returns here after respectable third behind two progressive rivals at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month but Centara is unlikely to allow him to play his preferred front-running role.

RaceName: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Back in prime form when holding on well to score over C&D (good) on last month's chase return and now 4-10 over fences; recent 3lb rise does not look excessive and there's a good chance he'll be right in the thick of things again.

RaceName: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Progressive 6yo with 3-4 strike-rate over fences, including two fast-ground C&D wins this season; the form of last month's 20l success in a three-runner race is tricky to evaluate (odds-on favourite below par) but a 4lb rise could have been worse and he may still be on the upgrade.

RaceName: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 3-10 over fences, the latest win gained at Newton Abbot (2m, good to soft) last autumn; returned from break with respectable fourth (a nose behind Sir Tivo) in race fought out by two progressive rivals at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month and has a big role to play if that outing brought him on.

RaceName: Silver Fox Classic Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Free-going front-runner who won five 2m chases in early part of last season; comfortably reeled in on both outings since returning from a break this spring, though, and comes here with a point to prove.

RaceName: PJ McGeever 70th Birthday Celebration Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Mrs Janet Cooper & M E Sowersby
Spotlight: Drew clear to clear by 9l over C&D (good) in April, his third hurdling success, and is now only 2lb above that mark but looked out of sorts on his latest outing and is not one to rely upon heavily.

RaceName: PJ McGeever 70th Birthday Celebration Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has mixed record for this stable since last autumn but returned from break to cause 25-1 surprise over fences at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) this month and is now 2-6 for the yard; it's hard to predict whether he'll be in the right mood again here but he has a lower mark over hurdles.

RaceName: PJ McGeever 70th Birthday Celebration Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Safely held when odds-on for stable debut at Warwick (2m5f) in May but, with a tongue-tie fitted, made amends over 3m2f there (also on good) last month; came clear of the others with a progressive rival that day and could still be well handicapped after 5lb rise.

RaceName: PJ McGeever 70th Birthday Celebration Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a point in the spring and is 2-4 since returned to racing under rules for new stable, the latter win gained off today's mark on chasing debut here (2m6f, good to firm) a week ago; likes to make the running, and could be hard to catch on this quick return to hurdling.

RaceName: Grace And Dotty Conditional Jockeys' Mares' Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Hale Racing, Lyle Farming Company & Ptnr
Spotlight: Useful on the Flat in her prime and came good over hurdles at fifth attempt, battling well for narrow course win (2m, good to firm; first-time tongue-tie) three weeks ago; open to further progress if stamina holds out over this new trip; respected.

RaceName: Grace And Dotty Conditional Jockeys' Mares' Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Below form when eighth behind Roarin' Success here last month but won readily in first-time cheekpieces at Worcester (2m, good) nine days ago and now 2-7 over hurdles; moves up in trip; big player if new headgear continues to aid.

RaceName: Grace And Dotty Conditional Jockeys' Mares' Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Runs this track well and posted career-best hurdling performance when scoring over C&D (good to firm) a week ago; 7lb penalty gives her a big weight to carry today but, nevertheless, she has strong claims.

RaceName: Grace And Dotty Conditional Jockeys' Mares' Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-10 over hurdles; two of this year's six runs for Fergal O'Brien offered significant hope but she was soundly beaten on her latest outing; now back in the care of Barry Brennan; others have much less to prove.

Hasn't looked back since debut second and has progressed with every run, landing the Group 3 Prix du Bois over 6f last time on what is likely to be similar ground; won twice here prior to that so obvious chance up against the two stablemates.

Made good progress on every start, and comes into this having won the Windsor Castle Stakes (6f, good to firm) at Royal Ascot about a month ago; shaped well over 7f prior to that behind another subsequent royal meeting winner, so unlikely to want this run at a dwadle.

Progressed, like her two rivals, with every run and was last seen finishing third in a 6f Group 2 at the Curragh for fillies on good to firm; figures suggest she has a bit to find but is the only one that gets the sex allowance.

Spotlight: Nowhere near her best in the Premio Oaks d'Italia (1m2.5f) when last seen despite having the run of the race, so better judged on her Listed win at Newmarket before that over 1m2f on good to firm from the front; could be hard to catch if allowed to dominate.

Useful for Charlie Appleby before joining this stable, and has two standout pieces of form, one of them last time in a mile Group 2 here over a furlong shorter, when beaten just under 3l; claims if producing her best form up a furlong in distance.

Only win came on the AW but mostly on the up during her career and capable of a good effort, but was beaten 9l when last seen in May on very soft in a C&D Listed event; can be involved if the fitting of blinkers off a break sharpens her up.

Mostly exposed filly, who has run creditably at a decent level throughout her career; shown some improvement for this stable in 2026 but needs to do better than last time as Naas to pose a threat; stays beyond 1m2f and handles a sound surface.

Making steady improvement and beat Eklleel a short-neck in March over a mile on very soft; shaped nicely in Listed events since without winning one, albeit behind Maintain last time, and should be in the mix for a place.

Half-sister to Saleymm, Saddadd and Almaqam, so bred to be a Group performer; made it fourth time lucky when winning at Lyon Parilly last time over a mile with a cosy success; step up in trip may bring about more improvement.

Half-sister to the classy New Ground; won on debut and produced some respectable efforts this season, including last time under this rider in a 1m2f Listed event at Longchamp, when Ecija was third; may still be capable of better.

Consistent sort who had three of these behind when a short-head second in the 7f Group 3 Porte de la Maillot at Longchamp last time; no problem with the return to this trip and he's likely to give another good account.

Turned in her best effort to win soft-ground Listed event over 1m2f on reappearance and a respectable effort over the same trip in Group 3 last time; likely to be found out over this shorter trip on quicker ground, especially if this turns into a dawdle.

Progressive colt who made it three wins from as many starts when beating a previous winner in convincing fashion in a Listed event on his AW debut at Deauville last time; yet to race on a sound surface but he's got plenty of fast-ground influences in his pedigree and is an exciting sort who is capable of better; the one to beat.

Prolific winner but one of his best efforts came in defeat in a strong Listed event at Doha in February; shaped well on his first run since when fourth in Group 3 at Longchamp last time; bit to find with Silius but should be better for that run and likely to get closer back at 1m.

Group 3 winner at Meydan (1m) and Longchamp (7f) last year but has yet to match either effort since then; shaped with more encouragement back on turf last time, where he's closely matched with Dark Trooper and Fort Payne; others appeal more.
Steadily progressive sort who ran well in a Group 3 over C&D on fast ground last time; no surprise should he get in the places once again.

OwnerName: Alain Jathiere, Mme Philippe Demercastel & Nicolas Caullery
Spotlight: Last year's Burj Nahaar winner (1m, dirt) at Meydan who returned to winning ways in a conditions event over 7f at Longchamp in spring; respectable effort in a Group 3 at the same course last month but faces a stiff task at these weights.

Spotlight: Second foal; dam French 7.5f AW winner, closely related to French 9.7f-12.5f winner Spiritueux, half-sister to French 1m/1m2f Group 1 winner Silasol, out of US 1m/8.5f Listed winner; top trainer won this race with a smart newcomer in 2021.
Showed some promise in two 6f novice runs on good ground in May; gelded since; his experience will be an asset but likely he will need improvement to take this.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Some promise on first two starts (6f; 2yo debut for Ed Walker) but her two 7f runs, including handicap debut (after wind op) three weeks ago, have been less convincing; 4lb lower today but not a solid option.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden; she made a promising seasonal reappearance when third of seven over C&D in May but that hasn't been a springboard to better things; Water Of Leith looks the yard's main hope.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden; quiet start for new stable but there was a welcome return to form when third of eight over C&D last week, keeping on and finishing in front of Water Of Leith; 3lb lower today and Danny Tudhope a good booking for the yard (three wins and three seconds from 14 rides); contender.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Three 6f AW wins for Iain Jardine in the spring; also ran well on turf at Hamilton in May but his form has dipped since; back to his last winning mark but he needs to raise his game; the removal of cheekpieces could be a positive.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Six-race maiden; promise on AW over the winter but he has suffered two heavy defeats in 6f handicaps (soft and good) this summer; drops in class but there are risks attached.

RaceName: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Three 5f wins to his name, one of them at this track, but unplaced in six runs over 6f+; finished behind stablemate Whiskey Kisses over C&D last week; new cheekpieces not enough to tempt.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Belatedly ended a long losing run with a smooth defeat of Ramon Di Loria over C&D last week; looks well in under a 5lb penalty and his claims are obvious.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: 14-race maiden; ran well when second of 11 at Catterick (7f, good) on his seasonal return in May but he failed to back it up at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) five weeks ago; others look stronger.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Hold-up performer who is thrown in on his 2025 form; yet to get going this time around but he wasn't beaten far at Carlisle 11 days ago and cheekpieces could give him a lift.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive in low-level 6f handicaps, winning at Newcastle in October and placed in both runs this summer; step back up to 7f can help; withdrawn after getting upset in the stalls here last month.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
OwnerName: D Jenkins J Glover R O'Donnell J Short
Spotlight: Won a 6f nursery at Redcar (good to soft) in September; slow start to this campaign but his third at Ripon (6f, good) was a personal best and the step up to 7f could spark further progress; high on the list.

RaceName: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap
Spotlight: Prolific winner down the years, adding two AW handicaps to his haul in February; arrives in good form but he was no match for Imperial Guard here last week and the turnaround in the weights may be insufficient.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
OwnerName: B Jordan, Brian Jordan, S Jordan & N McConnell
Spotlight: Not won since his stellar campaign in 2024 but there has been promise this year, including at Hamilton on Friday; 2lb lower today and now sports cheekpieces for the first time; chance.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
OwnerName: N Skinner D Jenkins J Glover
Spotlight: Running well in 6f handicaps this summer, beating a big field at York in May and running to a similar level in defeat twice since; no obvious reason why he wouldn't go well again.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: Made a winning stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good) in April; never featured at Epsom on Oaks day but he was back in form when third of ten at Thirsk 19 days ago; each-way shout.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well over C&D on her penultimate start; 2-1 joint favourite for a 6f fillies' handicap at Carlisle 11 days ago, making some late headway into fourth; should run her race once again.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
OwnerName: John Murphy & Miss L A Perratt
Spotlight: Useful on AW on his day but 0-21 on turf; handicapped accordingly but his latest C&D 12th didn't suggest he was the answer to today's puzzle.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well over C&D last September; beat 17 rivals when landing a Class 4 handicap at Ascot (6f, good to firm) in May but he was unable to build on it at Pontefract last month; perhaps vulnerable once more.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: The bulk of his winning has been done on AW but he did win a 5f handicap at the Curragh last August; recent efforts need bettering but he would seem likely to give his running.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: Another who has a better strike-rate on AW than turf; not beaten far into fourth in a 5f handicap at Doncaster 17 days ago, a race where he fluffed the start; yet to shine at Ayr; one of three runners for Jim Goldie.

RaceName: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
Spotlight: Well beaten in three handicaps for new stable this year, the latest over a mile nine days ago; latest 5lb drop in the weights is not enough to tempt.

In good form in the spring, winning at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) before near misses at Thirsk and over C&D; not at his best on his last two starts but this is an ease in class and he's a major player in his bid to win this race for a second time (successful in 2024).

OwnerName: David Orr & Miss L A Perratt
Spotlight: Beat Donna Nook over C&D in May when rated 1lb higher; put a couple of lesser efforts behind him when chasing home Runninsonofagun here last week; 7lb better off for 2l defeat so has a handicapping chance; new visor replaces cheekpieces; others still more appealing.

Gained first win since his 2yo days when making all in a Class 6 over C&D last week (blinkered first time); unlikely to get a soft lead this time and a 5lb penalty against stronger opposition demands more in any case.
Ended a losing run when beating 11 rivals at Ripon (1m, good) last month; respectable efforts since without suggesting she was ahead of her mark.

No turf win since 2022 but he has won three AW handicaps in the last 14 months; should be well treated but recent efforts haven't been his best; this is a drop in class so not dismissed, even though the return of cheekpieces wouldn't be an obvious plus based on previous usage.
Won four handicaps here (1m-1m2f, good or slower) in the second half of 2025; yet to fire this time around and may need both slower ground and further help from the handicapper.
Two solid runs to begin his time with this yard and the addition of cheekpieces saw him win a 1m1f handicap at Musselburgh three weeks ago; only 2lb higher and he should give it another good go.
Won three in a row over 1m and 7f at Musselburgh (all on good) last June and July but she wasn't seen after August and two runs this year have been poor; risky.

Ended 2025 on the up and she has maintained her progress in 2026, winning four times over 1m1f on good ground; not at her best last time but foolish to think she won't continue progressing; unraced on faster than good.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
OwnerName: J D Wright & Mrs S Wright
Spotlight: Second of nine at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) 18 days ago, after which he was sold out of Harry Charlton's stable for 18,000gns; should have more to offer over this trip; interesting.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last month; not so good in either run since, the latest over C&D two weeks ago; not ruled out but not the most solid option either.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Third in 1m4f handicaps at Musselburgh on her last two starts, staying on nicely on both occasions; drop back in trip on faster ground isn't sure to suit.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Veteran who was recording his 12th win at the track when leading close home over 1m5f last week; able to race off a 3lb lower mark today and he has to be of interest from a handicapping perspective.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: 11-race maiden; only one effort of note since joining Jim Goldie but he drops into his first 0-60 having undergone wind surgery since last seen; interesting to see how strong he is in the market.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Veteran with plenty of course form to his name; third of nine over 1m here last week (winner Runninsonofagun runs in the 4.00); one of three runners for the stable.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Back to the mark off which he won at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm) last August; finished third in his first two runs this year but not at the same level on his last two starts; drops in trip/grade and could bounce back to form.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice over 7f when trained by George Scott; initially struggled in Ireland but finished second in a couple of handicaps at around 7f last month; beaten favourite over 7f here two week ago, after which he left Maurice Ahern; stamina for 1m2f has to be taken on trust and he goes without headgear on his stable debut.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Runner-up in two of her four handicaps; her form dipped at Nottingham 18 days ago but no surprise to see her bounce back with a big run.

RaceName: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well from out of the handicap at Catterick (1m4f, good to firm) last week, poaching a big lead but reeled in close home; whether she can repeat that form in this bigger field remains to be seen.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: Made all to win a 5.5f handicap at Wetherby last month; unable to build on it at Windsor 11 days later but she still has low mileage.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: 5f AW win in December; knocking at the door this year, including when a close second on his return to turf at Thirsk (5f, good) last month; now 2lb higher but likely to give his running.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: Having dropped in the weights he ran his best race of the year when third of nine at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) on Thursday; now has something to build on.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: Steady progress in three novice/maiden runs and he took another step forward when second of nine on his handicap debut at Ripon (6f, good) two weeks ago (finished just in front of Soul Warrior who runs in the 3.00); open to further improvement and looks quick enough for 5f.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Redcar (5f, good to firm) in May off a 2lb lower mark and she followed it with a good third at Ripon; played up beforehand and then in the stalls when disappointing at Beverley four weeks ago; needs to show that temperamental display was a one off.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap
Spotlight: Improved for the addition of a visor when easily seeing off six rivals in a 5f handicap at Wolverhampton in March; well beaten on next three starts and sold out of Robert Cowell's stable for 2,200gns in May; fine effort when short-headed on his stable debut at Musselburgh three weeks ago and a repeat would see him go well despite a 2lb rise.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: 0-12 on turf on the Flat; ran respectably in a couple of handicaps earlier this season, but last three runs haven't been great; could do better now dropped into claiming company, but needs to leave behind recent form.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: In-form filly arrives in search of a hat-trick after knuckling down to win claimers at Bellewstown (1m, good) and Killarney (1m, good); this longer trip is a query, but should be on the premises again if she stays (stamina in pedigree but ran poorly over 10.5f before).

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: Maiden has shown promise in a couple of his runs; not beaten that far when a 5.25l third in 1m4f Tramore claimer latest in first-time cheekpieces (retained); rated 69, so best treated by race conditions and this drop in trip should suit; can't discount.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: On a long losing run and no sign of it ending in recent starts; tailed off at Bellewstown latest and rated just 34 now; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: Won twice in Britain with cut in the ground; after a spell over hurdles, didn't show much on return to the Flat at Killarney; a bit to prove for now and might prefer softer conditions.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: C&D winner for Joseph O'Brien; no impact over hurdles for this yard; modest effort in 1m4f handicap at Tramore on return from 98 days off latest; cheekpieces go on and drops into claiming company for yard with good record in these races.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: Well backed both starts for this stable; kept on well over 7f at Limerick for a never-dangerous sixth; had an excuse (coughing) when soundly beaten at Leopardstown latest (1m1f, god); tongue-tie (worn on best runs for former yard) returns and also sports blinkers; interesting.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: Close third at Limerick in June 2025 beginning to look like a flash in the pan; poor form over hurdles and on the Flat this year; tailed off at Fairyhouse latest (1m6f, good).

RaceName: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race
Spotlight: Minor promise in a couple of 7f/1m handicaps last October on soft/heavy off basement mark; toiling this season, however, and impossible to fancy on recent showings.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Not a bad level of form in two maiden outings; might have finished closer but for shipping a bump in a 1m3f maiden at Killarney last week; looks the stable second string here, though.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Second to a subsequent winner in 1m4f optional claimer at Limerick last month; predictably outclassed by 92-rated foe, who was 1-5, at Killarney last week, but handicapper gave her a 3lb rise all the same; step up in trip will suit.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Some encouraging word for her before her debut at Dundalk in November and ran with a deal of credit behind a Listed-class winner; reportedly failed to handle the softer ground at Cork in May; tongue-tie tried here and probably still some upside to this filly; has an ideal opportunity here.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Fared okay after a slow start on debut at Fairyouse over 1m2f; back up to a similar trip here after failing to build on that over 1m at the Curragh.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Poor performer on all known form; step up in trip unlikely to lead to an upturn in fortunes.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Down the field in a pair of better maidens; hard to make a case for here.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Well beaten in maidens over further at Fairyhouse and Tramore; needs this for a mark.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: No show in three runs in maidens over 7f to 1m; steps up in trip here and hard to ignore completely coming from these quarters; needs a lot more though.

RaceName: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden
Spotlight: Two decent efforts in ordinary maidens over 1m2f and 1m4f at Dundalk; steps back up in trip after an ordinary effort in an ordinary Killarney maiden last week; should fare better here.
Best run when fourth in a fast-ground handicap at Leopardstown last month over a similar trip; needs to bounce back here, but has the plum draw and certainly respected on that form.

Runner-up in a heavy ground nursery at Galway last October; failed to cut much ice on her seasonal bow at Down Royal last month; slower ground and probably a longer trip might be more of an optimum for her; best watched.
Overcame plenty of adversity when a strong-finishing third over C&D last month; experience of this track could be invaluable and has a very good draw, if able to get away on terms this time.
Showed a little ability in three runs in maidens; beaten out of sight in a Fairyhouse claimer since; others preferred.
No show in three maidens and never competitive on her handicap debut over 1m1f at Leopardstown, despite not being beaten far; cheekpieces tried this time.
Not a huge amount of encouragement from three runs in maidens; likely to do better in this sort of race, but a watching brief looks the prudent option here.

Far from disgraced in a maiden and a handicap on soft ground in the spring; step up to 1m4f proved beyond her in a Leopardstown handicap in May; champion jockey booked and clearly better is expected here, back down in trip.
Modest level of ability at a very low level; 5lb wrong here and unlikely to figure.
No show in three maidens and few chances have been taken with his opening mark; looks up against it.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Gained a first win for almost three years in a 1m Gowran handicap in April; failed to cut much ice in two efforts since; might just prefer it softer these days.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
