Spotlight: In good form this season without winning; just touched off over this trip at Gowran and a close second over 1m3f at Naas; needs to bounce back after a below-par effort at Killarney last week but every chance that he will; cheekpieces tried.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Six career wins and undergoing a real new lease of life this season with victories in handicaps at Killarney and Leopardstown; 11lb rise for those two wins is not excessive and every chance of going close once more.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
OwnerName: W Keeling & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick
Spotlight: Seven career wins and probably not as dependent on soft ground as he once was; consistent this season without really threatening to win and likely to run his race again.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Fair third off 70 in a heavy-ground maiden over this trip at Gowran last October; handicap mark going the right way, but overall form disappointing; the drop back in trip could be a positive.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Decent operator at a level on turf and AW, his most recent win coming in a 1m2f Dundalk handicap in January last year; not seen since third in a Tipperary handicap 14 months ago; market may prove the best guide.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Consistent enough filly; touched off in a heavy ground maiden over 1m2f for John O'Donoghue; seemed to see out longer trips quite well on her last two runs, here and at Tramore; drop back in trip  not certain to suit, but certainly respected.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Plenty of ability but has two ways of running; at her best when winning a competitive 1m heat at Gowran in June, much less so off a 7lb higher mark at Leopardstown 17 days later

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Started the season with victory in a 1m handicap at Cork and has kept his form well since without winning; close second over that trip at Bellewstown last time saw him go up another 2lb; new headgear combination tried here and unlikely to be far away; draw is the main negative

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Good level of form last summer culminated in a deserved success in a 1m2f handicap at Navan; very regressive this season, though, and hard to fancy on current evidence.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: Quite lightly raced since winning this race off 68 two years ago; encouraging effort after more than nine months off in a 1m4f handicap at Tramore two weeks ago; foolish to discount.

RaceName: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap
Spotlight: AW winner for Charlie Johnston last year,  but hardly a glimmer of form for her current connections; makes no appeal at present.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: No win since 2023; big chance off this mark on best runs over 1m6f/1m4f last season and though well beaten in both runs this term, they were over an inadequate trip; this distance much more suitable and Colin Keane takes over; interesting.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Hold-up sort signed off last season with a 12.5f win at Thurles for Dermot Weld; winning start for this yard at Leopardstown in May over 1m2f; has gone up 14lb for those two wins, but could continue to progress; chance.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden winner; below par first two runs this term (including when well held behind Londonofficallin in Cork Derby); step in the right direction when 3l third behind Daboya at Tramore latest in first-time tongue tie (retained); mark unchanged and place claims if backing that up.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: A winner of ten races over hurdles and on the Flat; scored in the Cork Derby (1m4f, soft) on most recent start in this sphere; just 4lb higher now, handles better ground and has run well over hurdles here before; okay run over fences latest and can't discount back on the level.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Four-time AW winner in France is just 1-10 on turf; has failed to beat a rival in first two runs for this stable; needs to revive upped markedly in trip.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Six-time winner, five of those coming on turf; ground-versatile and showed signs of returning to form when coming from the back for a 6.75l fourth of 15 at Leopardstown on latest; eased 2lb but has not run well on both previous visits to this venue.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Showed promise in a couple of starts for former yard in France; bought for E40,000 at Arqana last July and is likely best watched on stable debut after a 407-day absence, unless the market speaks.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Promise in maidens and far from disgraced on handicap debut at Navan (1m2f, good) where a 3l fourth of 11 in first-time blinkers (retained); could go well if he stays this longer trip, but pedigree raises questions.

RaceName: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Dangerous when gets his favoured soft conditions, as he did when bolting up at Bellewstown in October; however, he's never won off a mark this high, he lacks a run and this ground may be on the lively side.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Dual hurdles winner is 0-10 on the Flat (0-4 on turf); beaten 45l on stable debut after long layoff at Tramore latest; may need another run or two to find form; cheekpieces on.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden is 0-5 on turf but her last run at Killarney was encouraging (stayed on well over 1m for a 5l fifth); small yard has been in sensational form and it would be no surprise to see this filly run a big race upped markedly in trip; 1lb wrong but rider's claim negates that.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Won a 1m5f (good) Leopardstown handicap off basement mark of 40 on final start for Mags Mullins in May; solid first two runs for this yard; 5l third of 16 at Bellewstown (1m4f, good) and denied by short head at Down Royal (1m5f, good) three days ago; big chance off 2lb lower.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Admirable veteran gained a fourth turf win on the Flat at Sligo in May (1m6f, yld-sft); has come up short off revised mark since but has C&D form figures of 124 and the win came off 6lb higher than he is here; could go well.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Four wins in Britain for Ian Williams at 1m2f on all sorts of ground; yet to find form for this stable; new headgear combination tried after 8.5l defeat at Fairyhouse latest.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Heavy defeat when last seen on the Flat at Dundalk in January; pulled up over hurdles on return from 168 days latest; remote third over C&D last June off 8lb higher, so can't fully discount but needs to rediscover best.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Back to form with 1.5l third of 15 behind in-form Arch Enemy at Killarney (11.5f, good) five days ago; might prefer a bit of an ease in the ground, but place claims again off the same mark.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Solid strike rate of 4-18 on the AW but 0-11 on turf and has yet to trouble the judge; beaten 22l at Bellewstown 17 days ago; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Six-time AW winner is 0-19 on turf; hasn't looked like ending that winless run on last three starts, beaten 13l at Navan on latest; others hold stronger claims.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Pulled up in a bumper here; minor promise in AW maidens; soundly beaten in first two handicaps at Dundalk and can only be watched after 129-day break.

RaceName: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Has placed in three of his five runs this season, including when a 0.75l second to Arch Enemy (who has won again since) on latest at Navan (1m2f, good); also has placed form at 1m4f so decent chance he'll stay this far; place shout at least.
0-11 but has run some excellent races in defeat in stakes company; beaten 7.75l in 1m6f (good) Fairyhouse Group 3 on latest; rated 96 and a surprise if she didn't win this.
Three-time winner over hurdles; okay efforts over fences the last twice and now makes her belated Flat debut; probably best watched.

Built on mildly promising debut at Gowran (9.5f, soft) to chase home Ashikita when upped to 1m4f at Roscommon (good); an extra furlong here should pose no problems and she looks the main danger to Nuit; cheekpieces go on.

Bumper and maiden hurdle winner for Harry Kelly; creditable efforts on both Flat starts for this yard; 0.5l third of 8 at Bellewstown in April 2025; 7.25l fourth after layoff at Roscommon latest (1m4f, good); sharper for that and place chance.
Maiden hurdle winner at Kilbeggan in May; form otherwise poor, including heavy defeats in both bumpers; tailed off on handicap hurdle debut at Tramore on latest; best watched on Flat debut.

Chase and hurdle winner ran well on latest when runner-up in the Connacht National at Roscommon; beaten 12l when fourth on sole Flat start over 1m2f at Leopardstown in July 2024; would prefer softer ground.
A winner over fences and hurdles; not disgraced on belated Flat debut in a Tramore maiden on latest (1m4f, good), but much more needed to take this.
Off the mark at the fifth attempt in bumpers at Wexford on latest (2m1f, good); nicely bred (dam a half-sister to Casamento) and could challenge for place money on Flat debut.
Point-to-point and hunter chase winner; modest Flat debut at Leopardstown over 1m7f; a bit better when a 10.5l fourth over 1m6f at Killarney latest; should get a handicap mark after this.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Changed ownership for £380,000 prior to finishing 16th of 27 in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot, running respectably on the figures despite ending up further behind Pershaada than had been the case at Goodwood (5f, good) where she was an eye-catching second amid traffic issues; the form pick.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Effectively the most exposed contender, having raced five times; placed on three occasions, including twice over C&D; creditable second at Hamilton most recently; reasonably solid but figures in the 60s reflect that he's ordinary.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Absent and gelded since coming home last of the seven finishers at Thirsk in early May; that race has worked out well and he's half-brother to a multiple 5f winner for his yard, so improvement is plausible.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Invincible Army filly; dam unraced half-sister to useful winners Mannaal (1m-11.4f) and Bilhayl (5f), out of 6f 2yo Group 3 winner; probably best watched in this field on debut.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showed some promise over 6f on debut, without quite getting home; fared better over C&D (good to firm; finished second of seven) since and is evidently going to take after her 5f-winning dam; one of the main form players.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Has shown signs of ability at Bath (5.7f) and Chester (6f) while looking the type who'll be more interesting in nurseries shortly; chance today partly depends on whether the drop to a bare 5f prompts improvement.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: 10,000euros yearling; by Invincible Army; sibling to winners in Italy (5f/6f, including 2yo) and Poland (1m/1m2f); dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Dark Reckoning; check the betting.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Brings the worst form having finished last of five, achieving little, in 5f contest at Nottingham; looked green but he needs to improve markedly for that run.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 37,000euros yearling; by Ten Sovereigns and first foal of unraced half-sister to useful 6f 2yo winner Zumbi and daughter of unraced sister to smart sprinter Land Of Dreams; heed the market signals.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 40,000gns yearling, 70,000euros (breeze-up) 2yo; Havana Grey half-brother to 4.5f-6f winner Fondest Dream (including 2yo/US); dam maiden (RPR 56), sister to 6f Group 3 winner Keystroke; judged on sales information and the stable he represents, looks the pick of the newcomers.

RaceName: Racing TV EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Restricted Qual') (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 37,000gns yearling, 30,000gns (breeze-up) 2yo by Sioux Nation and first foal of unraced half-sister to Group-placed 7f 2yo winner Sparkling Beauty; yard is 0-34 with 2yos in last five seasons.
Scored on AW in April; inconsistent otherwise of late; has plenty of C&D form, including in this contest, but posted a substandard effort returned to this scenario last time.
Multiple winner in previous seasons; 0-11 this year but is proving consistent, close second returned to AW most recently; remains 1lb below last winning mark; in the mix.
Retains ability aged eight; made all at Nottingham (5f, soft) last time, building on his reappearance effort and registering an eighth success; has never gained back-to-back wins, though.

Struggled in Class 4 event last time; in good form in Class 5 otherwise of late, including C&D success in June; drops back to Class 6 but still needs to prove he can win off marks higher than the 50s.

Has gained both wins over 6f, including narrowly at Carlisle (good to firm) last time; back up only 3lb he may remain competitive, provided this drop to 5f proves no issue; opening mark was 13lb higher.
Bounced back to form at Leicester (5f, good to firm) but beat only two rivals and has gone back up 5lb for that win; returns to a deeper field, albeit has landed the plum draw.

OwnerName: J R Dwyer And B Smart
Spotlight: Has made the frame plenty of times since AW maiden win, close third at Thirsk most recently; 0-16 in handicaps but holds a fighting chance off unaltered mark, which is 12lb lower than opening one.
Prevailed in small field at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) last time, taking record in blinkers to 3-9; back up 4lb but Jack Callan takes off useful 3lb; has won over C&D; enters calculations.
Multiple winner down the years but is 0-7 this term and her form has declined to some degree, as current mark reflects; drops back to Class 6 for the first time in a while.

Far from consistent this season but got up in the final strides over C&D (good to firm; off 1lb higher) in May; possibilities provided he's back in similar form and the race again pans out favourably.
Back in form with three placed efforts this summer; the latest one took his C&D record to 1113; this front-running 8yo remains just 1lb above last winning mark; solid chance.
Scored over C&D in June; below par returned to this scenario last time but that race possibly came too soon after a good effort three days earlier; may rebound.
Ties in with some of today's rivals on recent C&D form but is still seeking a first success at this trip; has gained all Beverley wins over the extended 1m.

Narrow success in April took his C&D record to 2-3; has remained in form elsewhere since and his latest effort, in Class 2 at Epsom, can be marked up (hampered then rallied for third place); respected back here.

Lightly raced 5yo who has shown some useful form on the Flat and was placed in a good-quality Newbury novice (2m, good to soft) on hurdle debut in March, having travelled strongly for a long way; had wind op in May; needs to be taken very seriously.

Won on the Flat in France last year and had Listowel maiden hurdle (2m4f, good to yielding) at his mercy before last-flight fall on stable debut in May; first runner at this track for top Irish trainer Willie Mullins; obvious contender.

Formerly smart on the Flat (fourth in 2022 Derby) but was knocking about in low-grade handicaps last year; well beaten on stable/hurdle debut in May but shaped with much more promise when third over C&D (albeit well held in the end) later that month, and might collect another minor prize today.
Won Irish maiden point in May but hasn't shown much on her two hurdling starts here (2m1f/2m6f) this summer, the latter on Saturday.

Useful on the Flat, albeit yet to add to French maiden win in spring 2024 and not at best for new stable this year; has good standard to reach on hurdling debut but could have a future over jumps; had wind op in April.
Well beaten in a bumper and on both hurdling starts.
Lowly rated Flat maiden who was pulled up when a big-priced outsider for both hurdle runs last season.
Has shown some fair Flat form but became disappointing for David O'Meara last year and was soundly beaten in two 2m novice hurdles for new stable this spring.

Placed in all three bumpers last year in 2024; did not show a great deal over hurdles last year but had soft ground as a plausible excuse when tailed off here (2m1f) on handicap debut a year ago; tries a new trip on this first start since; worth a glance in the betting.
Unplaced all six hurdle starts; not disgraced when fourth of seven over about 2m6f (if additional yardage is included) at Market Rasen (good) last month, though, and may yet have a bigger run in him.

Three-time C&D winner, including last two editions of this race; would appeal sightly more on ground slower than good but his fourth here (3m1f, good) two starts ago was a good effort and his well-held fifth over C&D last month came in a much stronger race than this; high on the list.
Came good at ninth attempt, drawing 13l clear to score over C&D (good) last month; hiked up 10lb for that and too inconsistent to rely upon heavily but still an obvious one to consider.

Useful on the Flat; back over hurdles for new stable this season, with by far the best of three runs a close second at Warwick (2m, good) two starts ago; pulled up over 2m1f since and not easy to predict over this new trip.

Won over 2m1f (good) here last summer and was second here on next two outings (2m6f/3m1f); not at same level this year (four runs) and was tailed off last time (2m1f) but can't be ruled out off current mark.
Free-goer who won twice at Bangor last year (2m3f/2m7f); absent since consecutive heavy defeats last July/September, though, and returns with quite a bit to prove.
Consistent in defeat last autumn and winter (2m3f-2m4f) but well below best since returning from three-month break this spring (three runs), and was pulled up over C&D on only previous visit here.
0-9 in points and 0-7 under rules; tailed off on last month's chasing debut (1m7f), after a break, and now reverts to hurdling in new headgear; 9lb out of the weights; difficult to enthuse over.
Bumper winner; made quite promising start to hurdling career last autumn but looked out of sorts in two handicaps this spring (3m2f/2m7f) and it takes a leap of faith to support him here.
Beaten over 19l when third over C&D last month and now 0-8 over hurdles but ran big race when second over C&D (good) on stable debut in May and has strong claims if judged on that performance.

Five-time hurdle winner, most recently off today's mark at Huntingdon (3m1f, good to soft) in November; has become inconsistent, though, and dropped out quite tamely after making the running at Fontwell in May.

Returned from seven-month break with creditable third over C&D (good) in May and has obvious each-way claims if judged on that effort but Market Rasen last month was a backward step and he's now 0-14 over hurdles.

OwnerName: Mrs G Jenkinson And Mrs B Butterworth
Spotlight: Regressive 7yo who had a disappointing campaign last season; returns from four-month break on a dangerous mark but was soundly beaten on both previous starts here and has quite a bit to prove.

Seemed to have been aided by a wind op when placed at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) in April, his second handicap, but was pulled up on next two outings (latter was chase debut) and has since left Ben Pauling; has tongue-tie refitted for stable debut; cheekpieces removed after one use.

In-form 7yo who comes here after two narrow wins at Market Rasen (both 3m+, good); latest 4lb rise ought to be manageable and this drop back in trip won't be a problem; big player if suited by this different track.

2-17 over hurdles; not yet proven over quite this far but posted good effort when third at Perth (2m4f, good) this month and didn't run badly over 2m1f on only previous visit to Cartmel; could have a say.

0-47 under all codes, having spent the bulk of his career in Ireland; flopped badly when favourite for recent stable debut at Stratford (2m2f, good to firm) but tries a new trip and sports first-time blinkers here; no surprise if Dan Skelton finds the key to him soon.
Four hurdle wins, including this race in 2022; well held in C&D selling handicap in May, after a break, but last month's keeping-on second here was much better and he remains on a workable mark.

Resurgent 10yo who led close home at Perth (2m, good) last month and has now won three times since April; unlucky to come to grief when back at Perth last week and remains of strong interest, albeit he was well beaten over C&D on his only previous start here.

Took a while to get off the mark for current stable and had become expensive to follow but exploited much-reduced mark when winning stylishly at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good to firm) a week ago and still looks well treated under a 7lb penalty.

Swapped usual cheekpieces for refitted visor and gave good account when third from 3lb out of the weights over C&D (good) on Saturday; will effectively be 1lb lower if he turns out again but his 0-42 career strike-rate is not easily overlooked.
Now 9lb lower than when making all over C&D (good) last August but his form has slumped since and a revival is needed.

Ran well for a long way when third at Kelso (2m2f, good) in April but two lesser efforts have followed and he's now 0-7 for current stable; sometimes races too freely; others have more pressing claims.

Improved to cause 25-1 surprise in C&D (good) novice last month, her fourth start over hurdles, but the value of that form is open to question (market principals disappointed) and her opening handicap mark probably demands further progress.
Out of form for new stable this year and needs recent wind op to have made a big difference.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Very useful in his prime and enjoying a revival this year, with the latter of two wins gained here (3m5f, good) in May; last month's C&D third was perfectly respectable and he ought to be right in the thick of things again.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Former pointer/hunter chaser who won a Sedgefield handicap (3m2f, good to soft) off 2lb higher for Ruth Jefferson in January; not quite in same form on first four starts for new stable and fell on latest outing a week ago but it's difficult to put a line through him.

RaceName: RF Miller & Co Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Left clear at final fence to exploit reduced mark at Down Royal (2m4f, good to yielding) on Boxing Day 2024 and will be fine over this longer trip but this is his first run since and he's a 12yo now.

RaceName: Weatherbys Design & Print Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Delivered on promise shown in Irish points/bumpers when making all twice over hurdles in novice company at Hexham (2m/2m4f, good) in May; respectable third on handicap debut there (2m4f, good) last month and looks quite interesting on this chase debut, even from 4lb out of the weights.

RaceName: Weatherbys Design & Print Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won novice hurdle in April and is 3-3 over fences since, the latest win gained in three-runner contest at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last month; may still have more improvement to come if aided by first-time cheekpieces but contests a stronger race here and the drop back in trip is not sure to suit.

RaceName: Weatherbys Design & Print Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Signed off for Twiston-Davies stable with creditable second behind a next-time-out winner over hurdles in May, having made the running in first-time cheekpieces; last throughout on stable debut without headgear in four-runner Newton Abbot chase this month but the cheekpieces are back on here and it will be interesting to see whether connections revert to more positive tactics.

RaceName: Weatherbys Design & Print Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slightly disappointing when weakening fifth on last month's chasing debut at Hexham but now 2lb lower than when close third over hurdles here in May and will be dangerous if able to transfer that form to fences.

One of two to pull clear of the others when opening account at Newcastle (2m7f, good to soft) in March, and both subsequent fourths (3m/3m1f; latter was here) were perfectly respectable; may benefit from this drop back in trip; no surprise if he features.
Well handicapped on old form but failed to complete three consecutive races in April-June and was well beaten here (2m1f) on Saturday; difficult to enthuse over.
Bettered low-key stable debut (over hurdles) when second to very progressive rival over C&D (good) last month and remains well handicapped on some of his form for Jamie Snowden; likely contender.

1-16 over hurdles, having gained a hard-fought course win (2m6f, good) in May; evidently well suited by this track but will need to find hidden reserves to overcome a 4lb higher mark on this chasing debut.

Gained all three chase wins at this track (2m5f-3m1f); bounced back from two lacklustre efforts when staying on to go close here (3m1f, good; usual tongue-tie/blinkers left off) on Saturday and remains well handicapped but it's hard to predict whether he'll be in the right mood again; wears cheekpieces for first time since 2024.
Well beaten on both starts this year (3m1f/2m3f) and makes no appeal from 10lb out of the handicap.

OwnerName: Dennis J Coppola & Mrs Dianne Sayer
Spotlight: Placed in two 2m7f Kelso chases in the autumn (good/good to soft) but ran poorly over 3m1f here on Saturday, after a five-month break, and will need to rebound quickly.

Led close home to cause 25-1 surprise over C&D (good) in May, form that has been very well advertised by the placed horses (one was Kingofthegame) since; not in same form over hurdles last month but still strongly considered; wears first-time cheekpieces.

OwnerName: T J Stubbins and M E Sowersby
Spotlight: Placed three consecutive times in March-May (2m4f-2m5f, good/good to soft) and has claims if judged on that form but didn't fire when well-held third of four on latest outing and also disappointed on only previous visit to Cartmel; usually ridden patiently; others appeal more.

Modest form in his first two starts but he found plenty of improvement when a close fourth of ten at Doncaster (6f, good to firm; 20-1) 17 days ago; needs to build on that but it's still early days and he's a half-brother to a useful sprinter; in the mix on nursery debut.

Weakened into a remote fourth on Haydock debut (6f, soft) in May but he left that form behind when runner-up to an emphatic winner at Pontefract (6f, good) last month; that form has been boosted by the third since and he needs a close look on nursery debut.

Showed promise in her first two runs before battling well to beat the two market leaders in tight finish at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last month; should have more to offer now switched to a nursery and she's a key player.

Faded into fifth in his first two runs but he kept on well for a last-gasp success in a Bath novice (5.6f, firm) 19 days ago; the runner-up's rider had some issues with the reins in the closing stages but this well-bred colt is going the right way and he's respected on nursery debut.

Promising third on Newmarket debut (6f, good) in May; ran respectably when in midfield in Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot next time and she had another stiff task in a Group 2 at Newmarket ten days ago; this is more realistic and she needs watching in the market on nursery debut.

OwnerName: The Lamb Inn Wantage Racing Team
Spotlight: Comfortable winner at Bath (5.6f, firm) in May but that was a small-field maiden and he struggled in the Woodcote at Epsom (6f, good to soft) last time; now back in calmer waters on quicker ground but he has a mixed record so far and needs to kick on again after a gelding operation.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: 28,000gns breeze-up 2yo; closely related to Italian 6f-7.5f winner Dottor Misagu (including 2yo); dam Italian 7.5f 2yo Listed winner, half-sister to winners Raneenn (6f including 2yo) and King Of Scotia (7f/1m including 2yo); plenty to like on paper but yard is 1-20 with 2yos this season.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Didn't show much on her Sandown debut but she kept on well when fourth of ten at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 11 days ago; that was a promising effort and she could be dangerous if she can build on that.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: 50,000gns yearling; second foal; half-sister to 6f winner Flash Harry (RPR 106); dam sprint maiden (51), half-sister to 5f/6f winners Benny And The Jets and Wiley Post, out of 6f winning sister to Listed-placed 6f winner Poppy Seed; yard 23% with 2yos this season and she's an interesting newcomer; tongue-tie on.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: 40,000gns yearling by Showcasing; 12-1 on Newbury debut (6f, good to firm) last month and she ran green before finishing a well-held seventh of ten; should know more this time but she needs a major step forward.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Out of Irish 1,000 Guineas/Yorkshire Oaks winner Pleascach; well-held sixth in both runs, but it was a step forward at Epsom (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago and she shaped as though this drop back in trip could suit; not ruled out.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: 8,500gns foal, £55,000 yearling; third foal; Harry Angel half-sister to 8.3f winner Sylkie (RPR 77); dam 1m2f winner (79), closely related to 1m4f winner Caledonian Crusade, out of 1m2f winning half-sister to 10.5f Group 3 winner Dance Dress; has speed and stamina in pedigree and market should guide on debut.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Didn't live up to market expectations on Yarmouth debut last month but she left that form a long way behind when beating a clear second at Ripon (6f, good) two weeks ago; has a penalty but she showed a good attitude last time and this well-bred filly is open to more progress; key player.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (EBF Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Half-sister to three winners including Whenthedealinsdone (5f/6f including 2yo; RPR 102); wasn't beaten far when sixth on Kempton debut in May but she found plenty of progress when a clear third at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 11 days ago; didn't get much luck in that race and could be a big factor if she gets the breaks this time.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 375,000gns foal; gelded brother to 1m2f/1m4f winner Bay Bridge (including Group 1; RPR 125), half-brother to winners Stormy Sea (1m; 90) and Nataleena (1m5f-2m; 73); dam sprint maiden (59), half-sister to 1m2f Group 2 winner Shimraan; lots to like on paper and he needs watching in market.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: RC Syndicate X and Gary Gillies
Spotlight: 90,000gns half-brother to a 1m3f winner in Germany; well held in sole 2yo run but he's been knocking on the door in novice events at York (1m, good) and Thirsk (1m, good to firm) this season; sets a clear standard on that form and he's open to more progress at this new trip; strong contender.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 100,000euros yearling; second foal; dam twice-raced (runner-up at 1m4f; RPR 76) half-sister to winners Pakistan Star (Hong Kong 1m2f/1m4f Group 1) and Ninas Terz (useful German 6f 2yo); has good standard to aim at on debut but she needs watching in market.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 150-1 and beaten out of sight in a novice at Salisbury (7f, good) last October; gelded since and can only be watched on return for new yard.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 330,000gns foal, 500,000gns yearling; second foal; half-brother to 7f/1m AW winner Breakdancer (RPR 87); dam 5.7f/6f 2yo winner (including Listed; 106), half-sister to useful 1m4f/1m5f Flat and 2m hurdle winner Nessun Dorma; interesting newcomer and he needs a close look.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 210,000gns yearling; third foal; gelded half-brother to winners Lava Stream (1m/1m2f including Listed; RPR 107) and Iron Lion (1m2f/1m4f; 103); dam 1m 2yo/1m2f winner (95), half-sister to winners Journey (1m4f Group 1) and Mimikyu (14.5f Group 2); one of two newcomers for Godolphin and interesting to see how he figures in the market.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Struggled in two bumpers and he's been beaten 16l at big prices in both Flat runs (1m2f) this summer.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Tailed off at big prices in both runs (1m6f/1m3f) this summer, with RPRs in the 30s on both occasions.

RaceName: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 125-1 and he finished a tailed-off last on recent Chepstow debut (7f, good to firm).

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: His last win was in December 2024 but he's finished runner-up over C&D (good to firm) in his last two starts including behind Lequinto on his penultimate run; didn't get much luck when returned to hold-up tactics last Monday and he looks interesting with Oisin Murphy booked again.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Eight of his 14 wins have come at Windsor and latest was a comfortable success over C&D (good to firm) three weeks ago; up 5lb but he still looks on a workable mark and has been in good form since April; big player.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Four-time turf winner including off 5lb higher over C&D (good to firm) last spring; well held at Wolverhampton when last seen in March but that was after a good spell on AW including a Kempton win; has good record when fresh and he needs a close look back from four months off.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Made a successful 2yo debut but he was soon in deep water and his form deteriorated; seen only twice in 2025 but he's been placed a couple of times this season including when third over C&D (good to firm) on his penultimate run; looks interesting on that form and he's not ruled out off a dangerous mark.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Two turf wins last summer and three AW wins this year, the latest at Wolverhampton in April; ran well when third of five at Salisbury next time but three lesser runs have followed and he needs to raise his game.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Won at Dundalk (6f, AW) in January but he's not come close to that form since and was was well held on recent stable debut; now goes back up in trip but he's 1-19 on turf and others are preferred.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Won on Bath debut (5f, good to soft) last October before a second at Wolverhampton 11 days later; well held on handicap debut over C&D last month but he may have needed that run and he's still unexposed; not ruled out.

RaceName: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Exposed mare who is 6-45 on turf; beaten in claimers on final two runs in Ireland in May and was well held in an Epsom handicap (6f, good; 33-1) on recent stable debut; has something to prove and all of her wins have been over further.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: 250,000euros yearling; made it third-time lucky with an easy win at Southwell (1m, AW) in May and she had a tough task on handicap debut at Royal Ascot (Sandringham) last month; finished in rear in that race but she still has potential and is bred to be suited by this new trip; could resume her progress back in calmer waters.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to connections' Oaks winner Soul Sister; close second to useful rival at Kempton (1m, AW) on sole 2yo start; disappointing on Sandown reappearance in April but she bounced back with an emphatic win at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) last month; looks on fair mark now switched to a handicap and she's open to more progress back on turf; interesting contender.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Generally progressive filly who has form figures of 42321 and she landed the odds with a runaway win in a Pontefract novice (1m, good) three weeks ago; this is tougher off a revised mark back in a handicap but she should have more to offer at this new trip; respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Reappeared with a clearcut win at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in April but she's lost her way with heavy defeats at Sandown and Newbury in last two runs; has plenty to prove again and overall record is now 1-14.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Started this season with two wins at Nottingham (8.3f, good) but she's been well held in her last two starts; didn't get the best of runs at Sandown last time but she needs to find more on this step up to 1m2f.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Four-race maiden but she started her handicap career with a creditable second at Lingfield (1m2f, good; 20-1) last month; nudged up 1lb but she kept on well last time and is open to more progress at this trip; in the mix.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Support The Big Bear Voyage Fillies' Handicap (GBBplus Race)
Spotlight: Off the mark at the sixth attempt when scoring on Wolverhampton reappearance (8.6f, AW) in May; backed that up with a close call at this track (1m, good to firm) but her progress stalled with a disappointing run at Newmarket last time; has bit to prove again after that and she needs to bounce back with tongue-tie added; stablemate of Molo Del Palazzo.

Returned to form with a brave win at Epsom (1m2f, good) 19 days ago and he backed that up with a creditable third at Brighton (1m2f, good to firm); a 2lb rise has now kicked in but he remains feasibly treated and should go well again.

Four-time course winner (1m-1m2f) but his last success was over 2m on AW last March; on dangerous mark but he's returned from a lengthy absence with two low-key runs this summer including over C&D; bit to prove and needs to rediscover his spark.

Six-time AW winner who is 0-12 on grass but he's been placed on turf in his last three runs including when runner-up at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) 16 days ago; on same mark here and he should be in the thick of things again.

Progressive once handicapping over this trip last year, winning four from six (three on Polytrack), latterly off a 2lb lower mark; held in three runs this season but she wasn't beaten far at Lingfield last time and that was more like it; not ruled out.
Inconsistent ten-race maiden who was tailed off in a Bath handicap (11.6f, good) last time; others preferred.

Won two in a row at Nottingham (1m2f, good/good to soft) last summer but she's been out of sorts this season and failed to beat a rival at Nottingham last time; now 8lb lower than for her last success but she needs to turn things around.

Runner-up off this mark at Newbury (1m, good) in May but slow starts can be an issue and he's been well held in his last two runs; didn't get much luck at Nottingham last time but he's not easy to predict and others are more persuasive.

No win in his first 18 starts but he made the breakthrough in a handicap here (11.4f, good to firm) last month and backed that up with a creditable third on his return visit seven days later; now drops back in trip but he ran well over C&D in May and he still looks on a workable mark; shortlisted.

His last win was two years ago but he's been placed in all three runs this season including close calls over C&D (good to firm) and at Ffos Las (1m2f, good); remains well handicapped on his old form and he should make another bold bid.

OwnerName: Mrs Wendy Jarrett & J S Moore
Spotlight: Won 1m handicaps at Bath (good to firm) and Lingfield (AW) last year; well treated on that form but she's been generally disappointing since her last success and was beaten 4l when third at Bath last time; needs to raise her game and she's untried at this trip.

Got off the mark with tongue-tie added at Kempton (1m, AW) in April 2025, but he had a long spell on the sidelines before finishing tailed off in two runs this summer; still has low-mileage but he needs a revival.

Six-race maiden who has not finished closer than fifth and was never dangerous at Bath (1m, good) last month; wasn't disgraced behind a major improver last time but he needs to produce a more dynamic effort here.

Won at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February and runner-up at Southwell (1m, AW) and Bath (1m, firm) in the spring; still looks on a workable mark but his form nosedived at Brighton last time and he needs to bounce back; one of three runners for Tony Carroll.

Added to his two turf wins when finishing well to score on AW at Lingfield (7f) last October; hasn't hit the same level in two subsequent runs but he returned after wind surgery with a fair third in a Class 4 at Salisbury (7f, good) last month; looks worth another try at this trip and he's in the mix on this drop back in grade.

OwnerName: Mrs R Coleman And G Glendining
Spotlight: Turf and dual AW winner who ran near her best when runner-up from wide draw at Kempton (1m, AW; 11-4 favourite) 12 days ago; that was behind an improver who made all and she's a key player off unchanged mark.
11-time winner, with five on turf and six on AW; his last success was off 2lb higher at Southwell in March but he's struggled since and needs to get back on track.

Pulled up on hurdle debut when last seen but he's a dual AW winner who is well handicapped on his second at Doncaster (1m, good) last summer; has run well when fresh in the past and he needs watching in market on reappearance; refused to enter stalls in last intended start.

Turned things around with a breakthrough win at Wolverhampton (8.5f) in May; disappointing at Ffos Las next time but he bounced back with an eye-catching fifth at Kempton 12 days ago; remains well handicapped on old form and has claims if this sets up for his closing style.

Placed all three bumper starts for John McConnell, including Cheltenham third in October where he was a neck off a Skelton horse who has won three hurdles since and is now rated 137; after six months off, unplaced in a Kilbeggan bumper on stable debut; good third of 17 on hurdling debut at Listowel in late May; not much of note behind him, but winner had landed a bumper impressively and runner-up was sixth in the Asoct Stakes next time.

Beaten favourite but not a bad run in first bumper at Galway in October, beaten 9l; not as good next time and, for one from champion trainer's yard, significant that she was sent off 22-1 when beaten 42l on hurdling debut at Roscommon

Tailed off in soft-ground bumper here last year; was shaping well on hurdling debut at Clonmel when knuckling on landing two out, fourth at the time and with running left to give; well beaten in Roscommon novice latest, but the three ahead of him were all previous winners; place chance.

Phoenix Of Spain half-brother to five Flat winners was second in 1m2f maiden at Ripon last year, when trained by the owner's son; well beaten in three starts on the Flat in Ireland; tongue-tie fitted for hurdling debut; can be keen.
20s when ridden by Harry Cobden in Roscommon maiden hurdle, beaten 43l; will need more time.

Won on his third bumper start for Andy Slattery when making all at Roscommon in August; well held on yard debut in Listowel maiden hurdle the following month, and ran like he needed his comeback at Tramore in late May.
Nothing so far Flat or hurdles.
Well beaten in a bumper and maiden hurdle.

Diamond Boy mare cost 50,000euros at three; half-sister to winners Scorpion's Revenge (bumper/useful US 2m2f hurdle), Arthur Fonzarelli (2m1f hurdle) and Neigh Botha (bumper and 2m/2m1f hurdle/chase); dam unraced half-sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Native River.
40s, never invoved when beaten 30l on debut in maiden hurdle at Sligo.
Valirann gelding off the mark on seventh starts in points in May, when with John Edward Walsh; hood on for stable/rules debut.
33s, hampered and unseated rider at the second at Roscommon; will need this experience.
Newcomer by Aizavoski cost 12,500euros as 3yo; second foal; dam unraced sister to bumper and useful jumps winner Shoal Bay.
Modest on the Flat, rated just 34; can only be watched on hurdling debut.
Big prices and well beaten so far, although the Sligo maiden in which she was beaten 22l on her penultimate start has produced three winners.
Fancied for two points but failed to complete; 30l fourth over 2m4f on hurdling debut at Limerick gives him something to build on.

Unplaced in two bumpers before hurdling debut sixth at Tramore; 2-1 fav at Kilbeggan, travelled well to challenge but stuck his head up on the run-in and was inclined to lug in behind the winner; that raises a concern and bit to find with Whats New on the figures.

Waldgeist gelding is a sibling of nine winners, notably smart hurdler Colonel Mustard; beaten favourite all starts; one-paced in two bumpers over farther; no extra in fifth on hurdling bow at Roscommon, after being messed about by a loose horse and making mistakes; a less eventful contest should see a better performance in a first-time tongue-tie.

Godolphin cast-off related to Group winners; decent maiden form last summer for Matt Smith, including  narrow defeat in 10.5f maiden at Down Royal, and raced off 78 when last seen in that sphere (Whats New is 62 on the Flat); lame on hurdles debut; after seven months off, beaten 20l at Sligo in May where jumping was novicey late on.

OwnerName: Ms Margaret Nevin & Ms Alana Insole
Spotlight: Homebred Jukebox Jury mare whose dam was useful 2m4f/2m5f hurdle winner for Willie Mullins; fine run when 100-1 in 2m maiden hurdle here, beaten 17l and splitting two subsequent winners; gets an extra furlong here, but will probably want 2m4f before long; still, should go well in first-time tongue-tie.
Best of four point runs was on debut when 4l off useful type; tailed off in bumper latest.
Rules debut for Berkshire half-sister to smart staying jumper Salvador Ziggy; pulled up in two point runs with a week of each other last October.
Best run was when beaten 27l in Roscommon maiden hurdle; tailed off other starts under rules.
Second in Roscommon bumper last year; two mishaps after, including a fall when out of contention on only hurdles run; beaten 20l in bumper latest.
Pulled up in a point and only got as far as the first flight of hurdles here in May.
Big prices and has shown little in bumpers and over hurdles; new headgear combination.
Affinisea half-brother to 2m3f/3m hurdle winner Cosmo Renfro; dam unraced half-sister to useful 2m4f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Shang Tang, out of bumper/2m hurdle winner.

Flat winner has a kink in him, and has twice run out, but solid seconds last twice and there was good money for him last time when clear of the remainder at Sligo, beaten around 2l by 115-rated rival; ground suits and this is a good opportunity.

Ended last Flat season with a respectable fifth on handicap debut in a 25-runner 1m2f Curragh race on heavy ground; fit from hurdling before beginning new Flat campaign with an encouraging fifth at Leopardstown; not as good at that venue last time, but may improve on previous hurdling form.
Had been mixing Flat and hurdling action to useful effect before an off-day at this venue in May; hard to fancy after another poor run at Limerick.

Won 2m1f Clonmel handicap in April (yielding), followed that with a couple of ordinary runs off revised mark; good chance now following a return to form with Wexford second; yard has been among the winners lately and tongue-tie added.
Some promise in 2024 maiden runs; tailed off at Listowel in May on first run after a long layoff; handicap debut now.

Shock win when bolting up at 40-1 off 93 at Cork in April (2m, yielding); mid-field off revised mark at Limerick later that month, when testing ground may not have suited; unplaced favourite in a novice contest at Downpatrick last month.

Won a Downpatrick maiden hurdle for Gordon Elliott in April 2024; Galway fifth (2m, good to yielding) last October was best effort since joining this yard; should be better for his run at this track in May.
Took a small step in the right direction on seasonal debut at Sligo, much more required; 2lb wrong but useful 5lb claimed.

Some promise in two maiden hurdles in 2024 but was disappointing when favourite on return at Tipperary early last season; pulled up on handicap debut last August; absent since; from a top stable, so not ruled out
Has shown his best form at Clonmel, but was pulled up at that venue on his most recent start; previous fourth at Limerick was no more than satisfactory.

RaceName: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a bumper in France, but had proved frustrating over hurdles until off the mark on ninth start in this discipline when making all over this trip in a Sligo maiden; runner-up has leading claims in 5.06 on this card; son of It's Gino with poster-boy looks and should make a nice chaser in time.

RaceName: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Plenty of experience over hurdles and fences in France, had nine runs as 4yo; after a break, was well-backed winner of 2m maiden hurdle at Limerick and third won by a street lately; tackles good ground for the first time, but Doctor Dino's progeny are rarely troubled by it, nor is his talented brother and stablemate Zurich.

RaceName: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle
OwnerName: M R D Fleming & G Bruce & J P Ryan & Miss G Ryan
Spotlight: Up front throughout when winning Sligo handicap over this trip; effectively 10lb higher, but further progress is likely.

RaceName: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Unplaced all eight starts and all of 31lb wrong at the weights; would need to start now.

RaceName: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Long-standing maiden in both codes; second in claiming hurdle at Sligo two runs back; 7lb wrong at the weights and hard to fancy in this company.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has lost her way since winning a Kilbeggan maiden hurdle last August; beaten 24l in mares' handicap hurdle at this venue

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had shown little, Flat or hurdles, before running way above expectations (300-1) in a conditions hurdle at this venue in May; another fair run in a Downpatrick maiden hurdle; down the field in a Flat handicap at Limerick last time; new headgear combination.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has recorded three of his five hurdle starts at Cartmel; below his best there last time; overall Irish form is unconvincing.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 2-14 over hurdles; returned from a long layoff with a decisive Flat win at Navan in March (1m6f, heavy); well beaten off this hurdles mark at Roscommon last month; capable of better, appears to be ground-versatile.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Ended his time with Fergal O'Brien with back-to-back hurdle wins at Taunton and Chepstow in March/April 2024; after a long absence, had two Flat runs (including a satisfactory display at this venue) before being sent back over hurdles at Sligo nine days ago; made all and has a good chance despite 5lb rise.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole win for Ross O'Sullivan came in a Thurles maiden hurdle (2m, good) the season before last; weak handicap form last season; hard to make a case for him on stable debut.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Came back from a long layoff to start last season's campaign with back-to-back handicap wins at Navan (soft-to-heavy) and Leopardstown (yielding); beaten favourite in two novice hurdles in January; perhaps some doubt about how he will handle the ground.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a Tipperary maiden hurdle last year; pulled up in a chase at Wexford last month; had an excuse (badly hampered four out) when well beaten at last year's Galway festival on his only handicap hurdle outing.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Mrs Helen Mullins & M J Lomax
Spotlight: No success since a juvenile maiden hurdle win at Fairyhouse in November 2024; has dropped a long way in the ratings from an opening mark of 111 to 94; should enter calculations based on a third placing at Clonmel in April.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Returns from an 11-month layoff on a hat-trick after back-to-back victories at this venue and Bellewstown, both on good ground, last August; has gone up a total of 13lb; further progress is feasible.
Weak form in maidens; pulled up in handicaps at Kilbeggan (twice) and Tramore in recent months; transformation required in first-time cheekpieces.

Won a maiden on good-to-yielding over 2m3f at Limerick last October; probably not suited by testing ground in two runs before a break; encouraging run after five months off when third in an 18-runner contest at Limerick in May; stable in good form, solid chance.
Dual hurdles winner; badly out of form last summer; back from absence when pulled up in Cork handicap hurdle; suffered the same fate over fences at Limerick.
Some improvement at Limerick last time, but still needs plenty more; cheekpieces discarded.

OwnerName: Profit In Your Pocket Racing Club
Spotlight: Has struggled in four handicap attempts; 66-1 chance when pulled up at Sligo nine days ago.
Sole win came at Downpatrick (2m6f, good) nearly two years ago; third at Thurles over same trip last October her best run since; down the field in two runs in May,

All three hurdle wins have come at this venue, the last one in 2025; pulled up over C&D in May; was in the process of running a good race when falling in the lead two from home at Clonmel last month; 10yo mare could go well if suffering no ill effects.

Brought off an 80-1 shock at Kilbeggan last autumn when fitted with cheekpieces for the first time; remote seventh at Limerick early this month after a break; got a lot closer to the same winner when fifth at Kilbeggan the following week.
Never a factor in four maiden hurdles; needs to step up considerably from his first handicap run at Limerick.
Point winner two years ago; respectable run on debut at Gowran last November; given a break after two subsequent poor efforts; tongue-tie on now for handicap debut.
Placed three times at around 2m4f; lost form after a good run at Cork 12 months ago; towards the rear in a maiden at Dowpatickm last month.

C&D winner in May 2024; lost form after fourth placing at Limerick later that year; failed to make his presence felt over fences last season; struggled on his return to hurdling at Roscommon recently.
Returned from almost three years off when pulled up in a point in February; weakened to finish tenth of 16 at Sligo six weeks ago on his first hurdles start since 2023.

Runner-up in races at Down Royal (twice) and Downpatrick in March/April; struggled in first-time cheekpieces at Kilbeggan; same story when cheekpieces discarded for chase debut at Downpatrick; hard to be confident.
Fair placed form in points; has a modest record on the track; needs to raise her game after finishing sixth at Limerick last time.
Veteran was a long way out of the handicap when achieving a Punchestown win last month, the third success of a 34-race career; solid display when third at Kilbeggan off his revised mark; stays well.

OwnerName: John Patrick Ryan & Miss Gillian Ryan
Spotlight: Took a step forward over hurdles when third at Clonmel in March (2m3f, soft); well below that level over fences at Tramore next time; has failed to complete his last two races; stable in form, good 5lb claimer.

OwnerName: J R Robinson & Mrs E Keane
Spotlight: Easily won a 2m5f Tramore handicap hurdle off in August 2023; down the field at Punchestown after a very long absence.
Lightly-raced mare; improved display when third over 2m at Kilbeggan last time; this trip may not be ideal.

Promoted to third at Limerick in May after the winner's disqualification; followed that with a fair third at Sligo; hampered and unseated at the sixth at Bellewstown; back in the money when third at Kilbeggan last time; one of the more appealing runners.

Point winner for Colin Bowe; placed in a modest maiden hurdle for Gavin Cromwell last summer; shaped promisingly when second to a fellow outsider at Bellewstown on first run for this stable; could provide the solution.
Beaten around 10l in seventh at Kilbeggan in her first handicap; left with quite a bit to do then; open to improvement.
Two Flat wins in 2022; finished last in two Dundalk runs after a long absence, and well held in latest three runs on turf; fifth in a Tramore handicap in 2024 was his best effort over hurdles.

Won a Punchestown handicap hurdle (2m4f, good) last October off 87; decent third on handicap chase debut at Punchestown in June; brought down in a hurdle race at Bellewstown early this month; holds a definite chance after a recent third placing at Sligo; cheekpieces may help.
Has looked badly out of form in two 2026 outings; maiden, placed twice from 15 starts.
Maiden after 39 starts, placed 11 times; unseated in a chase on latest; not a betting proposition.
Won a 2m6f Tramore handicap hurdle in April last year; fair run at Clonmel early last month; down the field when quite well fancied (9-2) at Limerick last time.
Modest overall form; has failed to reach the first six in six outings in 2026; hard to be confident unless a tongue-tie makes a big difference.
Moderate French hurdles form; unraced during a spell with Gordon Elliott; has done nothing to advertise his chance of gaining a breakthrough win.

Homebred Getaway gelding; dam placed over 1m5f, sister to yard's high-class jumper Peregrine Run and Takeyourcapoff (1m6f Flat and useful 2m-2m4f hurdle), out of bumper winner; only 11-2 when mid-division in 18-runner bumper at Punchestown; should be capable of better and anything Adam Ryan rides in bumpers is always worth a second glance.

Cost 40,000euros as 3yo; half-brother to bumper/2m hurdle winner The Model Kingdom and dam also won a bumper; smart family farther back in the pedigree as well; fancied for both points but failed to complete.

Jet Away 5yo was only 9-1 for Kilbeggan debut; raced prominently and keenly before fading; beaten less than 7l, but the fact that only around 10l covered the first 10 home gives the form a dubious look; hood might help.

Nathaniel half-brother was a cheap yearling; half-brother to four winners, notably Stuart Crawford's useful bumper and hurdles performer Mongibello; dam French 1m1f/10.5f winner, half-sister to French 2m5f Grade 3 hurdle winner; bar set low for debut.
25s for Navan debut last September, prominent until weakening 2f out when beaten 18l in fair race.
Tailed off in heavy-ground contest at Naas before being beaten 36l at Bellewstown lately.
Homebred by Rajj; fourth foal; unraced dam is out of half-sister to Champion Hurdle winner Flakey Dove; yard only 3-86 in bumpers last five seasons.

Diamond Boy half-brother to three winners in France, including Le But (1m2f-1m3f Flat and useful 2m1f-2m4f hurdle/chase); dam Flat/hurdles winner, half-sister to Eoin Griffin's smart dual-purpose mare Lounaos; no joy in two point outings.
80s, much better on second start when beaten 8.5l at Kilbeggan where he looked green before staying on late; that's not hectic form, but has a place shout.
Has run twice in Roscommon hurdles; beaten a long way last year and early exit lately.
Has run in three points, a bumper and a maiden hurdle; seems modest.

Newcomer by Feels Like Dancing; first foal; dam unplaced bumpers/maiden hurdles, sister to 2m3f-3m hurdle winner Onlyfoolsownhorses, half-sister to three other hurdle winners; yard 0-35 in bumpers last five seasons.
In-form yard but 5yo has shown nothing so far in a bumper and maiden hurdle; headgear left off this time.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
Spotlight: Scrambled home in a 1m6f handicap here (good to firm) last month; no threat in an Epsom handicap since; drops in trip and wouldn't want this to become tactical.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
Spotlight: Over two years since the last of his three wins; yet to shine in 2026 but he drops into a 0-50 classified for the first time and he can't be discounted.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
Spotlight: Two 1m2f wins this year, the latest a fast-ground handicap at Leicester in May; respectable efforts since without hitting quite the same heights; should give a good account.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
OwnerName: Gee Gee's Racing & Hold My Beer
Spotlight: Modest form in maiden/novice company at up to 8.6f; tailed off in a 1m2f handicap at Leicester 17 days ago; drops in grade with cheekpieces added but plenty to prove.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
Spotlight: Second of six, beaten over 3l, in a similar event at Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm; cheekpieces first time) last month; modest hurdle form nine days ago; not fully exposed on the Flat.

RaceName: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse "Hands And Heels" Apprentice Classified Stakes (RE Series)
OwnerName: M L W Bell Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Comfortable win in a similar event at Wolverhampton (1m4f) in February; runner-up in Yarmouth events (1m2f/extended 1m3f) twice this month; another big run expected.
She has been consistent rather than progressive in novice events; return to sprinting should suit and she holds place claims once again.
She has improved her RPR with each of her three starts, all over 7f, keeping on for third at Yarmouth six weeks ago; drop in trip a slight niggle but she's open to further progress.
Her debut run at Bath (5.7f, good) was encouraging but she hasn't kicked on in two subsequent runs (both on AW), the latest at Wolverhampton (6f) last week; needs more.
Ran green when a well-beaten fifth of six in a 5f fillies' novice here (good to soft) in October; sold out of Ed Walker's stable for 11,000gns later that month; hooded for stable/seasonal debut.

Well-related filly who fared best of the newcomers, behind a long odds-on favourite, on her Windsor debut (6f, good to firm) early last month; reared as the stalls opened when fourth of five at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) ten days ago; now tried in a hood; capable of better.
50-1 for her debut at Kempton (7f, AW) nine weeks ago, weakening in the final furlong; drop in trip/addition of a tongue-tie needs to spark a jolt of progress; worth a market check all the same.
Modest form in two sprint runs this summer; no appeal.
Modest form in two sprint runs this summer; minor handicaps should prove more suitable.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Now Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who hit a flat spot then rallied well in first-time cheekpieces over C&D (good to firm) most recently, getting up close home; may build on that novice win and show further progress in the retained headgear; not disgraced at Royal Ascot the time before; respected.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Now Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Possibly going to prove an ordinary sort, having produced best effort in a seller on penultimate start; however, ran respectably (fourth of seven) in C&D nursery latest and looks a reasonably solid contender kept to this scenario; Warren Fentiman takes off a useful 3lb.

RaceName: Watch Racing TV Now Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Creditable second off top weight in Class 6 event at Ffos Las (5f, good; nursery debut) last Tuesday, backing up the form of his 66-1 placed effort a couple of starts earlier; upped in grade but receives weight all round this time, albeit from rivals who already have course form.
His two wins have come over 1m at Bath, the more recent coming off a 3lb lower mark in April; runner-up on his last three starts and no obvious reason why he wouldn't be in the thick of it.
Ran well from the front here (1m, good to soft; blinkered first time) in May but she has followed it with two heavy defeats; down in the weights but she is not a solid option.
Off the mark for new stable when taking a 1m2f handicap here (good to firm) 19 days ago; a 3lb rise shouldn't be an issue but he wouldn't want this to get tactical.
Just a glimmer of promise in her five starts, the latest her handicap debut at Windsor (1m, good to firm) five weeks ago; still has time to do better but she needs more for the additional yardage.

Comes here chasing a hat-trick after narrow 1m2f wins on fast ground at Beverley and Redcar (cheekpieces first time); a 6lb penalty for the latter success (on Sunday) asks a stiffer question, but he could enjoy the run of the race and looks the one to beat.
Consistency has been a major issue for him but he has the ability to win at this level; this will be the longest trip he has tackled but it looks worth trying.

RaceName: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Got off the mark with a narrow success in a Leicester maiden (6f, good to firm) in May and was beaten less than a length by Darzah on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last month; now 2lb better off with her old rival, but a couple of those behind haven't boosted the form since.

RaceName: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Hooded all starts; dead-heated in her sole outing as a 2yo and back to form when beaten a head at Sandown (1m, good) last month; up 4lb, but the form of that race is working out well; respected.

RaceName: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Julie & David Martin, Dan Hall & Partner
Spotlight: 2-3 since handicapping, with both wins coming at around 1m on good to firm ground at Hamilton and Beverley; high on list despite a 4lb higher mark.

RaceName: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Disappointed when sent off favourite for her stable debut/reappearance at Newmarket (7f. good; first-time hood) last month, but made no mistake at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) 19 days ago; 3lb higher and meets some less exposed rivals, though the sole 4yo beat four 3yos in this race last year.

RaceName: Hospitality At Nottingham Racecourse Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: A bit up and down in her four starts, but she did it well enough when successful at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last month, beating Luna Celeste by just under a length; 3lb rise fair enough, though not quite sure how strong the form is with the third and fourth both finishing out of the frame since.

OwnerName: Ged Mason, Sir Alex Ferguson, Jim McGoff
Spotlight: Second to Jenever over C&D last October but held by that rival at the revised weights; his form has dipped on his last two starts but he's capable of a prominent showing.

Won a Newmarket novice (6f, good) last May, his third start, but beaten 11 times since including all four runs for John Butler; his penultimate second at Thirsk was a good run though and when down the field at York last time it was a Class 4; not out of it.

Like many from the yard he has had a quiet year but he has dropped down the weights and is now 6lb lower than for his C&D win last October; quite possible the winners will start flowing for Jessica Macey now and he's of some interest.
Two wins and a second from three visits to Nottingham, all over this trip on fast ground; 1lb higher than for his latest second; one to take seriously.

Unplaced in six runs for David O'Meara, but he's tumbling down the weights and he showed more at York (6f, good to firm; visored first time) ten days ago; this is a drop in class and something bigger is brewing.
Better on AW than turf but handicapped accordingly; not beaten far at Wetherby on his penultimate start but this is a better race and he has since finished down the field at Wolverhampton.
First and second in two 6f novice runs on AW over the winter; no impact in three handicap runs, including her turf debut 17 days ago, and may need further help from the assessor.
His 6f AW win for George Scott in March came off this mark; unplaced in both runs for his new stable and others have more pressing claims.

RaceName: RMG Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap
Spotlight: Has not had much luck and continues to give the impression that this mark, which is just 2lb higher than when winning at Windsor in the spring, is within range; another who tends to be ridden from off the pace and he wouldn't want a messy affair.

RaceName: RMG Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap
Spotlight: Winless on turf since 2021 but showed more on his second run back from a break last time, is now 2lb lower and this is easier than the handicaps he's used to contesting; tends to be held up and a speed-favouring 5f in a small field may not be optimal but he's capable.

RaceName: RMG Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap
Spotlight: York win last summer came off 15lb higher, which shows how things have gone in the meantime; can miss the break (including in first-time headgear latest; now removed) but this race is easier than he's used to; career-low mark.

RaceName: RMG Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap
OwnerName: Come On Over Syndicate & A H Yates Ltd
Spotlight: No problem with 7f last backend and he has been running over 6f this summer, latterly when making all at Doncaster early in the month; came away with a subsequent winner that day and finally getting off the mark should have helped confidence; a 4lb rise looks fair.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Inconsistent this season but posted one of his better efforts last time; dual winner at Salisbury, including narrowly under Freddy Tett in this race last year; respected off a workable mark.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time AW winner who is only 1-22 on turf but has been placed a few times since returned to this sphere, runner-up at Leicester most recently; fighting chance off current mark in this field.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden prior to building up a good strike-rate (3-6) on AW this year; however, disappointing when favourite last time and has something to prove back on turf.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Scored at Lingfield in most recent turf start; record at Salisbury features two wins (2023/2024) and a close fourth in this contest 12 months ago; again has frame possibilities.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Novice winner who is 0-6 in handicaps but ran encouragingly at Chepstow (6f; finished well from rear) most recently and is now a stone below her opening mark; interesting dropped to 0-55 level.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: 1m AW winner in 2024 for previous yard; missed 2025 and trailed home last of five at Salisbury (6f) ten days ago on reappearance; still has broadly poor form on turf.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Campaigned mostly at sprint distances; scored three times for previous yard but has inconsistent results for current stable; something to prove back over 7f.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Has gained all wins over 6f but went very close (off 3lb higher) in this race last year, albeit was in better form at the time; admittedly may prove resurgent with Brighton reappearance under his belt.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Campaigned mostly on AW but ran well (close fifth off 4lb higher) in this contest 12 months ago and that form puts her in the picture; possibly needed latest run (back from a break).

RaceName: Highclere Castle Horse Feeds "Carnarvon" Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Inconsistent maiden who has raced mostly on AW; posted one of her better efforts last time; no certainty to back up that form, especially returned to turf.

RaceName: Kinross British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 105,000euros yearling; by Invincible Spirit; sibling to four winners, notably Light Blush (Listed-placed 7f; 96) and Happy Hadeda (6f AW 2yo; RPR 75); dam 1m2f winner (including Listed; 105); one of three newcomers who add interest to this race.

RaceName: Kinross British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Justified market support with neck success at Ffos Las (6f, good) to contribute to his stable's excellent strike-rate (5-9) with 2yos on turf this term; the clear pick of the runners with experience and represents last year's winning connections.

RaceName: Kinross British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 55,000gns (breeze-up) 2yo; by Havana Grey; sibling to two winners, notably Star Of Lady M (prolific 5f-6f including 2yo/Listed; RPR 108); dam 7f AW winner (80), from family of top-class 1m2f-1m4f performer Fantastic Light; yard's 2yo strike-rate this season bodes well; respected debutant.

RaceName: Kinross British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Always towards the rear in 6f contest at Newbury where he was a 40-1 shot; perhaps one for handicaps later on.

RaceName: Kinross British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 36,000euros foal, 40,000gns yearling; by Space Blues and first foal of 1m6f Flat (RPR 72) and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner and daughter of Italian 1m2f Group 1 winner; owner is also represented by form pick Soldier Of The Sea; heed the market signals.

RaceName: Seamus Mullins Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Met a spot of trouble on her way to finishing in the back half of big field at Royal Ascot; that effort is flanked by second-place finishes, latest at Newbury (6f, good to firm); leading contender at the weights.

RaceName: Seamus Mullins Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Debutante by Ten Sovereigns and first foal of once-raced half-sister to 7f Group 3 winners Dancing Star and Foxtrot Lady and granddaughter of Nunthorpe winner Lochangel; notable connections; interesting.

RaceName: Seamus Mullins Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Havana Grey half-sister to two 7f winners, notably Back In Black (including 2yo; RPR 101); dam 7f 2yo winner (78), out of 6f 2yo winner; one of three newcomers in the field; check the betting.

RaceName: Seamus Mullins Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
OwnerName: Whitsbury Manor Stud And Mrs M E Slade
Spotlight: Finished last of seven, about 12l behind Topaz, in 6f contest at Newmarket; may improve with the outing under her belt but has a lot to find in the rematch with that opponent.

RaceName: Seamus Mullins Racing / Roger Jowett Memorial British EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: 11,000gns foal, 25,000euros yearling, 2,000gns (breeze-up) 2yo; Caturra half-sister to three winners, notably Lightning Leo (7f 2yo; RPR 83); dam 1m4f/12.5f winner (91); yard has a poor strike-rate with 2yos.

Usually held up in rear; hasn't won since his 2yo days but has slipped to an attractive mark and could pop up when the cards drop right, which admittedly isn't guaranteed in this small-field scenario; less exposed at 1m than over shorter.
