Has a record of 0-5 on turf, compared to 2-2 on AW, and isn't particularly solid on his form in this sphere (possibly flattered by best RPR); however, this combination of drop back in trip/class and first-time headgear may have a positive effect.

Justified favouritism at Salisbury (7f, good) on penultimate start and consistent otherwise this season; creditable third at Kempton (1m, AW) last time; still well treated on peak form, which includes a win off 4lb higher at Glorious Goodwood two years ago; solid.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who won at Epsom in sole outing last term; no further progress this season but retains ability and ran creditably in second-time cheekpieces at Ayr most recently; possibilities, provided the switch to blinkers has a bigger effect.

Missed last season but has come back an improved filly and now bids for a 5f hat-trick after classifed/handicap wins, latest at Leicester (good to firm) seven days ago when beating Dreambird Dolly by just over 1l; respected under 5lb penalty with further progress possible.

OwnerName: T Beeches, C Stone, J Gallagher
Spotlight: Has a record of 2102 since wearing blinkers, the success in Leicester classified contest (maiden previously); just over 1l behind Dottie Diamond there last Tuesday and now gets a 5lb pull with that opponent, who admittedly is open to further improvement; important contender.

Seven-race maiden; has made the frame in three of her four starts since running in Class 6 races, latest a Leicester classified (6f) seven days ago; possibilities, provided she shows some progress with Oisin Murphy up for the first time.
Has lacked consistency this term and failed to beat a rival last time, while also failing to back up his penultimate effort; yet to win away from Brighton on turf.
Placed plenty of times since last success and current mark is attractive; well capable of taking a serious hand but his losing run is mounting up and latest effort wasn't one of his best.

Back in much better form, having won a Lingfield classified event (6f, good) in clearcut fashion last month then finished a neck second in Bath handicap (5f, firm) last week; enters calculations despite still having a modest strike-rate.
Gained sole success off a higher mark but isn't particularly solid on 2026 efforts, both in the spring; left Michael Attwater since; possibly best watched unless the betting speaks positively.
Registered sole success in AW contest in February; returned to turf with a creditable effort but subsequent form is inconsistent; never figured on debut for new yard last time.
Not particularly consistent this term for new stable but his most recent Class 5 attempt resulted in Bath win (1m6f, good; narrowly off 1lb lower) in June; possibilities returned to this grade.
Has done most of his winning over jumps and gained his only Flat success three years ago; placed in ordinary handicap hurdle last time; returns to this code for first time since last autumn.

Gained his most recent success in C&D event (good) last October; best effort this term when going close at Salisbury (1m4f) on penultimate start; not disgraced in higher grade here latest; fighting chance returned to Class 5 and back up in trip.
Maiden on Flat and over hurdles; not wholly disgraced at Bath (1m6f) last week when returned to this sphere but finished only a modest third of five and best form remains on AW.

RaceName: Get Raceday Ready Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Strong in the market on her first run in almost a year when third at Yarmouth a fortnight ago; comfortably held that day in a race than didn't pan out her way and she is entitled to improve, but has stamina to prove.

RaceName: Get Raceday Ready Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices and well beaten in three runs over 1m2f to date; possible she'll improve for the new trip but she'll have to off this opening mark; jockey rode his first Flat winner early in the month (had two over hurdles as well); market useful.

RaceName: Get Raceday Ready Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Dual 1m4f winner here in April, latterly off a 2lb lower mark; back in form without the usual cheekpieces (on again tonight) on turf last time and won't mind being back on Tapeta; goes on the shortlist.

RaceName: Get Raceday Ready Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Dam was a miler and he's not bred for this sort of trip; performed below market expectations all four runs since handicapping and, while his trainer-jockey combination will draw some in, stamina is an obvious concern.

RaceName: Get Raceday Ready Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Starman filly who took her record to 3-4 when seeing off eight rivals in 6f Goodwood Listed race (good) in early May and better again when third in Group 3 Summer Stakes at York 12 days ago, having shown plenty of pace; sets a good standard and major chance.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Mixed form last season but has come good on latest two starts, in AW maiden in February and 11 days ago in Limerick rated race (6.5f) staying on late to assert; type to continue improving but this a considerable step up in class.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Very promising start to her career, winning a Curragh 2yo maiden in September 2024 before narrowly denied in a rated race over today's C&D on last summer's comeback run; some okay runs this season, not least on latest when good fourth (having had to be switched) in Curragh Listed last month; one to consider.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Leopardstown Listed winner at two (7f) hasn't won again since but ran well in Group 3 there last summer over same trip; just okay runs both starts this term, blinkers tried at same track last time; takes a drop in trip here which could prove troublesome.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Series of placings in maidens and has made an immediate impact in handicaps, winning at Down Royal (7f, soft) and early this month back at 6f when getting up late at Fairyhouse on quicker ground; clearly progressive but this represents a big jump in class.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
OwnerName: Mary B Hogan & Michael M O'Brien
Spotlight: Progressing really well at 5f this campaign, recording back-to-back handicap wins last month at Cork and Down Royal and only narrowly denied the hat-trick at the Curragh in the valuable Rockinghan; not sure the return to 6f will suit but thriving and well worth this shot at Listed level.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Wolverhampton maiden winner has been tried at Listed level in all three starts since, notably at Ayr last month when career-best second over 5f in Land O'Burns Stakes; back to 6f here and this stiff finish may not suit.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Landed Bellewstown maiden from the front early this month (5f, good) and ran well for a long way in Curragh handicap on Sunday; different kettle of fish here though.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Fairyhouse nursery winner last season her sole win but huge improvement to finish third in Group 3 Lacken Stakes over C&D in May; not at same level in Curragh Listed on latest so more needed.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
OwnerName: Mrs Michael J Byrne & Jerry P Murphy
Spotlight: Sole win in 19 starts came in Cork maiden but has strung together a series of good efforts in decent sprint company this season, notably seconds in Listed events both here and at Cork, most recently third in conditions event here early in the month; best form at 5f so possibly vulnerable at this longer trip.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Won a C&D handicap off 75 last season; safely held since, most recently seasonal return in Curragh Listed last month; lots to find.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Likeable mare ran a cracking race on her return from the AW to finish a close third in Fairyhouse conditions event (6f, good) in June; not at same level later in month in Curragh Listed and good bit to find with Fregada on that run.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Landed Cork maiden last month and improved hugely early this month when only reeled in close home by a 102-rated rival (Likedbymike third) in five-runner conditions event here (5f, good); has lots of speed, not sure this extra furlong will play to her strengths.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: In good form this season since joining this yard, winning twice and career-best second in Group 3 Lacken Stakes over C&D in May (good); well below that level however both starts since at Listed level (hung left latest); visor now replaces hood.

RaceName: Yeomanstown Stud Irish EBF Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
Spotlight: Lightly raced filly whose four runs have all been over further, notably Dundalk AW maiden win at two; last month's comeback run in Navan Listed was disappointing (slow to break) but remains open to improvement; drops in trip with cheekpieces tried.

Two wins to his name; best effort in four runs this year when close third at Limerick (7f, yielding) in May; slow break costly at that track a day later; not beaten far in fifth at Bellewstown early this month; first time with cheekpieces.
A 1-22 turf record is worrying; however, he holds a good chance if reproducing the form of recent Dundalk second, which gives him an edge over Akashaa (sixth).
Losing run on turf stretches back to 2022; stronger record on AW but good effort at Bellewstown on latest.
All six races in 2025 were over longer distances; hard to fancy unless the change of emphasis makes a big difference.

A 17-race maiden; plenty to prove at this stage; failed to run to expectations at Killarney last week; quite well fancied then, at a venue where he has produced some of his better efforts; blinkered now.
Maiden's best efforts have come in Leopardstown handicaps, including when a staying-on fourth of 22 (having hung left) on penultimate start; failed to match that form at Killarney last time.
Two Flat wins came in 2024; last month's third over 1m1f at Leopardstown was encouraging; unplaced twice this month; closely matched with Medieval Night on last week's Killarney run.
Went close at Dundalk last August; fair seasonal debut over 1m1f at Leopardstown, was disputing the lead a furlong down before fading; has a bit to find with Famous Enough on recent Dundalk running.
Best form at Cork, the scene of her only win (over 7f in September 2024) and last season's best effort, in a 6f contest; failed to make much impact on seasonal debut at Killarney six weeks ago.
Struggled in three handicap attempts at this trip, marginally better over 7f last time; hard to fancy despite reduced mark.

OwnerName: Patrick M O'Brien/Larry Murray/Richard W Walsh/Derek Cummins
Spotlight: Is 1-34 on turf; won on heavy over 7f at this track in 2024; reasonably consistent form this season; fifth at Leopardstown 13 days ago matches him closely with Medieval Night and Morning Approach.

Was in the form of his life around this time two seasons ago with back-to-back 6f wins for Michael O'Callaghan; signs of a revival when seventh of 21 at Naas last month; another reasonably encouraging run when fourth at Leopardstown last week.
Sole win came on the beach at Laytown last September; yet to make his presence felt this term.

1-42 on turf; struggled on the AW last winter but showed more when fifth at Roscommon in May; failed to repeat that effort at Gowran; one of her better turf efforts at Leopardstown last time; four years since she recorded a 1m victory at that track.

Four AW wins; 1-20 on turf; failed to make much impact in first two starts for this stable; despite not much luck in running, better when seventh of 15 at Limerick; fifth at Leopardstown a month ago suggests he could be competitive off a career-low mark.
A 22-race maiden, placed ten times, including five in a good spell between July and October last season; reported coughing at Down Royal on seasonal/stable debut; better in mid-field at Leopardstown.

No sign of worthwhile form in five maiden outings; fifth of 13 over 7f at Limerick on handicap debut was a step in the right direction; suffered slight interference inside the last furlong; not as good over a slightly shorter trip at the same venue last time.
Poor form as a juvenile, ran only twice last year; no encouragement from reappearance, 66-1 when in rear in 22-runner Leopardstown contest.
Two-time AW winner is 0-14 on turf but has gone close in defeat, including at Down Royal on penultimate; too keen over 1m last time, will appreciate return to 7f.

Off the mark at the fourth attempt in maidens last September at the Curragh (6f); safely held at same venue on last month's return (handicap debut) and plenty to find with second-placed Little Empire on that.

Three-time AW winner who sole turf success from nine starts came over this trip at Leopardstown in 2023 off 65; two runs in premier handicaps this season leave him with a bit to find although was out of the handicap last time; down in grade here and runs off his correct mark so don't rule out.

Needed every yard of this trip to justify strong market support on handicap debut at Fairyhouse a fortnight ago, getting up in three-way photo, still looking green; 7lb rise enough but this stiffer 7f should bring more out of him, major player.
Curragh maiden win came on soft but handled quicker ground well in Fairyhouse handicap early this month, albeit changed legs late on when headed; first attempt at 7f this season, possible vulnerable.

Both turf wins came on quick ground at 7f-1m at Ayr; AW winner last winter and posted career-best on latest when only caught late on in 17-runner Curragh handicap over this trip last month; trip/ground remains in his favour, can go well again.
Five wins between turf and AW for Johnny Murtagh; best effort for this yard came when fourth over 7f at the Curragh in April (soft), well held since; different headgear combination now tried.

AW promise last year and off the mark on second turf run this year, sent on some way out under a positive ride over this trip at Leopardstown 13 days ago, relishing the quicker ground; 8lb rise looks plenty but quite likely has more to offer under these conditions.

Looked potentially very smart last year, winning Group 3 at the Curragh and finishing runner-up in the Group 2 Debutante; two runs this term well below that level however, too free in Group 3 at Leopardstown and never landed a blow over today's C&D when fourth of 6 in rated race in first-time tongue-tie; still respected and yard in fine form

Better than ever last summer, winning Cork premier handicap (7f, good) and career-best second in Scurry Handicap at the Curragh; matched that effort when beaten just a neck by Headmaster in the Habitat Handicap back at the Curragh on seasonal return in May and following month fared best of those racing far side when third in repeat Cork bid; in fine form but stiff enough task conceding weight to a pair of less-exposed 3yo fillies.

All four runs have been at this trip, notably Leopardstown 2yo maiden win and recent seasonal return when second in 6-runner Group 3 Brownstown Stakes at same track, staying on well after not getting clear run on far rail; remains capable of better and cheekpieces now added.

Smart hurdler won a Grade 3 mares' novice at Down Royal last November; well beaten in the Cheltenham mares' novice after a break and was poor in a Punchestown handicap since; however, point winner ran well over fences on second go last year so is respected.

One of two runners for yard; point, bumper and hurdle winner is rated 129 in the latter sphere though she didn't really progress; looked like winning over 2m3f here on second chase start but maybe got outstayed; back to this trip should suit and a big player.

Second runner for yard; bumper and dual hurdle winner wasn't at her best on last two 2025 hurdle runs; returned from an absence with a sound chasing debut at Killarney in May; should be better for that and looks a big player.
Bumper and hurdle winner ran her best race over fences when second at Tramore in May over this trip; poor back over hurdles at Sligo last time and others have stronger claims.

Point, bumper (here) and dual hurdle winner began her chasing career with a solid second at Cork last November; has been disappointing twice since including a poor effort back here last time; questions now.
Pulled-up in three of four point starts this year; can't be fancied against these on rules debut.

Smart hurdler has run some fine races in defeat over fences; best effort when second in a 2m1f Cork handicap off a mark of 130 in April; not as good twice since but cheekpieces are added and a big player if at his best.

Bumper winner for Nicky Henderson in 2024 but lightly-raced since, latterly for this yard; not a bad chase debut at Punchestown last November but was pulled-up at Kilbeggan 12 days ago so questions to answer.
Second runner for yard; dual hurdle winner in 2023 scored on the Flat in 2024 and some good hurdle runs in defeat too; likely best watched on return from a long absence and chasing debut.

OwnerName: Mrs Suzanne McAuley & Ms C A Jennings
Spotlight: Yet to win on the Flat but ran a fine race in a Killarney maiden over 1m last time; juvenile hurdle winner in 2024 was disappointing when last seen in that sphere; has a bit to find on chasing debut.

One of two runners for yard; bumper and maiden hurdle winner for John Queally has had seven chase runs, with best effort a close second at Tipperary last year; has a shout if at his best on return for a new yard.
Maiden and novice hurdle winner last season up to 2m6f but lost his form afterwards; rebounded with a fine effort over C&D on chasing debut, running on late; has a shout if building on that.
Dual point winner won a Limerick maiden hurdle in 2024; two solid chase runs in 2025 but lost his form since and has to do better; drops in trip.

Second runner for yard; point winner won a maiden hurdle at this track last August but was hit and miss in handicaps after; solid chase debut at Tramore behind a mare who won in Killarney last week; looks a player.
Third runner for yard; maiden over hurdles but opened her account in a 2m2f handicap chase at Thurles last November; has been below that level thrice since and needs a return to best.

Dual hurdle winner at Clonmel is yet to score over fences but has posted several solid runs in defeat; beaten 7l at Kilbeggan over 2m4f but was out of his comfort zone early over C&D last time; the cheekpieces worn then are removed; needs best.

OwnerName: Paul M Butler & James Patrick Byrne
Spotlight: Two of his three hurdle wins came at this track; some solid runs in defeat in beginners' chases but seemed to do too much in front when well beaten in a C&D handicap last time; can do better with more restraint.
Three-time hurdle winner scored sole chase win at Down Royal in November 2024; however, lost his form last summer and two runs this year don't inspire confidence.
Won a 2m4f maiden hurdle at this track last year; hit and miss since but her best chase run came in a C&D handicap two starts ago; well below that level since and has to rebound.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Winning hurdler and although 0-8 chasing finished second in this race two years ago and went close on a few occasions last year; going okay when unseating three from home when back chasing at Thurles when last seen in November; may need this but goes well here so worth consideration.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Wexford specialist, winning twice over hurdles last year and off the mark chasing in C&D handicap last month, overcoming attentions of loose horse at the last in outstaying L'Amiral Fromentin by 3.75l (good); up 6lb but major player.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Sole win came in 2m5f Bellewstown handicap hurdle last year (good); handicap form in the spring was modest and tries fences again (well held sole previous attempt last summer).

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 5yo remains a maiden but generally running well in handicaps, most recently making much of running until outstayed from the last by 3.75l winner Chosen Shant over C&D last month (good); 4lb better off with that rival here so has his chance at revenge.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Both hurdle wins came on easier ground but has been running well in defeat on good ground this year; having just third run over fences when third of 4 finishers in 2m5f Cartmel novices' handicap last month, only weakening late on; back in trip here and not one to rule out.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Second in 2m1f maiden hurdle here last autumn but struggled in handicap hurdles; chase debut at Downpatrick (2m4f) was encouraging but didn't get home as well under a more positive ride here early this month at same trip; down in trip here.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Now 0-4 under rules, chase debut third in Tramore handicap last October probably her best effort; lots to find with a couple of these on last month's C&D debut effort.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Gained second hurdles win back on his favoured good ground over 2m1f at Clonmel last month but well held off 4lb higher over slightly further 12 days ago; switches to fences now but lack of experience a possible negative.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won a maiden over hurdles but only placed form (including here) in handicaps; chase debut was a tough one at Tramore in late May, switches to handicap ranks here.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Down Royal handicap hurdle winner last year (2m2f, good) is 0-5 chasing, encouraging Thurles debut effort yet to be built on, unseating at the first over today's C&D last month; may yet improve but opposable for now.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 0-13 under rules for previous trainers, struggling in handicap hurdles when last seen; absent since January and hard to be confident in on chase debut straight into handicap company.

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Profit In Your Pocket Racing Club
Spotlight: Veteran bagged a fourth win in 2m1f handicap hurdle here last summer (good); recent hurdles form just okay so more needed on return to fences (hasn't won over fences in nearly 5 years).

RaceName: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual point-to-point winner (soft) is 0-4 in hunter chases and dropped out tamely after forcing much of running on handicap debut at Roscommon last month; first run on ground this quick and hard to have confidence in.

Progressive in handicaps in the first half of last season, gaining a third handicap success in 2m4f Clonmel mares' event in October; back to her best in first-time cheekpieces in 2m1f Limerick Grade 3 early this month, staying on for third behind two much higher-rated rivals; dam has already produced a couple of winning chasers so quite possible she could improve for the switch to fences.

119-rated when winning 2m1f Down Royal maiden hurdle at Christmas (yielding); well held in valuable auction series final at Punchestown festival four months later and has had a break since; yard's runners usually expected to improve for the switch fences so greatly respected.
Two-time winning hurdler is 0-6 in chases, standout effort when good second in C&D beginners last summer (good); absent since Christmas bit to prove now.

Dual-purpose 5yo gained his third win on the Flat in 1m5f Navan handicap in April, okay run in better-class Curragh contest following month; hurdles win came in 2m1f maiden here last summer, soft ground was probably against him in subsequent handicaps; back on better ground here could go well if taking to chasing.
118-rated hurdler won Bellewstown maiden and Kelso novice late last summer on good ground; two chase efforts underwhelming, may need more time.
Three wins in 2m4f handicap hurdles, including repeat victory in Clonmel contest in May; none too fluent on chase debut over C&D last month so plenty more needed.
Maiden in all spheres after 47 starts; has run well in defeat at times over fences but hard to see him making the breakthrough here; first-time visor.
Became disappointing over hurdles after winning his maiden and has offered very little in two attempts chasing, including on Tramore comeback in late May; jumping needs improvement.

Down Royal maiden hurdle winner early last year; 0-8 chasing but has shown a useful level of form in beginners' events and when second in 2m1f Cork handicap; dropped out tamely at Punchestown last month over 2m4f so questions to answer on that run.
Dual hurdle winner including once here, is 0-14 over fences but has been placed lots of times including third in this race last year; pulled-up over hurdles last time but a player if rebounding.
Got off the mark over fences when taking this race last year but hasn't repeated that form since between hurdles and fences; however, is 1lb lower than a year ago so has to be respected.
Maiden over hurdles opened her account when winning a Down Royal handicap chase in May; was below that level at Roscommon on soft since but can do better back on lively ground.
Has a poor win record, 1-13 over hurdles and 1-30 over fences; however has been in the frame lots of times including last four chase starts up to 3m2f; should go well again off an unchanged mark.

Hurdle winner has taken well to chasing, winning two of her five starts; won a Killarney beginners' last October and a Limerick handicap on return, both over approx' 3m; fell at Down Royal in between; up 4lb but should go well again.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden over hurdles; didn't jump that fluently but still ran a decent race at Downpatrick on chasing debut last time; one to consider now in a handicap.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Has been in decent form lately, winning at Downpatrick over 2m7f and third here over 2m3f since; going back up in trip will suit and can go well.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Beaten a long way in three handicap chases lately and doesn't make any appeal.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Placed in a point; maiden over hurdles was poor in that sphere last time and others make more appeal on chase debut.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Kilbeggan maiden hurdle winner last year has run some fine races in defeat over fences since; however, has been poor on last three starts and has to rebound.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Got off the mark when winning a Listowel handicap hurdle over just short of 3m last time; point winner has to be respected on chasing debut.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won for the second time at this track when scoring in May but was pulled-up at Punchestown since; coming back here is a plus.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won over hurdles at Punchestown and solid efforts twice after in that discipline; however, was beaten 20l over fences at Killarney five days ago.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden has been pulled-up over hurdles and fences the last twice and has to rebound in a major way.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Showed just a hint of ability for Mouse Morris and fell on return over hurdles; others appeal more on stable debut.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Both chase wins have come on soft ground; in poor form since last autumn and makes no appeal.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Sole win in 25 chase runs came at this track in 2022; back from a break and others appeal more.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual hunter chase winner ran a solid race in a Cartmel handicap over a similar trip to this last time; can be involved with a repeat.

RaceName: Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
Racing Again Tomorrow 23rd July Family Day Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Exors of the Late David Cotter
Spotlight: Was a close second over fences at Sligo last October but no sign of that form in different spheres since; still, can't be dismissed for these connections.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Off the mark on his fifth attempt over fences at Fontwell (2m2f, good) in May and made the winner pull out all the stops when second over C&D (good) last month; in decent nick at present and looks sure to give a good account.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: His sole success over fences came at Market Rasen (2m1f, soft) last July off 2lb higher; didn't offer a great deal once headed when third at Southwell (2m5f, good) last month in a first-time visor (retained) but has dropped to a career-low mark with Sean Bowen on board so all is not lost.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Nothing special over hurdles but made an immediate impact over fences, scoring at this track (2m, good; 28-1) last month; unable to replicate that form when beaten 47l over the same C&D three weeks ago and needs to bounce back on this step back up in trip.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: 0-9 under rules; not a bad effort when runner-up on her chasing debut at Southwell (2m5f, good) last month but beaten 23l over C&D since; needs to show more.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has taken well to fences at around this distance, winning at Stratford and Fontwell before unseating at the last when still in front at Stratford (2m4f, good to firm) last month; she must come under consideration to get back on track.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Two of his four wins over fences have been over C&D but he has been well below that level recently and is hard to fancy.

RaceName: Widmer Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Twice placed in 2m4f hurdle races here last summer (good) but ended last year's campaign on a low, achieving little on October's chasing debut; can't be certain he will hit the ground running in 2026.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Scored for the second time over fences at Market Rasen (3m, good) in April when making all; pulled up after not being allowed an uncontested lead over C&D (good) the following month; still holds claims if on his game.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Landed a couple of bumpers last year and got his act together on his third chase start when scoring over C&D (good) three weeks ago, just ahead of Gwash; there should be more to come with that first win under his belt and he's another with possibilities.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Signed off with Henry Daly with her second win over fences, at Ludlow (2m4f, good) in May; subsequently sold for £22,000 and made an immediate impact for her new stable when securing wins at Uttoxeter (3m, good) and Market Rasen (2m6f, good); this will be tougher but she's in top form and should go close.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has only finished out of the first two twice in 11 runs over fences; should be sharper for her second at Stratford (2m7f, good) last month, following an eight-month absence, and holds place claims at least.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Bumper and dual hurdle winner; made a promising start over fences when runner-up over C&D (good) in May; may have had his stamina stretched when last of four at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) last month and may warrant another chance.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: All three chase wins have been over C&D, including in this equivalent race in 2023; equally effective over hurdles with three wins, the most recent at Uttoxeter (3m, good) last month; last of five finishers when back over fences at Cartmel (3m1f, good) last time but cannot be dismissed around here.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Hasn't won since landing a Warwick maiden hurdle in April 2024; has an inconsistent profile but ran well on his second start over fences when runner-up to Axel Bleue over C&D (good) three weeks ago; that run puts him in with a shout.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner whose only win over fences (seven starts) came at the expense of two rivals at Newton Abbot in April 2025 (2m5f, good); last three runs, in particular, leave him with some questions to answer right now.

RaceName: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won twice over C&D last summer but has been beaten off this mark three times this term and likely needs to come down the weights before he can be seriously considered.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Record of 0-5 on Flat and 0-3 over hurdles but he has proved broadly consistent and penultimate effort has worked out well; creditable third over C&D latest; solid claims.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Has shown some promise in Irish point and Uttoxeter bumper, finishing second then third; represents the champion trainer and remains open to progress; respected hurdles debutant.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Comfortably held over C&D (hurdles debut) last time but this looks a weaker race; one of the main players on his bumper form, which culminated in third-place finish at Worcester.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Rules debutant who has to overcome a long absence and holds poor claims on his point form (bumpers/fences); best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Stablemate of Iwanttobreakfree; has cut little ice in three races (both hurdles attempts over C&D) and looks one who'll be more interesting when qualified for handicaps.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Took seven attempts to open his account in Irish points; folded tamely over 2m4f switched to rules last time; drops further in distance.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Has shown promise over hurdles; caught the attention of the stewards last time; may be more interesting in handicaps but he is one of the better types in this field, being a dual Flat winner.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Low-grade maiden on the Flat; modest fifth over C&D in latest attempt over hurdles; no certainty to improve on that effort.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div I)
Spotlight: Thrice-raced mare who isn't solid on form; recorded a meagre RPR over C&D on hurdles/stable/seasonal debut.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who was successful (at about 1m4f; fair form) in last two Flat starts for Kevin Philippart de Foy, latest in October; sold for 52,000gns and gelded since; interesting, assuming he transfers ability to hurdles.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Not the force of old (one-time useful Flat handicapper) but has shown consistent hurdles form at Stratford this summer, close second to odds-on shot over 2m last time; solid claims.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Record of 0-6 on Flat and 0-4 over hurdles but has largely consistent form, creditable third over C&D most recently; this race is of a similar standard; again has place claims.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Scored by wide margin, albeit in weak race, at Stratford on final bumper start; finished 12l behind Penzance over hurdles there since but may do better still; one of the main players.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Record of just 1-20 on Flat, the success in Class 6 handicap over 1m2f in April; form dipped last time; brings limited potential to this change of code.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Has shown poor form on Flat for current yard and remains a maiden under that code; pulled up in both hurdles attempts; enough to prove back in this sphere.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Beaten about 14l in both attempts over hurdles but likely to fare better today as this looks an easier assignment and he's one of the stronger options on Flat form, which includes a win.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Best effort in bumpers when third at Worcester; soundly beaten over C&D switched to hurdles last time, however, and may be more interesting in handicaps later on.

RaceName: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB) (Div II)
Spotlight: Represents major stable but was friendless in the betting and well beaten in Warwick contest in March; had wind surgery since; the market may again guide the way.
Yet to win over hurdles and hasn't kicked on from his promising second at Taunton (2m, good) on his handicap debut in March; first-time cheekpieces need to have a significant impact.
Opened his account over hurdles with a smooth success at Stratford (2m, good to firm) last month; there should be more to come but this looks a better contest so a bit more improvement required.

Got off the mark on his third run over hurdles, following wind surgery, in a maiden over C&D (good) last month, without his usual cheekpieces (also absent today); makes handicap debut and there should be more to come.
Scored over hurdles for Olly Murphy last August; below that form for current yard in two runs this term but scored on AW last month; more required back over hurdles.
Scored at the third attempt over hurdles in a maiden over C&D (good) last month with first-time tongue-tie (retained); there should be more to come from this mare on her handicap debut.

Ex-Irish; got off the mark over hurdles at Stratford last July; had three runs on AW in the autumn and makes first handicap start over hurdles in Britain following eight-month layoff; could have a say if fully tuned up.

Two of his five wins over hurdles have been over C&D; has a decent record fresh and made a solid return when runner-up over C&D (good) last month; 5lb higher than his last winning mark though and a career-best is required.

Encouraging hurdle debut when 12l second at Doncaster (2m, good to soft) in November and ran to a similar level when fifth at Haydock the following month before pulling up in January; has since undergone wind surgery and his pedigree suggests this longer trip will suit on handicap/stable debut for Dan Skelton; interesting contender.

0-8 over hurdles but made the frame on all three starts since switched to handicaps, most recently at Market Rasen (extended 2m5f; just in front of Estacas) in June with a tongue-tie added; looked hard work there and cheekpieces are now tried, but Sean Bowen returns and he's a leading contender.

1-39 but was runner-up at Southwell (2m4f, good) in June and ran well for a long way from the front  at Market Rasen last month before fading into fourth; enters calculations on the strength of his earlier effort.
Back on track to some extent when runner-up at Hereford (2m3f) in first-time cheekpieces, which are retained, albeit beaten 21l; more is needed again.

Gained a tenth career success when scoring over fences at Fontwell in October off a 13lb higher  mark, but ended the year with two pulled-up efforts; returns from a 277-day break with something to prove back over hurdles, but he's bounced back from quiet spells before.

Twice runner-up in Irish points but has only hinted at ability in three novice/maiden hurdles (2m-2m1f) for this stable; needs to take a marked step forward on this switch to handicaps but the move up in trip should suit.

TrainerName: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole right
Spotlight: Couldn't hold on when attempting to make all at Market Rasen (extended 2m5f, good) in June but that was still a solid effort, only narrowly denied second by Little Ledgend late on; should go well again, with Luke Scott able to claim 3lb this time.
On a long losing sequence but returned to some form when back from a break and finishing a 12l third of five over C&D 12 days ago, ridden by Rian Corcoran; respected off 4lb lower.

Sedgefield winner in September under Freddie Keighley; that form has some substance but he failed to build on it in a higher grade next time; ran well enough on his return at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) in first-time cheekpieces last month and blinkers are now tried, but he remains on a tough mark.

Built on June's reappearance when keeping on for third over 2m here 12 days ago, in a race she had won in 2024 and 2025; yet to prove she needs this far but is on a good mark and could figure if staying the trip.

Still a maiden over hurdles after 13 starts but looked set to put that right at Fontwell (2m3f, good) in April, only to fall at the last when mounting his challenge, after a similar break to today's; up 2lb but Paddy Hanlon retains the ride and this 6yo is worth considering.
Dual hurdle winner in late 2024 but pulled up on both starts (over fences/hurdles) since an absence; cheekpieces (worn on last three starts) are removed; others make more obvious appeal.

Hasn't beaten a rival on the Flat this year since switching stables and has been well held in three hurdle starts, although he wasn't beaten far when sixth of nine here (2m) in May; moves up in trip for handicap hurdle debut with something to prove.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: French claiming hurdle winner on debut in April 2024 and opened his British account under a typically strong Sean Bowen ride over 2m4f here in May; pulled up next time but quickly back on track when runner-up here (2m4f) 12 days ago; Sean Bowen returns and he's a leading contender if seeing out this longer trip.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won her third point when beating two rivals in April; made an encouraging stable/chase debut when second at Stratford (extended 2m3f, good to firm) last month but may have done too much without the hood when fading into fourth over 2m6f there ten days ago; reverts to hurdles from out of the weights and others make greater appeal.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has struggled to recapture his earlier promise since returning from almost a year off in March and has made little impact in two handicap starts this summer, most recently when pulled up over C&D three weeks ago; may be capable of better but first-time blinkers need to prove a positive addition.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner, all at around this trip on good ground; he needs things to fall right and remains on a challenging mark, though a reproduction of his Southwell second last month would give him place claims.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Back over hurdles just four days after a below-par chase run at Cartmel; twice runner-up in this sphere during the summer, including over C&D in refitted cheekpieces last month; major player if bouncing back to that level.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed more in a first-time visor when third at Market Rasen after a three-month break last month and backed that up with a 5.25l fifth of 12 on handicap debut there 17 days ago; eased 1lb in the weights and another step forward would put him firmly in the picture.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Just 1-27 under rules, with his sole success coming more than two years ago; recent efforts have offered some encouragement with the addition of cheekpieces and he's been eased a further 2lb, but still has something to prove with blinkers now tried.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Still a maiden after eight hurdle starts (0-12 overall) but ended a run of poor efforts when a clear second at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) in May; 4lb out of the weights here and needs to build on that performance.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden but went close when beaten a head at Stratford on stable debut for Dan Skelton, his first attempt at 2m6f; was well backed and saw the trip out strongly, offering encouragement he'll stay this slightly longer distance; up 4lb but remains a leading contender.

RaceName: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has yet to show anything worthwhile in five hurdle starts, including in two handicap runs since cheekpieces were fitted; steps up in trip with a tongue-tie added after a 112-day break but has plenty to prove.
