RaceName: Racing Again On 8th August Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Two hurdles wins came some time ago; 0-7 chasing, most recently back from point-to-points when pulled up in Cork hunters chase in April; hard to make a case for.

RaceName: Racing Again On 8th August Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdle winner over three years ago; 0-10 chasing, good C&D effort last summer, not so good of late, 3m probably too far on latest; can't rule out back at a more suitable trip.

RaceName: Racing Again On 8th August Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden's best effort last year when runner-up in 2m2f handicap hurdle here; absent until pulled up halfway after never counting in 2m5f Bellewstown handicap hurdle early this month; only second attempt over fences now.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Hit the ground running for George Baker with 1m4f/1m3f wins on the AW and was close up at Epsom despite stumbling at the start; that was no backward step and he should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Eight wins divided between hurdling and the Flat; off the same mark as when narrowly beating Mrembo in this 12 months ago and returns off the same mark; penultimate run was on a par with that performance.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced filly who kept on for fifth on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f; 50-1) and there could be more to come now she's sent further.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Reliable mare who wasn't beaten far last time at Epsom when just behind Imperical Cult; has run well in the last three renewals of this race, beaten 2l or less; considered.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Has won on turf but boasts a far superior strike-rate on the AW and hasn't been that threatening on good to firm in his last two races.

RaceName: Close Brothers Asset Finance Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Off since a quiet run on the AW in December and that was after 147 days away so current wellbeing is an issue; however, only 3lb higher than when making all at Salisbury last summer (1m2f, good to firm) so not handicapped out of it.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: No Nay Never filly and the first foal out of a 6f winner (RPR 96) and sister to 6f winner Craved; the betting should offer clues as to expectations.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: No match for the long odds-on winner at Wolverhampton (5f) where Elpeeare was a bigger eye-catcher in finishing hot on this one's heels.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Mrs Paul Shanahan & Mrs M V Magnier
Spotlight: Seventh of ten, beaten about 5l, over 6f at Yarmouth a month ago; raced prominently before weakening and may do better with the outing under her belt, now dropped to 5f.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 95,000gns yearling; not a lot went right for her when a keeping-on third (just behind Delighfully Hot) at Wolverhampton (5f) so appeals as one who could leave that form behind; however, it could significant that Darragh Keenan rode that day but now partners her stablemate.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
TrainerName: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole right
Spotlight: 65,000gns foal by Showcasing; half-sister to winners Calafiori (5f-8.5f; RPR 79) and Mechayekh (1m); dam 6f winner and half-sister to winners Go Angellica (1m 2yo Listed) and Southern Belle (useful 5f/6f); doesn't have the best of draws, especialy for a newcomer.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 400,000euros yearling; beaten 11l when made favourite at Beverley (5f) but her inexperience was evident from the outset and should be all the wiser this time; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Palace Pier filly who cost 110,000euros yearling and is half-sister to winners Fort Rock (7f 2yo; RPR 95), Nubuck (French 12.5f; 91) and Chuck Taylor (6f-1m1f; 69); dam a useful 1m winner; interesting debutante for a yard that had a successful newcomer last week.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: £110,000 yearling by Mehmas; first foal out of a 5f winner (Listed; RPR 101) and half-sister to winners Volterra (Group 3-placed 7f/1m) and Inishbeg (7f); market support could be significant when the yard's 2yos have been going great guns.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Hot To Trot 1 & Mrs R Pease
Spotlight: Ground this fast is a nagging concern but she's building up some momentum this season and was nailed late on over C&D 41 days ago; only had the 12 races and she's consistent.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: In good form over hurdles and on the Flat earlier this year, last time going close in a 2m AW handicap off 1lb lower; if in the same form after his break then should be involved.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Career win number 11 when coming clear at Goodwood (1m6f, soft) on his debut for Tony Carroll; effective on faster ground and a 6lb rise might not stop him if he's turned a corner.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Completed a top-of-the-ground hat-trick this year (1m6f-2m1f) and remains in good form, as a tactical race wouldn't have suited at Yarmouth and she was never ideally positioned after starting slowly last time (finished 8.5l behind the winner); another to consider.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Strike-rate of 7-50; won off this mark in March but well beaten in three of his four subsequent runs and has become hard to predict.

RaceName: Close Brothers Premium Finance Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Dual turf winner at 1m2f and 1m3f for Charlie Johnston last spring; back to form in winning a 1m4f selling handicap on the AW earlier this month and was then second under a penalty; 3lb higher now but should be fine back on turf.

150,000gns yearling by Palace Pier; all races at 1m2f, getting off the mark in comfortable style at the expense of two rivals at Nottingham (good); brings potential into handicaps and connections won this last year.
Showed clear promise in novice/maiden events; doesn't appear to have anything up her sleeve mark-wise after two defeats in handicaps (at about 1m2f) and contested a lower-grade race last time.

The close fourth at Newcastle in November is his standout run and disappointed favourite backers the last time; however, now gelded ahead of this handicap debut and would command respect if at all strong in the betting.
Not that threatening in his qualifying races (1m1f-1m2f) but showed ability and the potential is there to improve for a gelding operation; also hooded for this handicap debut; market helpful.

Novice winner at two; always doing enough for a successful handicap debut at Salisbury and then denied late on at Ascot (again at 1m on good to firm), where she dictated a steady pace; had no excuses that day but this longer trip should help, as she's out of a 1m4f winner.

Progressive in blinkers before switched to a visor and winning narrowly at Epsom (1m127yds); he did some hanging but that was probably due to the track; a 6lb rise seems hefty enough but he's trending in the right direction.
Both wins have been at 7f but has form over this far and it might yet end up being his best trip; due a 1lb rise after finding one too good at Yarmouth last time (7f); unlikely to be too far away.
Dual winner on turf for Tim Easterby; has dropped to a good mark and close up in a couple of Class 5s over 1m at Kempton; likely to need more here.
First turf win when a neck victor over C&D earlier this month (good) and might have followed up off this 3lb higher mark had he not been carried left late on at Windsor; 2lb higher in future; player.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Gelded in February and made successful return to the track with a narrow verdict over Beverley's extended 7f (first-time tongue-tie), beating another well-bred 3yo with potential; that could be a springboard to better things in handicaps.
Both wins on the AW but he bled when disappointing at Nottingham before a solid 2l defeat in a big field at Ascot (7f, good to firm); he was boxing on that day and now returns to a mile; respected.
Only 1-10 but pushed a Prescott improver close last time at Salisbury (1m) and dropping back to 7f looks beneficial; respected.
0-9 but twice runner-up and latest race at Ffos Las didn't suit his hold-up style; there's a race in him off this mark.
Dead-heated in a Chelmsford maiden (6f, AW) on second run for current yard but has offered very little since.
Beaten between 10l and 18l in 7f/1m races, the middle one at Meydan; goes handicapping with much to prove.

OwnerName: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
Spotlight: No closer than 5.5l in four handicaps since winning a 7f maiden at Chester last summer; second last time back there but was hammered by the winner; hard to call him well treated at the minute.
Some sign of ability in 6f/7f AW races before struggling in a new tongue-tie at Newmarket (1m); handicap newcomers from this yard always need checking in the betting.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: 40-1 at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) last week but she was always prominent and gave it a good shot before finishing a 3l fourth of 12; that was a promising start and has each-way claims if she can build on that.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: 110,000euros yearling by Blue Point; weak 15-2 shot at Carlisle (6f, good to firm) last month and she got outpaced before finishing a remote third of five; should be more streetwise this time but she needs a transformation upped in trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: 350,000gns yearling; sister to five winners including Expensive Queen (US 1m/8.5f inc Grade 1; RPR 116), Antonia De Vega (7f-1m4f including 2yo/Group 3; 112) and Al Haarith (1m; 96); dam Listed-placed 7f winner (100), half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Al Wukair; has a striking pedigree and she needs a close look on debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: New Bay filly; closely related to winners Queen Me (Group-placed 6f 2yo; RPR 104) and Bint Queen Kindly (7f; 95), half-sister to two winners including Alia Choice (5f AW/5.4f turf; 97); dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo Group 2; 112), out of 6f Group 2 winner; lots to like on paper and she's an interesting newcomer.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: 140,000euros yearling; didn't live up to market expectations at Yarmouth (6f, good to soft) in May but she ran green before making some late headway; that debut form is modest but she should know more this time and it wouldn't be a surprise if she took a major step forward upped in trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Inc' Race)
Spotlight: 50-1 and she faded into a well-held fourth of five at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; that form is well below the standard here and she could be more of a handicap prospect.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 105,000euros yearling; by Sioux Nation out of unraced half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Emaraaty Ana; weak 14-1 shot at Carlisle (good to soft) last month but he finished a promising third from a wide draw; should know more this time and he's a likely improver upped in trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 80,000euros yearling; second foal out of a 5.7f-1m winner (including 2yo Group 3; RPR 106); 11-1 on Newbury debut in April but he led 1f out before keeping on well to beat a clear second; gelded since but that was a bright start and he's open to progress on this step up in trip; respected under a penalty.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has improved with each of her three runs but she was still beaten around 5l when fourth of eight at York (6f, good to firm; 50-1) last time; needs another major step forward here and others are preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-brother to four winners including Raaeb (5f-7f including 2yo; RPR 108); disappointing when 6-4 at Ayr last time but the soft ground may have held him back and he showed plenty of promise on his York debut (fourth of 15) in May; just about sets the standard on that form and and he's a big player if he can bounce back.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 50,000gns yearling; second foal; dam French 1m winner, sister to 1m4f winner Blowing Dixie, half-sister to winners Cursory Glance (7f 2yo Group 1) and Sweet Memories (1m4f Listed), out of 1m2f winning sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Time On; has good standard to aim at on debut and he could be a longer-term prospect.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has struggled at big prices in her three runs (6f, good to soft/good), with best RPR of 26.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: £28,000 yearling; sister to winners Scarlet Bear (Group-placed 6f; RPR 98), Elinor Dashwood (6f 2yo/7f; 92) and Spring (6f 2yo; 63); dam placed 7f AW (60), out of 6f 2yo/7f Group 3 winning half-sister to useful 7f-1m winner Bronze Prince; this looks a tough starting point and yard is 0-5 with 2yos this year.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the fifth attempt when making all for an emphatic win on nursery debut at Catterick (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces added) last week; this is a much deeper race but she was never in any danger last time and looks well treated under a penalty; key player.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Hasn't threatened in her four starts but she's only been beaten around 3l in last two runs (6f, good/AW) and her RPRs have been progressive; looks on fair mark now switched to a nursery and she should get a good tow into this race; dangerous.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Got closer to the target on nursery debut when third of eighth at Pontefract (6f, good) two weeks ago; rallied well in the closing stages of that race and she's a player if she can find some extra spark.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Well held in his three runs so far, most recently when a 6l third in a Beverley maiden (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; still unexposed and now goes handicapping but he needs improvement back up in trip.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Has plenty of speed in his good pedigree but he's not progressed so far and was beaten 6l on nursery debut at Pontefract (6f, good) two weeks ago; still early days but he needs to significantly raise his game.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Her form has been up and down so far but she won a Beverley claimer (5f, good to firm) in May and was a close fourth in a Catterick nursery two weeks ago; looks worth a try at this new trip and she's in the mix off same mark as last time.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices and she finished ahead of just two rivals in three maiden/novice events at Chester (6f); still early days but slow starts have been an issue so far and she needs a transformation on nursery debut.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Promising third on Ripon debut (6f, good) in May but she's been disappointing in both subsequent runs; still early days but she needs a transformation back up in trip on nursery debut.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Well held in a Newcastle maiden (7f, AW) last month but that may have come too soon after his promising third over 6f at Ripon (good); looks interesting on that form and he's in the mix back in trip on nursery debut.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Good third on nursery debut at Catterick (5f, good to firm) 16 days ago but she finished 8l behind Lady Dublin over C&D (third of four) last week; has bit to prove again after that and she's now 0-5.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Nick Bradley Racing 13 & P J Makin
Spotlight: Has improved with each of her three runs and she went very close in a Musselburgh seller (7f, good) last month; now switches to a nursery but that was bold bid last time and she's respected on this drop back in trip.

RaceName: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Well held in three runs at 5f, with a best RPR of 40; half-sister to a 6f winner but she needs plenty of improvement upped in trip on handicap debut.

RaceName: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap
Spotlight: 50-1 second in a Windsor maiden (11.4f, good) last May but he was tailed off in his final two runs (novice/handicap) last season; still unexposed but he's untried at this trip; non-runner when due to make his reappearance at Newbury (8.15) on Thursday.

RaceName: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap
Spotlight: Still a maiden after 12 starts and was last of four in a Doncaster handicap (14.5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; wasn't beaten far in that race but he needs to find more to get off the mark.

RaceName: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap
Spotlight: Eight wins at up to 2m2f and he's versatile ground-wise; his last success was off 5lb higher at Catterick (1m4f) last autumn but he's been out of sorts this season and was tailed off at York last time; now drops back in grade but he needs a major revival.

RaceName: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap
OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Xxiii & M Hulin
Spotlight: Won handicaps at Leicester (1m4f, good) and Redcar (1m6f, good to firm) in the spring but he's failed to beat a rival in last two starts; bit to prove but he got shuffled back in a tactical race at Chester last time and has possibilities if he can bounce back.

RaceName: Graham Lee Injured Jockeys' Fund Donate Today Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive 4yo who made it 2-5 on turf when completing a double at Nottingham (1m6f, good) in May; 4lb higher after a short break but he remains feasibly treated and is still unexposed at staying trips; key player.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed 3yo who returned after 207 days off with a dominant display in a Lingfield handicap (6f, AW) last Monday; 3lb well in under a penalty for that success and she's open to more progress on this switch to turf; strong contender.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Recorded her eighth turf win when scoring at Hamilton (5f, good to soft) last month but she's been well held in both subsequent runs; has bit to prove again and she's never won over this trip.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in February but she's not gone on from that and has been well held in her last four runs; continues to drop down the weights but she has plenty to prove back up in trip for another new yard.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won this race last year and she scored over 5f here (good) last month; can be a bit up and down but she's finished a creditable third in last two runs, including at Catterick (6f, good to firm) on Wednesday; shortlisted.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Last-gasp winner on AW at Lingfield (7f) in February but she's struggled since and was last of six at Catterick two weeks ago; that took her turf record to 1-23 and she has plenty to prove back at this trip.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins have been on good or slower ground but she's been knocking on the door in her last five runs including when runner-up on good to firm at Ayr last time; on unchanged mark and she should be in the thick of things again.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Seven-race maiden; runner-up at Redcar (6f, good) in June but she's been hard to predict so far and was beaten 16l on her stable debut at Ripon last week; comes with risks attached and others are more convincing.

RaceName: NRFC Leading Roof Excellence Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won a Wetherby maiden (5.5f, good) in June 2024 but she's been lightly raced since and has struggled in her last four runs; mark is tumbling but she needs a major revival on her second run after a year off; cheekpieces added.

Won four times over hurdles between July and September last year, but he lost his way in that sphere and has struggled in three Flat runs this summer; now makes his Flat handicap debut but he needs a transformation back up in trip; cheekpieces reapplied.

Low-mileage 5yo who made it 3-6 in 1m4f handicaps when justifying favouritism at Pontefract (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; up 4lb but that was a comfortable success and he's open to more progress at this trip; key player.

Just one win in his first 18 starts but he doubled his tally when coming from off the pace to score at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm) two weeks ago; up 3lb but that was a brave win and he shaped as though this trip should be within range; respected.

OwnerName: Mrs S D Pearson & Ollie Pears
Spotlight: Seven-time hurdle winner who is 1-11 on the Flat; faded back over hurdles at Newton Abbot three weeks ago but she was runner-up at Ripon (1m4f, good) last month, and that was a bold bid after wind surgery; has claims on that form and she's in the mix back in this sphere.

Both wins have been on Tapeta and latest was 15 months ago; respectable third at Redcar (1m6f, good) and Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW) in his last two runs but this is a competitive race and others are more persuasive.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: 0-8 on AW but she made it second-time lucky on turf when scoring by 6l at Lingfield (5f, good to firm) last week; this is a deeper race but she hit a clear personal best last time and is a major player again under a penalty (due to be up 1lb in future).

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Record of 2-40 on turf but his last win was at Thirsk last spring and he was runner-up at Beverley (5f, good to firm) last week; looks interesting off 1lb lower here and he's respected back at this track.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Well below form at Catterick last week but he had a near-miss over C&D (good) last month and he made all when winning this race last year; has claims if he can bounce back again and he's in the mix.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Some creditable efforts season including when fourth of ten over C&D (good) on his penultimate run; that form puts him in the picture but overall record is now 2-31 and his last win was in 2023.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
OwnerName: D B & Mrs C Lamplough & Partner
Spotlight: Nine-time turf winner who is well treated on his win at Catterick last spring; has been up and down since but he's finished runner-up four times this year including at Catterick (5f, good to firm) on his penultimate run; could be dangerous in another switch of headgear.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: 0-9 but she finished a respectable third off this reduced mark at Beverley (5f, good to firm) ten days ago; could go well again but she needs to find something extra to make the breakthrough.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
OwnerName: Ursa Major & Mark Walford Racing Club
Spotlight: Showed some promise for George Scott last season but she's finished down the field in her three handicaps including on recent stable debut at Ripon (6f, good); may have needed that run but she's now 0-7 and others are more convincing.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: 12-race maiden who has form figures of 556097 in handicaps and was always in rear at Beverley (5f, good to firm) last Tuesday; opposable.

RaceName: Racing Excellence Apprentice Handicap (Apprentice Training Race - Racing Excellence Series)
Spotlight: Third in a Catterick novice (5f, good to firm) in May but that form has taken several knocks and she's failed to get competitive in three handicaps since.
Placed in her last two Irish points so has ability and Harry Cobden is booked for her rules debut; still likely best watched over this trip.

Won her Irish Flat maiden (1m4f) on heavy but it was good ground for her two visits to Newton Abbot and she won by 10l three weeks ago; penalised accordingly but clearly going the right way and her form is up there.
1m3f/1m4f wins at a lowly level and it was a modest race in which she ran second on jumps debut at Cartmel (good; jumping lacked fluency); others preferred.

Respectable Flat form for the Crisfords and has made a bright start over hurdles, winning as he liked last time at Worcester (good); the second nearly went one better next time; a strong contender even with a penalty.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Lady Cobham
Spotlight: Won the Bunbury Cup in 2023; unraced beyond 1m on the Flat but seemed to stay the trip okay on jumps debut here following a long absence; however, what he achieved behind an easy winner in that small field is questionable.
15-race maiden off the Flat with a basement handicap mark; no real appeal on hurdling debut.
Left Karl Burke for 7,000gns and as a seven-race maiden; beaten 49l and 24l in two runs over hurdles.
Early casualty on debut; didn't show a lot when beaten a long way here 17 days ago.
Finished last in his two point bumpers when trained by Lily Bradstock; showed more on stable/bumper debut when beaten 12l at Market Rasen but there will probably be other days.
150-1 when tailed off in a bumper here only 17 days ago.
Beat one home in a 1m AW maiden and was 300-1 when pulled up on hurdling debut (hooded).
Ran okay in two bumpers but it's hard to rate her form too highly; best watched.
Tailed off in a bumper and pulled up in a recent maiden here after a long absence.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Only sixth when favourite for handicap hurdle debut at Wetherby (2m, good to soft) in March and signed off for Jedd O'Keeffe with a poor Flat run in May but joined Dan Skelton for £21,000 soon afterwards and was quickly given a wind op; interesting to see what new trainer can do with him.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Unplaced all seven hurdling starts but was prominent in the betting for all four handicaps and held third place before last-flight unseat over C&D (good) nine days ago; may yet have a bigger run in him.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Just held on to make all off 3lb lower at Warwick (2m, good) last May but, following a layoff, has dropped out quite tamely once headed here on both starts this season.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Front-runner who won three times (once over C&D) last spring; pulled up over fences at Worcester last month but her second there in May was a fairly good effort and she reverts to hurdling on a workable mark.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Managed a win off lowly mark at Huntingdon (2m3f, good) in October 2024 but absent since heavy defeat the following month (albeit on slower-than-ideal ground) and might need this outing.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Low-grade Flat winner for another stable last year; still unexposed over hurdles and wasn't given a hard time when fifth of 12 over C&D (good; beaten about 21l) on recent handicap debut, having almost lost his jockey when stumbling on the home turn.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Kept on for third of 13 in Hereford maiden (2m, good) in April but safely held when filling same position in two subsequent handicaps (both 2m, good) and needs improvement here.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Weakened out of contention on handicap debut at Market Rasen (about 2m6f, good) 19 days ago but that was his first run since February and positives can be taken from it; not out of this if suited by the drop back in trip; cheekpieces removed after one use.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Has modest strike-rate on the Flat and is 0-4 over hurdles; placed off today's mark on handicap hurdle debut at Southwell (2m, good) last month but subsequent run in Worcester maiden was underwhelming; others have more persuasive profiles.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
OwnerName: G C Myddelton & V E C Taylor
Spotlight: Not seen over hurdles since 65l defeat on handicap debut in April 2025 but pretty consistent over fences since; reverts to this code with trip/ground suitable; might be the answer.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div I)
Spotlight: Had jumping issues and struggled in Hexham chase on last month's stable debut; now 5lb lower than when placed over hurdles at Stratford (2m2f, good) on final start for Daisy Hitchins but still has something to prove.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Resumed winning ways (in a change of headgear) in C&D handicap 17 days ago; he's not always proved the most reliable so needs to back it up now from a 5lb higher mark.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: A fair 1m4f Flat winner; quite lightly raced in this sphere and he came in a well-held third of four in 2m3f handicap at Stratford last month; needs to take a step forward.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
OwnerName: Mr & Mrs R Newiss & Gavin Teversham
Spotlight: Gained a first hurdling success over C&D last May but his more recent form is far less encouraging, a well-held fifth in 2m Worcester handicap 23 days ago; others appeal more.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Scored over C&D in May and has continued in good nick, fifth of ten over C&D 17 days ago; not out of things off a 2lb lower mark.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: A two-time 2m hurdles winner but ended last season on a low note; better signs on return with fourth of nine in 2m Worcester handicap 23 days ago; needs considering.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Fair 1m4f Flat scorer who gained a first win in this sphere at Fakenham (2m) in January; faded from last flight when sixth of nine in 2m Worcester handicap on his return 23 days ago and should strip sharper here.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Off eight months and much improved for his new yard with an easy first success in 2m handicap hurdle at Stratford last month; up 7lb but not taken lightly.

RaceName: Bridal Rooms Uttoxeter Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Lightly raced mare who took a step forward on her handicap debut with fourth of five at Fakenham (2m7f) in April; drops markedly back in trip here after a break.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Returned from 12-week break with poor run last month and is now 0-7 over fences but was close second off this mark to a dual subsequent winner at Doncaster (3m2f, good to soft) in March; player if back on song.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Came good under rules at 12th attempt with C&D success (good; clear second won next time out) in May but was pulled up when back here last month; had another wind op (his second) soon afterwards and is now tongue tied; not an easy one to predict.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Seemed to run well when second of three in tactical race at Cartmel (3m1f, good) on Monday and remains 2lb lower than when winning for another stable in January but others appeal more all the same.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Mostly out of form since joining current stable just over a year ago and was pulled up when upped to 2m7f for Bangor hurdle race last month, after a layoff; reverts to chasing in first-time visor; has too much to prove.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Won two modest 3m2f chases in the autumn (good/good to soft) and returned from break with encouraging run at Cartmel (2m5f, good) in May but others in this line-up look a bit stronger; 1lb wrong.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Bounced back to form to cause 14-1 surprise in four-runner chase at Huntingdon (2m7f, good to firm) in May and is still on a workable mark after 2lb nudge but it's hard to predict whether he'll be in the right mood again.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Ran quite well when second of four behind a next-time-out winner over C&D (good) last month and her subsequent run is best overlooked (pulled up; jockey presumably felt something was amiss) but she's too inconsistent to rely upon heavily.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Won maiden hurdle here (2m7f, good) in September but has lost her way since, and was tailed off on recent chasing debut; might be aided by the refitted tongue-tie but it takes a big leap of faith to support her.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Lacked fluency and was well beaten when back under rules at Stratford (2m6f, good to firm) last month but has good strike-rate in points (10-22) and can't be ruled out off current handicap mark.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
OwnerName: The Galloping Dentist At 45 The Green
Spotlight: Generally disappointing since last summer's 2m7f hurdle win for a different stable but took big step back in right direction and ran well for a long way when third over fences at Worcester (2m4f, good) last month; back up in trip here; a possible.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: 0-16 over hurdles but ran big race in defeat over C&D (good) on chasing debut six weeks ago and has obvious claims if able to replicate that performance.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Perhaps unlucky not to finish closer than third on stable debut at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good to soft) in April, having made a jumping error two out, but two lesser efforts have followed; first attempt at 3m under rules; needs to up his game.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: 0-13 under all codes and absent since struggling in heavy-ground C&D contest in December (first-time cheekpieces); might be happier on this quicker surface but still makes only limited appeal from 5lb out of the weights.

RaceName: Craig Reid Retirement Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Dual Irish point winner; launched chasing career with two underwhelming runs this spring (3m/3m2f) and is now 0-5 under rules but can't be written off just yet.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has some useful form on his CV but has become very disappointing this year, usually weakening quickly; had wind op before penultimate run but it didn't appear to make much difference; others look much safer.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Came from off the pace to win C&D mares' race (good) nine days ago and is now 3-17 over hurdles; due only a 3lb rise for that and faces tough task under 7lb penalty instead, but at least we know she's in good nick.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Posted three respectable efforts at around 2m4f this spring and continues to edge down the weights, but he is not bred to benefit from this step up in trip and others in this field have more interesting profiles.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Low-mileage mare with 2-4 strike-rate for current stable, the latter win gained in first-time cheekpieces at Worcester (2m4f, good) last month; disappointed here on latest outing but could have untapped potential over this new trip if quickly back in the groove.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: In good form in the autumn, most notably when winning in first-time visor at Stratford (2m6f, good), but failed to build upon a satisfactory reappearance run when well beaten back at Stratford last month (wore cheekpieces); goes without headgear here; has a point to prove.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has worked her way back to peak form, following a break, and scored by just over 4l over C&D (good) six weeks ago; 5lb higher now but ought to make her presence felt again.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Battled well to hold on over C&D (good) last month and is now 5-10 since joining current stable just over a year ago; up another 5lb but a likely contender again.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual Irish point winner who built upon her promising rules debut when winning a Bangor maiden hurdle (2m3f, good) last month; has a lot more on her plate in this handicap but has obvious scope for further progress over the longer trip; commands respect.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Just 1-12 over hurdles but ran quite well when third at Newton Abbot in May and was in contention for a place before last-flight error cooked his goose at Warwick (also 3m2f, good) last month; could have a say.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Regressive 9yo who has modest strike-rate in recent years and made a low-key reappearance this month (2m4f); tries a new trip here; not the percentage call.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Ended last season in career-best form, winning easily at Taunton (3m, good) before finishing third over same C&D off new mark; probably needs to find more again on this first run for three months, though.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Gained both British wins at Bangor, latterly when making all (2m7f, good) four weeks ago; remains unexposed over this sort of trip and is probably still on a workable mark after recent 4lb rise; high on the list.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won this for Olly Murphy in 2024; returned from long absence with two lesser efforts towards end of last season but ran well for a long way when fifth in higher-grade C&D (good) contest for new stable this month; considered.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: A C Bound & Mrs C J Djivanovic
Spotlight: In good form when last seen in autumn 2024 and will be suited by today's trip/ground but he is entitled to benefit from this outing.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Suggested her turn might be near again when second at Bangor (2m7f, good) in May but Cartmel last month was a backward step and she's now 0-6 for current stable; cheekpieces (worn once last year) tried again.

RaceName: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Safely held in 2m4f chase here last month and now 0-9 under rules; back up in trip and fitted with tongue-tie for this return to hurdling; considered only if lively in the betting.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; thriving for Tristan Davidson and bids for a hat-trick following handicap wins at Hexham (2m7f) and Cartmel (2m6f) last month, getting up late each time; up another 5lb but this likeable sort is a player once more.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: A three-time hurdles winner (around 2m) for Jamie Snowden but signed off for him with a below-par fifth in 2m6f Cartmel handicap 14 months ago; needs to hit the ground running for his new handler.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Gained a first hurdling win on yard debut at Worcester (2m) last August; back in good form of late, third of six in 2m4f handicap there two weeks ago; not out of things.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Yet to get her head in front but she returned from six months off with a very good second of ten in 2m handicap here 17 days ago; she's proven over this longer trip and well in the mix nudged up 2lb.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Made a winning start for current yard over fences at Southwell (2m4f) in November but only eighth back hurdling in 2m7f handicap here 17 days ago; visor and tongue-tie are retried now.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Made a winning start for current yard over hurdles at Bangor (2m4f) last July; has failed to build on it though, coming in a remote fourth in 2m5f handicap chase at Market Rasen last month; has it to prove back in this sphere.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Landed novices at Huntingdon and Kelso in spring 2024 for Patrick Neville but off since posting a solid sixth in 2m5f handicap at Market Rasen over two years ago; the market can guide on this comeback run for new yard.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: On the up since sent handicapping and he gained a second success in his last three starts over C&D last month, edging out Gardener; up another 5lb but merits serious consideration.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Mrs J M Plummer & M E Sowersby
Spotlight: Bagged a pair of 2m4f Hexham wins in the spring and comes here on the back of a good second of seven to Dream's Ka over C&D last month; enjoys a 2lb weights pull here, so very much one to consider.

RaceName: Louise Hall Hen Party Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Six months off before a win at Bangor (2m4f) in May and still going well when she fell four out in another 2m4f handicap there four weeks ago; this course winner must enter calculations in refitted cheekpieces.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Failed to complete all three Irish points in spring 2025 but made the frame in two slow-ground bumpers for Ralph Beckett in early part of this year, despite racing too freely; subsequently changed hands for £12,000; major player if coping with this quicker surface on debut for Dan Skelton.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Ebadiyan (Flat/smart hurdle), Ensaya (Listed-placed 1m4f) and Ebasani (useful 1m-1m4f); trainer doesn't run many in bumpers; well worth a glance in the betting.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a fair bumper/hurdle winner; no match for winner but kept on well for second of 14 on debut at Worcester (good; hooded, as today) six weeks ago; shortlisted.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fifth foal; half-sister to a French/Spanish Flat winner; dam French 1m4f winner, half-sister to a Listed Flat winner and two useful hurdlers; trainer is not known for bumper winners but has booked James Bowen (3-10 for stable) for this newcomer.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a hurdle-winning sister to smart bumper/jumps winner Super Duty and useful jumper Grandads Cottage; faded into seventh of 14 on debut at Worcester (good) six weeks ago and needs that run to have done her good.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
TrainerName: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole right
Spotlight: Hooded for both starts; bettered last November's low-key debut when fourth of 11 over C&D (good; against males) nine days ago and any further progress will give her each-way claims at least.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Delivered on promise shown in Irish points when making all in a conditional/amateurs' bumper at Stratford (good to firm) last month; escapes a penalty for that and features prominently in calculations.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: First foal; dam fourth in a bumper and well held in novice hurdles, half-sister to high-class jumper Whisper and a French Listed hurdle winner; stable not that prolific in bumpers but this newcomer still looks interesting.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of sister to Listed Flat/smart jumps winner Noble Prince but well held when 33-1 for debut at Hereford (good) in April; hood removed.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a 7.5f Flat winner; kept on for fourth of seven (just over 5l behind Thetype Istitle) on last month's debut at Stratford but others have more pressing claims.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Closely related to useful 2m7f hurdle winner Doc Penfro; not beaten far when fifth of seven behind Thetype Istitle at Stratford (good to firm) last month but needs to build on that performance; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: QuinnBet Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to a bumper winner; not beaten far when fifth of six at Newton Abbot (good) last month but it's not form to get that excited about.
Prominent racer who has been running well in defeat over 6f this season, including here; his last win came over 7f at Musselburgh last April and he could be in the mix back up in trip.

Won at Carlisle (6f, good) last month before keeping on for third at Pontefract (6f, good) six days later, and back on the scoresheet at Carlisle (6f, good) three weeks ago; won over 7f last July; could be in the mix.

OwnerName: Total Asbestos Solutions Ltd & A Frost
Spotlight: Sixth of 22 over C&D (good) in May on reappearance and further respectable efforts when fifth of 14 on his next two starts (7f, good to firm); however, he needs something extra to return to winning ways today.

8yo who has displayed mixed form this season and was below par over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago, but he showed spark when third of 22 over C&D (good) two starts ago and he has an excellent record in this race, having won it in 2023 and dead-heated for first last year; respected.

He's done well since this visor went on and he won a big-field C&D handicap (good) in May; merely midfield here four weeks ago but the blindfold was removed late and he was stretched by 1m; in calculations back at 7f.

He's on a long losing run and can be inconsistent, but this front-runner was third of 22 over C&D (good) in May and wasn't beaten far when seventh of 20 over C&D (good) last time; each-way possibilities from low draw.

1m 2yo Group 3 winner at Longchamp in September 2024; he's nothing like the same force now but has dropped down the weights and wasn't beaten far in seventh of 17 at Ayr (6f, good) last time despite a slow start; not ruled out back up to 7f.
Returned to form to exploit a reduced mark at Thirsk (7f, good) last month on his third start for this yard; a modest 3lb rise has followed and he's a contender if backing up that latest performance.

His wins have come on slow ground and he's unraced on a fast surface, but he kept on for a respectable sixth of 17 at Ayr (6f, good) last time and could have an each-way shout if the going isn't an issue.

Enjoying good campaign for new yard, winning at Doncaster (7f, good) last month and short-headed there (7f, good to firm) latest; still mileage in his mark on old form (2yo Listed win here in 2022); didn't run well in 2023 when he wore blinkers (replacing cheekpieces) but lots to like otherwise.

Won two in a row in May (6f, good to firm/good) and finished close up on final two runs for Ben Haslam (6f, good to soft); changed hands for 14,000gns recently and he should be fine back up to 7f on his stable debut; might not be far away in a first-time visor.

Won at Ayr (7f, good to firm) in May and has continued in good form, beaten a short head when second of five at Hamilton (6f, good) a fortnight ago; back up in grade today but could give another good account.

Lightly raced 4yo who won two 7f novices last August/September; dropping down the weights and a market check is advised but he's been down the field at Doncaster on his three starts this season (7f, good to firm).

Third at Pontefract (6f, good) last month and another good run when second at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) next time; however, soundly beaten here (6f, good to firm) latest and he's been unplaced on his eight visits to York.
Fully 15lb lower than when winning at Lingfield (6f, AW) last December but this 9yo has regressed in recent months; has to turn things around.

10yo who went close at Ripon (6f, good) in May and stumbled at the start when an unplaced favourite there last month; however, his last eight wins have come at Ripon or Newcastle and he's 0-8 at York.

Made it five wins from his last six starts when scoring at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) last month; only third of six when unpenalised at Beverley (7.4f, good) eight days later but not discounted given his previous form.

He's tackling a competitive handicap on this first run of the year and it's possible he'll be rusty; however, he was progressive for Stuart Williams during last season's 3yo campaign and is of interest on stable debut.

Some good runs in defeat this spring at up to 2m1f and he bounced back from his Newbury flop to win at Chester (1m6f, good) a fortnight ago; he was given a good ride last time but could still be a force today up 4lb.

Arrives with something to prove having been well beaten here on her two starts this summer (1m2f/1m4f); however, she was progressive last July/September, winning at up to 2m, and she won over hurdles in March; possibilities if she's back on song in a first-time tongue-tie; watch the betting.
He's gradually worked his way back into form for his new yard this year, finishing second over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago; one to consider.

Some good form over hurdles, including a win at Hexham (2m, good) last month; shaped when fifth in this code at Hamilton (1m3f, good) in May as though he could do with a longer trip, and he gets it today; interesting.

Tailed off here on final run last season and pulled up at Musselburgh on reappearance, but this lightly raced 4yo got back on track when third here (1m6f, good) four weeks ago and could build on that effort; chance.

Behind a couple of these when fourth over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago but that was still a respectable run and she won at Carlisle (1m3f, good) prior to that; went close in this race in 2024; not ruled out.

Won at Ripon (2m, good) in April and at Catterick (2m, good to firm) last month; a case can be made on those performances but he hasn't been at the top of his game on his two runs since, including over C&D last time.
Edging down the weights and the return to a more galloping track could help, but his claims aren't compelling based on what he's shown at Chester this year on his three starts for a new yard.

Won at Lingfield (2m, good) in May on his second start of the season and has also scored with something to spare on both outings since (2m, AW/good); in a much deeper contest today but he's clearly on the up; player.
Won at Carlisle (1m6f, good) last month and bounced back from lesser run there (1m3f, good to firm) when third over this C&D a fortnight ago (stablemate Furhaan second); might not be far away.

Kept on for reasonable third of six at Doncaster last month on first crack at 1m4f before winning over 14.5f there a fortnight ago (good to firm each time); had just three rivals to beat last time but she's unexposed over staying trips and could be in the shake-up.

Two wins at Newcastle (2m, AW) early this year and another at Carlisle (2m1f, good) three weeks ago; this 7yo is up 5lb to a career-high mark and everything dropped right last time, but he's nevertheless entitled to respect having won in fine style.
His sole win came back in June 2024 but he often runs well and was third of seven at Chester (2m, good) four weeks ago on his second stable start; might be in with an each-way shout.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Brings the strongest form into the race having finished second of 13 in a fillies' maiden at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) five weeks ago; obvious chance of going one better.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Attracted a bit of support ahead of her Ripon debut (6f, good) 18 days ago but she got worked up in the stalls and never featured in the race; should do better at some point.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: 100-1, slowly away and always in rear at Beverley (7.4f, good) last month; should do better in time.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: 5,000gns yearling; eighth foal; brother to 7f AW winner Pascalia (RPR 69), half-brother to winners Leodis Dream (prolific 5f including 2yo; 106) and Battle Point (5f AW; 68); dam 5f 2yo winner (73); one of two runners for the stable; likely best watched on debut.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Three runs at 6f, showing her best form when third at Ripon 18 days ago; she was coming with a threatening run when getting squeezed out in the final 150 yards on that occasion and the performance can be upgraded; worth a crack at 7f; should go well.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: 28,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-brother to four winners including Plage De Havre (1m4f/12.5f; RPR 108), Batz (Group-placed 1m 2yo; 96) and Borjina (7f; 74); dam maiden half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 2 winner Rich Legacy; stable has low strike-rate with 2yos these days.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: Sent off at 33-1 when never in the hunt at Ayr (7f, good) 18 days ago; a big step forward is required.

RaceName: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice (Bands C-D) (EBF Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
Spotlight: 25-1 for his debut at Carlisle (7f, good to firm) last month but he made an encouraging start, finishing second of the 11 runners; improvement will be needed to win but it's certainly not out of the question.
Yet to win a handicap but he shouldn't be long in putting that right judged on his last two runs at Windsor and Newmarket (both 6f, good to firm); one to take seriously.

Made the frame in big-field C&D handicaps on his last two runs; would have finished much closer 13 days ago but for being hampered in the closing stages; mark left unchanged and he should be in the thick of the action once again.
Won two 6f events (good/good to soft) for Michael Dods as a 2yo; drew a blank in 2025; 50-1 when down the field behind Magic Boy on her seasonal/stable debut 13 days ago.
Ready winner of a 5f Class 5 handicap at Newcastle last October; low-key return to action over C&D six weeks ago; others bring more pressing claims.

Had strong handicap form over C&D last summer and he is well handicapped on last July's second here (behind Aberama Gold); running well in small-field events this year; should give it another good go.

OwnerName: Mrs S Hibbert, Foulrice Park Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Bids for his third straight win in this race, 2lb higher than for his 2024 win and 1lb higher than 12 months ago; slow starts have been an issue in recent outings but he retains ability and it will be no surprise to see him go well with cheekpieces now given a go.
Well backed when coming from off the pace to beat 18 rivals over C&D 13 days ago; a 4lb rise doesn't look excessive; respected.
Ended 2024 on the up and he continued the good work last season, winning three turf handicaps (5f); the handicapper has been on top since and this year's two runs leave him with a point to prove.
Four wins this season; not ideally positioned when down the field over C&D 13 days ago but, even so, an improved effort will be needed to defy this mark.
It has been a while since he won on turf but he has turned in three solid efforts this summer, albeit over shorter trips and in a lower grade; others have more pressing claims.

OwnerName: S Thompson, Mrs R Carr & G Shields
Spotlight: Good run of form came to a halt when 17th of 19 behind Magic Boy here 13 days ago; while he wasn't ideally drawn on that occasion, he will need a full revival to emerge victorious.
Still seeking a first win for this yard and, although he continues to drop down the weights, this looks too competitive.
Didn't run badly in the corresponding race 12 months ago when an unconsidered 50-1 shot (after nine months off); running well on AW when last seen but this veteran may find a few stronger this time.
Drew a blank in 2025 but he has slipped a long way in the weights; absent since a poor run at Newcastle (7f) in February; headgear absent for his return and dropping back to 6f isn't sure to suit.

OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: Has not matched this year's AW form since returned to turf; should be well treated now but not sure stall 22 will be an advantage.

OwnerName: Mrs C M Clarke, Foulrice Park Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Finally exploited a big drop in the weights when landing Class 5 at Doncaster (5.6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; similar form when second at Pontefract last week; 3lb ahead of the handicapper and one of two solid form contenders for Liam Bailey, although a lower draw would have been preferred.

Underwent a second wind operation prior to her return to action in May and it appears to have done the trick, as she followed her breakthrough win at Carlisle (7f, good to firm) with a comfortable success at Ayr (5f, good) 19 days ago; 6lb higher and connections now reach for cheekpieces; still respected in current form.
Below par on his last two starts but he went close at Ripon (6f, good) in May off a 3lb higher mark and his AW win in March was impressive; likely to pop up again soon.

OwnerName: Hard Held Partnership And Angus Racing
Spotlight: Landed the ninth win of his career when keeping on well in a Class 5 at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) five weeks ago; 4lb higher mark in a stronger race could find him out.
C&D winner; runner-up on his last two starts but this is more competitive and more minor money may be his best hope.
Fair reappearance at Pontefract but that hasn't been a springboard to better things; down the field behind Magic Boy here 13 days ago.

RaceName: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Placed in two North American Grade 1s last August/November; improved for May's comeback run here when short-headed in Group 3 at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) four weeks ago, when clear of the third; leading form claims.

RaceName: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Reappeared with an easy win in Class 4 handicap at Salisbury (1m2f, soft) last month; has also won on fast ground; this 4yo is lightly raced and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie, but she's in a much hotter race than last time and others have more substance to their form.

RaceName: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Made it 2-4 when winning on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in May before good third in 3yo Listed race at Sandown (1m, good to firm); her dam was a 1m2f/9.5f winner at the top level for connections and she could have more to offer now up in trip; in good hands to progress; interesting.

RaceName: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won two in a row (7f novice then 8.6f handicap) before staying on for close third at Goodwood (1m2f, good) in May in a race that has worked out extremely well; well beaten in the Oaks at Epsom last time but the good to soft ground may not have suited; this 3yo retains potential for her good yard.

RaceName: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Listed winner at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) last May and added a Group 2 win at Longchamp (1m4f, good to soft) last July; soundly beaten in Group 1 races on her two starts this season and she could do with settling better than at the Curragh last month, but not written off back down in grade.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 0-8 but he has been banging at the door this year, placed four times between April and June; not at his best here (6f, good) four weeks ago but it was still a fair run and dropping back in trip won't hurt.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 5f novice winner as a 2yo; made a winning handicap debut with her front-running success at Pontefract last month and a subsequent defeat on soft ground (6f) is easy enough to excuse; still has untapped potential.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins as a 2yo, including here (5f, good), and he has run some solid races in defeat this year; latest fourth here (5f, good) came in a Class 2; one to take seriously upped a little in distance and dropping back down in class.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Ran okay at Thirsk (5f, good) in May but that is sandwiched by two lesser efforts; others look more persuasive.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: This intermediate trip could suit but he was hit quite hard by the handicapper for his easy soft-ground win at Yarmouth in May and has been unplaced twice since; others look stronger.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice as a 2yo, notably a Listed success at Ripon last August; life has been tougher since and hopes rest on the drop in class and addition of a tongue tie giving her a lift.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 0-7 but she arrives having finished second in handicaps at Newcastle (5f, AW) and Nottingham (6f, good to firm) on her last two starts; up in class today and could prove vulnerable for win purposes again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Two modest turf runs either side of a cosy 6f AW win in January; still has time on his side but this opening mark doesn't look especially generous.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Just one win (6f, good) to his name from 14 attempts and that came at a lower level; others bring greater potential this time.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Finished third in four of his five 2yo starts; bled from the nose when fifth of seven in a race won by Dragon Spin on his seasonal return last month; not obviously ahead of his mark.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: Twice a winner in 5f handicaps this year, latterly at Thirsk last month; creditable fourth in a Class 4 at Doncaster last time but she will need another career best to come out on top.

RaceName: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap
Spotlight: 6f win at Yarmouth in April and she has been placed on her last two runs, beaten just a nose at Thirsk on the first occasion; has the ability to be in the thick of it again.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: By No Nay Never out of 5f/5.7f winner (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 108); 15-2 when second of 11 for novice at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 26 days ago, running on from midfield; that form has taken some knocks but still makes appeal in this line-up and this Group 2 Gimcrack entry showed plenty of promise.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 135,000gns yearling by Siyouni; third foal; half-brother to 10.6f AW winner Seola (RPR 70); dam French 7.5f 2yo/10.5f Listed winner, closely related to useful French 7f winner Markhor, out of 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Vorda; from a leading stable, so needs a close look.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 180,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Havana Grey; 11-1 when beaten a shade over 3l in a novice at Nottingham (6f, good) early last month, coming from towards rear for fourth of 12; non-runner twice since; looks sure to improve and has major each-way claims for in-form stable.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 110,000euros yearling by Showcasing; 10-1 when sixth of 13 in maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 33 days ago, making some of the running; showed ability but big improvement is needed.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 55,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; second foal; dam US 5f-8.5f turf winner, out of graded-placed US 1m winner; gelded and others look more striking on paper, even though stable was off the mark with this year's 2yos this month.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: Seventh foal; Havana Grey half-brother to winners Mister Winston (7.6f-8.5f; RPR 106), Kinks (5f-7f including 2yo/Bahrain; 96) and Crazee Icon (7.6f; 84); dam 6f AW winner (70), closely related to Listed-placed 5f winner Thesme; late foal but with in-form trainer who won this race in 2022 and 2023, both with something second time out.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 75,000euros yearling, 280,000euros breeze-up 2yo by Perfect Power; third foal; dam unplaced at 7.5f-10.5f in France, sister to US 1m Grade 2 winner Tamahere, half-sister to 10.5f Listed winner Shadan; leading yard has not yet found its stride with 2yos this term but he still needs a check.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 3,000gns yearling by Sergei Prokofiev; ran a great deal better than 150-1 suggested he would in a novice at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 16 days ago, getting hampered at the start but running on into sixth of 18, beaten just over 2l; it's not the best form in this field but was a promising debut.

RaceName: Dentakay EBF Crocker Bulteel 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (Not Run More Than Once)
Spotlight: 260,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Naval Crown; no show, however, when 25-1 for maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month, behind Public Affection.

Made all at 5-1 in small-field novice at Kempton (6f, AW) on debut then went close at 66-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes here (6f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, racing prominently throughout; on the shortlist.

16-1 winner for Michael Keady on debut at Thirsk (5f, good) in May, despite being denied a clear run, and then sixth of 25 at 80-1 in the Group 3 Albany over C&D (good to firm); she has just over 3l to find with Dark Issue (who was fourth) on that Royal Ascot form but could have more to offer; sold for £150,000 just before the Royal meeting; respected on stable debut.

OwnerName: Gary Matthews, Steve Weston & Lucky Hat
Spotlight: Made it 2-2 with easy win in four-runner Listed race at the Curragh (5f, good) in May; faded in Group 3 at Naas (6f, good) next time but kept on well when eighth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here (5f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, where she didn't enjoy an ideal passage; closely matched with Alta Regina on that latest form and the return to 6f is worth a go; chance.
280,000gns yearling who won at 12-1 on this month's debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm); others have more substance to their form but she's a likeable prospect who has plenty of scope to progress.

95,000euros yearling; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Arcano; 6-1, won by 7l in six-runner novice on last month's debut at Chepstow (6f, good to soft); this is a vastly tougher race but she's clearly a bright prospect; remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

Improved upon her first two runs when 1l third of 25 at 125-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm; Moonrise second); can be in the mix if backing up that performance.

240,000gns breeze-up buy who won easily on debut at Lingfield (5f, good to firm) in May and kept on well for sixth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here at the Royal meeting (5f, good to firm); the step up to 6f could be a positive move and she's a leading contender.

Impressive on debut at Goodwood (6f, good) in May and confirmed that promise when fourth of 25 in the Group 3 Albany Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm); she has to be firmly in calculations.

Made all on debut at Windsor (6f, good to soft) last month then dead-heated for first in a Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good to firm), where she was the 7-4 favourite; open to further improvement and represents last year's winning yard; she's one to consider.
Won modest novice race at Kempton (6f, AW) in May on second run, then well beaten at 300-1 in the Albany over C&D (good to firm); hard to fancy.

Won at Ripon (6f, good) in May on second start and suited by the return to 6f when close Listed third at Newmarket last month (good to firm; led; behind Glorious Game); stable won this in 2017 and 2023 but she needs another step forward if she's to come out on top today.

Missed the rest of the season after finishing seventh in the Coronation over C&D at 2025 Royal Ascot but has returned with two fine runs behind Blue Bolt, latterly when fourth of 15 in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D (good to firm); the one likely to give Touleen most to do.

Stepped up on reappearance form when winning Listed event over 1m2f at Newbury (good) in May; can probably be forgiven her subsequent effort in the Prix de Diane at Chantilly after pressing the pace out wide; drops back to 1m now; even a return to her best probably won't be enough, though.

Highly tried last season, showing pretty smart form when second in Leopardstown Group 3 and when beaten under 4l in Group 1 Moyglare at the Curragh; dropped to maiden company to edge out subsequent Oaks winner Thundering On on 1m Leopardstown reappearance; off since but evidently capable when fresh and likely to have a say if handling the quicker ground (raced on good or softer so far).

Edged out by Sukanya in the Fred Darling at Newbury on reappearance but had that reopposing rival behind her when an improved second to Precise in the Group 1 Coronation over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting; even better than the result (met trouble a few times) on that occasion and a similar level of performance will make her hard to beat back in a Group 3.

Came up well short in Group 1/Listed events in the second half of 2025 but different story on Kempton AW reappearance, readily seeing off ten rivals in 1m Listed race; something presumably not right when favourite for an Epsom Group 3 on Derby day (good to soft), finishing a distant last of seven; given seven weeks to get over that.

Improved upon her 2yo form when coming from the back of the pack to beat Touleen and win the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) on her reappearance; bounced back from a tame effort in the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh when sixth of nine to Precise in the Coronation over C&D last month but Touleen was 2.5l ahead of her in second on that occasion.

Losing run up to 16; has run some fine races in that period but her hold-up style dictates that things need to drop right and she got going too late when third in 1m Pontefract Listed race 18 days ago; prior to that she finished around 2l behind the reopposing Kon Tiki when eighth of 15 to Blue Bolt in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm).
Won this race on good ground 12 months ago but was on an upward curve at that stage and doesn't obviously arrive in anything like the same form this time round.

Won at Kempton (6f, AW) last month before near-miss at Epsom (6f, good), and back on the scoresheet with ready win here (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; under a 3lb penalty this progressive 3yo is 5lb ahead of the handicapper today, and he showed promise over 7f last season; major player.

Won this last year (good) and followed up in the Stewards' Cup at Goodwood (6f, good to soft); after a very good start to this year at Meydan he hasn't hit the same heights since; his recent seventh in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket was a step back in the right direction but he needs another today.

His career-best efforts have come in the last three runnings of the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good/good to firm), winning it in 2024 and a fortnight ago with a near-miss in between; under a 3lb penalty there's still mileage in his mark but he's never finished better than ninth from four visits here.

Novice wins on his first two starts and he made it 3-3 when winning a big-field handicap at York (7f, good) last month, doing it comfortably despite having to wait for a run; there is a strong suspicion he's a Group-race winner in the making and he could take an 8lb rise in his stride.

Inconsistent sort who is opposable on the majority of his form over the last 12 months and was only sixth at Newmarket last time; however, he's popped up with the odd big run, finishing third in this last year and filling the same position in a big field at York last month; not a forlorn hope each-way.

5yo who produced a career-best performance with authoritative win at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; following a 9lb rise he was well beaten over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting 12 days later, finishing fourth of six in the unfavoured far-side group, but he's not written off.

Denied a clear run when fifth at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) latest and he's a type who needs things to drop right; however, he got up on the line at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) two runs ago and may have an each-way shout.

Two wins last term (1m/7f, AW/good) and he added another on his reappearance at Haydock (7f, good) in May; again ran well when fourth of 15 at Newbury (7f, good to soft) latest but his form needs to go to a new level today.

Merely mid-division behind Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket a fortnight ago but this C&D brings out the best in him, as evidenced by this season's close-up finishes in the Victoria Cup (good) and Buckingham Palace Stakes (good to firm); could be bang there now back at Ascot.

Admirably consistent in defeat this term and he was a close second to Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) recently; races off the same mark today (due a 2lb rise) and could again be thereabouts.

Won early this year on first three runs for James Horton (7f/1m, AW) before good third here (1m, good to firm) and a fifth of seven at Sandown (1m, good); won at Kempton (1m, AW) next time; could give a good account but he's 6-9 on AW as opposed to 0-10 on turf, which tempers enthusiasm.

Reappeared with a win in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (good to soft) before good third at Newbury (1m, good), and took another step forward to win the Buckingham Palace over C&D (good to firm) at Royal Ascot; this 4yo is clearly progressive and could play another leading role up 4lb for last time.

Returned to form when dropped back in trip in first-time cheekpieces (retained) in the Wokingham here (6f, good to firm) last month, finishing fast under Ryan Moore for a head second; on that evidence the return to 7f could be a good move and he's one to consider.

Reappeared with a convincing handicap win at Newbury (7f, good) in April; underwhelming favourite in Listed races at Newmarket and Epsom on next two starts but gelded since and returns to a handicap this afternoon, and he could have a part to play if rediscovering the Newbury form.

Below his best on his last two runs, most recently over C&D at the Royal meeting; has some good C&D form, however, such as when fourth in both this race last year and the Victoria Cup in May; not ruled out each-way.

Won in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in April and has continued in good heart on his two outings since; however, he's up in grade this afternoon and needs something extra.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: She's won the last two runnings of the Group 1 British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes here in October and she was a 1l second of five to Calandagan in this race last year; short-headed in the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting and she might not be far away.

RaceName: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
