Three-time AW winner, two of them over C&D, and he is 4lb lower than for his win here last September; wouldn't judge him too harshly on a couple of low-key 6f runs when last seen; strong claims back at 5f on AW.
Exposed low-grade maiden; 80-1 when well held over 6f here four weeks ago.
The form of his 5f win at Wolverhampton in May has been franked since; a 5lb higher mark should be in range and the booking of Billy Loughnane suggests he will be ready to go after 81 days off.

Big prices and he has run to a modest level in three sprint novices this year; did hint at better last time and his trainer has enjoyed plenty of success with his half-brother Sugar Baby; worth a market check now handicapping.

Appeared to show improvement when fourth of eight at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago but they went steadily to halfway and it may not be a reliable piece of form; yard do well with this type though and she is at least unexposed.
Seven-race maiden who was held at Carlisle (6f, soft) last month following a wind operation; others have stronger claims.
Course winner (6f) for another yard in February 2025; runner-up over C&D in June and a subsequent lesser effort on turf isn't the run to judge her on; each-way shout.
Runner-up at Catterick (5f, good to soft) and Beverley (5f, good to firm) this summer; not so good at Southwell on Thursday but this test could suit better.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Veteran who gained the last five of his 13 wins here (7f-1m); not firing on all cylinders in recent weeks, though, and needs to up his game.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-17 but bettered his low-key seasonal debut when second in this grade at Nottingham (6f, soft) last month and will also be suited by today's trip and ground combination; a possible.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Needs to bounce back quickly from duff effort on turf nine days ago but has been placed here three times (7f-1m) since his 1m course win in February and has a big role to play if back on song.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Won two 7f Catterick handicaps in May and was placed in this grade at Wolverhampton (7f) when back on AW last month; didn't fire when back at Catterick 17 days ago but still a major player here.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Always behind in 6f Redcar handicap last month and now 0-7; wore a visor last time; cheekpieces given a whirl here; considered only if lively in the betting.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: The Jocks And The Geordies II
Spotlight: Has modest 1-31 strike-rate but gave good account when third of 13 in 6f handicap here last month and now dips into this basement grade for the first time; fine over 7f; high on the list.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Brian Ellison Racing Club & M Dale
Spotlight: Versatile 7yo who gave fairly good account when fifth in 1m2f handicap here last month, after a 556-day absence; that run might have brought him on but this is his first 7f start since 2022.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Eight-race maiden; respectable fourth in Catterick handicap (good) when upped to 7f and fitted with cheekpieces in May but last month's 6f run was a backward step; cheekpieces now removed; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Not beaten far when sixth of nine on handicap debut at Doncaster (7f, good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) in May but came last of ten on latest turf start; others have much stronger claims.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Displayed promise when fourth of six in Catterick novice (7f, good) in April and may not have handled soft ground when soundly beaten in her other two qualifying races; remains unexposed and is sure to appreciate this ease in grade on AW debut; interesting.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Beaten about 8l when third in Redcar handicap (7f, good) last month but has now been placed on consecutive starts over that C&D; should be fine back on Tapeta; more appealing than most.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Ursa Major & Mark Walford Racing Club
Spotlight: Held on gamely to make all in 1m handicap here last month and is now 2-31; evidently in good nick but this drop back in trip is not sure to suit.

RaceName: After Party At Tup Tup Palace Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Seven-race maiden who has struggled to get competitive off basement marks in handicaps in recent months; swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-brother to Irish 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Aloha Star; looked threatening before fading into fifth behind impressive winner at Newbury (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; should build on that performance here.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a useful and well-connected 6f 2yo winner; made promising debut at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago, keeping on well from the rear and losing out only by a neck, and makes obvious appeal.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: James Dellaway And Jon & Kay Collins
Spotlight: Out of a 6f Listed 2yo winner who has produced a US Grade 3 winner; displayed only a modicum of promise when a down-the-field 33-1 shot on debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month.

RaceName: Starman At Tally Ho Stud British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Starman (6f including Group 1 July Cup) and Sunday Star (Group-placed 6f/7f); good market support will bring her into the equation.

Sixth foal; brother to 7f winner Consecrated (RPR 98), closely related to two winners including Enshrine (1m; 81), half-brother to 5f-7f winner Sacred (including Group 2; 116); dam French 12.5f winner, half-sister to US 1m-1m2f Grade 1 winner Lady Eli; with a top stable and no surprise if he features on debut; tongue-tie fitted.
Fair form when fourth on both starts, latterly in six-runner Redcar novice (1m2f, good) five weeks ago; needs to improve here but is well bred and has the potential.

Raced too freely and was slightly disappointing when fifth in 1m2f Pontefract maiden this month but made the frame over that trip on first two starts and will be a threat if able to match that level of form over 1m.
Struggled when 250-1 for debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) 18 days ago.

Runner-up twice this spring (5.7f/5f) but form has dipped on last two outings; needs to be perked up by switch from usual cheekpieces to first-time blinkers, and to prove himself on fast ground (only win came on heavy).
Dual C&D winner, more recently in this race a year ago (good to firm); has questions to answer after some below-par recent efforts but is too well handicapped to rule out.

Came good for current stable at third attempt, with quite stylish success at Ripon (6f, good) last month; still on good mark after recent 4lb rise and this stiffer track ought to suit him; good chance.

A maiden after nine starts but all three runs this season have been respectable, and she appeared not to use her energy efficiently when a weakening sixth at Leicester (6f, good to firm) last time; hooded for first time here; enters calculations.

Spoiled chance by refusing to settle on seasonal/stable but this month's midfield finish at Newbury (6f, good to firm) was more encouraging; has slipped to a dangerous mark and should now be approaching concert pitch.
Progressive mare who won twice over C&D this spring (good/soft) and led close home to complete her hat-trick at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; could still have more to offer; respected.

Returned from break with disappointing run in May but placed twice since, more recently when close second of five over C&D (good to firm) a fortnight ago; can go well from the front again but others appeal more.
Didn't find much after travelling strongly at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last month but that was his first run since February and he's on a good mark if the outing brought him on.

Unexposed filly who made the frame in all three qualifying races, most recently when second in Chester maiden (7f, good) on seasonal/stable debut a fortnight ago; drops back in trip for handicap debut; probably still has potential.
Displayed some promise in three 2yo maiden/novice races last summer (5.7f-6f) but this seasonal/stable/handicap debut comes after a one-year absence, and she's entitled to benefit from the outing.

Easily won three-runner juvenile hurdle last month but reverts to the Flat after odds-on defeat six days later; will be suited by the trip/ground here and is probably on a workable mark but a couple of the others have less to prove; sports first-time cheekpieces.

Posted career-best performance when winning on Poytrack at Lingfield (1m2f) in April, after a break, but subsequent turf form has been underwhelming and he's still on a fairly tough mark; cheekpieces refitted in bid to perk him up.

Scored over 1m on Polytrack in May and placed twice behind same progressive rival over that trip on turf at Ffos Las last month; benefits from Mason Paetel's useful 5lb claim here and shapes as though well worth a crack at 1m2f; might be the answer.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Battled well to prevail in bunch finish at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) this month, opening account at fifth attempt; only 2lb higher and still unexposed over this trip; ought to make her presence felt again.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Denied clear run before keeping on well to go close on handicap debut at Newbury (1m2f, good) in May and, after struggling on soft ground, again ran well when fourth over that C&D (good to firm) three weeks ago; upped in trip here; must be considered.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Suited by step up in trip when keeping on well for clearcut success at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) last week ago and now 2-7; open to further progress over this distance; likely contender.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: P Hickman And Lord Lloyd Webber
Spotlight: May have been flattered by proximity when third of six in steadily run Redcar novice (1m2f, good) last month and has since finished last in a Yarmouth maiden over that trip; however, this well-bred gelding is open to improvement in handicaps.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field on first two starts (1m/1m2f) but fared better when third of seven here (1m2f, good to firm) last month, albeit no threat to front pair; should have more improvement to come in handicaps.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
OwnerName: J O'Mulloy And W R Muir
Spotlight: Runner-up on two of his three starts this season, losing out by only a neck after game attempt to make all at Chepstow (1m4f, good to firm) this month; moves up from 0-60 grade today, though.

RaceName: Madar Corporation 'Proud To Support Salisbury' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed after only four runs but was just a respectable fourth of six in 0-55 grade on last month's handicap debut at Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm) and is effectively 1lb higher from out of the weights here; needs combination of new trip and first-time cheekpieces needs to prompt improvement.
0-15 under all codes and absent since well-held fourth over hurdles in October; will probably find this trip too sharp; best to look elsewhere.
Came good with two narrow wins last month in Chepstow handicap (1m, good) and Lingfield classified (7.6f, good to firm); may need to find a bit extra but is respected in her current mood.

2-2 since switched to handicaps this season, with both wins gained over 7f on fast ground; raised just 1lb for latter success and the form has been well advertised by the runner-up since; hard to beat if stamina holds out over this new trip.
Dangerously handicapped on old form but looked out of sorts during five-race turf/AW spell from August to January; gelded in March; needs to have been revitalised by 203-day break.

Began season with three disappointing runs but was seeemingly aided by first-time blinkers (retained) when third at Leicester (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago, when she was denied a clear run close home and might have been unlucky; another 1lb lower for first attempt at 1m; one to consider.
Nine-race maiden who is yet to hit top gear after three runs in blinkers this season (1m-1m2f); slipping down the weights but needs to up her game; refitted hood is added to the blinkers.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Returned to form when fourth in first-time visor at Ripon (5f, good) three weeks ago despite stumbling and nearly losing his rider at the start; possibilities off same mark if the headgear has the same effect.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before returning to form when second of 12 at Newcastle last month, coming close to landing a gamble; still 4lb below his last winning mark and should be in the mix again.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Has had far less racing than most of these and showed he retains ability when fifth of eight at Beverley (5f, good to firm; 11-1) three weeks ago after a long absence, a gelding operation and a stable switch; big player if coming on for that run and Danny McMenamin was the successful rider in this race last year, for the same connections.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Seems to be going through the motions and his losing run stretches back over two years; needs to stop the slide but he's on a dangerous mark if staging a revival, so impossible to rule out.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: In good form in the spring, winning over this trip at Southwell, but his two most recent runs have been some way below par; others preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Tough cookie who arrives in peak form after a close third over C&D two weeks ago; one of three with serious claims for her local yard.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Prominent racer; on a lenient mark but his losing sequence is mounting and he had no obvious excuses when beating just one home at Beverley three weeks ago.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Probably best at 5f and went down by only a head at Pontefract five weeks ago; had previously shaped well when fifth in a big field on this course; trainer has won this race three times in the last eight seasons and Johnny Burke looks a positive jockey booking.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Hard to fancy on recent efforts with no better than a tenth-placed finish in his last five starts; however, he could be revived by a recent stable switch (from Seb Spencer) and he's fully 18lb lower than when eighth in the 5f handicap at Royal Ascot last summer; worth monitoring in the market.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: 4lb lower than for his last two 6f wins but recent efforts have been underwhelming and he's unproven over the minimum trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Two 5f wins in 2026 and he ran respectably when third at Hamilton two weeks ago; prone to the odd poor run, however, and others are higher up the list.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Plucky veteran who retains plenty of vim and vigour, another fine run when second in amateurs' race at Doncaster last time; 3lb out of the weights but has finished third in the last two runnings of this event and has each-way possibilities once more.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: 3-11 on turf; steadily progressive but most recent success came off 11lb lower and she'll need another personal best to notch win number four.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
OwnerName: Ingleby Bloodstock Ltd & The Ivy League
Spotlight: June win came in a small field at Catterick (5f) but he finished behind Kodiac Thriller when only seventh of nine at Ripon next time; well beaten on only run at York; bit to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Winning for the fourth time when scoring at Beverley in June, and he was narrowly beaten in a blanket finish there on Monday; not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: Front-runner who was beaten off only inside the final 1f at Lingfield last time; should make another bold bid but he's still 4lb higher than when making all at Yarmouth in the spring.

RaceName: Sky Bet 'Jump Jockeys' Nunthorpe' Handicap (To Be Ridden By Professional Jump Jockeys)
Spotlight: C&D winner earlier in career and also won off today's mark at Ripon in May, but he's been tailed off on his last two outings and urgently needs a reversal of fortune.

Just one win to his name since returning to action in November and that is scant reward for some fine efforts, including an unlucky defeat over 5f here in May; good third at Chester (6f, good; drawn wide) four weeks ago; remains a sprinter of interest.
Made good progress in the second half of 2025; the handicapper has held the upper hand more recently though and this might not set up ideally for his style of racing.

5f win on this card last year and he followed it was a hugely eye-catching third over 5.4f at the Ebor meeting; back in the winners' enclosure at Beverley in April and he has run well in defeat here and at Newcastle on his last two starts; can fluff the start and he still has to prove himself at 6f but there is an air of unfinished business surrounding him.
Made a winning stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) in April; two good 6f runs this month too but he will need to pull out more if he is to come out on top this afternoon.

His form has taken off since dropped to 6f, winning at Ripon and Hamilton in May and posting fine efforts in defeat over C&D and at Newmarket since; no obvious reason why he wouldn't be in the shake up again.
Ended 2025 in fine form on AW; 0-7 in 2026 but he has slipped 6lb below his last winning mark and has Toby Moore taking another 7lb off his back; suspicion a few will prove stronger.

Beat 17 rivals at Thirsk in April and he has finished second three times since, including a big-field C&D handicap; missed out by a short-head at Newmarket last week; solid form claims despite small rise in the weights.
Stayed on from well off the pace to take third in a 0-80 over C&D a fortnight ago; this is tougher but likely to give another good account.

Began the year with two good efforts at Newbury and Newmarket; beaten favourite on his last two starts but that is not to say this mark will prove beyond him if things pan out more favourably; each-way shout if a high draw doesn't prove to be a negative.

Admirable campaigner down the years and although he hasn't placed in three visits to York, he has been poorly drawn in two of them and ran well in Listed company on the other occasion; looked to retain ability when third at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on 2000 Guineas day and he shouldn't be crabbed for his Wokingham effort as he trounced the only other rival to race up the stands' rail; it has been a long time since he's had a mark this low; big run on the cards.

OwnerName: Doug Graham, Ian Davison, Alan Drysdale
Spotlight: Veteran who ran a cracker behind a stablemate over C&D at last season's Ebor meeting; runner-up twice in Bahrain in January; low-key return to Britain last week; on a good mark but this is a tough race in which to try and rebound.
The winner of two of his three starts in 2026, notably a big-field Class 4 over C&D six weeks ago; 4lb higher in a stronger race and his draw may not be advantageous.
Run of in-frame efforts came to an end here two weeks ago but he still ran with more promise than his finishing position suggests; still likely vulnerable at this level.

Rated 5lb higher than when a close fifth in this race 12 months ago; has done well on AW since, winning at Southwell (well backed) on New Year's Day and finishing a good fourth at Newcastle four weeks ago; not obviously thrown in but could still have a bit more to come.

He has run well over C&D in the past and he arrives in fine form, winning 5f handicaps at Haydock and Carlisle (soft/good to soft) this summer; the 5lb rise is less of a concern than either his draw in stall 22 or the forecast faster ground.

Won last season's Portland handicap at Doncaster off a 1lb higher mark; she made a slow start to 2026 but there have been encouraging signs more recently, fourth at Ayr (6f, soft) and then second at Doncaster (5f, good to firm); form dipped here (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; could bounce back.

Progressive sprinter in 2025 (following wind surgery) and he has carried on the good work this year, winning 6f handicaps at Doncaster in May (good to soft) and June (good to firm); well beaten at Thirsk 24 days ago, however, and this is a deeper race.

Promising at up to 1m for Ger Lyons as a 2yo; unplaced in his first two runs (7f/1m1f) for this yard but he turned in a career-best effort when second of 14 (behind a handicap blot; pair clear) over C&D four weeks ago; showed good speed on that occasion and he should make a bold bid from stall 1 despite a 4lb rise.

Won a good C&D handicap last year and also successful at Ayr last September; 0-7 in 2026 but he retains all his ability and ran well for third (of 17) at Ayr 19 days ago; high draw a potential stumbling block.
Promising in his first three 2yo runs but he couldn't quite cut the mustard in nurseries thereafter; gelded prior to his reappearance; still has time to do better but he returns in a warm race.

Three poor runs to begin his turf campaign but he underwent wind surgery in June and returned to form with a close second at Chester (6f, good) four weeks ago; not certain to confirm those placings with Stratusnine.

Beat subsequent Derby winner Christmas Day in the Group 2 Dante over C&D (good ground) in May, only to finish well beaten behind that rival on much softer ground at Epsom (11-2); still low-mileage and looked potentially top-class in the Dante; may get back on track on today's forecast firmer ground.

Has an unblemished record at York, winning the Dante (1m2f) and Great Voltigeur (1m4f) last season; had a delayed start to 2026 due to a bruised foot and almost certainly needed the run when last of eight in the Group 1 Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud three weeks ago; interesting with that outing behind him and back on the Knavesmire.

Second to Pride Of Arras in last year's Dante over C&D; looked set for a stellar 2026 when trouncing five rivals in Group 3 at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on reappearance, but hasn't repeated the form in 1m Group 1s since; stepping back up in distance looks a sensible move and he's the one to beat judged on that standout Newmarket effort.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Nine wins in a varied career include this race 12 months ago and a Group 1 in Saudi Arabia (10.5f, good to firm) in February; far from disgraced in Hong Kong last time and now returns from three months off; should give his running but a 5lb penalty makes the task more difficult.

Most recent success came in Group 2 at Sandown (1m, good) last April; not at best in three runs this season, including in same race and when returned to 1m2f for Group 1 at Royal Ascot five weeks ago; needs a revival.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: Consistent type who won six times last season and arrives on the back of two close seconds; this race looks deeper than his last two but he's in fine form and unlikely to be far away.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins on the AW but he's just as effective on turf; needs to bounce back from a poor run at Newmarket's July meeting but he's down sharply in grade here and his form from the spring has a solid look to it.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Just three wins but has been second or third 17 times, including on his last four starts; stall 17 could be tricky.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
OwnerName: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor
Spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before winning at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) on Sunday; not certain to be as effective back at 1m and he's ridden by an apprentice with a smaller claim.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; hasn't had the rub of the green of late, repeatedly denied a run when stepped up to 1m at Newcastle four weeks ago; respected.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Campaigned solely at 7f this term but shapes as if he'll be well suited by this return to 1m; has met trouble in running on his last two starts; thrown in on the pick of his form for Richard Hannon and could be ready to strike.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Arrives on a recent high after a win at Musselburgh and a second at Ripon (both 1m, good); should give his running but he's up in grade here.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Won two from five last season and looks as good as ever this term, fourth in a big field at Ascot two weeks ago; effective at 7f and 1m; should be in the thick of things again.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Front-runner with a favourable low draw; shaped nicely at Newmarket (1m, good) on reappearance and quick ground was blamed for a poor run next time; below the mark of his last win (over C&D) and no surprise if he makes a bold bid from the front, especially if the rain materialises.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Upped markedly in trip here (1m6f) four weeks ago and predictably failed to stay; previous form (7f-1m1f) is solid enough but a wide draw could be difficult to overcome.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Has a better strike-rate on AW than grass but she's in better form than her last two turf runs suggest, short of room at Ascot on latest; less obvious than several of these but not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Falling in the weights and ran respectably when third to Rajapour at Redcar on Sunday, but the winner bolted up that day and it's hard to see the tables being turned.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Nosed home at Redcar (1m, good) in May and ran creditably when a close third at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) two weeks ago; her mark is unchanged but she's up from a 0-65 to a 0-80.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Far more miss than hit this season and beat only one home at Newmarket last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
Spotlight: Had been bubbling under prior to winning easily at Redcar (1m, good to firm) on Sunday, and given the style of that success he looks an attractive proposition under a 5lb penalty; high on the list.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: £50,000 yearling, £75,000 breeze-up 2yo; by Mehmas; dam Group-placed 7f/1m winner (including 2yo; RPR 108), out of US 8.5f Grade 2 winner; upwardly mobile stable had its first 2yo winner of the season earlier this month; well worth a market check.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: 200,000gns yearling; too green to do herself justice (slowly away, flashed tail soon after start) when fifth on debut over C&D (6-1) earlier this month; plenty of improvement required but she might have learned a lot.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Seemed to know her job and shaped encouragingly when 1l third of nine at Redcar (6f, good to firm; 5-2) in May, always up with the pace; that form is probably nothing special but she's in good hands and should progress.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: N Bradley Racing 29, D Scott & P Spencer
Spotlight: Overcame slow start to win comfortably at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month; open to further progress and should be just as effective back at 6f, but carries a penalty in what looks a stronger race.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Did her best work late on after a slow start when sixth at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; 17-2) two weeks ago, finishing a place behind Hout Bay; like that rival, she could make quite a bit of progress for the experience.

RaceName: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: 150,000euros breeze-up buy; went off 50-1 but shaped nicely when fifth of 11 at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago, rallying after being short of room; could improve significantly and commands major respect.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Bred to be useful and has been steadily progressive; clearcut winner at Lingfield (1m4f) towards end of 2025 and shaped well over inadequate 1m2f at Chester (good) on reappearance; this step back up in distance should be perfect and she has rock-solid claims.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Could be unexposed at 1m4f and ran creditably on first attempt at trip when third of eight at Ascot (good to firm) two weeks ago; goes well for positive tactics and Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a bonus.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Useful 3yo when based in France, largely disappointing for Joseph O'Brien last year; some promise for current yard, not helped by racing wide at Chester (1m2f) last time; moves into unknown territory trip-wise but his mark is falling and he's impossible to discount.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo; has an impressive strike-rate but all six of his wins have come on the AW and he hasn't been placed in four runs on turf; below par last time and has a fair bit to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Arrives on a hat-trick after 1m3f AW wins for Andrew Balding at Kempton and Southwell, after which he was sold for 50,000gns; not fully proven on turf, although he did show promise at Haydock on his debut; has joined a very capable stable and may not have reached his ceiling just yet.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: On a long losing run and never a threat here two weeks ago, but he'd previously been beaten just a nose in the Queen Mother's Cup over C&D in June; none too reliable but a danger to all if he's on a going day.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Hasn't been long with David O'Meara and he looks to be building up to something, bumping in to an improver when second of 12 at Ayr (1m5f, soft) five weeks ago; quick ground would be an unknown but otherwise he has plenty in his favour.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Represents a new trainer in excellent form and has won at Goodwood (1m4f, good) and Epsom (1m4f, good to firm) on his last two outings, proving himself better than ever; edging up the weights only gradually and in the mix again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Awarded C&D Queen Mother's Cup last June and much lower in the weights now, but that's because his form has fallen off a cliff; dangerous if blinkers (replacing other headgear) spark a revival but carries clear risks.

RaceName: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Formerly trained by Andrew Balding and Nicky Henderson; sole Flat win came over 1m2f in 2023 but she has since won five times over hurdles; ran creditably over 2m at Lingfield at the start of the year before being sold for £6,000 in May; worth a check in the market.

Promising start to handicap career, chasing home Toastmaster at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) before finishing a couple of places ahead of that rival when third of 11 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm again) a fortnight ago; handily drawn and should go well again.

Sent off 5-4 when beating six rivals on his debut at Newcastle (6f) in December; hasn't advanced his form in two subsequent outings but it was a sound start to his handicap career when third of 14 in 6f course handicap (good) latterly; stuck on after getting outpaced in a style which suggests this extra 1f will suit; has to enter the reckoning.

OwnerName: Follow The Majer Partners & S Herrington
Spotlight: Struck at the third time of asking for Micheal Herrington when seeing off Flight Control and 11 others in handicap at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; Flight Control finished a couple of places ahead of him at the Newmarket July meeting since but it was another sound effort from this son of Cotai Glory.

Bar a blip on AW in the spring (wore a first-time tongue tie which was quickly discarded) his profile is steadily progressive, edging out Alpha Capture (due to run here on Friday) in 7f Doncaster handicap (good to firm) 16 days ago; 4lb higher now back in a 3yo only race but he may have more to give.

Ended time for Jane Chapple-Hyam by making all in 7f Yarmouth handicap (good to firm) four weeks ago; changed hands for 30,000gns since; new stable, which continues in good form, also runs Toastmaster; drawn wider than ideal.

Beaten on first ten starts but got off the mark at the 11th attempt at Ripon (6f, good) in May and followed up in big field at Doncaster (7f, good); his winning run was ended back at Doncaster but ran with credit again in fourth.

Scored with authority on his return in Pontefract novice (6f, good to soft) in April; never on the pace when well-beaten eighth of 14 in 6f handicap here 12 weeks later but it's possible he'll benefit from this step up to 7f and remains unexposed after four starts; going than firmer than good would be a first.

Shaped well when runner-up on three successive starts (6f/7f, good to soft/soft) but never better than midfield when faced with a firmer surface over 1m here 15 days ago; quickly drops back in trip with a visor also added.

OwnerName: Mrs Tabor, Mrs Mv Magnier, Mrs Shanahan
Spotlight: Narrow winner of a Beverley maiden in April; matched that when fifth on her handicap debut at Thirsk (1m, good) but two lesser runs have followed; Mr Noble is the more obvious of the Karl Burke pair.

Built upon the promise of her debut fourth at Newbury (7f, good) in April when winning maiden at Lingfield (7f, AW) in May; well beaten on soft ground at Salisbury next time but bounced back with a respectable sixth on Chester handicap debut four weeks ago; that was a 0-95 so this represents a slight drop in grade; remains lightly raced for a leading yard.
Got up late to win a 5f Catterick novice (good to firm) in May but beaten upwards of 10l in his five other starts, including course handicaps over 5f and 1m the last twice.
Of interest on her 2yo best but beaten a long way on both 6f starts this year; the combination of a step up in trip and addition of a tongue-tie needs to spark a big upturn in his fortunes.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Resuming (32-weeks). Ex Michael Grantham in WA. Took his game to another level winning the Northerly Stakes last prep. Excellent first up record. Soft jump-out here 1/7. Leading contender.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: R A Holburt, B R Holburt Et Al
Spotlight: Annexed the (Bm84) at Caulfield 27 Jun. Rallied powerfully from midfield to salute this venue. See no reason he can't bring up a hat-trick of wins.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: N S Psaltis, Mrs G C Psaltis Et Al
Spotlight: Great run at Flemington 20 Jun. Put in some good work late this course. Very fit and not out of this.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: D M D B Syndicate, Grahame Begg Racing Et Al
Spotlight: Midfield and worked home solidly in rain affected going at Flemington second-up. Others with greater appeal.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
TrainerName: Leon & Troy Corstens & Will Larkin right
OwnerName: Bennett Racing Pty Ltd (N Bennett), D Hardie Et Al
Spotlight: Let-up (49-days). Sent out $13 when unable to threaten at Eagle Farm when second-up. Sharper now and can make his presence felt with even breaks.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: A J Hehir, D W Rasheed Et Al
Spotlight: Knuckled down with purpose in choppy conditions here last time. Key player.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: D J Oliphant, P J Salter Et Al
Spotlight: Went back, closed intently this track off long break. Will be better for the outing. Must be considered.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
OwnerName: A T Biacsi, D Angely Et Al
Spotlight: First-up (23-weeks). Ex S V Vahala in Victoria. Last win was 23 Nov 2024. 1st & 4th at recent jump-outs. Place claims preferred.

RaceName: The Big Screen Company Bletchingly Stakes (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Raced in back half and was never in a position to mount a serious challenge this track. Needs to recapture form.
On target four times in her last seven outings; scored in the Acorn Stakes last month; jockey's C&D record from low draws is useful and expected to be in the thick of things.

OwnerName: Douglas Scharbauer & Three Chimneys Farm LLC
Spotlight: Behind Counting Stars when beaten just under 4l to finish second in the Acorn Stakes last month; has won three of her four career runs and landed the Kentucky Oaks three months ago; major player.

OwnerName: Gary Barber, Bridlewood Farm & Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners
Spotlight: Went down by 1l behind Directive last month in an allowance optional claimer.

Behind Always A Runner at Churchill Downs when sixth of 13 in the Kentucky Oaks in May; winner of three of her five runs to date; wears first-time blinkers; warrants consideration as has some big wins on the CV; also engaged in race 7 at Monmouth Park.

OwnerName: Trott Racing Stable, Five Sisters Farm & John Polizos
Spotlight: Career wins-runs record of 4-11; 15-2 winner by just over 2l at Delaware Park last month in a black type; despite that Delaware Park success, unlikely to trouble the principals; also engaged in race 7 at Monmouth Park.

No impression when fourth of eight in April, finishing well behind reopposing Always A Runner at Aqueduct in an allowance Grade 3; workout history raises concerns this race may be needed so not hard to turn elsewhere; was due to run at Saratoga Friday.
Missed the frame (beaten 7l into sixth) in an allowance Grade 3 at Churchill Downs two months ago; on target twice in her last five outings.

OwnerName: Madaket Stables LLC, Kisber Racing et al

X-Men Racing V LLC & Madaket Stables LLC

Malcolm Prescott 80th Birthday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Gestuet Schlenderhan Gmbh U Co Kg
Spotlight: Minor honours all four starts; back to 1m from 1m2f when second in a Windsor novice (good to firm) 13 days ago, put firmly in her place by the winner; not progressing but clearly the best form claims in this tiny field.

RaceName: Malcolm Prescott 80th Birthday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten 22l at Carlisle (7f, soft) on debut but his 6l second of four when 33-1 again in a novice at Chester (7.6f, good) four weeks ago was a great deal better; shapes as if 1m will help but Asset has markedly better form.

RaceName: Malcolm Prescott 80th Birthday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fifth of six in maidens at Beverley (8.4f, good) in June and Redcar (7f, good to firm) last Saturday, showing modest form on debut but suffering a heavy defeat last time; may prove capable of better in due course but seemingly best watched for now.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 115,000euros breeze-up purchase, by Blue Point; 20-1 when fifth of six in a maiden at Yarmouth (5f, good to firm) 11 days ago, making an awkward start and never dangerous; could be a lot wiser this time but two of today's rivals have clearly accomplished more.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 200,000gns breeze-up 2yo by No Nay Never; first foal; dam US 1m/8.5f turf winner (including Grade 3) out of maiden half-sister to 1m4f Grade 1 winner Sarah Lynx; tongue tied for debut; needs a close look.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Very green when last of six here (6f, good) on debut but he left that form way behind when an always-prominent third of six in maiden at Hamilton (5f, good) three weeks later, finishing narrowly in front of Calef on same terms as today; should figure prominently again.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Front rank long way when third in a Catterick maiden (5f, good to firm) on the third of her four starts, her most professional performance and best form; get messed around early and looked less straightforward at Hamilton (5f, good) last time but ran on to finish a head behind Onslaught on same terms; they are the two leading form contenders, albeit not setting a high standard.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Too green on debut at Bath (5f, good) but made most in a novice at York (6f, good to firm) four weeks later, finishing only sixth of eight but that performance showed promise and she has a useful sprinting pedigree.

RaceName: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Holy Roman Emperor; fifth foal; sister to 1m/1m1f winner Way To Dubai (RPR 96), half-sister to two winners including Lady Zoumzain (Listed-placed 5f/6f including 2yo; 92); dam German 7.5f 2yo winner, half-sister to Italian 1m Group 3 winner Salford Secret; one to note from powerful stable whose 2yos continue to make a serious impact.
0-15 overall; Ayr (1m2f) 13 days ago saw her finish runner-up for the third time but she dictated the pace in a five-runner race that day and others seem to have more pressing claims.

Last four wins have been over C&D, including when he was switched to this headgear nine days ago and got up close home to register his best show this season (The New Bay Pearl fourth); back up 3lb but still well treated on 2025 form; has to be in serious calculations.

3yo who wore an eyeshield over 1m2f on last three starts, winning at Leicester (good) and Wetherby (good to firm) on first two occasions; never dangerous at Beverley latest but it was another creditable run; not the most straightforward and needs extra on this return to 1m, but still respected given questions over today's opposition.
0-8 (placed three times) for Roger Varian but hasn't shown enough in her four races for new yard this term, fourth of seven to Mount King over C&D last time; continues to fall in the weights.

Finished second or third in her first six starts, before off the mark in a five-runner handicap at Hamilton (1m, good to firm) nine days ago in second-time blinkers; often front-runner, including for that win; up 5lb but just a 3yo and could have more to offer.
Six-race maiden who's failed to make a serious impact in his three handicaps (7.6f, 6f and 7f); dropped 5lb in the process and returns to 1m but others are more persuasive.

Has gained all four handicap wins over the extended 1m at Beverley, two this May; underwhelming prospects judged on two runs here, admittedly back in 2024 but he looks opposable seeing as he may well need a career best.

OwnerName: N White, S White, T White & E Burke
Spotlight: He hasn't won as often as one of his ability probably should but he is a tough and reliable performer who was as good as ever with his excellent second of eight in a Group 2 at Ascot (1m, good to firm) 15 days ago; sets the standard and looks the one to beat.

OwnerName: Julie And David R Martin And Dan Hall
Spotlight: Front-runner; successful in this race in 2024 but that wide-margin win represents his last victory; solid fourth in a good York handicap in May; should be in the thick of it.

OwnerName: J Fyffe, A Edmondson & L McGurty
Spotlight: Not far behind Crystal Flyer when fourth in a fillies' Listed event over C&D 19 days ago; this is a deeper race though.

Two wins in 1m handicaps at Goodwood last autumn; began the season with three good runs, notably his second of 18 in a 1m handicap at York in May, and latest disappointment can be attributed to his messy start (reared as the stalls opened); should go well.

OwnerName: Castle Racing Co Ltd & Mps Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Back to her best when 66-1 second in a fillies' Listed event over C&D 19 days ago; this represents a much stiffer assignment.

Prominent racer; close third in a handicap at Goodwood (1m2f, good) 12 months ago represents her best form but it is still a level or two beneath what will be required today; hood (tried on final 3yo start) returns.

RaceName: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Back down to 1m when first and second in his last two outings, on his only appearances at this track; an in-form candidate who has plenty of earlier form at 1m2f, including an AW win; respected.

RaceName: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: All three wins were 1m2f on Newcastle AW last October-December; his three races this year suggest that the handicapper has caught up; this is also only his third race on turf, having twice been towards rear last June, so he has a bit to prove on this first run since his second wind surgery.

RaceName: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Often front-runner; commenced handicap career with a five-timer in May/June 2025; ran respectably under Rose Dawes at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) on latest start but that was good enough for only fifth of seven; others may have the edge.

RaceName: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Made the running when 1m2f handicap winner (good to firm) this year at Doncaster and Beverley; this is a less demanding task than her last two starts, so a return to winning ways can't be ruled out.

RaceName: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ended 2025 with a breakthrough win at Nottingham (1m) and back on the scoresheet by a short head when making all at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) last month; rather mixed this term but his seventh of eight at Windsor last time came in warm race and today's opposition is less demanding.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Huge chance on last summer's best, as he's 7lb lower than for his Thirsk success last July; yet to shine this season but drops in grade and needs a close market check.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice at Brighton last season; the odd good effort this time around but her last two runs haven't been her best; return to 6f is a plus, at least.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Made it tenth time lucky with her win at Catterick (6f, good to firm) last month; 7.4f probably stretched her last time and this should prove more suitable.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: 0-26 on turf and, while he is likely to give his running, he remains opposable for win purposes.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Ended a losing run with a front-running 6f win at Thirsk in April; not so good since but he is well drawn to attack and this track suits his aggressive racing style; one to take seriously.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: 22-race maiden but he has shown winning potential, including when second in a 0-50 classified event at Leicester (6f, good to firm; blinkered first time) on his recent stable debut; draw could have been kinder.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Not beaten far on his last two starts and this veteran is only 1lb higher than for his win in this event last year; well drawn; solid claims.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: 0-15 and he hasn't really threatened to put that right this time around; well drawn but likely vulnerable again.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Below par on her last two starts but she was in good form in May and is only 2lb higher than for her Bath win (5.7f, good); revival may be predicted by the betting.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Just a whiff of promise at a low level; last of eight when favourite at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 12 days ago; returns to 6f with new headgear.

RaceName: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap
Spotlight: Exposed maiden; well beaten in two runs for new yard this year; too much to prove.
Back to winning ways with a hard-fought success at Catterick (6f, good to firm) 11 days ago; goes well at Pontefract and he is a major player despite a small rise in the weights.

OwnerName: SBK Racing & B & J Parr Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Prominent racer; series of good runs at around 7f since May; slipping down the weights and should be a key player back at 6f.
Best known for her Hamilton exploits (12 wins) but she ran well over 5f here in the spring and couldn't be arriving in better form, winning three of her last five; contender.
Two wins at Ripon (6f, soft and 5f, good) last summer; good run over 5f here on his seasonal return in June; backwards step at Ripon latest; others look more persuasive.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Limited Flat maiden who was well beaten in a small field on his hurdling debut; opposable.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: After a gelding operation he won two 1m2f handicaps and comfortably accounted for three rivals on his hurdling debut; suffered early interference when only fifth in his latest Flat run; in good nick but the penalty asks something of him.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Had six runs for Dan Skelton on the Flat, finishing second and first in opening two handicaps (at about 1m4f) before a poor final run; has since had wind surgery and should make a hurdler.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Nine-race Flat maiden but was placed and had a similar level of form in that sphere to Salkadan; could go well on hurdling debut and Sean Bowen is 7-14 for the yard.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: One competitive run in six Flat starts and exposed as modest; runner-up last week at Newton Abbot but he was beaten 12l by the winner in a poor-looking race.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Left Ralph Beckett for 9,500gns and as a five-race maiden (1m-9.4f); it wasn't a bad final run (fifth of ten; in a tongue-tie and cheekpieces) and as a 3yo filly she receives all the allowances.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 9-4 for a Newton Abbot maiden and was competitive when running out at the penultimate flight, albeit in a three-runner race; could have some part to play.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ran three times for Andrew Balding, the standout run when fourth of eight in a 1m AW novice in December; changed hands for 2,600gns and now gelded.

RaceName: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Modest form in five defeats for Jack Channon (7f-1m) and wouldn't be the obvious answer on hurdling/stable debut; cheekpieces replace a visor.
Now 0-26 over hurdles after last week's defeat at Stratford but she's knocking on the door; unlikely to be far away off the same mark.
Longstanding Flat maiden who is 0-5 over hurdles; beaten about 9l last time at Hexham but she's unconvincing.
Winning pointer; lightly raced over hurdles and latest second at Worcester (back at 2m) was her best run yet; has to be of interest.

Has won over hurdles and fences off slightly lower marks and ran a solid race in defeat in a 2m4f handicap chase at Worcester last time (second run for this yard); this drop in trip shouldn't hurt her chances.

OwnerName: Castle View Racing & W F Corbett
Spotlight: Bumper winner but no sign of that form over hurdles and now makes her handicap debut; risky.
Bumper/hurdle winner; had plenty of chances in handicaps and was a long way behind No Risk Today in the latest; now goes in a tongue-tie.
Flat winner who is 0-19 over hurdles and hasn't been running well this year; 1lb out of the weights.
Taunton winner in April (2m1f, good) but signed off for Tom Lacey on a low note and ran fairly miserably on last month's stable debut.
Won her first two handicaps by a length and latest Bangor run (after a collective 13lb rise) was too bad to be true; could yet prove herself worthy of this mark.

After a wind operation she was first and fourth in 2m4f/2m7f handicaps for previous yard; joined this one for £3,000 and coped fine with the drop back to 2m when a clearcut winner here 11 days ago; raised 8lb but she's clearly turned a corner.
16-race maiden who has the odd piece of respectable form but she hasn't always looked straightforward and best efforts have been between 2m4f and 3m; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

RaceName: CL Cleaning Services Ken Boulton Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: It was only a Class 5 he won at Worcester (2m, good) but that was straightforward in the new tongue-tie and he ran fairly well off a 6lb rise in a small-field Class 3 at Newton Abbot; travels strongly and well worth considering down 1lb.

RaceName: CL Cleaning Services Ken Boulton Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Lightly raced and off the mark in ready fashion in a 2m maiden at Worcester earlier this month; this mark might be okay.

RaceName: CL Cleaning Services Ken Boulton Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Not straightforward and hard to win with at the best of times; tailed off last time at Stratford on yard debut.

RaceName: CL Cleaning Services Ken Boulton Memorial Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Case Racing Partnership & Anita J Lush
