OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Home-bred by Farhh out of a 7f/1m winner; beaten 4.5l when third on last month's debut at Wetherby (7f, good to firm; 8-1, second won at Epsom next time); improvement likely; chance.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Won two 6f handicaps on good ground last season; plenty of good runs without winning this season, including when placed at Pontefract and Carlisle on last two starts (6f, good); on a good mark; well drawn; good chance.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-Richard Fahey; runner-up on last two starts, both over 5f here (soft/good to firm), last time finishing clear of the rest when beaten a neck by one completing a four-timer; now tries 6f again; interesting.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: 6f winner at Newcastle last October; fair form back on turf this year, although pulled too hard when beaten nearly 6l over 7f here last week; should fare better back at 6f.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark on second handicap start over C&D last week (good to firm; second run after wind op); should go well again.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
OwnerName: Adam Mills And Jonnie Delta Racing
Spotlight: 12-time winner, three of them here (5f/6f); not beaten far on last two starts and is on a fair mark so could go well.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Completed a hat-trick on first three starts in 2024 (7f/1m, good/good to soft); hasn't won since, and below-par last three starts (6f/7f); bit to prove at present.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Only win was in a 1m2f novice at Bath (heavy) for Marcus Tregoning in October 2024; tried at various trips by Jim Goldie, best run when third over 7f here two weeks ago (good to firm; made the running); interesting on her first run at 6f.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-Irish; six-race maiden (last three runs for this yard); becoming well handicapped, but a bit to prove.

RaceName: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Handicap
Spotlight: Placed in two 5f Hamilton maidens in June/July 2024; disappointing since, and was beaten 15l when 12th of 13 over C&D when back from a break three weeks ago.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap
Spotlight: Comes into this in good form having won over C&D on last two starts (good to firm), last week scoring by 3.5l when an 8-15 shot; 7b higher here, but should go well again.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap
Spotlight: Has won twice over 7f this year, the first at Newcastle in January, the latest at Musselburgh in April (good); creditable third on last three starts, latest over C&D three weeks ago; each-way chance.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed; sound run on second handicap start when runner-up over 1m here last time (good; 22-1); quite interesting down in trip.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed filly; beaten over 5l when eighth of 11 on her handicap debut at Sandown last time (1m, good; 8-1); may fare better down in trip.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap
Spotlight: 3-3 over this C&D, latest success coming three weeks ago (good; Abduction a length back in third but 2lb better off); up 2lb; chance.
All three wins have been on AW (7f/1m); fair second to in-form rival at Musselburgh in May (1m1f, good) but a bit more needed.

Not totally straightforward but in good form since blinkers went on and off the mark for this yard when scoring in them over C&D three weeks ago (good to firm); close third off this 5lb higher mark over C&D last week and this looks easier; should go well again.
Five turf wins at around 1m (good/good to firm), the latest off this mark at Leicester in May; not at his best on last two starts but he could go well in a modest event.

Tough, consistent sort; hasn't won on turf for more than three years but plenty of decent placed runs this term, including when second over 1m here in May (good to firm) and when close third over 6f at Hamilton in June (good to soft); yet to win over 1m.
Won at Beverley (8.5f, good to firm) and Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) last season; a bit disappointing this term but has dropped to a good mark; could go well.
Won over 1m1f at Musselburgh (good) in June in first-time cheekpieces but soundly beaten in same headgear over C&D last week; needs to bounce back.
Well beaten in three runs in novice/maiden company last season; makes handicap debut after a break of 321 days having had wind surgery for the second time; probably best watched.

OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: Two wins this season, a Musselburgh handicap in June (good) and last time a C&D classified (good); this is tougher but has an each-way chance.
Won twice over 1m at Redcar last summer (good to firm/good to soft); fair effort on June's belated reappearance but a bit more needed.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Unexposed 3yo who has been a big improver since switched to handicaps and he won by 8l at Nottingham (8.3f, good to firm) last time; 10lb higher at this new trip but he still looks feasibly treated on that latest form and is out of a half-sister to a smart 10.5f winner; strong contender for in-form yard; first-time blinkers replace cheekpieces.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Easy winner of a Bath novice (1m2f, good) in April but he's been disappointing in two handicaps since; still lightly raced but he has hung right a few times and he needs to find more progress.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won over 1m here (good to firm) in May and she's finished runner-up at Hamilton (1m3f/8.3f) in her last two starts; continues to edge up the weights but she should go well again back up in trip.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Eight-time turf winner who made 2-6 for Jim Goldie when justifying favouritism over C&D (good to firm) two weeks ago; remains feasibly treated off only 2lb higher and he won't mind if the forecast rain arrives; respected.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Had only won once since the autumn of 2023 until he fired off a hat-trick under Lauren Young this May, culminating with a Carlisle win (good; made all); still looks feasibly treated on that form but he's been disappointing in his last two runs and this is step back up in grade; one of three runners for Jim Goldie.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Four of his eight wins have been at Ayr including three over C&D; his last success was 12 months ago but he's been placed in two of his last four runs and has each-claims again.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins have come on AW and latest was off 1lb lower at Chelmsford (5f) last September; 0-7 on turf but she's run respectably in small fields at Leicester and Doncaster in her last two starts; now drops back in grade and she shouldn't be far away.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Recorded his seventh AW win when scoring at Wolverhampton (5f) in April; two fair efforts at Ayr (5f/6f) since but he was quiet at Hamilton last time and is now 0-23 on turf; others preferred.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Made all at Musselburgh (5f, good) in June but she's been up and down since and was a well-held fourth at Hamilton last time; overall record is now 2-30 and she comes with risks attached; one of three runners for the yard.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Triple 5f winner (good) including in this race last year; his last success was off 9lb higher last August but he's finished down the field in most of his runs since; now drops back in trip but he needs a major revival in second-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Ten-race maiden who was runner-up here (6f, good to firm) last Monday but this is a deeper race and she needs to find more on this drop back in trip; yard also runs Wee Mary and Doon The Glen.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Dual C&D winner who had a near-miss at Wetherby (5.5f) last month but she failed to beat a rival at Hamilton last time; handles most ground but has a bit to prove again after that last run and others are more solid.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Get Extra Places On Selected Races' Handicap
Spotlight: Acts on good to firm and good to soft; has patchy profile but he's won twice at Hamilton (6f) this summer including with a late thrust 11 days ago; now drops back in trip but he's only 2lb higher than last time and could be a big factor again if he gets a good pace.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Triple turf winner who made it 2-2 over C&D when bouncing back with a comfortable success (good) three weeks ago; remains feasibly treated off only 3lb higher and he won't mind if the forecast rain arrives; key player.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Record of 2-37 and both wins came over 1m1f (good) last August; has mixed record this season but he had a close call at Pontefract (1m2f) last month and was runner-up behind a big improver over C&D last Monday; on the same mark here and he's respected.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Triple course winner who made all over 1m at this track last September; has generally struggled since but she showed signs of a revival here (fourth of 12) three weeks ago and is now 6lb lower than for her last success; could be dangerous back up in trip and she's versatile ground-wise.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
OwnerName: A Sinclair, I Jardine & V Renwick
Spotlight: Overall record of 3-54 but he's been placed over hurdles in his last two runs and is well handicapped on his best Flat form in 2025; hard to rule out back in this sphere and he has won at this track.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Now 1lb lower than for his Musselburgh win (1m, good) last September but he hasn't posed a serious threat this season and was well held over C&D last Monday; needs to raise his game.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Won a classified event here (1m, good to soft) last July and reached the frame in his next five starts; looks interesting on that form but he lost his way during the winter and has bit to prove after 198 days off.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Four-time hurdle winner who was a respectable third at Perth (2m, good) 25 days ago; still lightly raced on the Flat but she's 5lb higher than for her win here (1m5f, soft) last autumn and not sure this drop back to 1m2f will suit; others are more persuasive.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
OwnerName: D J Jones & M T Brougham
Spotlight: Returned to form with a comfortable win off a reduced mark at Pontefract (1m, good) 12 days ago; back up 6lb in the weights but that was a personal best last time and he's effective at this trip; shortlisted.

RaceName: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap
Spotlight: Well treated on her best form for Ian Williams but she's failed to beat a rival in both runs for current yard; overall record is now 1-14 and she needs a major revival in new headgear.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Half-sister to three winners; dam a half-sister to brilliant staying hurdler Big Buck's; ran twice on the Flat in France last autumn; jumped tidily and won readily on introduction to hurdling at Ballinrobe in May; stable has won this in three of the last five seasons, and seven of the last 12.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: AQPS winner; joined Willie Mullins; Punchestown second in February was quite promising; soundly beaten in the Fred Winter; costly failure at Cork; left Mullins to join Gordon Elliott; took advantage of a 10lb concession when much too strong for his former stablemate Beauvallon (odds-on) at Bellewstown; penalty makes this a much tougher task.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a minor event on the Flat at Roscommon last year; much stronger form when second in a 1m4f Listed race at Leopardstown; has not looked a natural over jumps, but managed a maiden hurdle win at Cork in May; below par in a Listed race at Limerick last time, much better at the Curragh previously.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
OwnerName: Ms P Twiss & J Twiss & M O'Sullivan & S Nevin Twiss
Spotlight: Flat maiden; placed on all six starts over hurdles; beaten favourite in a maiden at Killarney; likely to find this opposition too demanding; stablemate Munsif is rated 4lb higher.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Two Flat wins in 2024; hurdling credentials are weak; unplaced in three Flat handicaps this month.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Ran in two bumpers; not a big price when finishing with only one behind him at Leopardstown in March; contested a strong event at the Punchestown festival; switch to hurdling did the trick when won a 2m3f maiden at Kilbeggan; promising but this looks too demanding.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed a good attitude when making a winning debut at Roscommon three weeks ago; promising sort, but this rise in class may come too soon.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Unplaced in maidens at Clonmel and Sligo; no apparent chance against previous winners.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed ability on sole start on the Flat in Germany (1m2f, soft) last October; made a satisfactory introduction to hurdling when third in a maiden at Roscommon in May; well held in third behind Mino Des Mottes at Bellewstown; can win a maiden but faces a tough task here.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Won three of his six races (at up to 1m4f) for Roger Varian; 0-6 over hurdles; has failed to build on a third-placing in a Naas event in which the top-class Saratoga was second; twice a beaten favourite since then (including in a 4yo handicap at Ascot) and looks vulnerable.

RaceName: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Rated 86 on the Flat, won a 1m4f Cork maiden on soft-to-heavy in May; made a bright start over hurdles when trouncing penalised winners from the Elliott and Mullins stables in a 2m3f conditions event at Kilbeggan six weeks ago; tongue-tie added.

Paid immediate dividends on his first run for the stable when winning a Clonmel handicap hurdle in June and followed up in good style four days later at Sligo; up 16lb in total, but looks to have been prepared with this in mind and his rookie trainer is already showing himself to be a good operator.

13-race maiden over hurdles; easily held by a couple of these in maiden hurdles; unseated when still with a chance at Ballinrobe last week; Darragh O'Keeffe booked ,but needs to find a bit more to land this.

OwnerName: P McCormack & David P McCormack & Sarah Glynn
Spotlight: Winning hurdler and comes here in good form after a convincing success in a 2m handicap chase at Roscommon last month; 9lb lower over flights and a good 5lb claimer booked; makes a compelling case.
Winner on the Flat and very lightly raced over hurdles by comparison; good run in a 1m handicap at Leopardstown in April, but little in her profile marks her out as a potential winner of this.

Kilbeggan maiden hurdle winner two years ago for Liam O'Brien; consistent this year but keeps finding one too good; hold-up horse and likely to need a bit of luck in running; could get into the frame.

Improved significantly on better ground and reportedly settled better when getting up late to land a Sligo maiden hurdle last month; might benefit from a longer trip but probably still capable of improvement, and the stable has been known to come alive at this meeting.
Bumper winner in 2024; some respectable efforts over hurdles but not enough to suggest he can win off this mark; mid-division in a Roscommon Flat maiden last month after seven months off.

Fair form over hurdles in the final months of last season; second in a maiden at Wexford and fourth in a 21-runner handicap at Fairyhouse despite not jumping well; potentially interesting on handicap debut

OwnerName: Michael J Mulligan & Patrick G Walsh
Spotlight: Got off the mark on his first start for the stable in a first-time tongue-tie when landing a 2m handicap hurdle at Ballinrobe in May; emerged with plenty of credit when a good runner-up to a useful performer on the Flat at Bellewstown since; plenty of weight but should make his presence felt.

Gained his second win over hurdles when landing a Downpatrick handicap hurdle in May; mid-division but not disgraced in a 1m5f Ballinrobe Flat handicap since; withdrawn twice on good ground so an ease in the ground would most likely enhance his chances.

Winning hurdler for Joseph O'Brien; took a step forward in his headgear combination when a solid third in a handicap hurdle at Killarney two weeks ago; this is more competitive again but has a squeak if he can improve again.
Last of three wins for Philip Rothwell came at Downpatrick last summer (2m3f); Clonmel claiming second in May his best recent run; debuts for new yard here.

Got off the mark on his only start for John McConnell in a handicap hurdle at Wexford in March; sold for £29,000 at Goffs UK since and makes his stable debut here; has shown preference for cut in the ground but is clearly of interest.

Three-time winner over hurdles for Paul Kiely; ran well despite jumping left on her stable debut at Listowel last month; down the field in a Tramore Flat handicap since; would not be a total surprise if she got involved.

Consistent efforts in bumpers and maiden hurdles rewarded when readily accounting for today's rival Whats New in a Sligo maiden hurdle last month; up 5lb for that and more needed in his first handicap but looks to be going the right way.

OwnerName: Martin Baker & Owen O'Connor & James McCarville
Spotlight: French import has done reasonably well in three maiden hurdle outings; tough ask on his handicap debut and will probably appreciate further, but not dismissed.

Took a keen hold in defeat in maiden hurdles at Clonmel and Tramore; settled better but still found one too good on his return to Tramore in May; handicap hurdle debut here and respected but there might be one or two better handicapped.

Beat Whats New in a juvenile maiden hurdle here in October; no impact in conditions races over hurdles since and down the field in a Fairyhouse Flat handicap last time; others preferred on his handicap debut over hurdles.

Maiden hurdle winner; returned from a six month with a very eye-catching effort when a staying-on fourth to Can Happen at Ballinrobe in May; has the hallmarks of one laid out for this and has the services of a decent 7lb claimer; interesting.

Admirable veteran gained a fourth turf win on the Flat at Sligo in May; has come up short off revised mark since; first run over hurdles since unseating at Cork in March last year for Sneezy Foster; others more likely.

Strong-finishing third on debut at Fairyhouse in June; no obvious reason for a lack-lustre display in a Curragh maiden since; National Stakes entry gives an idea of what he might be thought capable of; adds a fair bit of interest to the contest.

Failed to enjoy much luck in running when fifth in a 6f maiden on debut at Fairyhouse; plenty of improvement likely and looks the first string of the Ballydoyle duo, although cheekpieces have been reached for on just his second start.

Seventh foal; half-brother to winners Poker Face (1m/1m2f inc AW/Group 2; RPR 118) and Star Devine (US 5.5f/6f turf inc stakes; 107); dam 1m2f AW winner (70), half-sister to 1,000 Guineas/Irish Oaks winner Blue Bunting; newcomer with a couple of Group 1 entries; looks the stable second string and likely to improve for this.

E80,000 Y; sixth foal; brother to 1m-1m3f winner Mylady (inc 2yo/German Group 3/US Grade 3; RPR 114), half-brother to three winners inc Maigret (German 1m/8.5f inc 2yo/dirt/Group 3; 114); unraced dam out of French 11.5f winner; mostly middle-distance pedigree; best watched this time, but should be worth watching.

Chased home a subsequent Group 2 winner on his Curragh debut in June; never got involved in the Windsor Castle (behind Our Boy Bailey) but did take a forward step when  a keeping-on third in a Listed 1m contest at Naas; drops back in trip here, but a prominent ride can be expected and he could be tough to pass.
Showed some nice promise on debut in a 7f Curragh maiden last month; might just be up against it a little here, though.

Solid late work when a close second on debut over this trip at Roscommon in May; ran well in the circumstances (One Number behind) in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot; sure to win a maiden and this could be the day.
Last of five and little impact in a 1m maiden at Killarney; Colin Keane booked, but looks a forlorn hope on that evidence.

Most recent of his five wins was in a valuable 2m handicap at Naas in October 2024; ran poorly when well fancied for this race last year, others seem more dependable; one of three in the field for his owner, Derek O'Connor rides.
Useful AW winner in France over 1m/1m1f; campaigned mainly over hurdles by current yard; won over 1m4f on soft at Gowran on penultimate start; big burden even with 7lb claimed.

Course specialist, four of his five Flat wins and both hurdle wins here; highlight when a winning favourite in this race in 2023; scored at a more modest level at last year's meeting, despite almost falling when clipping heels in the dip; rash to ignore; good point-to-point rider claims 7lb.

145-rated staying hurdler; good form in valuable handicaps at Aintree and Haydock in the spring; claimer-ridden when winning a 1m6f maiden at Killarney 13 days ago; could make his presence felt in his first handicap.

Talented hurdler, though inferior to stablemate Daddy Long Legs (first reserve); did well to win a recent Fairyhouse conditions event on his first 2026 outing; Patrick Mullins rides, but worth noting he has partnered only one of the stable's five winners of this since 2017.
Beaten favourite for this race last year, never looked likely to feature, 12th of 20; needs to step up on the form of two Curragh runs this season.

Showed good form in 2024 with a trio of wins from 1m2f-1m6f; runner-up in three of last four starts last term; fourth to Holy See on seasonal return at Gowran in April (1m4f, soft); another solid display when third over 2m at the Curragh.

In rear in the Ascot Stakes after a moderate run over hurdles; breakthrough win was over 1m4f at last year's festival; showed good form on soft ground in the autumn, winning twice, including over 1m5f.

Two from two in bumpers; gained a second win on the Flat when readily taking a 1m6f Gowran handicap in April (soft); raised 8lb for that; needs to reverse recent Faryhouse form with Tounsivator; any further easing of the ground would help.

OwnerName: Annus Mirabilis Synd'/Sean O'Driscoll/Middle Cow Unlimited
Spotlight: Dual-purpose mare; only Flat win came in Leopardstown 3yo maiden (1m2f); good form this term in very competitive handicaps, second at Navan, close fourth of 15 in 2m2f Chester Cup, seventh of 20 behind a stablemate in 2m4f Ascot Stakes; most recent run was in a Group race; one of five for the stable.

Has run only three times since her 50-1 win in this race in 2024 for this rider, also aboard for an emphatic victory over Smooth Tom in a 1m4f conditions event at the Curragh last October; lack of a prep-run could be a drawback.

Won a maiden hurdle at Sligo for Willie Mullins in August 2024; failed to win on the Flat for that stable (no Flat win since 2022); sixth in this last year for Mullins; ran respectably at Tramore on stable debut; however, that was in a claimer; tough task here.

Ex-Polish and German, placed in 1m2f Group races in 2024; took a while to find his level in Irish handicaps; decisively landed a gamble in a 24-runner handicap at the Curragh (1m6f, good) in May; never threatened in the Ascot Stakes; this trip should be within his range; live each-way chance.

Best form at this venue, the scene of three of his six wins; pleasing second at Leopardstown on seasonal debut; failed to improve his weak Curragh record (now unplaced on nine visits) a month ago; highly effective over the extended mile here, this trip may stretch his stamina.

Smart hurdler, 4-7 on the Flat; down the field behind Westminster Moon at Leopardstown on first outing this season; warmed up for this with an odds-on win at Bellewstown; lends substance to yard's strong challenge.
Runner-up in three maiden hurdles in recent months; unappealing on recent Flat form; unplaced favourite in a claimer last time.
Record of six wins form 27 Flat starts; uneven form in a busy campaign since a 2m win at Dundalk in January; hard to fancy against that background.
Eight wins (four on Flat, four over hurdles); ended last season with a Curragh second behind Sirius; confidence dented by recent form over jumps.

Won this readily last year; struggled off 10lb higher in the Irish Cesarewitch; ended the season with a fair sixth in a big 2m handicap at Naas; strong contender despite veteran status;  Dara McGill's 7lb claim an asset, as was Alan O'Sullivan's last year.
Ex-Jessica Harrington/Michael Bell; winner at Group 3 level for his two former trainers; despite reduced mark, does not look well handicapped at this stage; stable debut.

Won over this trip at Dundalk and a 6.5f rated race at Limerick; seemingly improved out of all recognition when a very close second in a 6f Listed at Naas last week; up 16lb for future contests and on that basis is not easily opposable here.
Deserved success when gamely landing a 7f maiden at Limerick last month; has only raced on soft ground to date, and interesting to see how he handles a sounder surface.

Stepped up on her debut effort to win a maiden over this trip for Jarlath Fahey at Limerick in June; changed hands since then. and certainly interesting as a potentially progressive filly on her handicap debut.

Runner-up in a Dundalk maiden last year for Natalia Lupini; returned from seven months off to run a fine race on his seasonal and stable debut when a luckless fourth over 6f at Fairyhouse; definite player although the draw is not ideal.
Broke his duck in a 7f handicap at Limerick last month; not as effective off a 7lb higher mark since, and the drop of 1lb here is not guaranteed to improve her fortunes.
Showed a good attitude to beat Dervo Annie in a Fairyhouse handicap earlier this month; up 6lb and disappointed at Leopardstown a week later; question to answer now.

Followed a good run against a much-improved rival at Down Royal by winning over 6f at Fairyhouse;  another good run at the same venue over 7f; lost a shoe at Killarney last time, but has gone up 11lb in total and will need a career best effort here.
Good run on her handicap debut at Roscommon and go no run when mid-division over 6f at Fairyhouse since; plum draw for a filly likely to go forward and certainly respected.
Has come into a decent level of form on his last two starts; his recent second at Navan franked by the winner at Leopardstown subsequently; should not be far away.
Runner-up in a Kempton maiden last year but struggled this year for Harry Charlton; bought for 20,000gns at the July sales and probably best watched on stable debut.

Fairly consistent level of form in maidens although never really came close to winning one; down 6lb to 73 after his Bellewstown maiden run last time, but even at that he might need to come down a little more.

Ran no race in the first-time visor behind Caitouna at Fairyhouse but seen to much better effect when just overhauled late at Dundalk over 7f two weeks ago; well drawn if she can get a prominent sit and one of the each-way players.
Little to be gleaned from three runs in maidens and well beaten on his handicap debut at Ballinrobe last week; makes little appeal.
Ran too keen and hung right but managed to just about get home in a 7f handicap at Limerick in June; 3lb wrong here, but should get a good pace to aim at and could go well.
Some useful maiden form last year; yet to find his form in two maiden runs this season and others preferred on his handicap debut.
Consistent apart from a poor Navan run on penultimate start; bounced back to win the Ulster Derby over 1m5f at Down Royal last month; stamina assured, new mark is demanding.

Promise when fifth on debut at the Curragh (1m1f, yld-sft) last September; denied by a head over 1m at Leopardstown in October; should be near peak fitness now after a run at Gowran eight weeks ago; dam won over 1m4f, trip should suit.

Ordinary form in maidens; little impact in his first two handicaps; took a step in the right direction when second to Nermal at Roscommon; bound to be fully primed for this; fair chance that this trip will prove close to his optimum.
Consistent in maidens; beat Vantage Code on handicap debut at Roscommon; may struggle to uphold form on 6lb worse terms.
Some promise at two; hard to be confident after his opening handicap attempts at Leopardstown and the Curragh.
Landed a Dundalk maiden early in the year; has found life a little tougher in handicaps; out of her depth in Listed company before a fair fourth at Killarney; stable's best hope is probably Themis.

Eight-race maiden; ran poorly when favourite for a maiden here 12 months ago; mixed signals from this year's form; second to Darius Dark at Cork in April, close fifth behind the same rival at the Curragh; no surprise if she is in the mix.

RaceName: Discover Valentina Luxury Photobooth Experience Apprentice Handicap

RaceName: Prestige Safety Your Competent H&S Service EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B/C/D) (Qual') (GBB)
Spotlight: Last of six on her debut at Beverley (7.5f, good to firm) 23 days ago but in good hands and no surprise were she to show significant improvement on this AW debut.

Spotlight: Missed more than three years after a few starts for Charlie Appleby; started 100-1 for his new yard, having been gelded, at Newbury last month, when well held after racing freely; likely best watched unless there's good money around.

RaceName: Prestige Safety Construction Safety Specialists Handicap (Div II)

Spotlight: Son of Soldier's Call who was much improved from his debut with third of 11 in maiden over C&D eight days ago; he may do better still though has a high draw here.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 9-2, made an encouraging start with second of six in maiden at Musselburgh (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; this Ardad colt is open to progress and must enter calculations.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 18,000 guineas foal, 12,000gns yearling; dam, placed over 9.4f/1m3f AW (RPR 64), is a sister to French Group-placed 7f/1m 2yo winner Rose Bloom; the betting can prove an accurate indicator for this Caturra filly.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Son of Persian Force who has shown fair form when placed in 6f Ayr maiden and 6f Pontefract novice this summer, no extra last half furlong on latter occasion having gone keenly in front; a player here dropping back in trip.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 66-1 but shaped with promise when a debut fourth of 11 in maiden over C&D (good to firm) eight days ago; this daughter of Invincible Army needs considering with likely better to come.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 80-1, ninth of 11 in novice at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) on his debut 27 days ago; lots more is needed from this son of Arizona.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Pearl Secret gelding; half-brother to five winners, notably Ey Up Its The Boss (7f-1m2f; RPR 93) and Ey Up It's Maggie (5f; RPR 91); dam unraced; the market can guide for this newcomer.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 33-1, last of five in maiden at Brighton (5.5f, good to firm) on her debut last month; this Territories filly needs to take a big step forward.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 50-1, well-held sixth of ten in novice at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) on her debut 27 days ago; plenty more is required from this Soldier's Cally filly.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Has failed to beat a rival in 6f Carlisle maiden and 5f Catterick novice this summer; it's easy to look elsewhere.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Lope Y Fernandez filly; dam, unplaced over 6f/7f (RPR 52), is a half-sister to 5f winner Country Carnival, out of Listed-placed 5f-6f winning half-sister to useful 6f-1m winner Yourartisonfire; in good hands and a considered newcomer, especially if the market vibes are positive.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Alkumait filly; well held in 5.5f Wetherby novice and 5f Catterick maiden last month; significantly more is required.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Yet to show any ability in his three runs to date; gelded before beating one in 7f Redcar maiden nine days ago.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Lucky Vega; 68,000euros yearling; beaten only 1.5l when fourth of five in an Ayr novice on debut 15 days ago (7f, good to firm; 5-2); should improve.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 600,000gns yearling by Too Darn Hot; 2l third of nine at Lingfield (AW) on debut this month (7f; more experienced Romanza was second); closely related to a very useful turf performer; major contender.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Best run when 4.5l seventh of 14 in the Chesham in June (7f, good to firm); fair second at Lingfield (AW) next time but not sure to confirm that form with third-placed Apulia Bay, who was making his debut.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Stradavarius half-brother to four winners at up to 1m1f, one Group-placed in Germany; bought for 140,000euros as a yearling; interesting newcomer.

In good form since 8,000gns buy in April, winning off 5lb lower at Brighton in June (7f, good to firm; 8-11) before a good second to a subsequent winner at Doncaster nine days later (1m, good to firm); contender.
Off the mark for the season when winning by a neck at Musselburgh last time (7f, good); could go well again but bit disappointing in only previous run here.
C&D novice winner last August (good to firm); hasn't recaptured her form in three handicaps this season (favourite on first occasion) but returns on a 6lb lower mark having had a wind operation.
Beat a 1-9 shot in a match at Leicester last month (1m, good to firm), but well-beaten last of 11 in a stronger race at York next time (1m, good to firm); bit to prove.

OwnerName: Buist, Shields, Thompson And Mrs R Carr
Spotlight: Two of his three wins last year were on fast ground over C&D; well beaten over C&D on belated reappearance two weeks ago; shpuld come on for that.
Won twice last season (6f, good to firm; 7f, soft), although was disappointing on last two runs; hasn't recaptured her form this season; best watched for now.
Ran his best race of the season when close second in a low-grade C&D handicap last time (good to firm); has a stiffer task up in grade here.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: Won three on the trot last season (5f/6f); off the mark for the current year when scoring at Ayr 15 days ago (6f, good to firm); up 3lb; should go well again.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to win on turf, but sound runs when runner-up at Thirsk (5f, good) and Ayr (5f, good to firm) on last two starts; one with a chance.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Three sound runs this term, winning his last two, at Wetherby in June (5.5f, good to firm) and over C&D two weeks ago (good to firm); this looks a stronger race, but he could go well again.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: Grange Park Racing XIII & Ruth Carr
Spotlight: Pontefract winner in April (5f, good to soft); two good runs in May, the first when second over this C&D; hasn't been in such good form on last two runs.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: Slaters Arms Racing And Ged Shields
Spotlight: Mainly in good form last season, winning over 6f at Pontefract in June (6f, good); disappointing this season, but now 3lb below his last winning mark.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Dual C&D winner last July (good to firm/soft); yet to hit top form this season, although hasn't been beaten far on last two runs.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Has been rather disappointing since winning off 1lb lower at Ripon in April (6f, good to soft), including in cheekpieces two runs ago (last of 13 at York); effective at 5f; easier ground suits.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins this term, the first at Southwell in April and the second over C&D last week (good to firm); could go well from her low draw, but lacks consistency.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Won 5f Ayr handicap off 6lb higher in May last year (5f, good to firm) but mainly disappointing since, including on last two starts; bit to prove at present.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Showed enough in three runs in the spring to think she can be a factor at this level now handicapping; goes on the shortlist for her much in-form trainer.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Didn't look to enjoy the Brighton experience last time, but his small-field selling second previously didn't amount to much anyway (Jazzy Bay third); trainer does much better with 2yos on the AW than turf and he'll need to improve now handicapping.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Not looked the easiest thus far and goes without the cheekpieces again having not seen out a stiffer 7f last time; trainer 0-27 with 2yos this season and it wouldn't say much for the others were she able to take this.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Run to a similar level all four starts, incuding behind Parading in a seller in May; didn't look to have any excuses on his nursery debut last time but coming back up from 6f won't hurt.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices for three runs to date (5f-6f) last month and finished a well-beaten last each time; trainer 0-24 with 2yos for the season and a shock were he the one to put him on the board.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Backward step at Newbury last time but has stamina on her dam's side and the extra furlong may help now handicapping off a lowly opening mark; holds each-way claims from the outside stall.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Done most racing over 5f, didn't look to see out 6f in one try, has hung both ways and is looking exposed; cheekpieces go back on and he doesn't make obvious appeal.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Trainer back among the winners and got on the board for the year with 2yos recently (nursery newcomer); he does well with juveniles here too and this filly, who ran green on debut before pulling hard second time, is open to improvement.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Disappointing in a seller last time (second run at that level) and the visor goes back on tonight; trainer among the winners and his strike-rate with 2yos is up a touch this season but he's looking exposed now.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Nothing exciting in three 6f starts round Windsor, latterly when said to have hung left late on; stable having a quiet year thus far (0-23 with 2yos) and he'll need to improve for the extra furlong.

Made a winning debut in 7f Salsibury novice in July 2024; lightly raced since but has posted good third placings in 1m handicaps at Newbury and Yarmouth this summer; very much one to consider off same mark.
Starman filly who is much improved of late, building on Windsor second with breakthrough success in seven-runner handicap over C&D 29 days ago; up 3lb but she merits serious consideration.
Got off the mark at the ninth attempt over C&D last August; yet to hit top form this summer, although saddle reportedly slipped when sixth of eight over C&D four weeks ago; not out of things.
Gained a first win at the third attempt in 7f Chepstow maiden in July; last of ten on handicap debut at Newbury (1m) 11 days ago; lots more is needed in a first-time tongue-tie.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Dixon, Wylam, M Baldry, J&s Harrod
Spotlight: Still capable of modest form on occasions last year, including two 1m wins on Southwell AW, but competitive only once (penultimate start) in 2026.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-21 before he won a classified at Chepstow (1m, good to firm) four days ago; he'd been knocking on the door with four seconds in his preceding five races this summer, including twice after six-day absences; concedes 5lb all round today but most of the others have been struggling.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Hampered and unseated on latest start; second in a 7.3f classified here the time before and had a turf win last July, with plenty of occasions too in which he's not been far away, so has each-way claims.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three wins in an industrious 2025 and another this March; three of those were AW, as was the respectable show in first-time cheekpieces on latest start, while last June's 1m classified win at Chepstow was on soft; others look more solid these days on today's likely good or good to firm ground.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Ex-Irish (1m1f winner in 2024); running for this yard since December and the odd piece of that form gives him a shout, including penultimate start but that was on soft ground; below form sole start on firmer than good.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 16-race maiden who has some modest form (mostly on AW) but was beaten 38l and 30l this month in his two starts for new stable; at least this drop back in trip looks a plus.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Hasn't shown much over jumps and same story this year switched to the Flat; keeps being slowly away and refused to race here on penultimate appearance, admittedly without her usual hood, but still hard to fancy.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Hood both starts; second of eight at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) and second of three at Chester (1m2f, good) in another maiden; not bred for this far but the same was true last time when she again did her best work at the finish.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 400,000gns yearling; second in a three-runner novice at Nottingham (1m2f, good) in June, behind a long odds-on favourite, and set the pace when fourth of six in a maiden at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) 18 days later; hooded for both; that's fair form, among the best in this field, and pedigree gives her a good chance to stay 1m4f.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 11th of 14 on debut at Lingfield (7f, AW) in November but spectacularly outran odds of 125-1 when third of 12 in a novice at Kempton (1m3f, AW) three weeks ago, nearly taking second; switches to turf but she's in the same ballpark on ratings as the best two of these.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Set the pace when last of four at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) and ran on from the rear when fourth of ten in a maiden at Pontefract (1m2f, good; 40-1) 17 days later; the latter showed promise but further improvement is needed against all three of today's rivals.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Went close in a bumper on her debut last spring before not taking to hurdles; well held in three Flat runs this season but this task is more realistic now handicapping and she's one to track in the market.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Hold-up performer who's odds-on to blow the start; landed a hat-trick last summer over about this trip on good to firm ground, latterly off a 1lb higher mark, but not as consistent this time round; needs more.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Goes well here and took advantage of the drop to 0-50 classified company when winning a weak race over C&D early last month; ran at least as well back into handicap company here four weeks ago to confirm himself still in good form.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
OwnerName: Mike Harris Racing & Nikki Evans Racing
Spotlight: Held a couple of times round his beloved Bath in 0-55 company since winning from Bobby Dassler there in the spring; usually dropped in and will want a decent test round this easier course.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: His 0-50 classified win here last month has been well advertised since and he just did enough back into a handicap at Leicester (1m4f) last time, despite hanging left on good to firm ground; up 3lb with good chance of the hat-trick.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Four defeats at short prices off this sort of mark since two Windsor wins late last summer; didn't look to love the Epsom experience last time, though, and will rightly be popular again; shortlisted.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has done a lot of his racing at 1m and has often pulled hard when going further, including in the hood (back on tonight; tongue-tie comes off) but does stay this far; not much room for manoeuvre off this mark and needs to leave two lesser efforts behind.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Strong in the market on comeback from almost a year off early in the month, when the race didn't set up ideally, and duly won a 1m6f amateurs' handicap on Wolverhampton Tapeta last Tuesday; fair claims under a 5lb penalty.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Irish trainer 14-51 with Flat runners brought over, which entitles this 4yo to some respect; it's hard to find any other positives, though, with him yet to get involved in a finish under either code; the market will likely tell a tale.
No problem with 7f and found the drop to 5f against him last month, when again running well off this mark; stable among the winners and he's high on the shortlist back up in trip.

Wins for two previous yards came in the autumn, mainly on the AW, and he's regressed in recent times; the step back up from 5f is a plus off a career-low mark, though, for a trainer who holds more obvious claims with Symbol Of Hope.
Longstanding maiden who's overall continued to regress this year, mainly over 7f; has been offering a bit more again of late, without having the breaks, but others look stronger.

New trainer won with six of his last 12 runners and is 4-12 with runners here; that's where the positives end, as she showed little for two previous yards (6f-1m) before being picked up for 900gns early last month; watch the market.

Winner over this trip but doesn't run over it often now, all starts this year having come over 5f; continues to tumble down the weights but has struggled in two runs back on turf latterly and others make more appeal.

Three wins and three seconds from eight runs here and he will be happier sprinting again having not seen out 1m last month; time has looked to be catching up this year, however, and Legendsoftheland appears his trainer's best chance.

Wins have all come after a recent outing and he's having just a second ever run on turf, in a first-time tongue-tie; it's therefore hard to say that everything looks in place for a big run, for a yard also responsible for Honour Your Dreams.
Closed out last year with a Tapeta win in first-time cheekpieces off 2lb higher; struggled this time round and will need to improve somewhat on previous turf efforts.
Best efforts have all come on Tapeta and he's struggled in both runs this season, having regressed last year; not easy to make a case for him.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Bumper winner; has made a flawless start over hurdles, winning a Punchestown maiden hurdle (16.5f, gd-yld) by 8.25l and a Roscommon novice (2m, good) by 3.5l; unexposed and preferred by Jack Kennedy; obvious chance.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Nicholas Fahy/Mrs Orla Fahy/Two Sheets to the Wind Syndicate
Spotlight: Close second in a Punchestown bumper in January (2m, sft-hvy); justified favouritism to land an ordinary Downpatrick mares' maiden hurdle (2m2f, good) two weeks ago; this is harder but she's unexposed in this sphere so don't discount.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: One of two for yard; 2-3 over hurdles and rated 130; won Punchestown 4yo maiden in mid-May (2m, good); added a 4yo hurdle at Ballinrobe (2m, good) later that month; could be more to come but Jack Kennedy prefers the chances of Lizzie Twigg.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a bumper in fine style at this meeting last year for Andy Slattery; disappointed in a Leopardstown bumper on debut for this yard in December; much more like it when winning on hurdling debut at Listowel (16.5f, good) latest and the third from that race has won since; big player.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Flat winner; 0-4 over hurdles and rated 103; 1.25l second in Market Rasen maiden hurdle 23 days ago (20.5f, good); cheekpieces go on but surely out of depth in this company; due to run 5.40 here on Monday.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Runner up in two of four starts in bumpers; filled the same spot on hurdling debut in a mares' maiden at Kilbeggan; this is much tougher.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Decent strike rate over fences (3-10) and rated 121; disappointed on sole start over hurdles at Punchestown in April and beaten 5l in Kilbeggan handicap chase on latest; cheekpieces worn that day discarded; others are more persuasive.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 0-2 in point-to-points and 0-4 over hurdles; beaten off 82 in Cork handicap hurdle on latest; this looks far too demanding.

Point-to-point winner; scored in a bumper at this meeting last year; 1-8 over hurdles and rated 137; half-brother to two chase winners and dam a half-sister to high-class chaser Empire Of Dirt; acts on good ground and interesting on chase debut.

Very useful over hurdles (5-18, rated 147); goes on any ground and should be sharper for his latest run in a Grade 3 hurdle at Limerick after an 87 day break; every chance he'll take to this game on breeding; big player on chase debut.

Novice hurdle winner here in October 2024 (20.5f, soft); lightly raced since; sent off the 6-4 favourite in this last year on return from 234 days off and found just one too good; similar preparation this year and Townend keeps the faith; player.

One of three for yard; bumper winner; 2-6 over hurdles and rated 135; has come up short in graded hurdles on last four starts; dam a useful chaser so could take to this discipline; tongue tie goes on; not discounted.

0-3 in point-to-points; 2-6 and rated 117 over hurdles; promising start to chasing career when runner up at Wexford; blotted copybook when unseating at the first back there on latest; probably up against it in this company.
2-18 over hurdles; rated 114 after two chase starts; rallied well for a close second in Punchestown novice chase on latest (20.5f, gd-yld); more needed dropped in trip.

One of three for yard; 1-6 over hurdles and rated 121; promising start over fences when a 2.75l third at Wexford (2m7f,gd-yld); soundly beaten over 19.5f (good) back there on latest, overlooked by Townend and this trip may be on the sharp side.
Useful dual-purpose performer; rated 83 on the Flat; 1-6 over hurdles and rated 127; out of form on the Flat this year, however, and not bred for chasing; others appeal more.
1-13 and rated 117 over hurdles; below best in that sphere in 2026 and moderate run in Flat maiden at Killarney on latest; best watched on chase debut.
Won just one of twelve starts in point-to-points; unseated in both previous starts under Rules; hard to make a case for.
Two wins over hurdles for Gavin Cromwell; 0-7 over fences and has a tendency to jump left at times; ground conditions will suit but soundly beaten over hurdles on latest and others make more appeal.
Winning hurdler yet to make much impression over the bigger obstacles; remote second at Bangor in May her best effort but soundly beaten at Hexham on latest; needs more.

Two-time winner over timber, including at this venue last September (16.5f, gd-yld); 0-5 over fences but hasn't run badly the last twice (trip too far on latest) and the handicapper is giving him a chance; likes it here and not dismissed.

Won off 3lb lower at Thurles (18.5f, yielding) in November; struggled on next three starts but step in right direction when a 5l third of seven at Wexford on latest (15.5f, good, jockey dropped whip after two out); eased 1lb and this longer trip more suitable.

In excellent form since return from long layoff; won over hurdles at Kilbeggan in April; added a Cartmel handicap chase (17.5f, good) last month; this is tougher, however, so will need a career best to follow up.

Point to point winner has yet to make much of an impact under Rules; well held in beginners' chase at Wexford on latest (behind Ned In The Park); previously pulled up in handicap chase at Tramore; in good hands but much more needed.

One of three for stable; flat and hurdles winner off the mark over fences off 6lb lower at Wexford (2m, gd-yld) when last seen in May; this longer trip should be fine and yard made hay at this meeting last season; can't discount.

Three-time winning hurdler; 2-13 in chases, his last win coming over 2m6f (good) at Thurles in January 2025 off 9lb higher; hinted at a return to form when staying on for a remote fourth at Wexford latest (2m, good); on a dangerous mark and this longer trip will suit.

2-9 over fences; won off 12lb lower at Clonmel in January (2m, heavy) and off 6lb lower at Tramore (15.5f, yielding) in April; not beaten far off 2lb lower at Wexford (2m, gd-yld) on latest; return to a right-handed track a plus; stays this far and in the mix.

Winning hurdler is 0-11 over fences; ran okay in handicap chases over further at Clonmel and Wexford earlier this year but seems best with cut in the ground; beaten 22l on good ground in a handicap hurdle on latest.

Has won over hurdles but 0-8 in chases and yet to trouble the judge; beaten 33l in 2m Punchestown handicap chase on latest; drops in grade, steps up in trip and cheekpieces go on; needs more for last year's winning stable.

One of three for yard; sent off favourite and rewarded backers with a first win over fences at Wexford (19.5f, good) on latest, beating A Snow White Park by 2.5l; 6lb higher now and steps up in grade but should go well again.

OwnerName: Ed Mulligan & John Finnegan & Aileen Saunders & Ann Holton
Spotlight: Point winner scored in a handicap chase at Ayr in December (16.5f, heavy); pulled up behind Finnians Row at Downpatrick on latest; may need softer ground than this.

Two-time hurdles winner; his good second over fences at Roscommon in June (16.5f, yielding) would give him a chance here but didn't back it up at Wexford and failed to fire back over hurdles at Killarney on latest.

One of three for yard; off the mark over fences in a Downpatrick beginners (19.5f, gd-yld) in May (Giant Haystacks 2.75l behind in fourth); unseated two out in handicap chase back there on latest when still in contention; can't discount off 2lb higher.

5-33 over fences and arrives on the back of successive front running 19.5f wins at Downpatrick, both on good ground; has gone up a total of 13lb but clearly in good heart and should make another bold bid here.
Veteran; 1-18 over fences, the win coming on testing ground at Listowel in September 2024; out of form when last seen in February and remains 4lb above that last success; others appeal more.

1-12 over hurdles; posted a solid effort on chase debut in a beginners' at Wexford (19.5f, good) last month, keeping on from the back for a 4.5l second of 14; not obviously well treated for handicap chase bow but not written off.

Promise in all three chase starts, including when a 2.5l second behind Giant Haystacks in a handicap at Wexford on latest despite not jumping fluently at times; nudged up 2lb and this is tougher but could go well if jumping better.

Won over hurdles at Downpatrick (2m2f, good) in May and rated 8lb higher in that sphere; 0-4 over fences but has shown potential, including when a 6.5l third at Wexford in June; runner up over hurdles on latest; more needed back over fences.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Only 1/2l behind subsequent winner Livenka when fourth on debut at the Curragh, a race won stylishly by Alpha who scrambled home at short odds in a Group 3 race at Leopardstown last week; promising.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Apprentice-ridden when 5l third of eight in a maiden at Listowel in May; form of that race has been boosted by runner-up Big Negotiator; picked up valuable experience when third in a 7f maiden at Newmarket 19 days ago; winner Scommessa Secura can be rated a useful yardstick.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Saxon Warrior filly; made a satisfactory debut in taking third behind the well-fancied Livenka on debut at Fairyhouse; just lost second to Star Of State who has since won a Leopardstown maiden with the greatest of ease; winner's form also linked to Samnina.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Finished first in a barrier trial; excellent effort in a maiden at Cork (6f, good) when beaten 1.2l into second by subsequent Group 3 winner Ballinea Star; overall form of the race is possibly suspect.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Zoustar filly; dam 7f winner, sister to 1m2f Group 1 winner Laganore; no match for the smart Folsom Blues (subsequent Group 3 runner-up) on soft ground at Gowran in June; Shane Foley on Samnina.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E380,000 yearling; seventh foal; half-sister by Zarak to four winners; dam unraced half-sister to 5f Group 2 winner Muthmir.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 65,000gns yearling; eighth foal; sister to Group 2 winner Wonderful Moon, half-sister to four winners; trainer also runs two who have form in the book.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 550,000gns yearling; eighth foal; Wootton Bassett filly is a half-sister to three winners, including a Group 3 scorer in France; dam a Group-placed winner by Sea The Stars, half-sister to dual French Classic winner Lope De Vega; apprentice aboard for debut.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E52,000 yearlong, E80,000 Breeze Up; fourth foal; half-sister by Bayside Boy to a seven-time winner in France; dam was a Listed winner in France and Germany.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Well held by Argentarius on Cork running; never involved at Leopardstown on second outing.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Stable's second-string now, as on her first two starts; will need a handicap mark.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 66-1, always at the back first time out in a maiden at Leopardstown 12 days ago.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won the Irish Lincoln last season; attempted to bring off the double at Doncaster and produced a fine effort to finish third of 22 behind Godwinson; has failed to prosper since third to Dunum in this last year; however, he is 8lb lower now and should be at peak fitness after a Curragh prep-run in a race dominated by Pierre Royal and Booyea.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won a Gowran maiden (1m, good) for Dermot Weld last May; met trouble in running on stable/seasonal debut in a Limerick race won by Monvoe; improved from that when beating Booyea in a 1m premier handicap at the Curragh a month ago; up 9lb, might struggle to confirm form with Booyea (up 5lb).

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won 2025 Irish Cambridgeshire for Dermot Weld, beating today's rival Genuine Article by a short head; maintained his good record in races over 1m when an emphatic winner from stablemate Far Form Dandy at Naas on seasonal/stable debut; mid-division in the Royal Hunt Cup, seventh of 20 in his group, not a bad effort.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Ran against smart Ballydoyle colts as a juvenile; won a three-runner 1m conditions event at Naas in March; did not quite see out the extended 1m2f when third in the Prix Noailles at Longchamp; failed to run to expectations in a valuable Gowran contest; could make a high-class handicapper, but no horse of his age has won this since 2004; cheekpieces added.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Enjoyed a terrific spell last October, notching three wins and two places during a hectic spell; maintained his rate of improvement when beating 24 rivals in the Irish Lincoln on return; early-season form also included second in a 1m2f premier handicap at the Curragh; unplaced twice in Listed races this term; handicap form gives him a leading chance; drawn low.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won on debut at Dundalk in 2024; ran well in top handicaps last season, including third in Victoria Cup at Ascot and second in Ahonoora over 7f at this venue; has taken a while to hit form this season; opened his turf account last month at the 15th attempt; up 7lb for that 7f Cork success.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Ended 2025 with a pair of heavy-ground wins at Doncaster (7f); useful form in defeat this year, in the frame in competitive York handicaps (good ground) on consecutive days last month; another good run when fifth of 17 on quick going at the same venue last time; ground-versatile, trip a worry.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Has failed to deliver on initial promise as a hurdler; out of his depth in top juvenile events; excuse for failure to take advantage of drop in class at Ballinrobe; won over an extended 7f in France at three; never out of the first three in six races; apart from one AW run, all Flat form on soft or worse; drawn high.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Has done most of her racing at 1m, odds-on for her sole win in a Killarney maiden last autumn; more recent form over longer distances in good company; this is closer to her optimum.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
OwnerName: Just The Two Of Us Partnership
Spotlight: Last of five wins was in 2023 when he ran well in a Group 3 at Leopardstown and a Listed contest at Killarney; not the force he was, though he has run well from time to time, including when sixth of 14 at 80-1 in this race last year; fair third at Killarney last time; valuable 5lb claimed, could go well at a decent price.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Only two wins from 22 Flat starts; however, he won a C&D handicap 12 months ago, and has been placed nine times; below best on seasonal debut at the Curragh in April; more like it when fifth at the same venue in May; drawn high.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Completed a four-timer when winning a 7f handicap here in 2022; won the 7f Ahonoora Handicap at the 2023 festival; made it three from six at this venue (also placed three times) when winning this event last year; third in the Ahonoora later that week; absent since last September; stiff task against that background, despite his liking for the track.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: No win on turf since September 2024; has run well in defeat in good handicaps this season, including fourth to Ribee in Irish Lincoln; also second to stablemate Jagged Edge at Naas; below-par last time in a Curragh race dominated by Pierre Royal and Booyea; drawn low.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Seven-time winner, including Listed and Group 3 races; not a bad effort (seventh behind Pierre Royal at the Curragh) on first handicap start since 2023; towards the back at Leopardstown last time; cheekpieces tried.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won on good ground at two in France; ran only twice for William Haggas in 2024; same last year for this stable, the best of those a second at Leopardstown on the first of two late-season handicap outings; dismal form in three subsequent outings

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Four-time winner at 7f/1m, the last two at Listed level over 1m on heavy ground in the Knockaire Stakes at Leopardstown, the scene of his best form; beaten only a neck in this race two years ago, tenth behind Dunum last year; drawn low.
Two AW wins last year; opened his turf account at the 15th attempt at Naas last week; one of three for the stable here; could feature with the champion jockey booked; draw should help.

Nine-time turf winner, including a 6f Group 3 in 2023; has also won at Listed level and was once rated 108, so has dropped a long way; inconsistent in recent years; has run well in two sprint handicaps at the Curragh lately.
7f maiden winner at Limerick last season on his sixth and final start for Aidan O'Brien; went close in a 6f handicap at Navan four three starts ago; more recent form is much less encouraging.

OwnerName: B White & M W White & D Sheridan & Ms H McGuinness
Spotlight: Good second at Leopardstown on seasonal debut; race may have come too soon at the Curragh four days later; solid third at Cork next time; hard task now having been raised 9lb for beating Send Harry at Leopardstown; unplaced in this race last year.
Has recorded three of his seven wins at Listowel and also twice successful over C&D; out of form before signs of a revival at Limerick last month; still looks risky.

Prolific winner, latest in Gowran claimer nearly a year ago; 0-10 for current yard; best form this season represented by Down Royal second in May and third at Fairyhouse early this month, both over this trip.

OwnerName: F J Carragher/Yorkavenue Syndicate/Park Ave Syndicate
Spotlight: Only one win from 27 starts and that was on AW for Brian Meehan in 2023; fair AW form early this year and showed that a turf win could be within his range when second to Dancing Saxon at Limerick last time; form given a big boost by the winner in a Listed race; handicap mark reduced by a stone over the past 12 months; may come good now from low draw..

Both wins have come over 1m at Killarney; won a maiden there last summer (yielding to soft) and returned there a year later to record a first handicap success (good); finished 1 3/4l behind Zaraahmando when fourth at Gowran last Saturday.

Only win from 23 starts came on heavy ground at Gowran last September; failed to retrieve her best form in her first four outings this term; placed twice (7f/1m1f) at Leopardstown since then, both races run on soft; stamina stretched by 1m2f at the Curragh a month ago.
Gained second win of career over 1m at Leopardstown on seasonal return last month, beating Zaraahmando by a neck; went up 8lb for that, and Zaraahmando turned the tables last time.

Consistent form last year; won at Killarney's July fixture and ended the campaign with seconds at Leopardstown and Dundalk; raced too keenly when stepped up in trip on reappearance at Roscommon a month ago; probably best at 1m.

Four-time AW winner, sole turf success came in 5f handicap at Naas in May 2024; solid effort over 1m at Bellewstown in April and backed that up with a close third over 6f at Naas; a long way below his best at Leopardstown on latest.

OwnerName: Ian O'Connor & The Fox And Hounds
Spotlight: Only one pound higher than when winning at last year's festival; had the same high draw then, so should not be ruled out; has to bounce back from a below-par Salisbury run; previous fourth placings at Doncaster and Thirsk were respectable; had the same high draw last year.

Dual AW winner; highlight of British form when second to Big Evs in a Listed race at York in May 2024; rated 99 at his peak. gained his first turf success off 72 when making all in a 20-runner contest at the Curragh three starts ago; now 10lb higher.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Showed promise in making the frame in two starts last autumn; placed in three 7f maidens this term; beaten favourite when second at Naas on seasonal debut; eased up late for third at Gowran; rated 83 before chasing home the long odds-on Bamako Beach at Fairyhouse; 13lb rise to 96 may flatter him; obvious chance all the same.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Fair fourth over 1m at Leopardstown on the second of two starts at two; appeared not to see out the extended 1m1f at Gowran on return; better when going close over an extended 7f at Roscommon; should be able to win an average maiden; tough task here against Sindagan, a high-rated gelding in the same colours.
Respectable first outing when fourth in a 1m Gowran maiden won by a stablemate of Sindagan; form of that race has been well-advertised by runner-up Loughrea.

E29,000 Y, E330,000 Breeze Up purchase; had a run in a barrier trial but still looked a bit raw when sixth in an 18-runner contest at the Curragh in early June; confirmed promise when a clear second behind an 82-rated rival in a 6f maiden on second start.

Promising start in 7f maiden at Leopardstown in May, fourth of nine despite racing a shade keenly; again keen and got outpaced over the same trip at the Curragh ten days ago; unlikely to be good enough.
E50,000 yearling (bought in for E75,000 at a Breeze Up last year); sixth foal; half-sister to winners, best of them Asad Zabeel (five races and Listed-placed); dam French middle-distance winner.
66-1, looked very raw at the Curragh, when finishing in rear in the race in which Starborn Legend was second.
Beaten in excess of 15l in maidens at Limerick and Killarney; up against it.
Debut was over 1m4f; down the field in 7f Fairyhouse race in which Sindagan was second.
First foal; dam 5f AW winner, out of a half-sister to a 1m2f Listed winner and to the dam of Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Gaelic Warrior; 4yo Buratino gelding makes belated debut.
Has finished in front of only two of her 29 rivals in three outings at Dundalk; can be ruled out.
Third foal; Arizona filly, dam of little account but half-sister to two winning hurdlers.
Sixth foal; half-brother by Alkumait to two Italian winners and a winning hurdler; dam 1m AW winner, half-sister to an Italian Group-placed winner.

Showed promise in 7f maidens at the Curragh and Gowran on her first two starts; faced a tough task in the Goffs Million; strong form when a short head second to subsequent Sandringham winner Green Carrera in a 1m handicap at the Curragh on seasonal debut; a long way below that form over 1m1f at the same venue last time.

Five-time winner including twice this season; stayed on well to see off Elusive Duke at Ballinrobe (9.5f, gd-yld) eight days ago (Loingseoir fourth) and raised 7lb; has gone well here before but very wide draw not ideal.

Two-time C&D winner on heavy off higher marks; went close again over C&D in October, again on heavy; caught the eye when short of room and not beaten far at Killarney on latest (1m, good); softer conditions would be preferable but he's got plenty of decent form on this sort of ground and his yard targets this meeting; chance.

OwnerName: W Keeling & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick
Spotlight: Seven-time winner; hold up sort has run respectably in three of his last four starts; stayed on well for fourth behind Lady Arwen at Ballinrobe latest; placed at this meeting over 7f in 2022; ground versatile and could go well granted luck in running.

Four-time winner; scored on seasonal return at Cork off 8lb lower; chased home Bay Of Dreams off 2lb lower at Bellewstown on penultimate; never landed a blow behind Lady Arwen at Ballinrobe on latest; visor replaces cheekpieces.

One of two for yard; AW and turf winner for James Ferguson; off the mark for this stable on latest at Bellewstown (1m, good); 8lb rise makes things tougher but this prominent racer is well drawn and can't be discounted for last year's winning yard.
Five-time winner including here over 7f on heavy; off since a poor run here last October; is 9lb below last win but best form is on testing ground so could do with some rain.
2-5 on the AW; won on turf at Gowran last season (1m, good) off 12lb lower; moderate efforts over further the last twice and may be in handicapper's grip for now.
French winner has yet to fire since joining this yard; mark is tumbling, however, and he's worth monitoring in the market now dropped in class with cheekpieces back on.
Won a Goodwood novice for James Horton; gradually finding form for this yard and not beaten far at the Curragh on latest; cheekpieces now go on but she's drawn in the car park here.

OwnerName: Charles Kerwin & Brendan Kerwin & Liam Kehoe
Spotlight: One of three for yard; gained second turf win at Roscommon in May (7.5f, good) off 9lb lower; soundly beaten in three runs since including off lower AW mark latest; drawn wide.

Gained first turf win off 8lb lower at Limerick (1m, yielding) in June; narrowly denied in follow up bid two days later at Gowran (9.5f, yielding); handles good ground and top rider booked but the draw gods haven't been kind.
One of three for yard; gained second turf win at Gowran in June (1m, yielding), making all; beaten off revised mark twice since and wide draw not ideal for this front runner.

One of three for yard; 2-16 on turf; won over 1m at Leopardstown (good) last season off 66; scored at Down Royal (7f, good) off 67 in May and just 1lb higher here but in poor form since and needs to revive in new headgear combination.

One of two for yard; back-to-back wins at Leopardstown last summer over 7f on soft and good ground; yet to hit top form this term but is now 2lb below her last win and rider takes off another 3lb; ran poorly at this meeting last year.
Decent strike rate on the AW (4-10) but just 1-16 on turf; that win came over 1m2f (good) at Fairyhouse in May; struggled off revised mark twice since and wide draw to overcome here.
Won over C&D at this meeting in 2024 off 15lb higher; that win came on yielding and his last win came on heavy so while well handicapped, could probably do with a drop of rain.

Had sunk markedly in the weights before first-time blinkers saw him take a six-runner race at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) 11 days ago in clearcut fashion, coming from last for his first win since a 2yo; back up 5lb but maybe he's turned a corner in the headgear.

1-8 for William Haggas; second run for new connections when he resumed improvement to make all in ten-runner race at Leicester (1m2f, good; acts on good to firm) in June, well clear through the final 2f; those wins are two of the four times he's made the running, which will be more difficult in this larger field and after a 10lb rise but he looked good last time.
Runner-up in 2024 on his only appearance at this track; reliable sort who hit new heights over 1m4f on last three outings, so this drop back in trip asks a question but he needs respect.
